The resulting thermal evolution follows a broken power law as the ejecta transition from the optically thick to the optically thin regime. We incorporate this thermal history into a relativistic spectral calculation that accounts for the equal-arrival-time surface geometry and Doppler boosting, enabling us to model the observed kilonova spectrum and constrain the underlying ejecta properties. We investigate the effects of the model parameters and relativistic corrections on the observed temperature and spectral shape, and find that light-travel-time delays and Doppler shifts can produce significant spectral distortions at high ejecta velocities. We apply the model to the early-time X-shooter spectrum of the kilonova AT2017gfo and infer the ejecta mass, opacity, and velocity through Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fitting with a Student's $t$ likelihood. We find that relativistic effects become increasingly important for fast ejecta ($v \gtrsim 0.5c$), particularly at large viewing angles, where the observed temperature can differ substantially from the rest-frame effective temperature. These results highlight the importance of incorporating relativistic and equal-arrival-time effects when interpreting early-time kilonova spectra, especially for rapidly expanding ejecta.

title: Production of vacuum particles from relativistic scalar particles in a deformed spacetime
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the quantum dynamics of relativistic scalar particles in a (1+1)-dimensional de Sitter spacetime deformed by rainbow gravity, in which the spacetime metricdepends explicitly on the energy of the probing particles. We begin by deriving the covariantKlein–Gordon equation in this modified gravitational background and obtain its exact solutionsby two independent methods, in terms of Whittaker and Hankel functions. Building upon thisformulation, we analyze the corresponding energy spectrum and the semiclassical solutions, andsubsequently examine vacuum particle production within the Bogoliubov approach. Both sets ofsolutions lead to the same particle number density, which takes the form of a thermal Bose–Einsteindistribution depending only on the temporal rainbow function f_1. In the large-mass limit, it reducesto a Boltzmann factor characterized by an effective Gibbons–Hawking temperature T = f_1H/2π,showing that rainbow gravity rescales the de Sitter horizon temperature and can either enhance orsuppress particle creation relative to general relativity.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Probing the Single Production of First-Generation Singlet Vector-like Leptons at Future $e^+e^-$ Colliders
abstract: We study the single production of first-generation weak-isosinglet vector-like leptons (VLLs) at future $e^+e^-$ colliders through $e^+e^-\to e^\pm E^\mp$, with the subsequent decays $E^\pm\to W^\pm\nu_e$, $e^\pm Z$, and $e^\pm h$. For the heavy VLL masses considered, the hadronic decays of the $W$ and $Z$ bosons are reconstructed as fat-jets, while the Higgs boson is reconstructed from two resolved $b$-tagged jets at $\sqrt{s}=1~{\rm TeV}$ and as a fat-jet at $\sqrt{s}=1.5~{\rm TeV}$. Using detector-level Monte Carlo simulations for the 1~TeV ILC and 1.5~TeV CLIC, we perform a baseline cut-based analysis in which the well-defined two-body production kinematics are exploited through a mass-hypothesis-dependent selection on the associated-electron energy. At fixed nominal center-of-mass energy, this observable is in one-to-one correspondence with the VLL recoil mass and therefore provides a common mass-sensitive discriminator for all three decay channels. We derive the $2\sigma$ exclusion and $5\sigma$ discovery reaches on the VLL--electron mixing angle $\sin\theta_L$ as functions of the integrated luminosity. For the benchmark points studied, sizeable sensitivity is retained at $m_E=900~{\rm GeV}$ at the ILC and $m_E=1400~{\rm GeV}$ at CLIC, while the accessible values of $\sin\theta_L$ extend below the reference electroweak precision bound used in this study. These results demonstrate the complementary potential of direct searches for first-generation singlet VLLs at future lepton colliders.

title: Parton distribution functions of the proton in a hot isospin-asymmetric nuclear medium and finite nuclei
abstract: When a nucleon is bound in a nucleus, its quark distributions are modified, and the change in the spin-dependent distributions can differ in size from that in the spin-independent ones. We compute the unpolarized $f_1(x)$, helicity $g_1(x)$, and transversity $h_1(x)$ distributions of the $u$ and $d$ quarks in a proton immersed in hot and isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter. The proton is described in the diquark spectator model, with the medium effects entering through the effective quark, diquark, and proton masses computed using the chiral SU(3) quark mean field (CQMF) model. The axial and tensor charges are obtained for baryon densities up to saturation density and temperatures $T = 0$ and $0.1$ GeV, in both symmetric nuclear matter and pure neutron matter. The distributions are then carried to $^{40}$Ca, $^{56}$Fe, $^{197}$Au, and $^{208}$Pb at zero temperature through the local density approximation. In symmetric matter at saturation density and zero temperature, the peaks of the three $u$ quark distributions move toward larger $x$ and fall least for the unpolarized distribution and most for the transversity distribution, so the spin-dependent $u$ quark distributions are modified more strongly. Between vacuum and saturation density, the axial charge of the proton drops from $1.28$ to $0.844$, and the tensor charge of the $u$ quark decreases while that of the $d$ quark grows in magnitude. At the center of each nucleus, the axial charge of the proton rises from $0.699$ in $^{40}$Ca to $0.817$ in $^{208}$Pb as the central baryon density decreases, which suggests that the modification at the center follows the central density rather than the mass number.

title: Parameter Constraints on $f(R^{1+\epsilon},T_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu})$ Gravity from Exotic Compact Objects
abstract: According to General Relativity (GR), gravity is described as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. Although GR has been highly successful in describing gravitational phenomena, exotic compact objects with high mass and strong gravitational fields, as well as low-mass objects, have motivated the study of modified theories of gravity. One of the modified gravity frameworks is $f(R,T^2) = R^{1 + \epsilon} + \alpha \kappa^2 T_{\mu \nu} T^{\mu \nu}$, which provides an extension of GR by introducing modifications to both the geometric and matter sectors. In this study, we investigate the mass-radius structure, physical viability, and stability of quark stars in $f(R,T^2)$ gravity using the MIT Bag Model equation of state. We compare results from the exact $f(R,T^2)$ model, its first-order Taylor expansion, and GR. The values of the gravity parameter $\epsilon$ and $\alpha$ are constrained by evaluating the ability of the model to reproduce the observed mass-radius configurations of compact objects, including HESS J1731-347 with a mass of $M = 0.77_{-0.17}^{+0.20} \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R = 10.4_{-0.78}^{+0.86}$ km, GW190814 with a mass of $M = 2.6 \, M_{\odot}$, PSR J1614-2230, with a mass of $M = 1.928 \pm 0.017 \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R > 10$ km, and PSR J0437-4715, with a mass of $M = 1.418 \pm 0.037 \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R = 11.36_{-0.63}^{+0.95}$ km. We assess the physical viability and stability of the stellar configurations using the energy conditions (strong, weak, null, and dominant) and the speed of sound. Overall, the $f(R,T^2)$ gravity model can accommodate quark star configurations and reproduce the observed properties of massive compact objects, particularly those associated with GW190814 and the lightest compact object observed, HESS J1731-347, respectively.

title: In Search of the Gravitational Wave of Fast X-Ray Transient in the Second Part of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Fourth Observing Run
abstract: Fast X-ray Transients (FXTs) are brief, intense X-ray flashes unassociated with persistent X-ray sources or known stellar objects, typically lasting from seconds to hours. With the launch of the Einstein Probe in January 2024, the study of FXTs has entered a new phase. Its large field of view significantly increases the discovery rate, enabling more robust statistics. The leading discoveries have revealed a fraction of gamma-ray bursts, while the rest remain unexplained. We propose a methodology to search for possible relations between gravitational waves (GWs) and FXTs, as it may serve as a discrepancy among proposed theoretical models. To achieve this, we intend to utilize X-Pipeline, an unmodeled search algorithm, to identify excess coherent signals in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) O4b observations. Out of 64 FXTs events, we obtained 19 FXTs for constructing robust searches. Given the absence of any detectable GW signals, we subsequently calculated upper limits and estimated exclusion distances for each source. In order to enrich the sample base and statistical analysis, this methodology could henceforth be conducted through future GW searches, including KAGRA in the O4c and O5 observations.

title: Formation and Detectability of PSR J0653+0443-like Extremely Eccentric Binary Neutron Stars in the Milky Way
abstract: Recently, the Five-hundred-meter-Aperture-Spherical-radio-Telescope (FAST) Galactic Plane Pulsar Snapshot (GPPS) survey discovers an extraordinary binary neutron star (BNS) system, PSR J0653+0443, possessing the highest known orbital eccentricity ($e\approx0.992$) among Galactic BNSs (Yang et al., 2026), which provides a unique probe into the formation and evolution of BNSs. In this Letter, we perform compact binary population synthesis calculations with self-consistent neutron star spin evolution to model extremely eccentric BNS population detectable by the FAST GPPS survey, explicitly incorporating observational selection effects. We find that BNSs with $e>0.99$ constitute only $\sim0.6\%$ of the detectable population, with an expected detection number of $\lambda_{\mathrm{GPPS}}\approx0.31$ over the full planned footprint. Thus, although rare, systems as eccentric as PSR J0653+0443 are compatible with standard binary evolution. We further demonstrate that extremely eccentric BNSs arise preferentially from core-collapse supernovae, whereas imposing $P\lesssim0.1$ s select older, more frequently recycled systems, which naturally reproduce the observed properties of PSR J0653+0443. We further predict that the completed GPPS sample has a $\sim15\%$ chance of finding another $e>0.99$ BNS, but a much higher $\sim88\%$ chance for $e>0.90$ systems. By contrast, future facilities are expected to enlarge the detectable highly eccentric BNS population, with SKA potentially detecting PSR J0653+0443-like systems and sub-mHz gravitational-wave detectors probing a larger population with $e>0.9$, enabling much more in-depth population-level constraints.

title: Exploring PSR J0901-4046 as an ultra-slowly rotating neutron star versus a white dwarf
abstract: The source PSR J0901-4046 shows a very long rotational period, of $\approx 75.88$ s. In fact, its long period suggests that it could be a white dwarf. We examine the properties of the source and compare the outcomes under the hypotheses of the source being a highly magnetized white dwarf (B-WD) and neutron star. We find that assuming it to be a B-WD with a surface field $\sim 10^{10}$ G explains many properties, including its storage/rotational energy, explaining luminosity. On the contrary, the neutron star-based idea, particularly if examined under the conventional spin down mechanism, requires an unusually high surface magnetic field $\gtrsim 10^{14}$ G, even exceeding $10^{16}$ G, depending on the obliquity angle and emission mechanism. The source also sits very close to AR Sco, a white dwarf pulsar, in the period and period-derivative plane. We suggest that the source is a B-WD. Along with AR Sco, it being a B-WD constrains the death line model. B-WD hypothesis alleviates the necessity of an unusually high magnetic field hindering pair production for PSR J0901-4046 under the neutron star hypothesis. We argue that some rotation-powered pulsars with extreme properties may possibly be white dwarfs rather than neutron stars.

title: Early panchromatic spectra reveal helium in the thermonuclear supernova 2024kce
abstract: Faint Type I supernovae blur the boundaries between spectroscopic classes, obscuring their progenitors and explosion mechanisms. One proposed origin is a double detonation, in which ignition of an accreted helium shell triggers the explosion of a carbon oxygen white dwarf. Surviving helium is a direct prediction of this mechanism, but its strongest near-infrared feature overlaps with carbon and is ambiguous in isolation. Here we present SN 2024kce, observed with simultaneous optical and near-infrared spectroscopy eleven days before maximum light. We identify He I absorption at three wavelengths, all consistent with a velocity of 16,400 km/s, well above the photosphere. This is the first detection of helium before maximum light in a thermonuclear supernova. Helium at these velocities requires nearby radioactive material for non-thermal excitation, pointing to ash from a detonated surface helium shell. A double detonation model reproduces the optical spectral evolution, suppressed blue flux, and He I 1.083 micron absorption feature. SN 2024kce shares properties with both subluminous Type Ia supernovae and Ia-like calcium-rich transients, providing evidence that the same explosion mechanism operates across these classes. From early optical and near-infrared spectra to Rubin's First Look images, SN 2024kce showcases the full reach of modern observatories in exposing the physics of rare explosions.

title: Confirming candidate self-lensing binary detections with radial velocity measurements
abstract: Compact objects in approximately edge-on binary orbits with stars are able to produce a self-lensing effect, amplifying light from their companion once per orbit. To date, five white dwarf self-lensing systems are known, while none are known containing black holes or neutron stars. Discovery of such systems is a potential method of finding quiescent black holes and neutron stars, most of which will be pristine and unchanged from their formation. Photometric detections can suffer from degeneracies in the lens mass and orbital parameters when the amplification and crossing time are not well constrained, while photometric searches produce too many false positives to allow radial velocity investigation of every candidate. Therefore we investigate the minimal radial velocity (RV) observational requirements to characterise such systems by simulating detectable self-lensing light curves, using those light curves to generate targeted RV observations, and fitting RV jointly with photometry. We evaluate the median relative error in the recovered lens mass and orbital period, alongside compact-object class recovery. We find that adding RV measurements substantially reduces parameter error, with compact-object class generally easier to determine than the exact lens mass. Parameter accuracy is driven mainly by number of RV observations, with RV precision playing a weaker role except for the shortest-period systems, with even a small number of RV measurements resulting in substantial improvement in accuracy. These results suggest that multi-stage RV follow-up, starting with a small number of observations of many candidates, can efficiently classify self-lensing candidates and identify high-priority systems for further investigation.

title: Chandra and Multiwavelength Study of Pevatron Candiate HESS J1702-420A
abstract: Aims: HESS J1702-420A is a promising Galactic PeVatron candidate whose physical nature remains unknown. Previous XMM-Newton observations revealed hard, apparently extended X-ray emission from XMMU J170147.3-421407, offset from the center of the TeV source, suggesting a possible pulsar wind nebula (PWN) association. We aim to resolve its X-ray morphology, investigate compact-object candidates in the field, and assess their possible association with HESS J1702-420A. Methods: We obtained three new ACIS-I observations from the Chandra X-ray observatory (CXO) with a total exposure of 50.4 ks. We performed imaging, source detection, spectral and variability analyses, and multiwavelength (MW) machine-learning (ML) source classification. Neutron star (NS) candidates were further investigated using deep near-infrared and radio imaging. Results: The Chandra observations resolve XMMU J170147.3-421407 into a faint point-like source, Src11 (CXO J170144.5-421415), and asymmetric diffuse emission comprising eastern and western lobes. The X-ray spectral, variability, and MW properties of Src11 and the diffuse emission are consistent with those commonly observed in pulsar/PWN systems, further supported by the ML classifications. However, the asymmetric diffuse morphology is unlike a typical bow-shock/tail or jet/torus PWN, and the $\sim7'$ offset from HESS J1702-420A makes a firm physical association difficult to establish. A possible shell-like radio structure north-west of Src11 may indicate a more complex PWN/SNR environment. Other NS candidates are less consistent with a pulsar/PWN interpretation, making Src11 the most compelling candidate in the field.

title: Breaking the symmetry: X-ray polarization from a spreading layer on a tilted weakly magnetized neutron star
abstract: When modeling the emission from an X-ray binary system, we often assume that the rotational axis of the compact object is aligned with that of the binary system. While often considered irrelevant for spectroscopic observations, the orientation of the binary system is crucial for polarimetric properties. With the recent advent of X-ray polarimetric observations enabled by the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), indications of a possible misalignment of the neutron star rotational axis with respect to the binary axis have been reported. Following these indications, we present an analytical model for the polarimetric properties of emission arising from a spreading layer on an inclined weakly magnetized neutron star (WMNS). We discuss the expected polarimetric properties and study the impact of geometrical parameters of the system on the polarization of WMNS emission. We compare our results with those for aligned systems. Finally, we discuss applications of the model to recent and upcoming X-ray polarimetric observations with IXPE and mention the suggestions for further development of the model.

title: Axial Perturbations of Extended Tolman III in the New $f(R,T)$ Theory
abstract: We investigate compact objects using the extended Tolman III equation of state in the framework of $f(R,T)=R+2\chi T$ gravity. In the matter sector of the Lagrangian density, we employ a new formalism based on the evaluation of the second-order derivative of the matter Lagrangian with respect to the metric \cite{Jayawiguna:2026das}. We analyze the corresponding observational signatures through axial gravitational perturbations including stellar stability and gravitational echo. We find that the effective potential in $f(R,T)$ gravity is wider and deeper than its counterpart in general relativity (GR). The quasinormal-mode (QNM) frequencies are calculated using the Bohr--Sommerfeld (BS) fitting and both the lower- and higher-order Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin (WKB) approximations. For the ultracompact configurations considered, trapped modes can tunnel through the potential barrier, giving rise to gravitational-wave echoes. The imaginary parts of the QNM frequencies are found to be negative, $\Im(\omega_n M)<0$, indicating that the perturbations decay exponentially with time. Our results show that the echo train in GR contains more echoes than that in $f(R,T)$ gravity. Finally, assuming that the stellar object is a neutron star and adopting a stellar radius consistent with measurements by the Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER), we find that the $f(R,T)$ gravity model yields a characteristic frequency consistent with the estimated frequency associated with GW170817 for $\beta= 4.663\times10^{-1}$ and $\chi=0.96\pi$, whereas the corresponding GR model does not exhibit comparable agreement.

title: $\gamma$hosts from the past: reheating neutron stars with supernova-sourced ALPs
abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) can be copiously produced in the hot and dense environment of a core-collapse supernova. If their mass is within an order of magnitude of the supernova temperature, a non-negligible fraction of them will remain gravitationally bound to the neutron star remnant. This basin of ALPs can then decay to photons over the lifetime of the neutron star, thereby reheating it. Using the measured luminosities of several neutron stars, we close multiple windows in ALP parameter space while also satisfying the SN 1987A cooling constraint on the ALP-nucleon coupling. In particular, using the 35000 K upper limit on the temperature of the coldest neutron star observed, PSR J2144$-$3933, we derive the strongest upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling for 1$-$400 MeV ALP masses. Ceilings on these limits arising from ALP decays occurring within the neutron star lifetime may be overcome by using younger neutron stars such as the one in Cas A, probing couplings orders of magnitude higher. Observations of a $2000 \, {\rm K}$-hot neutron star in infrared observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope could reach ALP-photon couplings three orders lower and ALP masses one order lower than our current limits.

title: Reduced vortex descriptors linking polycrystallinity in magnetic nanoparticles with polarized magnetic small-angle neutron scattering
Machine Learning Neutrino-Nucleus Cross Sections II: More Leptons
abstract: Neutrino-nucleus cross sections are essential inputs for long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments, yet remain challenging to model with high precision. Recent work demonstrated that fully black-box data-driven cross-section models cannot accurately generalize between near- and far-detector fluxes, but imposing Standard-Model symmetries via structure-function parameterizations provides a well-posed learning problem in a simplified DUNE-inspired muon-neutrino disappearance analysis. Here, we extend this framework to multiple lepton flavors and both neutrino and antineutrino beam modes, incorporating the electron appearance channel and enabling a simultaneous determination of $\sin^2\theta_{23}$, $\Delta m^2_{31}$, and the CP-violating phase $\delta_{\rm CP}$. We find that the learned cross section model recovers the injected oscillation parameters without significant bias, with constraints comparable to those obtained using the exact underlying cross section. Flux uncertainties have more significant effects in the multi-channel case, and incorporating flux nuisance parameters into the learning problem is required for accurate results. Our results demonstrate that this data-driven approach can be extended to the multi-channel measurements needed for long-baseline neutrino oscillation analyses.

title: CURTAIN: Towards a Foundation Model for Neutrino Telescopes
abstract: Neutrino telescopes record more than a trillion photon detections per year, yet there does not exist a self-supervised learning (SSL) task which fully satisfies all three conditions: improving as the pretraining set grows, transferring to a different detector, and outperforming the best model trained without pretraining at all. We introduce CURTAIN, a temporal masking scheme and the first SSL task for neutrino telescopes that achieves all of these goals. Downstream performance monotonically improves with the number of pretraining events, as predicted by scaling laws. Our encoder builds on DeepIce, currently the leading model on the NuBench benchmarks direction reconstruction task. Pretraining it with CURTAIN reduces its median angular error by 45% and its median energy error by 31% compared to training from scratch. It also transfers to a detector geometry never seen in pretraining, reducing the median angular error by 36% compared to training from scratch. At matched capacity and pretraining data, CURTAIN-pretrained encoders beat those pretrained by existing SSL tasks on both tasks and at every pretraining set size.

title: ULTRAMAN: A Proposed ultrasound detector for macroscopic dark matter
abstract: We propose ULTRAMAN (ULTRAsound Macro ANalyzer), a passive ultrasound array experiment designed to search for macroscopic dark matter (macros) through coherent acoustic disturbances generated as compact objects traverse a controlled target medium. Unlike existing dark matter detectors that primarily rely on scintillation, ionization, or other signatures of energy deposition, ULTRAMAN exploits the acoustic response of matter to reconstruct individual highly supersonic trajectories using synchronized multielement ultrasound arrays. The framework connects macro stopping power and interaction cross section to the resulting acoustic pressure, while the expected event rate probes the macro mass and abundance. A genuine candidate would appear not as an isolated radio frequency spike, but as a correlated multichannel track consistent with a single highly supersonic passage through the target. Representative macro, nuclearite, axion quark nugget, and primordial black hole benchmarks are shown to occupy distinct regions of the resulting acoustic observable space. Existing ultrasound technology offers a realistic route to an event-level terrestrial search for macroscopic dark matter, with null observations translating into complementary constraints on its parameter space.

title: Experimental evidence of forward energy transfer induced by core-edge coupling in multiscale tokamak turbulence
abstract: Turbulence in magnetically confined plasmas is inherently quasi-two-dimensional and can exhibit both inverse and forward energy transfer across scales. Experimental evidence for cross-scale energy transfer in the hot plasma core has, however, remained scarce. Understanding such energy transfer is crucial because it governs turbulent transport, which directly impacts confinement quality of fusion plasmas. Here we report experimental evidence consistent with forward energy transfer associated with core-edge coupling in tokamak turbulence. We combined multichannel collective Thomson scattering (CTS) and radially localized Doppler backscattering (DBS) to resolve cross-scale fluctuation dynamics. The results reveal that a quasi-coherent mode (QCM) originating from the edge is also present in the core and resonantly couples with broadband turbulence, producing significant forward energy transfer and characteristic secondary instabilities. These combined measurements indicate that quasi-two-dimensional tokamak turbulence can support a net energy transfer from ion to electron scales through cross-scale wave-wave interactions, contrary to the inverse cascade paradigm of idealized two-dimensional turbulence. Such a plasma regime is attractive for fusion reactors, as it avoids large edge-localized modes (ELMs) that damage first-wall components and maintains high confinement quality even in the presence of high-Z impurities.

title: Benchmarking Compositional Generalisation for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials play a fundamental role in computational chemistry and materials science, enabling applications from molecular dynamics simulations to drug design and materials discovery. While recent approaches can estimate inter-atomic forces with high precision, it remains unclear to what extent they can generalise to previously unseen molecules. Do they learn the compositional structure of chemistry, capturing how molecular fragments and their combinations determine properties, or do they primarily learn to interpolate patterns that are specific to the training examples? To address this question, we propose a benchmark consisting of four tasks that require some form of compositional generalisation. In each task, models are tested on molecules that were unseen during training, but the training data is chosen such that generalisation to the test examples should be feasible for models that learn the underlying physical principles. Our empirical analysis shows that the considered tasks are highly challenging for state-of-the-art models, with errors on out-of-distribution examples often an order of magnitude higher than on in-distribution examples, even when using foundation models that have been pre-trained on millions of molecules.

title: Top quark differential distributions in the SMEFT
abstract: We discuss top quark processes, in particular $tW$ production and top-antitop pair production, as probes of dimension-6 Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We calculate top-quark double differential distributions in transverse momentum and rapidity, and we perform SMEFT fits at LO, NLO and, by adding second-order soft-gluon corrections, at approximate NNLO.

title: Search for high-energy neutrinos from Einstein Probe detected Fast X-ray Transients using 14 years of IceCube muon track data
abstract: We perform a time-integrated search for high energy neutrinos from 27 fast X-ray transients (FXTs) detected by Einstein Probe, using 14 years of publicly available IceCube muon-track data. We employ the unbinned maximum likelihood method which is used for IceCube point source searches. We do not find any statistically significant excess from any of the FXTs. The largest TS value is obtained for EP240801a (TS=4.77), corresponding to a local $p$-value of 0.04, which is not significant. We therefore calculate 90\% confidence level upper limit on the differential muon neutrino flux. The most stringent upper limit is obtained for EP241021a, with $E^2 \Phi(E)=2.1\times 10^{-10}$ (GeV cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$), for a $E^{-2}$ spectrum at a pivot energy of 100 TeV.

title: Probing imperfect axions with nuclear clocks
abstract: We show that $^{229}$Th nuclear clocks can probe departures from the Peccei-Quinn (PQ) solution to the strong CP problem. Explicit PQ breaking or additional CP-violating interactions can shift the minimum of the axion potential and generate CP-violating couplings to matter, inducing a clock response linear in the axion field. We investigate explicit PQ breaking and quark chromo-electric dipole operators as representative realizations of these \textit{imperfect axion} scenarios, consistent with electric dipole moment constraints. For axion dark matter, the linear signal oscillates at the Compton frequency and can dominate the quadratic response. Even without axion dark matter, the Earth can source a static axion field, enabling fifth-force searches with nuclear clocks.

title: Probing Heavy Neutral Leptons through New Gauge Interactions at the Forward Physics Facilities
abstract:
We investigate the prospects for improving the heavy neutral lepton (HNL) searches at the far-forward LHC experiments FASER and FASER$
u$, as well as their proposed HL-LHC successors, FASER2 and FASER$
u$2, using new HNL production mechanisms. We consider scenarios in which HNLs couple directly to a new $U(1)$ gauge boson and decay into visible Standard Model final states through mixing with active neutrinos. Focusing on the $U(1)_{B-L}$, $U(1)_{B-3L_	au}$, and $U(1)_B$ gauge extensions as benchmark models, we study HNL production through proton bremsstrahlung and Drell--Yan processes, which probe complementary mediator-mass regimes. We analyze several visible decay channels, including charged leptons, neutral mesons, and other hadrons, and evaluate the projected sensitivities for different neutrino-flavor mixing patterns. We find that these new production mechanisms that differ qualitatively from the conventional picture in which both production and decay are controlled by active-sterile mixing enable the far-forward LHC program to probe previously unexplored regions of HNL parameter space, with the first-ever demonstration of FASER$
u$ having sensitivity to HNLs and FASER2 and FASER$
u$2 offering substantially enhanced sensitivity during the HL-LHC era, even reaching the canonical seesaw prediction for all three lepton flavors. Our results demonstrate that new gauge interactions can substantially enhance HNL production independently of the active-sterile mixing that governs their visible decays, opening complementary opportunities to explore HNLs at the forward physics facilities.

title: Neutrino Transition Polarizability
abstract: We study Neutrino Transition Polarizability, where a light pseudoscalar $\phi$ couples active neutrinos to heavy neutral leptons $N$ and interacts with two photons. We consider an effective description of the active - sterile interaction, and a realization within the inverse seesaw mechanism; the coupling to photons is generated by heavy charged states. For $m_N>m_\phi$, the decay $N\to\nu\phi$ can greatly shorten the heavy neutrino lifetime, while $\phi\to\gamma\gamma$ produces a displaced photon pair. This changes the relevant search strategies, favoring production and decay inside detectors. We discuss existing constraints and estimate the sensitivity of displaced photon searches at DUNE, Belle II, LHCb and FCC-ee, highlighting the complementarity of neutrino scattering and meson and electroweak boson decays.

title: Isochrone fitting of Galactic globular clusters - IX. Tip of the red-giant branch for 27 clusters and constraints on new particle physics
abstract: Red-giant evolution is sensitive to non-standard channels of energy loss in stellar cores and therefore provides a probe of new physics. Such losses increase the luminosity of the tip of the red-giant branch (TRGB), the brightest point reached by a red giant in the color-magnitude diagram. Previous analyses of TRGB luminosities in globular clusters placed stringent bounds on the axion-electron coupling g_{ae}, but were limited by observational and theoretical uncertainties. To obtain a homogeneous and systematically controlled constraint, we use new parameters and TRGB estimates for 27 globular clusters, derived from Stetson, Hubble Space Telescope, and Gaia photometry, together with cluster-specific MESA calculations. Our primary likelihood uses 24 clusters after excluding three hot-flasher systems and explicitly accounts for stellar variability in identifying the brightest RGB stars. Finite sampling of the upper RGB is described by the full conditional distribution, and shared observational and stellar-physics uncertainties are retained as correlated nuisance parameters. The observed TRGB is fainter than the standard-cooling prediction by 0.078 (+0.036,-0.037) mag; to avoid an artificially strong bound from this downward fluctuation, we use the power-constrained profile likelihood method and obtain g_{ae}<6.4e-14 (95% CL). Sensitivity estimates for the neutrino magnetic dipole moment and for millicharged particles are also presented.

title: Gravitational Waves From an Entangled SO(3) Cosmic String Network
abstract: Discrete non-Abelian symmetries such as $\mathrm{A_4}$ are widely used in models of lepton flavor to explain neutrino mass hierarchy and their large mixing. If such a symmetry arises from the spontaneous breaking of a continuous group, cosmic strings can form. We study the breaking $\mathrm{SO}(3)\to \mathrm{A_4}$, for which the strings are classified by the non-Abelian group $\pi_1(\mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{A_4})\cong \mathrm{T}'$, the binary tetrahedral group. Because the string fluxes do not commute, colliding strings may reconnect, pass through each other, or become joined by a bridge whose flux can belong to a different string network. We derive the probabilities of these outcomes directly from the group structure; in network models they are usually treated as free parameters. Including them in a multi-network velocity-dependent one-scale model, we find that the correlation length of the networks decreases and their energy density increases relative to Abelian $\mathrm{U}(1)$ strings of the same tension. The resulting stochastic gravitational-wave background is enhanced by up to nearly three orders of magnitude, showing that the algebraic structure of $\pi_1$ leaves a direct imprint on the gravitational-wave spectrum.

title: Evidence for Kaluza-Klein excitations of the graviton, gluon and quark at LHC
abstract: Following our paper showing evidence for a sequence of Kaluza-Klein gravitons, we interpret the massive 4 jet excesses observed by CMS in RUN2 and RUN3 data. They could come from the decay of two heavy KK gluons gkk(3.6TeV) and gkk(8.6TeV) into pairs of KK quarks qkk(1TeV) and qkk(2.1TeV). Present limits on gkk seem to exclude gkk(3.6TeV) but these limits assume a dominant decay into top pairs, which can be questioned as was the case in our study of KK graviton decays. The cross section predicted for gkk(8.6) requires a BR into a pair of qkk(2.1TeV) or order 10% which is not unlikely. Prospect for reaching a 6 s.d. level local evidence with RUN3 data are promising for 3 channels.

title: Dark Energy and Neutrino Flavor from the Weak Axion
abstract: Dynamical dark energy offers an alternative to a cosmological constant with distinct observational signatures. However, the small energy density scale, Hubble-sized mass, and Planckian excursions make simple models fine-tuned and unnatural. In this work, we show that a weak version of the axion, identified with the phase field of the anomalous $U(1)_{B+L}$ of the Standard Model, can generate the scale hierarchies expected for dark energy. The axion potential is controlled by sources of explicit baryon and lepton number violation and is radiatively stable. We show that the leading contribution comes from two inequivalent Weinberg operators, one $B+L$-conserving and one $B+L$-violating, which generate the axion potential. We propose a flavor selection rule in the lepton sector that simultaneously removes the quadratic divergence and dominant temperature-dependent contributions to the effective potential. The resulting potential first appears at quartic order in the axion-dependent neutrino masses and, depending on the flavor model and PMNS parameters, its amplitude is parametrically close to the dark-energy density. Since the scale of dark energy is sensitive to changes in the neutrino parameters, improved measurements of $m_{\beta\beta}$, the sum of neutrino masses, $\delta_{\rm CP}$ and $\theta_{23}$ can favor certain models. Cosmologically, the field behaves as thawing quintessence, stays frozen by Hubble friction until late times and never enters the adiabatic regime.

title: A Chiral Nelson-Barr Relaxion
abstract: We present the chiral Nelson-Barr relaxion model, an extension of the Nelson-Barr relaxion framework with a gauged chiral $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry. It includes vector-like quarks to cancel gauge anomalies and a scalar whose vacuum expectation value generates their masses. The chiral symmetry forbids the leading operators responsible for the Nelson-Barr and clockwork quality problems. Right-handed neutrinos generate light-neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism and permit thermal leptogenesis. For the particular coupling considered, relaxion phenomenology gives $f_{\mathrm{max}}^{\mathrm{pheno}}\sim 4\times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{GeV}$, about eight times the corresponding phenomenological ceiling in the original model. The model can accommodate thermal leptogenesis if its right-handed-neutrino masses and reheating history satisfy the required temperature bounds.

title: A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe
abstract: We study a flat three-torus universe whose contraction is turned around by the negative Casimir energy of Standard Model fields. The trace anomaly forbids conformal matter alone to turn an anisotropic universe around, so matter with $w<1/3$, most cheaply a positive potential, must supply the negative trace; with antiperiodic fermions the Standard Model supplies the negative energy, and the universe turns at an edge of 722 reduced Planck lengths. The turning point can hold only about five quanta of the lowest modes, whereas a reheating coupling in a time-symmetric past would produce radiation exceeding the Casimir energy by at least $10^{94}$, so we read the turn as a beginning rather than a bounce. Negative Casimir energy cannot hold the shape of the torus: its shape state can be real at most once, and for a real Gaussian state survival of the shape on both branches with $90\%$ probability requires that moment to lie within $0.35$ Hubble times of the turn. The natural state, real at the turn, freezes the torus into a nearly rectangular box whose sides typically differ by $16$--$18\%$. The microwave background can read this fossil only if the shortest cycle lies between $0.985$ and about $1.04$ last-scattering diameters. At the turn the Higgs quartic coupling is negative, yet zero-point fluctuations of the gauge zero modes keep the Higgs zero mode near the origin with probability above one half for a top-quark pole mass below $172.96$ GeV, given a curvature coupling $\xi_H\gtrsim0.08$; a pole mass above $173.7$ GeV, within reach of FCC-ee, would exclude this beginning.

title: Spectroscopy, Regge trajectories and decay properties of the \(bc\bar q\bar q\) and \(bq\bar c\bar q\) tetraquark systems
abstract: Bottom-charm tetraquarks probe the interplay of heavy-quark dynamics, light-quark correlations, color structure and nearby hadronic thresholds. We investigate the spectroscopy and strong-rearrangement properties of the $bc\bar q\bar q$ and $bq\bar c\bar q$ ($q=u,d$) systems in a Cornell-type diquark--antidiquark framework with nonrelativistic (NR) and semirelativistic (SR) kinetics. Scalar and axial-vector cluster configurations are treated explicitly, and model-parameter uncertainties are propagated into state-dependent mass errors. For the $\bar{3}_c\otimes 3_c$ axial-axial ground states, the $0^+$ masses are $7530.1\pm75.4$ MeV (NR) and $7720.7\pm78.8$ MeV (SR) for $bc\bar q\bar q$, and $7307.6\pm90.5$ MeV (NR) and $7523.5\pm93.6$ MeV (SR) for $bq\bar c\bar q$. The multiplets follow $0^+<1^+<2^+$, and radial spacings decrease with excitation. In the $bq\bar c\bar q$ sector several low-lying configurations approach the $B^*D^*$ threshold: the axial-axial $0^+$ state lies $25.7$ MeV below it in NR but $190.2$ MeV above it in SR, so its threshold assignment is model sensitive and not evidence of robust strong-interaction stability. Spin and color wavefunctions are recoupled independently, giving configuration-dependent $PP$, $PV$, $VP$ and $VV$ rearrangement strengths and distinct color-singlet projections for the $\bar{3}_c\otimes 3_c$ and $6_c\otimes\bar{6}_c$ sectors. The strong short-distance attraction of the sextet coefficient $k_s=-10/3$ makes the finite SR expansion unreliable in that branch, so quantitative masses are restricted to the antitriplet sector. The results provide experimentally useful signatures and a baseline for coupled-channel and color-mixing studies.

title: Probing the Moderate-to-Large-$x$ Gluon Helicity with $J/\psi$ Production at $\sqrt{s}=\mathrm{GeV}$
abstract: We investigate the longitudinal double-spin asymmetry, $A_{LL}$, for color-singlet $J/\psi$ production in longitudinally polarized $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}\simeq27~\mathrm{GeV}$, relevant to the Spin Physics Detector at NICA. At these energies, gluon fusion probes moderate-to-large gluon momentum fractions, particularly at forward rapidity. We consider the leading-order color-singlet subprocess $gg\to J/\psi+g$ within nonrelativistic QCD and calculate polarized and unpolarized cross sections using analytic partonic hard-scattering coefficients. The color-singlet long-distance matrix element cancels in $A_{LL}$ at this order. We study the transverse-momentum and rapidity dependence of the asymmetry using different polarized and unpolarized PDF combinations, including LO and NLO PDF inputs, while keeping the hard-scattering calculation at LO. Factorization- and renormalization-scale variations are examined, and PDF and scale uncertainties are combined. The asymmetry is positive and increases with transverse momentum in the kinematically stable region. Its magnitude and uncertainty become more sensitive to the polarized gluon distribution at moderate and large $x$, with substantial differences among PDF combinations at moderate and large transverse momentum. NLO PDF uncertainties are generally smaller than LO uncertainties in central regions, but this reduction is not uniform; PDF and scale uncertainties can both become sizable at high transverse momentum and forward rapidity. Differential measurements of $A_{LL}$ at SPD could therefore provide complementary constraints on gluon helicity in a relatively unexplored kinematic region. A complete NLO hard-scattering calculation is needed for precision predictions and a quantitative assessment of higher-order effects.

title: Particle-level parton densities and uncertainties for the resolved photon at NLO
abstract: We present a new set of parton distribution functions (PDFs), PL$\gamma$26, for the resolved photon at next-to-leading order (NLO), the first to be fitted to a wide range of jet measurements from several experiments. Jet production in photoproduction at HERA and in $\gamma \gamma$ collisions at LEP is sensitive to both the quark and the gluon content of the photon, but the measurements lie at low scales, where non-perturbative corrections are large. We therefore choose a novel approach and fit the PDFs to these measurements at particle level, using NLO predictions from the general-purpose event generator SHERPA, matched to the parton shower and including hadronisation and multi-parton interactions (MPI). As part of the procedure, we tune the MPI model separately for photon--proton and photon--photon collisions. Modelling these non-factorisable effects in the fit, rather than through external correction factors, lets us include many more measurements and data points. We estimate the experimental uncertainties with replicas and compare the fitted PDFs with previous sets.

title: Ongoing and Post-Mass-Transfer Binaries: A Living Catalog and Unified Review of Binary Mass Transfer Products
abstract: Mass transfer is arguably the most defining interaction in binary stellar systems, yet many aspects of its physics remain poorly understood, from stability to endpoints and observable products. Comparing theory and observations is challenging because post-mass-transfer systems are studied across largely independent communities with different methods, nomenclature, and evolutionary frameworks. % We present a unified review and catalog of ongoing and post-mass-transfer binaries spanning the full stellar mass range, but restricted to systems likely to have experienced only a single episode of mass transfer (i.e., only one component is evolved). We review 16 observational classes of binary interaction products and compile a curated sample of 5,452 systems into a publicly available, community-driven catalog at https://binary-observations.github.io/post_mt_catalog/. % Using this catalog, we investigate global trends in orbital periods, eccentricities, masses, and mass ratios across post-mass-transfer binaries. We find I) non-zero eccentricities are common at all periods and system classes, with both median values and scatter increasing with period, II) the $e(\log P)$ relation depends on donor progenitor mass, with neutron-star and black-hole binaries showing the highest median eccentricities, likely reflecting effects of natal kicks, III) period distributions are broad and overlapping across evolutionary channels, and IV) the Gaia BH and NS systems are extreme in mass ratio but otherwise consistent with the general post-mass-transfer population. Together, these results support a unified empirical view of post-mass-transfer binaries that highlights several tensions between theory and observations.

title: Meson-isospectral pair interactions and the residual three-quark force
abstract: Meson-isospectral pair rotations can closely reproduce low-lying baryon energies while producing a substantial connected action under their consistent three-body embedding. Starting from an independently calibrated S-wave meson model, we compare ground-mass fits, joint ground-level and gap fits, and direct minimization of the connected remainder. With eighteen shared coefficients, a four-packet joint fit reproduces the nine calibration ground masses and first gaps with RMS errors of $\JointGroundTrain$ and $\JointGapTrain$ MeV, respectively. The excluded ground masses and gaps have RMS errors of $10.7$ and $8.1$ MeV in the same enlarged radial space. Its connected action on the eighteen calibrated inputs is $\JointActionCal$ times the unrotated source action. Eigenvalue agreement and removal of the connected interaction thus impose different tests. Separately optimizing the action with five packets gives a normalized residual of $\ShortActionAll$ for an intermediate-distance fifth packet; a long-distance extension also leaves a substantial remainder. An eliminated-state construction realizes the central color--color structure of an intermediate-configuration mechanism together with correlated pair dressing. These results favor a connected operator basis with three fitted strengths as an economical description within the tested pair family, and quantify its relation to the representation freedom of equivalent few-body Hamiltonians.

title: Inclusive weak decays of the $J/\psi$: single-charm decay and weak annihilation
abstract: Conventional estimates of $J/\psi$ weak decays, based on independent single-charm decays, suggest a branching fraction of order $10^{-8}$. Searches with samples of approximately $10^{10}$ $J/\psi$ events have so far yielded upper limits on exclusive modes. We calculate the inclusive weak branching fraction using the optical theorem, including single-charm decay, charged- and neutral-current annihilation, and their interference. The heavy-quark expansion identifies the leading pair-annihilation structure and motivates vacuum saturation for the leading color-singlet component. With tree-level hard kernels and leading-logarithmic Wilson coefficients at $\mu_0=M_{J/\psi}$, we obtain $B_{\rm weak}=(7.96^{+3.43}_{-0.43}\pm1.24)\times10^{-8}$. The contribution mediated by the $W$ boson alone, i.e. single-charm decays and $W$-exchange annihilation without the $W$-$Z$ interference, has a branching fraction of $(2.37^{+1.64}_{-0.42}\pm0.13)\times10^{-8}$. For the flavor sectors $(\Delta C,|\Delta S|)=(0,1)$ and $|\Delta C|=1$, the branching fractions are $(4.97^{+16.44}_{-4.97}\pm0.99)\times10^{-10}$ and $(1.86^{+0.20}_{-0.06}\pm0.02)\times10^{-8}$, respectively, including charge-conjugate channels. The first uncertainty estimates missing perturbative corrections through scale variation over $1~\mathrm{GeV}\leq\mu\leq3M_{J/\psi}$. The second is a hadronic uncertainty, obtained by jointly varying each vacuum-saturation and kinetic/chromomagnetic input within relative ranges of $\Lambda_{\rm QCD}/m_c\simeq20\%$. Pair annihilation dominates, with a substantial neutral-current contribution and scale-sensitive $W$-$Z$ interference.

title: Charting the Galactic Underworld II: Strategies for Identifying BHs and NSs with LISA
abstract: Stellar-mass black holes (BHs) and neutron stars (NSs) observed by space-based gravitational-wave detectors offer constraints on binary stellar evolution that are complementary to those from ground- based detectors. The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to detect hundreds of double compact objects (DCOs) containing a BH or NS, but distinguishing these sources from the far more numerous double white dwarfs (WDWDs) may prove challenging. We use adaptive importance sampling with COSMIC to synthesise large populations of BHBH, BHNS, NSNS, BHWD, and NSWD binaries. We combine these binaries with a Milky Way star-formation history and integrate their Galactic orbits with cogsworth, repeating our simulations for a grid of variations in uncertain (binary) stellar physics. We find that LISA detections are largely insensitive to the changes in Galactic position resulting from natal kicks. We then assess how well chirp mass, eccentricity, distance from the Galactic plane, and orbital frequency distinguish BH- and NS-hosting DCOs from WDWDs, accounting for LISA measurement uncertainties. Using chirp mass alone distinguishes only 50-60% of BHBHs and BHNSs, and ~40% of NSNSs, but combining this with orbital frequency recovers 90-100% of BHBHs and BHNSs and around ~50% of NSNSs, with eccentricity further improving the recovery of NSNSs to around 60-70%. Distance from the Galactic plane adds little discriminating power, though it can recover a handful of NSWDs that are missed otherwise. These methods will help identify a significantly larger number of BHs and NSs in LISA data that would be missed by a chirp mass cut alone.

title: ${\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_s^2\alpha)$ threshold corrections to inclusive $Z$-boson production
abstract: To match the experimental precision targeted by future collider programs, theoretical predictions for Drell-Yan production must incorporate higher-order mixed Quantum Chromodynamics and electroweak corrections. In this work, we present for the first time the ${\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_s^2\alpha)$ corrections to the inclusive cross-section for $Z$-boson production in the threshold limit. By systematically evaluating the missing singlet contributions, we obtain the complete set of ${\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_s^2\alpha)$ quark form factors, which we use to construct the soft-virtual cross-section by exploiting renormalization group invariance, the K+G evolution equation, and universal soft-collinear factorization. Our results capture the dominant threshold logarithmic enhancements, improve the theoretical scale uncertainties, significantly reduce electroweak input scheme dependence, and establish a crucial step toward complete ${\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_s^2\alpha)$ corrections indispensable for future precision programs.

title: GeoDiv KAN Solver for Time Fractional Navier Stokes Equations on Complex Domains to Realistic CFD Reconstruction
abstract: Scientific machine learning provides a promising framework for solving complex problems in science and engineering. Notably, physics informed neural networks (PINNs) have shown considerable potential for solving differential equations and modelling engineering systems. Solving time fractional Navier Stokes equations (TFNSEs) on complex domains is challenging due to temporal nonlocality, nonlinear flow dynamics, geometric complexity, and incompressibility constraints. To address these challenges, we propose a geometry gated, divergence-free Gaussian radial basis function Kolmogorov Arnold network (GeoDiv KAN). The proposed architecture uses geometry dependent feature gating and a streamfunction formulation to preserve incompressibility by construction. GeoDiv KAN is evaluated for the time fractional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on square, circular, and star-shaped domains. Numerical experiments show that GeoDiv KAN achieves higher predictive accuracy than PINN, PIKAN, RBF KAN, and DF RBFKAN across the considered benchmark problems. To establish practical relevance, GeoDiv KAN is applied to two data driven CFD cases: unsteady flow past a circular cylinder using the \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5039610}{Zenodo dataset} and turbulent RANS flow through a complex U bend using the \href{https://huggingface.co/datasets/JDecke/ubend-cfd}{U-bend dataset}.

title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
abstract: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.

title: Dihadron Transverse-Spin Asymmetries in Muon-Deuteron Deep-Inelastic Scattering
abstract: In 2022, the COMPASS collaboration performed semi-inclusive measurements of deep-inelastic muon-scattering on a transversely polarized deuteron ( LiD 6 ) target. From these data, transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries are extracted using pairs of oppositely charged hadrons. These asymmetries are directly sensitive to the quark transversity distributions and provide an independent handle on these fundamental quantities with respect to the Collins asymmetries measured in single-hadron production. The present results significantly improve upon the previous COMPASS deuteron measurements, which were the only available deuteron data worldwide, and reach a statistical precision comparable to that of the existing proton results from COMPASS. A small but nonzero asymmetry is observed at large Bjorken- x , consistent with theoretical expectations. A point-by-point extraction of the valence-quark transversity distributions yields, in particular, a substantially improved determination of the d -quark transversity. These measurements represent a major step towards a complete flavor mapping of the transverse-spin structure of the nucleon.

title: Real-time CXRS analysis on HL-3 tokamak with reliable neural networks and cross-device transfer learning
abstract: Abstract We present a neural network-based method for real-time charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) analysis on the HL-3 tokamak. To enhance model performance and reliability, we tailor the network architecture to the physical characteristics of CXRS spectra: the receptive field matches the Doppler-broadened line width, channel embedding encodes spatial awareness across diagnostic channels, and attention pooling focuses on the most informative spectral regions. These designs yield millisecond-level inference (0.56 ms per 32-channel) with accuracy comparable to conventional methods ( R 2 _ T i = 0.93, R 2 _ v t = 0.98). Furthermore, the model’s reliability is established through interpretability and uncertainty analysis. Interpretability analysis confirms that the model focuses on the Doppler-broadened wings of C VI for T i and tracks line shifts for v t , consistent with physical principles. Uncertainty estimates show that the model appropriately expresses higher uncertainty in regions where predictions are inherently more challenging. To address data scarcity on new devices, transfer learning from HL-2A tokamak markedly boosts performance in low-data regimes while retaining a modest advantage even with full HL-3 data, provided that the spectra are properly aligned and baseline subtracted. This work establishes a real-time, reliable, and data-efficient AI framework for CXRS analysis, offering a practical path to deploy machine learning approaches in plasma control on future fusion devices.

title: Revisiting p 11 B fusion: Updated cross-sections, reactivity, and energy balance
abstract: Abstract Recent experimental progress has substantially improved the available cross-section data for the p-$^{11}$B fusion reaction, particularly in energy regions that previously lacked direct measurements. In this study, we develop a high-precision analytical parameterization of the p-$^{11}$B reaction cross-section over the 0--10 MeV energy range, incorporating the new experimental data into a continuous and numerically efficient representation. Using this parameterization, we evaluate the thermonuclear reactivity of the p-$^{11}$B reaction and examine the effects of the dominant resonance at 0.6 MeV and a newly observed resonance around 4.7 MeV. Furthermore, we assess the energy balance by analyzing the fusion power density and the electron bremsstrahlung power density. Our results indicate that p-$^{11}$B fusion is not precluded by bremsstrahlung constraints when contemporary cross-section data and self-consistent thermal modeling are employed.

title: Nanosecond-LIBS-induced deuterium outgassing, diffusion, and surface modification in tungsten coatings
abstract: Abstract Tritium retention in plasma-facing components(PFCs) must be strictly controlled to ensure the safe operation of fusion devices. In ITER, compliance with the tritium inventory limit and assessment of fuel-removal strategies require in situ monitoring of fuel retention in PFCs. Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy(LIBS) is a diagnostic technique that can be implemented via remote handling to investigate fuel retention during maintenance shutdowns at ITER.In LIBS diagnostics, the selection of laser parameters plays a critical role in determining the ablation characteristics and thermal perturbation of the target. Used nanosecond(ns) laser pulses deliver energy on timescales that allow substantial thermal diffusion into the target, which could result in surface heating and melting. Under multi-pulse LIBS operation, these cumulative thermal effects can alter deuterium quantification, as deuterium may diffuse or outgas due to heating induced by earlier pulses. Such laser-induced perturbations can compromise accuracy of quantitative deuterium measurements if they are not properly accounted for in modelling.In this study, subsequent in situ ns-LIBS and in situ Nuclear Reaction Analysis(NRA) measurements were performed in Magnum-PSI on compact and porous tungsten coatings using a defocused, millimetre-scale laser spot(2.5×2.5mm). Deuterium retention and depth profiles were determined in and outside the LIBS crater. Under the investigated laser conditions, NRA measurements indicated a 66–79% reduction in retained deuterium within the sampled region of the LIBS crater, whereas pure material removal by ablation would account for only 21–42%, demonstrating additional laser-induced outgassing. Compact coatings further exhibited melting and intermixing with the underlying substrate. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for defocused ns-LIBS-induced perturbations in retention measurements. Further experimental and modelling studies are needed to assess the dependence of these effects on laser spot geometry and to determine whether picosecond(ps) LIBS, together with consideration of cumulative multi-pulse effects, could improve the reliability of fuel-retention diagnostics in future fusion devices.

title: First observation of anisotropic distribution evolution of hydrogen fast ions heated by ICRF in EAST
abstract: Abstract The continuous energy and pitch-angle distribution of hydrogen fast ions generated by ion cyclotron range of frequencies (ICRF) minority heating is measured in EAST using an imaging neutral particle analyzer (INPA). The measured two-dimensional fast-ion distribution exhibits a triangular structure: as energy increases, the pitch-angle distribution becomes progressively narrower, with its peak located around 0.4 < | v ∥ / v | < 0.5 . This behavior is consistent with resonance localization theory, which associates the pitch-angle peak with trapped orbits whose turning points are close to the ion cyclotron resonance layer. Through diagnostic response correction, the reconstructed spectrum shows a progressive enhancement of the high-energy minority-ion tail with rising ICRF power. A clear anisotropic evolution of the fast-ion distribution is also observed between discharges with different electron-temperature profiles. In the discharge with higher core electron temperature, the signal enhancement appears mainly for fast ions at energies above 100 keV and | v ∥ / v | ⩾ 0.5 , together with a broader measured pitch-angle distribution. This behavior is interpreted as the combined result of collisional pitch-angle scattering, fast-ion accumulation, and finite-orbit-width effects. The enhanced signal region corresponds to wide-orbit fast ions whose inner orbit legs extend to the hotter inner plasma region, making them more sensitive to changes in the electron-temperature profile. These results demonstrate the capability of INPA to resolve the anisotropic evolution of ICRF-heated fast ions and provide experimental insight into the optimization of ICRF heating schemes in EAST and future fusion devices.

title: Proton and neutron elastic scattering on He targets from ab initio symmetry-adapted no-core shell model optical potentials
Prospects For A New Light Nuclei, Fission Fusion Energy Cycle
abstract: Future advanced nuclear rocket propulsion, and the availability of new nuclear power cycle designs, will benefit substantially from the large current investment in alternative nuclear energy that is underway today. We propose a new nuclear cycle which includes the primary fission of lithium-6, followed by secondary fusion of deuterium and tritium, and a secondary fission of lithium-7 by tritium. This cycle does not produce nuclear waste from its nuclear fuel, since all byproducts of these cascade reactions are stable, provided that the triton production during the primary reaction is fully consumed in the secondary reactions. This cycle may, however, activate surrounding technical materials from its neutron flux. This light-element nuclear fuel is readily obtained through the ongoing expansion of the lithium mining industry and electric vehicle (EV) battery recycling industries.

title: Helium Detection in Technical Materials
abstract: Materials used to study nuclear fusion can retain atmospheric helium unless pretreated before an experiment. Understanding helium outgassing is important for accurate diagnostics in experiments surrounding nuclear fusion. The presence of helium is often cited as the primary evidence that a nuclear reaction has occurred, so it is imperative that known sources of helium are mitigated prior to proceeding with novel nuclear experiments. It is also necessary to ensure hermiticity when transferring gas aliquots from an experiment to a mass spectrometer. In this article, we present studies of detecting helium leak rates in systems used in novel nuclear experiments. We also present studies of helium retention in materials subjected to various heating profiles and atmospheric concentrations. Without pretreatment, stainless-steel 316 retains between 15 $\unicode{x2013}$ 240 pmol of $^{ 4}$He or an areal outgassing amount of 0.07 $\unicode{x2013}$ 1.20 pmol/$cm^{ 2}$. It also may reabsorb $^{ 4}$He from the atmosphere in time. These studies also demonstrate that it is necessary to pretreat most materials prior to performing experiments where the presence of $^{ 4}$He is being used as an indicator for novel nuclear reactions.

title: B$_{4/2}$ anomaly related to the shape coexistence in $^{94}$Zr
abstract: Solutions of the Bohr-Mottelson Hamiltonian with a sixth-order anharmonic oscillator potential, for both axially-symmetric and $\gamma$-unstable deformations, are applied to investigate the lowest states of the $^{94}$Zr nucleus. The experimentally observed $B_{4/2}$ anomaly is explained, within the present approach, by the presence of a coexistence between an approximately spherical shape ($2_{1}^{+}$) and an axially-symmetric deformed one ($4_{1}^{+}$). On the other hand, the energies of the $0_{2}^{+}$ and $2_{2}^{+}$ states and their associated electromagnetic transitions fit better a dynamical triaxial deformation configuration ($\gamma$-unstable). This overall picture of the lowest states in $^{94}$Zr corresponds to a triple shape coexistence scenario.

title: Radiative decay and electromagnetic moments in 229 Th determined within nuclear density functional theory
Astrophysical constraints on hadron-quark crossover in hybrid neutron stars
abstract: We investigate astrophysical constraints on hybrid neutron-star equations of state constructed by combining an extended linear sigma model description of quark matter with several representative hadronic equations of state through a smooth hadron--quark crossover. Four different hadronic models are examined in order to explore the model dependence of the resulting hybrid equations of state. After imposing stability, causality, perturbative QCD matching, tidal deformability, and maximum-mass constraints, only the eLSM+GMSR(BSK16) construction remains fully consistent with current astrophysical observations. The surviving parameterizations are further constrained using Bayesian inference based on NICER mass--radius measurements and the GW170817 gravitational-wave event. The posterior distributions favor a broad hadron--quark crossover occurring at relatively high baryon densities, while the formation of extended pure quark cores is strongly disfavored. Instead, the current observations favor neutron stars containing an extended mixed hadron--quark transition region. We also investigate the implications of the inferred maximum-mass distribution for the secondary object of GW190814 and find that, within the present model and adopted observational constraints, its interpretation as a neutron star is unlikely.

title: The FAST tool for synthetic SXR calculations and determination of impurity density and effective charge ( Z eff )
abstract: Abstract A new soft x-ray (SXR) synthetic tool has been developed: it is called FAST for FLYCHK-based Atomic physics and SXR Tomography. It is based on FLYCHK SXR emissivity spectra calculated for a variety of elements, from deuterium to tungsten. FAST creates 2D plasma emissivity for arbitrary plasma compositions and plasma profiles. It computes line-integrated SXR profiles based on a specific detector geometry and response. This tool is used to reproduce signals from an absolutely calibrated multi-energy SXR (ME-SXR) camera at WEST. Thanks to its energy-resolved measurement capability, the ME-SXR camera is able to separate spectral regions dominated by impurity line emission from others containing only continuum emission. At WEST, FAST and the ME-SXR camera are employed to determine impurity density profiles for tungsten and nitrogen (used as a proxy for low- Z impurities), as well as the plasma effective charge ( Z eff ), through SXR measurement reproduction at different energies, from 2 to 14 keV. Tungsten density is determined in two plasma scenarios at WEST: lower hybrid heating in the X -point radiator regime and lower hybrid heating with modulations of ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH). In the first scenario the tungsten profile is found to be moderately peaked in the core with a concentration of 0.8–1 × 10 −4 . This concentration is found to increase up to 1.4 × 10 −4 during ICRH. Tungsten peaking factor in steady-state conditions is also retrieved and compared to theoretical predictions. It is found to be slightly lower than the combined neoclassical and turbulent transport prediction.

title: Global polarization of $\Lambda$, $\Xi^{-}$, and $\Omega^{-}$ hyperons in Au+Au collisions at RHIC BES-II energies
abstract: We investigate the global spin polarization of $\Lambda$ hyperons and the multi-strange hyperons $\Xi^{-}$ and $\Omega^{-}$ in Au+Au collisions across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan II (BES-II) energy range, $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=7.7$--$27$ GeV. The polarization is computed using the modified Cooper--Frye formula, which includes contributions from thermal vorticity, the thermal shear tensor, and the gradient of the baryon chemical potential, combined with the (3+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamic framework CLVisc with SMASH initial conditions. We present the global polarization as a function of collision energy, centrality, transverse momentum, and rapidity. We find that the global polarization of $\Omega^{-}$ is systematically larger than those of $\Lambda$ and $\Xi^{-}$ because of its larger spin quantum number, but it remains below the central value of the recent STAR measurement. This discrepancy may suggest that additional mechanisms, such as spin correlations among strange quarks inside the $\Omega^{-}$, could contribute to the observed $\Omega^{-}$ polarization. We also find that the global-polarization splitting between hyperons and anti-hyperons increases toward lower collision energies and is dominated by the chemical-potential-gradient contribution.

title: Low Primordial Helium as a Probe of Non-Unitary Neutrino Mixing
abstract: The EMPRESS collaboration has reported a primordial helium mass fraction \(Y_P = 0.2402 \pm 0.0040\), which lies more than \(1\sigma\) below the standard Big Bang Nucleosynthesis prediction. Combined with the deuterium abundance and the Planck baryon density, this corresponds to a mild \(\sim 2\sigma\) tension with the standard value of the effective number of relativistic species, or to a \(\sim 2\sigma\) indication of a non-zero electron-neutrino degeneracy. We show that it can be explained by non-unitary three-neutrino mixing, a generic feature of seesaw extensions of the Standard Model. Non-unitarity makes the Fermi constant in beta decay exceed that in muon decay, enhancing the neutron-to-proton conversion rate and lowering \(Y_P\). A full numerical BBN calculation, combined with the EMPRESS \(Y_P\) determination and the deuterium abundance gives the best fit point at \(\alpha_{22}=0.982\), while the standard values \(N_{\mathrm{eff}}=3.044\), \(\xi_e=0\) remain allowed; the required level of non-unitarity is consistent with current experimental constraints.

title: Experimental determination of the double $K$-shell vacancy creation probability in the electron-capture decay of $^{55}$Fe with a microcalorimeter
abstract: The probability of double \(K\)-shell vacancy production following electron-capture decay is determined for $^{55}$Fe using a high-resolution microcalorimeter. The \(K\)-hypersatellite lines arising from double \(K\)-shell-vacancy filling are directly resolved within the measured spectra of X-ray emissions which are dominated by Mn \(K\)-X-ray diagram lines. The energies of the Mn \textit{K}-hypersatellite lines, \(K\alpha_2^h\), \(K\alpha_1^h\), and \(K\beta_{1,3}^h\), are measured as $(6143.5\pm0.5)$ eV, $(6162.1\pm1.5)$ eV and $(6811.9\pm2.6)$ eV, respectively. The relative intensities of \textit{K}-hypersatellite to diagram X-rays are measured to be $(1.30 \pm 0.07) \times 10^{-4}$. From the relative intensities together with established fluorescence yield values, the probability of double-vacancy creation per \(K\)-shell capture ($P_{{KK}}$) is determined as $(1.22 \pm 0.09) \times 10^{-4}$. Comparisons with previous experimental results and theoretical calculations are discussed.

title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
abstract: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.

title: Reformulation of the pionless effective field theory for practical few- and many-body applications
abstract: The effective field theory (EFT) of contact forces which describes few-nucleon systems at distance scales larger than the pion Compton wavelength ${\rm EFT}({\pi\hskip-0.54em /})$ can be defined in terms of momentum-dependent potentials that contain a fixed number of simple poles and generate the effective-range expansion to a given fixed order. These potentials provide a practical generalization of the standard ${\rm EFT}({\pi\hskip-0.54em /})$ power-counting scheme which, for instance, naturally accounts for the large effective ranges in the s-wave channels. Nucleon-nucleon phase shifts computed in this formulation of ${\rm EFT}({\pi\hskip-0.54em /})$ are compared to modern phase-shift analyses, and effective-range parameters are tabulated. The ${\rm EFT}({\pi\hskip-0.54em /})$ potentials, which provide a rational approximation of the S-matrix, are easily extended into the regime of pion physics through the inclusion of additional S-matrix poles and zeros, and provide an accurate description of data up to pion-production threshold. The potentials in this scheme are in an important sense weak over all relevant distance scales, and are therefore of utility for systematic calculations of many-nucleon observables.

title: Nuclear lattice effective field theory as a testing ground for $\alpha$-cluster structures in ${}^{24}\mathrm{Mg}$
abstract: The framework of nuclear lattice effective field theory (NLEFT) is applied to $^{24}\mathrm{Mg}$, with the perspective of obtaining a model-independent density map of the geometry of a sample of excited states of the nucleus. The Hamiltonian incorporates Wigner SU(4)-symmetric nuclear forces as well as the Coulomb interaction. The coupling constants of the spin-isospin symmetric nucleon-nucleon potentials have been adjusted in order to reproduce the experimental ground-state (g.s.) energy of $^{24}\mathrm{Mg}$ as well as the experimental Tjon ratio between the binding energies of $^3\mathrm{H}$ and $^4\mathrm{He}$. The ensuing parameter set turns out to be capable of capturing the experimental trend of the binding energy per nucleon, reproducing simultaneously within 1% deviation the measured values for $^{18}\mathrm{F}$, $^{22}\mathrm{Na}$, $^{26}\mathrm{Al}$, $^{28}\mathrm{Si}$, $^{30}\mathrm{P}$ and $^{32}\mathrm{S}$. Considerations based on the convergence rate of Euclidean-time extrapolations for the two lowest energy eigenvalues highlight the dual nature of the $0_1^+$ and $2_1^+$ states, of hybrid mean-field and $\alpha$-cluster type.
