title: Searching for Axion Dark Matter via Superconductor-Spin Hybrid Magnetometers
abstract: Axions are a compelling dark matter candidate suggested by theories beyond the Standard Model. The predicted axion-electron coupling and the resulting pseudomagnetic field allow for laboratory axion searches. Here we report an experimental axion search via a superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometer. A state-of-the-art broadband magnetometer with a sensitivity of sub-100 aT/Hz$^{1/2}$ at tens of kHz has been realized by coupling a ferrite spin sensor to a readout system based on a superconducting quantum interference device. The most stringent terrestrial constraints on the axion-electron coupling have been established in the frequency range 5$\sim$60 kHz. In the future, an improvement on the constraints of more than 4 orders of magnitude is foreseeable through arrays of superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometers with optimized designs. This work demonstrates the potential of superconductor-spin hybrid magnetometers in high-precision magnetic field sensing and the study of fundamental physics.

title: Hybrid Stars with Different Amount of Quark Matter
abstract: In a previous work, we explored the possibility of neutron stars with large quark cores. Through Bayesian inference, we obtained large sets of equations of state imposing constraints regarding the properties of nuclear matter, mass-radius data from NICER, the GW170817 data from Virgo-LIGO collaboration, perturbative QCD and causality. We also imposed that the maximum mass neutron star (NS$\text{max}$) must have a large quark core. In this work, we obtain a new set of equations of state (SmallQ set) with the same constraints as before. However, we relaxed the last constraint, imposing only that NS$\text{max}$ must have quark core, regardless of its size. We compare the results with the set from our previous paper constrained by NICER and GW170817 observations NJL-GW. For both sets, we use the Relativistic Mean Field model with nonlinear meson interactions for the hadron phase and the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model with four- and eight-quark interaction terms for the quark phase. The SmallQ set has higher values of phase transition density, with 3 -- 4.5 $\rho_0$, compared to the NJL-GW, with 2 -- 2.5 $\rho_0$. The new set describes NSs with smaller radius and smaller tidal deformability, and is more compatible with NICER and GW170817 data. A difference in the quark matter composition is observed, with a larger quark strange fraction occurring in the SmallQ set. Within this set, $2 M_\odot$ NSs may contain little to no quark matter. It is shown that there is a non negligible fraction of EOS whose mass-radius curve presents a positive slope for 1.8 $M_\odot$ stars, while for nucleonic stars this fraction is negligible and for hyperonic stars the slope is always negative.

title: Wave-energy partition governs weak collisional damping in cold plasmas
abstract: Abstract Weak dissipation can control wave propagation, mode competition, andinstability thresholds in plasmas, yet the physical origin of largebranch-to-branch differences in collisional damping is often obscuredby dielectric-tensor calculations. We show that weak collisionaldamping in cold plasmas is governed by wave-energy partition. In theone-rate cold plasma model with independent-relaxation collisions, the damping rate of a positive-energycollisionless eigenmode equals, to leading order in weak collisions, the collision frequency multiplied by thefraction of the total wave energy stored in plasma motion. This resultrecasts the standard perturbative damping formula into a compact andphysically transparent law, immediately explaining why field-dominatedbranches such as whistlers can be much less damped than the collisionfrequency, whereas quasi-electrostatic modes can exhibit damping ofcomparable magnitude. Analytic examples for Langmuir, transverseelectromagnetic, whistler, and extraordinary waves show that theenergy-partition form classifies weak collisional damping acrossdistinct branches and provides a simple diagnostic for modecompetition in multibranch plasma-wave systems.

title: The $b\bar{b}c\bar{c}$ Fully Heavy Tetraquark at the LHC and the FCC: Multimodal Fragmentation and Observability
abstract: We investigate the production of the all-heavy mixed-flavor $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark through a multimodal fragmentation setup combining direct-multiquark and scalar-diquark mechanisms. Standard Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) evolution is applied while preserving threshold consistency through the Heavy-Flavor NonRelativistic evolution (HF-NRevo) scheme. The resulting fragmentation functions (FFs) are then embedded into hybrid high-energy and collinear factorization at next-to-leading order for semi-inclusive tetraquark-plus-jet production. We compare the two mechanisms through rapidity-separation distributions at the 14 TeV High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) and at the 100 TeV Future Circular Collider (FCC), finding a clear phenomenological preference for the direct-multiquark channel over the scalar-diquark mode. Integrated cross sections and expected event yields provide favorable production-level prospects for future searches at the HL-LHC, with substantially enhanced statistics at FCC energies. These results establish a quantitative connection between microscopic formation mechanisms and the prospective observability of the $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark at present and future hadron colliders.

title: Realizing uniform implosion of double-cone ignition by combining a predictive model and Bayesian optimization
abstract: Abstract The direct-drive inertial confinement fusion (ICF) schemes like the double-cone ignition (DCI) scheme can efficiently utilize the laser energy, while it faces significant challenges in uniform implosion and achieving high areal density of the fuel. This is because of the P2 asymmetry driven by the laser and the high-mode Rayleigh-Taylor instability (RTI) growth. We propose an efficient optimization approach by integrating multiple algorithms and physical models to address these limitations. Based on two-dimensional (2D)radiation hydrodynamics simulations, a scaling law for the areal density is derived, incorporating laser parameters, target structure, and instability factors, all of which have significant effects on the areal density. The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed to optimize the irradiation positions and spot radius of the two-ring laser, improving the uniformity of laser intensity distribution on the target surface and thus reducing the P2 asymmetry. Combining one-dimensional (1D) simulations with the RTI growththeory, a quantitative predictive model for P2 asymmetry and a qualitative predictive model for high-mode RTI are established, significantly reducing computational costs. Finally, the outputs of the predictive models are used as input parameters to perform Bayesian optimization for iteratively optimizing laser profile and target structure. The areal density of the DCI in 2D simulations increases from 0.156 g/cm² to 0.274 g/cm² with 2 ×16 kJ drive lasers. This method provides a new paradigm for the experimental design of DCI and polar direct-drive (PDD) scheme.

title: On the superbursts as photodisintegrators of ashes from the rp-process -- Numerical simulations of superbursts with MESA II
abstract: Context: Superbursts are energetic explosions in the crusts of neutron stars in Low-Mass X-ray Binaries (LMXBs). At temperatures above 4 GK, photodisintegration of heavy rp-process ashes may play a major role alongside $^{12}$C fusion. Aims: We investigate how photodisintegration of rp-process ashes affects superburst properties and the initial $^{12}$C abundance required for ignition. Methods: We simulate superbursts with MESA v.24.08.1. Besides the canonical fuel of $20\%$ $^{12}$C and $80\%$ $^{56}$Fe, we test different $^{12}$C abundances mixed with scaled rp-process ashes. Results: Superbursts can ignite with only $10\%$ $^{12}$C when the remaining $90\%$ consists of rp-process ashes. Their luminosity is comparable to that of the canonical fuel, whereas $10\%$ $^{12}$C mixed with $90\%$ $^{56}$Fe yields lower luminosity. $^{56}$Fe remains the most abundant ash nuclide. Although photodisintegration drives nucleosynthesis, neutron, proton and alpha captures release energy at late times. We also find that $A=64$ nuclides or $^{20}$Ne help reduce the $^{12}$C abundance needed for ignition. Conclusions: The composition of accreted material - not just its $^{12}$C content - substantially affects superburst ignition, luminosity and nucleosynthesis.

title: Impact of energetic alpha particles on core turbulence in an ARC-class fusion power plant
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the impact of fusion-born alpha particles on core turbulence and transport in the ARC tokamak fusion power plant [1] using linear and nonlinear gyrokinetic CGYRO [2] simulations. A significant reduction in ion-scale turbulent heat and particle fluxes is observed in the inner core (r/a ≤ 0.5), which is associated with multiscale interactions between fast ion-destabilized modes, zonal flows, and the background turbulence. A nonlinear upshift in the ITG critical gradient is observed in the simulations with fast alphas compared to those with artificially thermalized alphas. The turbulence reduction is found to scale benefi- cially with alpha particle density and plasma βe, and the radial extent of the turbulence suppression is limited to the volume containing a sig- nificant density of fast particles. The suitability of local gyrokinetics and potential impacts of fast ion effects on fusion performance are discussed.

title: Hadronization in QCD and Fragmentation Functions
abstract: The hadronization of quarks and gluons is reviewed within the framework of collinear parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions closely associated with the notion of factorization in hard scattering processes in QCD. The state-of-the-art in calculating both the scale evolution of fragmentation functions and the partonic cross sections pertinent to their determination from data up to next-to-next-to-leading order accuracy is presented. Potential improvements up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic order are outlined as well. All relevant experimental data sets for single-inclusive pion, kaon, and unidentified charged hadron production are listed. The most recent sets of fragmentation functions and their uncertainties extracted from these data in global QCD analyses utilizing various different strategies are presented and compared to each other.

title: Automated shape optimization of stellarator divertor targets via Chebyshev parameterization and differential evolution
abstract: Abstract Managing extreme heat fluxes in the form of strike lines on divertor target plates is a central challenge that hinders the progression of reactor-relevant stellarators. We present an automated, fast, non-gradient-based optimization framework for shaping open stellarator divertor targets, applied to the Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) island divertor as a test case. The target surface geometry is parameterized using a Chebyshev spectral basis whose low-order modes naturally encode the physics motivated deformations, namely: translation, tilting and higher-order bending, which directly govern the incidence angle and flux tube connection-length distributions at the targetsurface. The heat flux distribution on a target surface is evaluated by EMC3 Lite, a fast three-dimensional Monte Carlo edge-plasma transport code that self-consistently solves an energy transport equation with a sheath boundary condition, thereby avoiding the fixed-velocity limitations of simpler field-line-diffusion proxies. A parallelized Differential Evolution algorithm explores the Chebyshev coefficient space, minimizing a composite objective that simultaneously reduces peak heat flux, promotes uniform heat spreading, and encourages power interception leaving the scrape-off layer. The optimizer redistributes the load toroidally rather than by broadening it across the field: the baseline plate collects 33% of its power in the final 0.84° of its toroidal span and almost nothing over φ ∈ [10, 20]°, whereas the optimized surface spreads the load over φ ∈ [0, 20]°, widening the toroidal deposition profile by a factor of 4.7.This results in a significant reduction of concentrated strike-line loading without sacrificing intercepted power. A secondary contribution is poloidal. At fixed toroidal angle the raised plate intercepts a broader radial swath of the island, widening the footprint by a further factor of 1.55-1.6. This is not flux expansion, which is measured to decrease by 16-32% between the two plate heights and therefore opposes the widening. Second-order Chebyshev modes are found to be essential because they reverse the sign of the curvature of Z(φ), letting the plate track the toroidal drift of the strike zone over the first half of its span and fall away from it over the second half, which is a combination that is inaccessible to pure tilting sured to decrease by 16-32% between the two plate heights and therefore opposes.

title: Application of low-Z materials for enhancing H-mode plasma performance and pulse duration in EAST with full metal wall
abstract: Abstract Wall conditioning plays a key role in controlling impurity accumulation and fuel recycling for achieving long pulse, high-performance plasmas in fusion device. In this work, the effects of real-time wall conditioning using low-Z materials—boron (B) and lithium (Li) powders injection—are systematically investigated and compared in the EAST tokamak equipped with a full-metal wall. Continuous boron injection effectively suppresses high-Z impurity accumulation and maintains a low effective charge (Zeff), reducing the core W concentration by up to ~ 30%, and enabling reproducible 105-s H-mode discharges. Lithium injection also significantly improves impurity and fuel recycling control, supporting a record-breaking 1066-second H-mode plasma under combined lithiation using a 20 g pre-deposited Li coating and 1 g real-time powder injection. A statistical comparison of lithium- and boron-conditioned discharges shows that lithium powder conditioning provides about 20% higher energy confinement than B conditioning. This confinement improvement is accompanied by systematically lower neutral pressure (pn) and reduced Zeff at comparable plasma conditions, indicating more effective control of particle recycling and impurity content under lithium conditioning. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of low-Z material-based wall conditioning in improving plasma confinement and extending discharge duration, offering important implications for ITER and future fusion devices.

title: Variable-Resolution Scattering Reveals Ensemble Properties
abstract: SAXS/SANS determine the size and structure of particles and macromolecules in solution. However, the conventional low-angle determination of the radius of gyration, Rg, cannot separately resolve its scattering-weighted mean and the width of its distribution. Because the apparent Rg includes a contribution from ensemble variance, the distribution width is required even to recover the mean Rg. Here, we introduce TENOR-SAXS, a method for estimating the scattering-weighted width of an Rg distribution by applying two anisotropic digital smearings to a single 2D scattering image. Comparing the smeared images provides curvature information unavailable from the conventional radial profile. The resulting observables require no explicit model of the native instrumental point-spread function and show only weak sensitivity over the range of native resolutions typical of SAXS measurements examined here. Analytical expressions are derived in the low-angle and narrow-distribution limits for ensembles described by a known or independently constrained single-particle form factor. For verification, we simulated scattering by particles with several form factors and ensembles with different size distributions, all agree well with the analytical theory. To leading order, the principal observable depends on the scattering-weighted mean and variance rather than on the distribution's functional form or higher moments. For simulated data corresponding to feasible synchrotron exposure times for biological samples, the distribution width and, expressed as a fraction of its mean, was recovered with a typical discrepancy of ~0.1, while the scattering-weighted mean Rg was recovered with ~2% relative discrepancy. TENOR-SAXS thus provides a framework for estimating ensemble width from existing 2D scattering data without explicit instrumental desmearing and for correcting the variance contribution to the apparent radius

title: Ultra-Fast 4H-SiC AC-LGAD for 4D Tracking Applications
abstract: 4H-SiC low gain avalanche detectors (LGADs) combine internal gain with the high carrier saturation drift velocity, thermal stability, and low leakage current of SiC. AC-coupled readout (AC-LGAD) adds position information to the precise timing, which enables 4D tracking. This work reports the first experimental demonstration of a 4H-SiC AC-LGAD. Devices with a $1.0\times1.0$~mm$^2$ active area and a $2\times2$ array of AC-coupled pads at a pitch of 500~$\mu$m were fabricated with two gain-layer doping concentrations, $4\times10^{17}$ and $5\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$, and characterized with a 375~nm ultraviolet transient current technique (UV-TCT) scanning setup. The hit position and time were reconstructed with the conventional discretized positioning circuit (DPC) and constant fraction discrimination (CFD) methods. They were also reconstructed with a transformer-based neural network, which processes the full waveforms of the four pads through a shared encoder and formulates timing as a per-sample segmentation task. With DPC and CFD, the best position and time resolutions are about 10~$\mu$m and 20~ps. The neural network mitigates the nonlinear distortions near the device edges and improves the position resolution to below 5~$\mu$m and the time resolution to about 15~ps, improvements of more than 60\% and 30\%, respectively. The higher-doped device reaches a high signal-to-noise ratio at lower bias and keeps good performance at low laser intensities. These results demonstrate the potential of 4H-SiC AC-LGADs for 4D tracking in future collider experiments.

title: Semileptonic decays of Λ → p ℓ − ν ¯ ℓ in light-front dynamics
abstract: We investigate the exclusive semileptonic decays of Λ → p ℓ − ν ¯ ℓ ( ℓ = e , μ ) within the standard model using the light-front quark model. The transition form factor behaviors of Λ → p are obtained from the effective treatment of nonvalence contributions in addition to the valence ones in the Drell-Yan-West frame due to the Bethe-Salpeter formalism. Based on these form factors, we obtain that the branching ratios of Λ → p e − ν ¯ e and p μ − ν ¯ μ , including nonvalence contributions, are around 8.32 × 10 − 4 and 1.31 × 10 − 4 , which are consistent with the latest measurements from the BESIII Collaboration, respectively. Our results indicate that nonvalence contributions can play a non-negligible role in the semileptonic baryon decays within the light-front framework.

title: Pulse Shape Model for a Light Enhanced Phonon Detector
abstract: COSINUS has tested prototype NaI-based cryogenic scintillating calorimeters with a composite design, in which the transition edge sensor (TES) is fabricated on a separate carrier crystal coupled to the NaI target. Measurements with the composite detectors showed deviations from the known pulse shape description for cryogenic calorimeters and did not reveal an identifiable nuclear recoil population during a neutron calibration. In this work we present a new pulse shape model which provides an explanation to these observations and that laid the foundation for the development of the final COSINUS phonon detector design named remote TES (remoTES). We demonstrate that the first COSINUS detector prototypes featured a phonon channel with signal enhancement by light absorption in the carrier, namely a light enhanced phonon detector. This design offers for the first time the chance to use a single channel phonon detector for particle discrimination. We present recent results using a novel pulse shape fitting method based on the Bayesian inference software package BAT.jl.

title: Performance of the TUCAN Magnetically Shielded Room
abstract: The TRIUMF Ultracold Advanced Neutron (TUCAN) collaboration has commissioned a large magnetically shielded room to be used for measuring the neutron electric dipole moment (nEDM) to a precision of $10^{-27}~e\mathrm{cm}$. The room is composed of five layers of MuMetal and one layer of copper and sits within the $\lesssim 370~\mu\mathrm{T}$ ambient field produced by the TRIUMF cyclotron. Within this environment, the quasi-static shielding factor was measured to be $2.95(2) \times 10^4$ at $0.01~\mathrm{Hz}$ with an external peak-to-peak perturbation of $2~\mu\mathrm{T}$. Without the large ambient cyclotron field, the shielding factor improves to $3.40(3)\times 10^4$ at the same perturbation amplitude and frequency. After idealization in the cyclotron field, the residual field at the room center was $B = 1.8(2)~\mathrm{nT}$ and the vertical first-order gradient across the central 1~m$^3$ ($dB_{\mathrm{z}}/dz$) was $-307(26)~\mathrm{pT/m}$. With additional improvement to the idealization, and with active compensation, we expect the room to be adequate for a $10^{-27}~e\mathrm{cm}$ nEDM search.

title: P-ONE-1: the first detector line of the Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment
abstract: Neutrino telescopes instrument optically transparent media with three-dimensional arrays of photosensors to detect Cherenkov radiation induced by neutrino interactions within or near the instrumented volume. The small cross-sections of the weak interaction and the low neutrino fluxes above TeV energies require vast detector volumes, which only natural media on Earth can realistically provide. Spurred by the detection of the first neutrino sources by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, a new generation of neutrino telescopes is emerging to increase the global instrumented volume and detection sensitivity. The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment (P-ONE) aims to install such a telescope in the Northeast Pacific Ocean, building on established neutrino telescope design targets in collaboration with Ocean Networks Canada (ONC). This article presents the design, integration, and testing of the first P-ONE line, P-ONE-1, in preparation for its deployment and integration into ONC's deep-sea observatory NEPTUNE. Alongside the detector design and integration methods, we detail in-air and in-water system-level validation performed at several test sites in Canada, culminating in the successful construction of P-ONE-1 and its preparation for deployment.

title: Open Science with the LHCb Ntupling Service
abstract: The data samples collected at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN are highly valuable, and the analysis of these data has led to numerous discoveries and the 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics. Preserving and providing open access to these data for future analysts is imperative to maximize the scientific output of the collected data. The LHCb collaboration has developed a novel approach to this pursuit of open science, the LHCb Ntupling Service: a web service for on-demand production and publishing of custom LHCb open data, providing open access to both Run 1, and for the first time, Run 2 proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment, amounting to over 4 PB of data to explore.
authors: Daan Eduard Rosendal (Now at Lakera company

title: Multi-Threshold Sampling: Local and Global Parameter Identifiability
abstract: Multi-threshold (MT) sampling records threshold-crossing times for parameter estimation in applications including positron emission tomography, oil well logging, and photon-counting X-ray imaging. We study whether the distribution of recorded crossings uniquely determines the signal parameters and how many thresholds are required for this identifiability. For a fixed MT sampler, we show that the ranks of distribution derivatives with respect to the parameters cannot increase through crossing, timing, and selection. Under suitable regularity assumptions, we characterize local identifiability by a full-rank Jacobian of finitely many event probabilities defined on recorded crossings and establish a necessary and sufficient global identifiability criterion under additional rank and topological assumptions. For a nonhomogeneous Poisson signal model with four intensity parameters, a fixed known single-photon response, and deterministic MT sampling, we prove that four cumulative probabilities of the first recorded crossing time establish local and global identifiability under their respective conditions using a single sufficiently small positive threshold. This attains the minimum number of thresholds for the specified model and sampler. Numerical experiments illustrate these results and reveal weak parameter sensitivity and substantial finite-sample estimation errors when estimation uses these probabilities. The results establish parameter uniqueness while highlighting the role of statistical sensitivity in accurate estimation.

title: Mapping a holographic QCD equation of state onto an inhomogeneous hydrodynamic background
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate space-time profiles of local equilibrium thermodynamic quantities by mapping a machine-learning Einstein-Maxwell-Dilaton (EMD) equation of state onto a prescribed inhomogeneous hydrodynamic background. The EMD model, calibrated to lattice-QCD thermodynamics and baryon-number susceptibility at vanishing baryon chemical potential, provides equilibrium thermodynamic observables in the $(T,\mu_B)$ plane. The hydrodynamic simulation supplies the local temperature and baryon chemical potential, $T(\tau,\eta)$ and $\mu_B(\tau,\eta)$, in Milne coordinates. We then evaluate the local thermodynamic fields cell by cell through the mapping $(T,\mu_B)(\tau,\eta)\longrightarrow(\frac{s}{T^3},\frac{p}{T^4},\frac{\epsilon}{T^4},\frac{I}{T^4},\chi_2^B,c_s^2)(\tau,\eta)$. Here $I=\epsilon-3p$, and $\chi_2^B$ denotes the dimensionless second-order baryon susceptibility normalized by $T^2$. \textcolor{red}{The resulting profiles show how equilibrium thermodynamic quantities evaluated from the same holographic EoS vary across the longitudinally inhomogeneous quark-gluon plasma fireball.} The thermodynamic densities are concentrated in the early, hot, midrapidity region, while the baryon susceptibility and sound velocity provide sensitive probes of the local trajectory in the QCD phase diagram. The construction should be viewed as a post-processing step toward a fully self-consistent hydrodynamic evolution driven by the same holographic EoS, and it provides a baseline for future studies of critical fluctuations and freeze-out observables at finite baryon density.

title: Holographic Calculation of Semileptonic Form Factors and the Isgur--Wise Function for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}$ Decays
abstract: We present a holographic analysis of the semileptonic decays $B \to D \ell \bar{\nu}_\ell$ and $B_s \to D_s \ell \bar{\nu}_\ell$ within the Softwall Model (SWM) and the Non-Quadratic Softwall Model (NQSWM). We extract the Isgur-Wise function from the overlap integral of bulk wavefunctions, with model parameters fixed by the heavy-light meson spectra. We impose Heavy Quark Symmetry (HQS) at zero recoil and address the apparent paradox of a non-conserved electroweak current dual to a massless bulk vector field. We argue that the non-conservation, arising from explicit flavor-- symmetry breaking by quark masses, does not generate an anomalous dimension. Hence the bulk field remains massless, and the non-conservation is \emph{encoded} in the independent boundary couplings $g_+$ and $g_-$. Our predictions for the branching fractions are in good agreement with LHCb data for $B_s \to D_s$ decays. The lepton-flavor universality ratios $R(D)$ and $R(D_s)$ are consistent with Standard Model and lattice QCD predictions. We find that the holographic models reproduce the universality of the Isgur-Wise function near zero recoil, while discrepancies at maximum recoil suggest that a more complete treatment of higher-order $1/m_Q$ corrections is needed.

title: Diffusion Monte Carlo study of deuteronlike fully light hexaquarks
abstract: We perform a diffusion Monte Carlo study of fully light hexaquarks containing three u quarks and three d quarks within a constituent-quark model. Both compact and baryon-baryon-like arrangements were considered separately. All compact hexaquark configurations are found well above their corresponding baryon-baryon thresholds, suggesting that deeply bound compact six-quark states are not favored in the light-quark sector within this model. By contrast, several dibaryonlike configurations lie close to, but above, the N N , N Δ , and Δ Δ thresholds and show spatial structures compatible with molecular states. One configuration exhibits two well-defined nucleonlike subclusters separated by several femtometers, characteristic of deuteronlike spatial clustering, although its calculated energy remains slightly above the corresponding threshold.

title: Analytical Chemistry at the Planetary Frontier
abstract: Planetary science depends on chemical measurements made under conditions very different from those in a terrestrial laboratory. This review treats the analytical methods of planetary science as one connected chain, from orbital remote sensing through in-situ measurements by landers and rovers and sample collection and curation, to the micro-analysis of returned material on Earth. Orbital methods, including visible and near-infrared reflectance, thermal emission and gamma-ray and neutron spectroscopy, are discussed first. In-situ techniques are then reviewed, including laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS), micro-focus X-ray fluorescence (XRF), deep-ultraviolet Raman and fluorescence spectroscopy, evolved gas analysis with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and miniaturized mass spectrometry. Contamination control and curation practices are described, followed by laboratory techniques such as secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS and NanoSIMS), atom probe tomography (APT), thermal ionization mass spectrometry (TIMS), synchrotron micro-XRF and X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. Accuracy, calibration and reference materials are discussed as the link between in-situ and laboratory data, and the role of chemometrics and data fusion is examined. Flight and laboratory instruments are compared in terms of spatial resolution, detection limit, sample consumption and throughput. Active neutron-gamma spectroscopy planned for the Dragonfly mission to Titan is also discussed. This comparison shows that in-situ and laboratory techniques are complementary. In-situ instruments provide context and select samples, while laboratory techniques provide isotopic, molecular and speciation data that cannot yet be obtained in situ.

title: A Radiation-Hardened, Fault-Aware Quantized Neural Network That Self-Heals
abstract: Deep learning (DL) models are increasingly being deployed into radiation-challenging environments in spacecraft, particle accelerators, and, soon, space-based data centers. Instantiated as a learned orchestration of numbers stored in persistent memory, models are susceptible to continual degradation as high-energy particles corrupt data. At inference time, new data passed through the network fundamentally break the off-line assumptions and guarantees of a static model determined during training. To preserve the quality and efficacy of the models, fault tolerance against bit flips is a clear objective. In this work we developed a runtime method for repairing the quantized weights of neural networks (NNs) after bit flips on commodity, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware, without storing extra replicas. Our work extends the well-established Fault-Aware Training (FAT) paradigm by adding an alignment penalty to concentrate undamaged activations and weights into a low-rank subspace, and we then reconstruct flagged corrupted coordinates from the uncorrupted survivors. We call this method {\it Projection Healing} and apply it to six regression benchmarks on quantized NNs. Holding a FAT checkpoint fixed and toggling only the runtime heal gives a further ${\sim}23\%$ reduction in the native-unit excess integral. Across those datasets the method extends the operational scrub interval by a median of $2.04\times$ at a $+5\%$ RMSE degradation and $1.96\times$ at $+50\%$, compared with $1.62\times$ and $1.07\times$ for classical Single Error Correction, Double Error Detection (SECDED). This introduces a new path towards designing resilient data-driven models, complementing established hardware redundancy, ECC, and FAT-based techniques.

title: $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda \ell^+\ell^-$ and $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda^{\ast} \ell^+\ell^-$ decays with polarized leptons
abstract: We present an analysis of lepton polarization observables in the rare flavor-changing neutral current decays $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda\ell^+\ell^-$ and $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda^*\ell^+\ell^-$. These decays are driven by the quark-level transition $b \to s\ell^+\ell^-$ and are sensitive to short-distance physics within and beyond the Standard Model. We work within an effective Hamiltonian framework and derive single lepton polarization asymmetries, double lepton polarization asymmetries, and polarized forward-backward asymmetries using the helicity method. The observables are expressed in terms of transversity amplitudes and evaluated using state-of-the-art lattice QCD form factors. We analyze the $q^2$ dependence of several observables for both the ground-state $\Lambda$ and the excited $\Lambda^*(1520)$ final states and discuss sensitivities of the observables to chiral structure of the effective operators and complex Wilson coefficients.

title: Observation and simulation study on bunch fill pattern dependence of absorbed power in cavity HOM dampers
abstract: In the SuperKEKB accelerator, higher-order-mode (HOM) power absorbed by the HOM dampers of the superconducting (SC) cavities limits the attainment of the design electron beam current of the High Energy Ring. As regards cylindrical ferrite dampers installed in the SC cavities, we observed that their effective loss factors considerably depended on the bunch fill pattern. To investigate this behavior in detail, wakefield simulations were conducted. HOM power is generally evaluated from the numerically calculated coupling impedance, which provides only the total beam power loss within the structure. However, when multiple absorbers are present, the absorbed power of each absorber remains unknown. To address this limitation, we introduce calculation methods that utilize the local electromagnetic fields to evaluate the absorbed power. In this study, the theoretical basis of the methods is presented and applied to the SuperKEKB SC cavity.

title: Models for differential cross section in neutron-proton scattering and their implications
abstract: A few analytic exponential models of the elastic differential cross section are proposed to analyse elastic neutron-proton (np) scattering. The models incorporate energy-dependent exponential slopes, power-law prefactors, and localized Gaussian modifications. Sub-leading exponential terms representing charge conjugation and isospin roles increase the applicability and quality of fit of the models to describe the differential cross section data of np, n \bar{p}, pp, and p \bar{p} elastic scattering. The models describe the characteristic features of all the elastic scattering data such as the dip-bump structure, shrinkage of the forward peak, and controlled curvature around the diffractive dip. Parameter values of the models are found by fitting the np experimental data in an energy range of (\sqrt{s}\) = 3.363 to 26.019 GeV and a momentum transfer range of 0.065 to 5.341 GeV^2. Employing the proposed models, total, elastic, and inelastic cross sections, slope parameters, interaction radii, and cross-section ratios for np scattering are calculated. A multi-stage error analysis is performed to evaluate the error in the calculations of the models. Implications of the results obtained by the models for nucleon structure and dynamics are discussed. The results show that the proposed models can be used for effective description of the np elastic differential cross section and for accurate estimation of the observables of elastic hadronic scattering. The findings of this study emphasize the significance of combining theoretical and phenomenological approaches, providing valuable information for investigations of future experimental data on the differential cross section from various colliders.

title: High-power attosecond x-ray free-electron lasers: Physics and design strategy
abstract: Attosecond pulses from x-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) have opened new opportunities for probing ultrafast electronic dynamics on the Ångstrom-attosecond spatiotemporal scale. Most attosecond XFEL concepts rely on generating an ultrashort high-current spike through either external laser modulation or accelerator-based beam manipulation. Despite their different implementations, these approaches share the same essential physics, namely, that the XFEL amplification is confined to a short effective lasing window within the electron beam. However, existing studies are often scheme-specific and do not yet provide a unified quantitative picture of how fundamental electron-beam properties constrain high-power attosecond performance. In this work, we investigate the general physics and scheme-independent requirements for generating high-power attosecond x-ray pulses from a short current spike. From the perspective of postsaturation superradiant evolution, we show that the electron-beam length governs both the attainable peak power and the pulse duration. We further examine the distinct roles of slice energy spread, slice emittance, energy chirp, and transverse beam tilt. Our results reveal the trade-off between peak power, pulse shortening, and single-spike probability, and provide facility-independent guidelines for optimizing electron-beam phase-space manipulation toward terawatt-class attosecond XFEL operation.

title: Features of magnetized motion of electrons in electron cooling devices
abstract: In electron coolers devices, at low energies the electron beam is immersed in a continuous solenoid, which provides a cold and tightly focused beam in the cooling and transport sections. At low energies, the electron motion satisfies the adiabatic criterion when the typical length of the magnetic field variation is much larger than the Larmor spiral length. At relativistic energies, this condition generally cannot be fulfilled, so a special method of transporting the electron beam is required. This article describes one such method, which involves the use of special “resonant” elements to guide the electron beam along the desired trajectory.

title: Cosmic birefringence from a stiff axion field and its cosmological implications
abstract: We propose a model in which the observed cosmic microwave background birefringence arises from the interaction of photons with a stiff ($w=1$) pseudo-scalar field that today contributes a subdominant fraction of the total energy density, distinct from both dark matter and dark energy. Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constrains the cosmological density of the stiff field, leading to a lower bound for its coupling with photons, $g_{\phi\gamma} > 8.9 \times 10^{-14}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Photon conversion in cluster-hosted quasars sets an upper bound, $g_{\phi\gamma} < 5.0 \times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Therefore, there is a narrow window for the discovery of this cosmological component that can be explored in the forthcoming years with astrophysical axion searches. Moreover, we show that this scenario leads to gravitational-wave signals that can be tested with planned experiments.

title: Flavor decomposition of electromagnetic multipole moments in $[q_1q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquarks: Light-quark analogs of $T_{cs1}(2900)^0$ with $J^P = 1^+$
abstract: We present a systematic study of the magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments of compact $[q_1 q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^P = 1^+$, in the diquark--antidiquark picture and within the light-cone QCD sum rule framework. By performing a flavor decomposition across all admissible $u/d$ configurations, we show that the charm-quark contribution to the electromagnetic moments vanishes algebraically at the operator level -- a structural feature of the specific spin organization adopted here, in which the heavy antiquark resides in a pseudoscalar antidiquark, distinct from the dynamical $1/m_c$ suppression operative in alternative compact constructions and in hadronic molecules. The magnetic moments follow a coherent light-flavor pattern -- positive for $uu$-, negative for $dd$-, and suppressed for mixed-flavor diquarks -- and the quadrupole moments are non-zero throughout, corresponding, in the customary geometrical interpretation, to intrinsically deformed charge distributions. We further identify the dimensionless multipole ratio $\mathcal{D}/\mu$ as a structural observable, independent of the normalization of the interpolating current, which probes the relative geometry of the spin-current and charge distributions complementary to the absolute moments. Taken together, the algebraic decoupling of the charm contribution and the operator-level distinction it implies among different singly-heavy tetraquark architectures constitute methodological signatures that discriminate among the corresponding internal organizations and, to the extent that a physical candidate is dominated by one of them, among compact and molecular interpretations.

title: Characterization of CharTPix-180A, a strip-shaped monolithic sensor for the STCF inner tracker
abstract: The Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF) is a future high-luminosity electron-positron collider operating in the center-of-mass energy range of 2 to 7 GeV. The monolithic active pixel sensor (MAPS) is one of the options being considered for the STCF inner tracking detector. This application requires a MAPS capable of providing simultaneous position, time, and charge measurements under a constrained power budget of approximately 50 $\rm mW/cm^2$. To address these requirements, a baseline sensor concept featuring a strip-shaped pixel geometry has been proposed to balance power consumption and detection performance. The first prototypes of this concept, referred to as CharTPix-180A, have been developed to evaluate the proposed design. Two prototypes with different design focuses were characterized in this study. An analog readout prototype, CharTPix-180A-c4, was used to evaluate the intrinsic sensor behavior, while a fully functional digital readout prototype, CharTPix-180A-c3, was used to investigate the overall sensor functionality on a small scale. Electrical, radioactive-source, and beam tests were performed to characterize the prototypes. The measured detection efficiency exceeded 99%, the fake-hit rate was below $10^{-3}$ /pixel/s, and the spatial resolution was better than 10 $\rm\mu m$. A best time resolution of 37 ns was achieved, and the power consumption was about 50 $\rm mW/cm^2$. These results support the feasibility of the strip-shaped MAPS concept for the STCF inner tracker and provide guidance for further design optimization.

title: A high-speed, large-aperture 3D printed laser shutter for cold atom experiments
abstract: Cold atom experiments require optical shutters with rapid and repeatable actuation. Existing solutions often involve high cost, limited aperture diameter and slow transitioning. We present a 3D-printable shutter design featuring a large aperture of 4.5 mm diameter, low-cost assembly, and robust performance. The device achieves switching times of $399\pm8~\mu$s with delays of $2.7\pm0.2$ ms for a fully illuminated aperture, with four different shutters demonstrating repeatable performance. We measure the shutter speed to be $7.0\pm0.1$ m/s. This approach offers an accessible, scalable solution for cold atom and other optical experiments requiring multiple shutters with precise light control and avoids the need to resize or precision-align a beam through an aperture.

title: A Discrete Amplitude-to-Time Conversion Circuit for TDC-Based Readout of Fast Scintillation Detectors
abstract: Fast timing measurements with scintillation detectors commonly employ leading-edge discriminators and time-to-digital converters (TDCs). Many applications also require an energy-related observable for estimating the deposited energy and correcting time-walk effects. Time-over-threshold (ToT) is frequently used for this purpose, but its relationship to pulse amplitude can be severely degraded by undershoot, ringing, and other distortions of the detector pulse tail. This work presents a discrete analog front-end circuit for amplitude-to-time conversion that is insensitive to pulse-tail distortions. An analog multiplexer and a high-speed comparator implement a sample-hold-discharge stage: upon leading-edge detection, the detector pulse amplitude is sampled near its peak and stored on a capacitor, which is subsequently discharged at a controlled rate. The resulting digital pulse width encodes the sampled amplitude, while the leading edge preserves the timing information. The circuit was designed for a short recovery time and a total dead time below 100~ns, making it suitable for high-rate detector readout. The approach enables simultaneous timing and amplitude measurements through a single TDC channel. An eight-channel front-end card implementing this concept was characterized using generated test pulses. The measured transfer function is approximately linear up to input amplitudes of 0.5~V and extends beyond 2~V, with a low-amplitude conversion gain of approximately 27~ps/mV. The estimated relative amplitude precision falls below \SI{0.5}{\percent} for input amplitudes above 0.5~V. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a low-complexity, multichannel amplitude-to-time converter for TDC-based detector readout, offering an alternative to conventional ToT measurement when pulse-tail distortions compromise amplitude estimation.

title: Transverse momentum dependence of $\Omega/\phi$ ratio in high energy collisions
abstract: Abstract We apply a constituent quark equal-velocity combination model to study the $p_{T}$ dependence of $\Omega/\phi$ ratio in $pp$, $p$-Pb and Pb-Pb collisions at LHC energies. We demonstrate that the relative change rate of the $\Omega/\phi$ ratio is dominated by a curvature property of $p_{T}$ spectrum of strange quarks just before hadronization. Using experimental data of $\phi$ mesons after a quark number scaling operation, we extract $p_{T}$ spectrum of strange quarks just before hadronization and study its curvature property in high and low multiplicity events in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=$ 7, 13 TeV, $p$-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$= 5.02 TeV and Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$= 2.76 TeV. We apply these curvature properties of $p_{T}$ spectra of strange quarks to explain the observed $p_{T}$ dependence of $\Omega/\phi$ ratio in these collisions. We discuss the possible origin of the change of curvature property for $p_{T}$ spectra of strange quarks just before hadronization by considering the influence of strong collective flow formed in partonic stage evolution in collisions at LHC energies.

title: Suppression of transient beam loading effects in storage rings via main cavity power source feedforward scheme
Physical design of a high-charge beam injector for the on-axis swap-out injection scheme in an electron-positron collider
Optimized bunch lengthening for beam extraction from J-PARC RCS
Design criteria for a beam-driven resonant passive transverse deflector for longitudinal beam diagnostics
3D initial-state dynamics across scales: A comparative study of saturation and string-based descriptions
abstract: We compare the longitudinal deposition of various conserved quantities in the initial condition models of a string based (SMASH) and a saturation based () approach. SMASH has been shown to work reasonably well at lower collision energies as an initial condition for the SMASH-vHLLE hybrid approach, while , based on the color-glass-condensate, works well in the regime of perturbative quantum chromodynamics. The two models are capable of providing longitudinally resolved initial conditions, which is essential for three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations. The goal of this study is to interface the different regions of applicability of the two models, to investigate the initial state dynamics in the intermediate energy regime. We analyze the deposition of transverse energy, charge and baryon number across a large range of collision energies (62.4 GeV to 5.02 TeV) and find that, while they are good agreement at lower energies, their energy and baryon deposition differs substantially at higher center of mass energies.

title: Direct Detection of Leptophobic Dark Matter with Electronic Collective Excitations
abstract: Abstract Some new-generation dark matter detection experiments are primarily designed to search for the dark matter-electron interactions, but they can also be utilized to probe models in which dark matter couples exclusively to nucleon via the quantum effects. The hadronic loop-induced interactions can directly excite plasmons in semiconductors, thereby providing an additional channel for detecting the leptophobic dark matter. In this work, we investigate plasmon excitations in silicon detectors induced by boosted dark matter and cosmic-ray up-scattering dark matter via the hadronic loop process. By analyzing the available experimental data, we derive new exclusion limits on the leptophobic dark matter-nucleon scattering cross section in the sub-MeV mass range. Content from this work may be used under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 licence. Any further distribution of this work must maintain attribution to the author(s) and the title of the work, journal citation and DOI. title: Search for Compact Binary Coalescences with Sub-solar Mass Components in Data from the Second Part of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's Fourth Observing Run
abstract: We report on a gravitational wave search for compact binary coalescences with secondary mass between 0.2 M and 1 M and primary mass between 0.2 M and 10 M, restricting the component mass ratio to lie between 0.1 and 1. The analysis uses data collected by the LIGO and Virgo detectors between 2024 April 10 15:00:00 and 2025 January 28 17:00:00, the second part of the fourth observing run of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration. Results from two out of three search pipelines show outlier candidates, but not at a sufficient level of significance to provide evidence for detection. We report the combined sensitivity of the current searches over the first and second parts of the observing run to the target sub-solar mass (SSM) black hole (BH) population, as well as to neutron star (NS) binaries with one or more sub-solar component. We place upper limits on the merger rate of SSM BHs, ranging from $50 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ to~$5000 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ (90% confidence) for different component mass combinations. We use the merger rate limits to constrain two illustrative dark matter (DM) scenarios that can form SSM compact objects: primordial BHs, and dark BHs forming in a dissipative DM model. Our search limits the fraction of DM in primordial BHs, assuming a monochromatic mass distribution, to be $\leq$ (0.018-0.032) at 1 M, and $\leq$ (0.10-0.18) at 0.35 M for early-forming binaries; or to be less than 1 at masses above (0.62-0.74) M for late-forming binaries. For the dissipative model, we constrain the fraction of DM for a range of minimum dark black hole masses below $1\,M$ to be as low as (1.0-1.1) x $10^{-5}$; we also exclude minimum masses above (0.62-0.74) M, if dark BHs constitute all of the DM. For binary NSs that include sub-solar mass components, assuming a simple, fixed population model we find a merger rate upper limit of $249 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$.

title: Probing freeze-in dark matter using Bose-Einstein condensate in neutron star
abstract: Neutron star (NS) is one of the most promising astrophysical targets to probe non-gravitational interaction of dark matter (DM) with visible matter. Their compactness makes them an ideal object which can capture particle DM efficiently over its lifetime using the DM-nucleon scattering cross-section. If DM particles are bosonic, then the captured DM population may form a Bose-Einstein condensate at the center of the NS, increasing the DM density significantly. In this work, we study the phenomenology of such scenario with enhanced DM annihilation rate due to the increased density in a condensate. The enhanced DM annihilation makes the NS surface `hotter' than in the standard cooling scenario. We show that the annihilation rate is enhanced by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15}-10^{20})$ if DM forms a condensate without large self-interaction, and DM with freeze-in value annihilation cross-section can heat up the NS to higher temperatures, bringing it within the reach of James Webb Space Telescope. It also allows us to probe DM-nucleon scattering cross section within the neutrino fog regime which will complement the terrestrial direct detection searches. Moreover, the enhanced annihilation from the condensate changes the lower limits on s-wave DM annihilation cross-section for capture-annihilation equilibrium and the formation of a black hole inside the NS. Finally, we show an example of a scalar DM model where such small annihilation and DM-nucleon scattering cross sections can generically arise.

title: Physics-constrained graph closures and working-point conditioning for a fast surrogate of linac beam dynamics
abstract: When a graph neural network estimates a physical quantity, its frame, edge direction, aggregation and feature normalization decide which laws it can break. Wrong choices leave systematic errors the loss never registers. We build a linac beam-dynamics surrogate on this observation. Space charge, short-range wakefields and coherent synchrotron radiation enter as bounded closures on analytic kernels, on graphs whose frame and direction follow the interaction and whose symmetry makes the net space-charge self-force vanish for any weights. Verified without training, with randomized weights, the invariants break by five to eight orders of magnitude once the responsible feature is inverted. Per-working-point models constrained by the rms envelope equation are distilled into one model conditioned on 15 machine settings. On the 18.4~m L0+L1 section of the Shanghai soft x-ray free-electron laser linac, this model predicts the transverse beam envelope at 50 unseen settings to about $7\%$, with the centroid trajectory and emittance, in 0.38~s on a single Quadro RTX 6000 GPU. Training is instead dominated by a normalization choice, a data-derived output range for the beam size: at all 16 working points it lowers the starting error 2.2- to 8.5-fold and fixes the convergence speed. The remaining accuracy differences between hybrid and data-driven architectures vary with the working point and with the density of observation. The held-out error scales roughly as $N^{-0.6}$ with the corpus size $N$. Whether the physics pays off where collective effects are strong, as in a magnetic bunch compressor, is in the next phase of our study.

title: Machine-learned spectral PDE solvers for fluids and plasmas
abstract: Sparse regression methods for discovering governing partial differential equations (PDEs) from data are sensitive to observation noise and are not constrained to reproduce the data under forward integration. We address both limitations by performing weak-form discovery in the spatial discretization in which the PDE is solved, learned by differentiating through multistep rollouts anchored at the observed states. The new method, Weak-form Anchored Rollout for PDEs (WARP), produces a machine-learned PDE solver. In this work, we focus on systems amenable to a spectral Galerkin solver. Across eight benchmark fluid and plasma systems, including high-dimensional turbulent simulations, WARP produces numerically stable rollouts from new random initial conditions and substantially improves coefficient recovery, rollout accuracy, and statistical measures compared with a single-step weak-form SINDy baseline.

title: Isospin breaking in $\rho\pi\pi$ couplings: $\rho^{+,0}$ width difference and muon $g-2$
abstract: The dominant contribution to the hadronic vaccum polarization (HVP) of the muon $g-2$ can be calculated using the hadronic spectrum in $\tau^- \to \pi^-\pi^0\nu_{\tau}$ decay, provided isospin breaking (IB) corrections are properly accounted for. Among these corrections, IB in the $\rho\pi\pi$ coupling has been pointed out as a missing ingredient. In this work, we calculate this IB effect within the impulse approximation using a symmetry-preserving framework based on Dyson-Schwinger and Bethe-Salpeter equations, incorporating fully dressed quark propagators and meson Bethe-Salpeter amplitudes. We then estimate its effect in the HVP contribution to the muon $g-2$. As a natural extension, we also compute the IB in the ratio of $\phi K^+K^-/\phi K^0\bar{K^0}$ couplings and compare with existing data. We obtain a coupling ratio $g_{\rho^0\pi^+\pi^-}/g_{\rho^+\pi^+\pi^0} = 1.0024(17)(1)$, which yields an isospin-breaking correction of $\Delta a_\mu^{\mathrm{HVP,LO}}[\rho\pi\pi] = -2.32(1.64)\times 10^{-10}$ to the two-pion contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment extracted from $\tau$ decay data.

title: Hidden engines in tidal disruption events: multimessenger signatures in a lepto-hadronic framework
abstract: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) provide a unique laboratory for studying transient accretion, outflows, particle acceleration, and the possible connection between stellar disruptions and high-energy neutrinos. Motivated by recent candidate TDE-neutrino associations and by the forthcoming sensitivity of multimessenger facilities, we investigate under which physical conditions TDEs can be detected in MeV, GeV, and TeV gamma rays, and in high-energy neutrinos. We develop a lepto-hadronic emission framework and apply it to three representative sources: AT2019dsg, AT2019ehz, and ASASSN-14li. For each source we explore a set of physically motivated models that vary the proton and electron spectral indices, the minimum Lorentz factor of non-thermal protons, the particle energy partition, the acceleration efficiency, the magnetic compactness, and the presence of a compact corona. We compute the broadband spectral energy distributions, the associated muon-neutrino spectra, and compare them with reference sensitivities for COSI, Fermi/LAT, CTAO, and KM3NeT/ARCA. We find that hard proton spectra and/or large minimum proton Lorentz factors are the most favourable conditions for TeV gamma-ray and neutrino detectability, while GeV-bright models can be predominantly leptonic and neutrino quiet. AT2019dsg and AT2019ehz can reach the CTAO and KM3NeT benchmarks in hadronically favourable configurations, whereas ASASSN-14li is more naturally bright in the MeV-GeV band and constrained by its radio synchrotron emission. Our results highlight the importance of combining MeV, GeV, TeV, radio, and neutrino observations to distinguish between transparent, hidden, and lepton-dominated TDE emission regimes.

title: Direct Urca process facilitated by non-Fermi-liquid quantum criticality
abstract: Conventional Fermi-liquid theories of dense nuclear matter predict that the direct Urca process requires a proton fraction above a threshold of $Y_p \approx 0.11$--$0.15$, which is rarely reached in low-mass neutron stars. Here we show that this stringent kinematic constraint is drastically relaxed by the non-Fermi liquid behavior arising from superfluid and superconducting quantum criticality in neutron stars. In the non-Fermi-liquid regimes, nucleons have a smooth momentum occupation without a sharp Fermi surface, and their chemical potentials develop a logarithmic temperature dependence. These intrinsic features fundamentally alter the standard $\beta$-equilibrium relation. Consequently, direct Urca neutrino emission can be activated even at low nuclear densities. This modifies the long-standing Urca-threshold paradigm and indicates that direct Urca process has the opportunity to occur in low-mass neutron stars.

title: Illuminating Light Dark Matter with Fixed-Target Experiments
abstract: Astronomical and cosmological observations provide overwhelming evidence for a non-luminous matter component, dark matter (DM), whose particle nature remains unknown. Experimental searches for non-gravitational DM interactions have largely targeted DM with GeV-TeV masses via nuclear recoils, yielding no discovery thus far. DM in the MeV-GeV mass range, however, is theoretically motivated, reproducing the observed relic abundance while remaining invisible to nuclear recoil searches. Such light DM is better probed via electron recoils or at fixed-target experiments. This thesis advances the theoretical and statistical toolkit for light DM searches at fixed-target experiments, spanning model building, statistical inference, global fits, and signal simulation. We survey the landscape of fixed-target searches for light DM, focusing on the Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX). We also simulate DM signatures at the next-generation experiment SHiP to assess its sensitivity. Within minimal DM models, we present a likelihood-based statistical framework for LDMX using the full two-dimensional recoil electron distribution, spanning exclusion, discovery, parameter estimation, and model comparison in frequentist and Bayesian formulations. This establishes the discovery potential of LDMX, and we quantify the direct detection exposure needed to independently confirm a potential signal. Beyond this paradigm, we perform global fits of scalar and fermionic light DM, combining cosmological, astrophysical, and laboratory constraints. We then extend fixed-target searches to spin-1 DM and higher electromagnetic moment dark photons, yielding rich signatures with strong complementarity to other probes. Finally, we go beyond standard nuclear modelling of dark photon production, incorporating elastic nuclear form factors and spectral functions from many-body ab initio methods in place of analytic treatments.

title: Floquet Instability of Photon-Axion Conversion
abstract: The discovery of axions would provide evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we investigate axion-photon conversion in the presence of a background magnetic field with simultaneous spatial and temporal periodicity. By performing a Lorentz transformation, the coupled axion-photon system is mapped onto a time-periodic linear system that can be analyzed using Floquet theorem. We find unstable modes associated with resonant crossing between Floquet replicas. The resulting complex Floquet exponents lead to exponentially growing modes, which we identify as a Floquet instability. Then, we determine the parameter regions in which this instability appears in a perturbative analysis. We further show that the Floquet instability enhances the axion-field amplitude generated from an initial photon field. Our results demonstrate that spatiotemporally periodic magnetic backgrounds provide a distinct mechanism for modifying axion-photon conversion through Floquet instability.

title: SN 2023iop: An Extreme 1987A-like Supernova and the Death of Very Massive Stars
abstract: Supernova (SN) 1987A showed that some hydrogen-rich core-collapse supernovae (SNe) rise slowly to peak, defining a distinct subclass. Wide-field surveys have uncovered more extreme members, such as OGLE-2014-SN-73, SN 2020faa, and SN 2023vbw, that challenge neutrino-driven explosion models. We present ultraviolet-to-infrared, radio, X-ray, and spectropolarimetric observations of SN 2023iop at $z = 0.1020$, the most extreme 87A-like event to date. It rose for $\gtrsim88$ rest-frame days to $M_r \approx -20.1$ mag, also placing it among the hydrogen-rich superluminous SNe, and radiated $\gtrsim4\times10^{50}$ erg. Its spectra resemble those of typical Type II SNe and remain photospheric at $\sim330$ days post-maximum. Continuum polarization of 0.8-1.0% indicates an aspherical system. Hydrogen-rich pair-instability supernova (PISN) models of a $190~M_\odot$ star reproduce the light-curve up to 150 days after peak, but not the late-time emission. A late-time spectrum shows a feature near 7300 {\AA}, tentatively identified as [Ni II] $\lambda$7378. The implied $\approx0.02~M_\odot$ of stable $^{58}$Ni is reached only in the most massive PISN models. The low-mass host galaxy ($\sim10^{8.2}~M_\odot$) is consistent with a metal-poor progenitor as required by the PISN channel. Fallback accretion reproduces the light-curve morphology, but not the colors. We consider a pair-instability explosion the most plausible scenario, with the late-time light-curve excess powered by circumstellar interaction, which shows no signatures in the spectra. SN 2023iop shows that the most luminous 87A-like events occupy an underexplored region of massive-star evolution.

title: Numerical shock broadening and supernova neutrino conversion: implications for DUNE
abstract: Hydrodynamical simulations spread the supernova shock front over a few grid zones, a width set by the numerical scheme rather than by the physics of the shock. Where the front crosses the H resonance, that width can make the computed MSW evolution artificially adiabatic. We quantify the effect on six three-dimensional blue-supergiant explosion models from the Garching archive by propagating individual rays twice: through the stored profile, and with the front replaced by a narrow reconstruction, 2.2 km wide, that approximates a sudden crossing while keeping the densities on either side. The stored fronts are 1.6 to 1.7 grid zones wide. Across twelve configurations, each chosen inside the energy band in which that model's front meets the resonance, the reconstruction raises the ray-averaged crossing probability $P_H$ by 0.44 to 0.76 in absolute terms, median 0.56; narrowing the reconstruction thirty-fold changes each difference by at most 0.055. Along all 12878 rays of one configuration, the sudden-limit formula evaluated on each ray's own densities agrees closely with the propagated reconstructed result. The change is largest when the density jump spans the resonance, over a band of energies that can be estimated from the presupernova density once the shock radius and the compression are known, with tails outside it. In a separate calculation with a parametrised shock and a published emission model, time-dependent conversion changes the $\nu_e$ charged-current count in a 40 kt argon detector by -4.4%, with a sign set by the flavour composition of the source. Folding the reconstructed three-dimensional fronts with a consistent emission model remains to be done.

title: Exact 1D Nonlinear Solutions for Proton-Driven Plasma Wakefields
abstract: We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the pristine fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using an intense two-bunch scheme, our adaptive integration model is validated down to machine precision against exact closed-form cold-fluid invariants, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ micro-bunch train, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a closed-form, parameter-free piecewise analytical envelope expression. This solution successfully maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic horizontal saturation horizon governed by nonlinear energy conservation. Furthermore, the framework analytically evaluates the transient envelope overshoot, tracking its decay onto the saturation boundary via an exact phase-slip integration length scale. Providing immediate, ready macro-envelope bounds, this computationally inexpensive tool eliminates empirical adjustments and yields a robust mathematical baseline designed to guide and accelerate complex, multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations through rapid parameter space exploration before deploying heavy computational assets. It establishes an efficient foundation to optimize asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles required to break the fundamental symmetric transformer ratio limit of 2 to make current particle accelerators more efficient.

title: Dynamical stability of Magnetic Supramassive Neutron Stars
abstract: We investigate the dynamical stability of strongly magnetized supramassive neutron stars close to the mass-shedding limit using fully general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations in three spatial dimensions. Equilibrium configurations are constructed using a microphysical equation of state and considering poloidal magnetic fields up to maximum strengths ${\sim} 10^{17}\,\mathrm{G}$. The initially unstable magnetic fields reorganize into mixed poloidal--toroidal configurations on Alfv\'en timescales shorter than the stellar rotation period. The subsequent dynamical evolution is governed by timescales set by the Lehnert number. For stars with masses sufficiently lower than the maximum mass, magnetic stresses redistribute angular momentum and drive the development of differential rotation, leading to a new quasi-stationary configuration that remains dynamically stable over several rotation periods. Magnetically-driven winds develop from the outer layers around the equatorial plane and remain baryon-matter dominated with magnetization ${\lesssim}0.2$. Over the simulated timescale, winds carry a total rest mass of order ${\sim}10^{-3}\mathrm{M}_\odot$ at outflow rates of up to a few $M_\odot/\mathrm{s}$. For stars close to (or beyond) the maximum-mass turning point along the stellar equilibrium sequence, strong magnetic fields trigger gravitational collapse by redistributing angular momentum away from the stellar core. The resulting black hole remnants are characterized by angular velocities up to ${\sim}49\%$ larger and angular momentum ${\lesssim}8\%$ smaller than those of the initial equilibrium stars. Our results show that extreme magnetic-field instabilities can significantly alter the structure of supramassive neutron stars, with possible implications for magnetars and long-lived binary neutron-star merger remnants.

title: Nonflow Subtraction Beyond Two-Particle Correlations
abstract: Establishing collective flow in small collision systems is a crucial and necessary condition for pinning down the minimum conditions for quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formation. In two-particle correlations, nonflow has been subtracted with good control, pushing the reach of flow measurements down to very small event particle multiplicity $N$. However, the multi-particle nature of collectivity has not been established in the same $N$ regime, because the residual nonflow surviving the subevent procedure in multi-particle cumulants has never been quantified. We develop a general nonflow subtraction framework for $m$-particle cumulants, built around the approximate $1/N^{m-1}$ scaling of nonflow in the independent-source picture. Correlators containing $v_1$ serve as nonflow-dominated estimators, since the $p_{\mathrm T}$-integrated dipolar flow is expected to be small. Using HIJING as a controlled nonflow-only environment, we test the subtraction for three target observables ($\langle v_2^2\rangle$, $\langle v_2^2\delta p_{\mathrm T}\rangle$, and $c_2\{4\}$) in O+O at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36$ TeV and 200 GeV and in $d$+Au at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 200$ GeV. Most of the nonflow is removed, with residual fractions typically within 20-30% when converted to the two-particle level, though the best estimator differs across the three targets. We identify a multiplicity-reweighting correction, previously overlooked in two-particle correlations, that explains the long-standing undersubtraction of the naive $1/N$-scaling method; its impact grows as a power of the correlator order. The framework gives a systematic route to nonflow subtraction beyond two-particle correlations, broadening the class of multi-particle observables accessible to the small-system flow program.

title: Jets as differential probes of hot QCD matter
abstract: Ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions create short-lived droplets of deconfined, hot QCD matter whose evolution connects far-from-equilibrium early dynamics to the hydrodynamic quark-gluon plasma. High-energy jets, produced in early hard scatterings and modified by this evolving medium, provide multi-scale probes of its microscopic properties. This thesis develops perturbative QCD tools to extract information about hot QCD matter from its imprint on differential jet substructure observables. Our framework is the BDMPS-Z description of high-energy partons propagating through stochastic colour fields. We first study anisotropic QCD matter by replacing the usual scalar broadening parameter with direction-dependent transverse momentum broadening. This relates anisotropic corrections to medium-induced splittings to spin information and azimuthal patterns in final-state energy flow. Energy correlators are then used as observables sensitive to these effects, including heavy-flavour EECs, azimuthally differential EECs and clover projections designed to isolate leading anisotropy-induced harmonics. We also examine how energy loss affects the interpretation of jet substructure modifications. Quantile matching defines reconstructed energy loss as a population-level shift between vacuum and medium-modified jet spectra. We further develop energy-loss functions, which encode the distribution of energy retained by jet-originated hadrons, and show how their moments enter multi-point projected energy correlators. Finally, we go beyond single $1\to2$ medium-induced splittings by studying spin-induced correlations between successive emissions and higher-point energy correlators including contributions from medium response. The results show that differential jet substructure can probe directional properties of QCD matter and multi-point dynamics of jets propagating through it.

title: Form factors and weak decays of $\Lambda_b\to\Lambda_c^*(2595)$ and $\Xi_b\to\Xi_c^*(2790)$
Entropy Production and Thermalization in Heavy-Quark Langevin Dynamics
abstract: Heavy quarks are often treated as Brownian probes of the quark-gluon plasma. We formulate the irreversible entropy balance of their momentum distribution and separate the production generated by collisions from the driving caused by an evolving medium. For linear dynamics the production splits into two positive contributions, from directed momentum and from the momentum width. A static bath obeys an exact H-theorem. A cooling bath adds an explicit driving term, and longitudinal Bjorken expansion enters as a separate kinematic drive rather than as collisional production. For a Bjorken temperature protocol we derive closed-form strong- and weak-coupling limits of the total production. At strong coupling it exceeds the initial relative entropy by a term linear in the relaxation time, whose quasistatic part has the thermodynamic-length form. At weak coupling it vanishes inversely with the relaxation time. A positive strong-coupling slope therefore guarantees maximal dissipation at intermediate coupling. The same structure holds for a relativistic Fokker-Planck equation with a J\"uttner stationary state, solved numerically for charm and bottom quarks under the temperature protocol. Linear-response coefficients computed from the static generator reproduce both limits, and the numerical entropy balance is satisfied to high accuracy.

title: The presence and order of QCD phase transitions from gravitational-wave observations of neutron star mergers
abstract: Gravitational-wave observations of neutron star mergers allows us to probe the dense portion of the nuclear equation of state. We develop a formalism for testing the existence and order of phase transitions in the cores of neutron stars using only gravitational-wave observations of their inspiral. We test our formalism on data from the first binary neutron star mergers GW170817 and GW190425, and use synthetic injections assuming the next and uber-next upgrades of the LIGO observatories, A+ and A#, as well as with Cosmic Explorer. We show that populations of mergers in either A+ or A# will be able to measure the existence of a first-order phase transition in observations lasting less than one PhD (less than half a US PhD!). On the other hand, with only the inspiral, we cannot distinguish populations of neutron stars with no phase transition from those with second- or third-order phase transitions or with first-order phase transitions with relatively large transition densities.

title: Slowly Rotating Fully Convective Stars at $\lesssim$ 1 Gyr: Evidence from the Hyades and Praesepe
abstract: We report the discovery of 10 stars in the Praesepe and Hyades clusters with unusually slow rotation that are likely not field contamination. Even though our search was general, all slow rotators are in the fully convective domain. We find that the fraction of slow rotators in the clusters is more than $5\sigma$ above the distribution expected from field contamination. They provide a potential link between the period distribution of the young open clusters and the field. These stars could be a distinct birth population, or they could be an indication that the onset of strong magnetic breaking is earlier than previously realized in this domain. Photometric variability and X-ray luminosity suggest the later but more data is needed to confirm. Searches for similar populations in younger clusters will help determine when slow rotators first emerge and constrain the timescale and physical mechanisms governing angular-momentum loss in fully convective stars. The discovery of these stars also highlights the importance of long-baseline photometric observations for detecting the long rotation periods of low-mass stars.

title: Parameter dependence of the mapping of the mean-field Ising model onto QCD in the first-order phase transition regime
abstract: We map the mean-field Ising equation of state onto the QCD phase diagram and investigate how scaling parameters alter the metastable and unstable regions, as well as the symmetrized pressure and density along an isotherm on the QCD $T-\mu_B$ phase plane. We find that, for both the conventional mapping scheme and the scheme valid in the small-quark-mass limit, increasing the scaling parameters $w$ and $\rho$ narrows the metastable and unstable regions. In the small-quark-mass-limit scheme, larger $w$ and $\rho$ reduce both the Ising-symmetrized pressure and density.
