So the process is iterative and includes a number of trial-and-error steps. We propose to replace the per-scenario controller tuning by a single goal-conditioned reinforcement-learning controller trained once, in advance, against a free-boundary equilibrium and transport simulator. A scenario is then specified only by the target waveforms of the physical quantities of interest (plasma current, line-averaged electron density, LCFS shape, x-point positions), and the controller produces the coil-current and fueling commands that realize them. We demonstrate the approach on an EAST plasma-current ramp-up: the controller takes over a small limited plasma, ramps the current and the density, grows the cross-section, forms two x-points and holds a double-null diverted configuration against sampled shape targets for the rest of a 1.2 s episode. The neural network controller is trained using TQC algorithm. On 1024 test scenarios sampled from a low-discrepancy scrambled Sobol sequence in 11-dimensional target space, the controller forms the divertor in 86% of the cases, holds it for more than 0.5 s in 67% and reaches the end of the episode in a diverted state in 58%, with flat-top tracking errors of a few kA in plasma current, $\sim 0.15\times10^{19}$ m$^{-3}$ in density, $\sim 2$ cm in position and $\sim 8$ cm in x-point location; the failures concentrate at the high-current density ($J$) region which is believed to be physically or from engineering perspective not feasible within ohmic mode.

title: Reconstruction of Unobserved Core Electron Density in Tokamak Plasmas with a Neural Operator Transport Surrogate and Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: Real-time control of tokamak plasmas requires the electron density profile. However, in a reactor-relevant device, diagnostic port access is limited and the profile can be observed only partially. In the present work we reconstruct the density profile by inferring the coefficients of a physics-based one-dimensional particle transport equation, using a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) surrogate of the transport solver as a fast differentiable forward model. The surrogate enables realtime-compatible gradient-based reconstruction and uncertainty quantification from the reflectometry and interferometry measurements. We compare four uncertainty quantification methods - multi-seed ensembles, the Laplace approximation, Metropolis-Hastings, and a Gaussian method independent of the reconstruction fit. The resulting uncertainty is scored with CRPS and coverage calibration, separately on the observed and unobserved regions. We further demonstrate advantage of our approach over standard analytical function fit on synthetic and experimental DIII-D discharges.

title: Neutrino production at the extreme vicinity of supermassive black hole in NGC 1068
abstract: The identification of NGC~1068 as an extragalactic high-energy neutrino source raises the question of the physical conditions required for neutrino production. Motivated by the newly updated IceCube data (down to $\sim 0.2 \,\rm TeV$) for NGC 1068, we present a statistical, model-independent inference primarily constrained by the multi-messenger observations. We calculate neutrino production from hadronic channels (including hadronuclear and photomeson processes) and the accompanying cascade gamma rays, and then employ the Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) method to explore the parameter space comprehensively, constrained by observational data. According to our results, the emission region is tightly limited: $R \gtrsim 10\,R_{\rm s}$ is excluded at $\sim 5\sigma$, and $R \gtrsim 6\,R_{\rm s}$ at $\sim 3\sigma$, where $R_{\rm s}$ is Schwarzschild radius of supermassive black hole (SMBH). Furthermore, reproducing $\gtrsim 80\%$ of the observed neutrino flux further restricts the emission to $R \lesssim 3R_{\rm s}$. Finally, we explore the possible particle acceleration mechanisms and find that stochastic acceleration naturally satisfies all constraints, whereas alternative mechanisms require extreme, fine-tuning parameters. We therefore identify stochastic acceleration as the most viable origin of the neutrino emission from NGC~1068.

title: Vacancy and Helium-Cluster Thermomigration in Tungsten
abstract: Strong thermal gradients in tungsten plasma-facing components can bias the migration of irradiation-induced defects and thereby alter their redistribution, interaction, and retention. Here, we extend an atomistic jump-statistics framework previously developed for hydrogen to quantify the thermomigration of a single vacancy and interstitial He$_1$--He$_4$ clusters in body-centered-cubic tungsten. Non-equilibrium molecular-dynamics simulations performed over several thermal gradients are used to determine the directional jump ratio, while geometrically derived projected jump lengths convert the fitted directional-bias coefficient into the heat-of-transport coefficient $Q^*=\alpha kT^2$, where $k$ is the Boltzmann constant, $T$ the temperature, and $\alpha$ a constant. All investigated defects exhibit negative values of $\alpha$, corresponding to net migration toward the hot region. He$_4$ has the largest response, $\alpha=-2.2457\times10^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$, followed closely by the vacancy, whereas He$_3$ exhibits the weakest response despite its intermediate cluster size. Independent constant-temperature simulations over 1000--1600 K show that He$_3$ is also the least mobile cluster and has the largest effective migration energy, $E_m^{\mathrm{eff}}=0.271$ eV. In contrast, He$_4$ is more mobile than He$_3$ and has the smallest effective migration energy, 0.087 eV. Agreement between the He$_3$ concentration profile predicted from the jump statistics and that obtained from a long molecular-dynamics trajectory provides an independent validation of the method. These results show that thermomigration cannot be inferred from cluster size, diffusivity, or migration energy alone and provide defect-specific heat-of-transport parameters for higher-length-scale models of tungsten under fusion-relevant thermal gradients.

title: Reduced Molecular Plasma Kinetics with Non-Boltzmann Vibrational Distribution
abstract: Vibrational kinetics can strongly affect energy transfer, chemical kinetics, and discharge behavior in molecular plasmas, but resolving all internal states is often impractical for reactor-scale simulation. Compact, physics-based vibrational closures are particularly needed when complete state-to-state (StS) data are limited. Starting from a detailed $\mathrm{H}_2$ StS plasma-kinetics framework coupled to an electron-Boltzmann calculation, this work develops a reduced vibrational-kinetics formulation. The $\mathrm{H}_2$ vibrational ladder is reduced to two non-Boltzmann groups that evolve their population and internal energy. State-resolved reaction rates and associated energy-exchange terms are projected onto the groups for subsequent tabulation in reactor-scale plasma models. StS-informed samples of the reduced-model are propagated for pulsed RF $\mathrm{H}_2$ plasmas across a scan of pulse-averaged absorbed power and compared with the corresponding StS simulations. Predictions from the sampled models reproduce the bulk plasma response, including electron density, atomic-H density, and $\mathrm{H}_3^+$ density. Discrepancies in $\mathrm{H}^-$ production and the upper-energy-group vibrational temperature persist across the sampled reductions. This indicates a limitation of the present VDF reconstruction rather than the nominal parameter choice. Tail-sensitive processes therefore require a more accurate representation of the vibrational distribution.

title: Beyond Radiation Hydrodynamics: A Coupled Kinetic Plasma and Radiation Modeling of NIF Polar Direct Drive Capsule
abstract: Predictive modeling of inertial-confinement-fusion (ICF) implosions increasingly requires resolving ion-kinetic effects beyond the reach of radiation-hydrodynamics, without sacrificing radiation transport. We present, to our knowledge, the first coupling of a kinetic-ion plasma model to thermal radiation transport. The iFP code - a conservative, spherically symmetric, 1D2V hybrid kinetic-ion/fluid-electron Vlasov-Fokker-Planck solver - is extended with a grey P1 radiation model, coupled through a high-order/low-order (HOLO) fixed-point solver and advanced on a shared adaptive moving mesh. Opacities are mixed on the fly from the LANL TOPS library, exploiting the per-species information intrinsic to a kinetic code. We verify the implementation against the optically thick Marshak-wave and Mach-45 radiative-shock benchmarks, and apply it to a NIF polar-direct-drive exploding-pusher capsule. Increasing physics fidelity systematically improves agreement with the measured neutron yield and burn width; the improvement is driven by kinetically enhanced fuel leakage and ballistic preheating, and radiation transport proves essential for quantitative agreement. This work establishes a proof-of-principle capability for higher-fidelity kinetic-plasma/radiation modeling of ICF.

title: ULYSSES the Third: An Odyssey Towards a Unified Python Toolkit for Leptogenesis
abstract: We present the third release of $\texttt{ULYSSES}$, a Python package for the numerical evaluation of the baryon asymmetry generated through leptogenesis. This version includes code implementing state-of-the-art density matrix equations for low-scale leptogenesis with three quasi-degenerate right-handed neutrinos. We extend the validity of the code in this scenario beyond the 100 GeV right-handed neutrino mass scale, into the regime of resonant leptogenesis, by including neutrino production rates valid in both the relativistic and non-relativistic regimes. In addition, in the high-scale vanilla scenario, we provide routines for computing $\Delta L = 1$ scattering processes, enabling full phase-space evolution of the right-handed neutrino and lepton asymmetry. A new $\texttt{--extended}$ parameter interface allows users to pass model-specific inputs beyond the standard leptogenesis runcard without modifying the core infrastructure and demonstrate its use with a toy module that simultaneously solves the vanilla leptogenesis equations and the freeze-in production of dark matter. On top of these improvements, we introduce an alternative parametrisation of the Casas-Ibarra matrix, update the default neutrino oscillation parameters and report cross-checks of the new low-scale leptogenesis module against published benchmarks and independent codes. $\texttt{ULYSSES}$ is publicly available on $\href{https://github.com/earlyuniverse/ulysses}{\texttt{GitHub}}$ and pip-installable from PyPI.

title: Testing Leptogenesis via CP asymmetries in Lepton-Number-Violating $W$ Decays at Colliders
abstract: In principle, searches for CP asymmetries in rare $W$-boson decays can test low-scale leptogenesis in the GeV-scale type-I seesaw with three quasi-degenerate-in-mass heavy right-handed neutrinos. To investigate this, we focus on the lepton-number-violating heavy-neutrino-mediated decay $W^{\pm}\to e^{\pm} e^{\pm} (\bar{q} q')^{\mp}$, with $(\bar{q} q')^+ = (\bar{d}u)^+$ and $(\bar{q} q')^- = (\bar{u}d)^-$. We determine the minimum branching ratio required for a CP asymmetry to be observable at colliders with a given statistical significance. We then perform a numerical scan of the presently-allowed parameter space, also solving the density matrix equations for low-scale leptogenesis, and identify regions where, simultaneously, the present baryon asymmetry of the Universe can be achieved and the collider CP asymmetry for the considered decay is observable at HL-LHC and FCC-hh. We find that these regions are sizeable. A future observation of a CP asymmetry in $W^{\pm}\to e^{\pm} e^{\pm} (\bar{q} q')^{\mp}$ within the regions identified here would provide evidence in favour of low-scale leptogenesis as the origin of the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the Universe.

title: Probing dark-matter scenarios of Belle II excess in $B^+\to K^+M_X$ with $K^+\to \pi^+ M_X$ decays
abstract: The hypothesis of top-philic dark matter as the origin of the Belle II excess events in $B\to K M_X$ decays has direct impact on $K\to \pi M_X$ decays: Both of these decays proceed via loop diagrams~with a top quark emitting some mediator field $R$ and the subsequent decay of $R$ into a pair of dark-matter fermions $\bar\chi\chi$. The Belle II results on $B\to K M_X$ allowed us to extract the parameters of the mediator $R$ with reasonable accuracy, whereas the sensitivity to the fermion mass $m_\chi$ proved to be rather low. In contrast to $B\to K M_X$ decays, the $K\to \pi M_X$ decays exhibit a strong sensitivity to $m_\chi$; therefore, if - upon reducing theoretical and experimental uncertainties - the tension between standard-model predictions for the $K\to\pi M_X$ decays and the most recent NA62 measurements becomes pronounced the latter decays may either enable the extraction of the value of $m_\chi$ or provide a lower limit on~$m_\chi$.

title: Phenomenology of Spontaneous CP-violation in 2HDMs
abstract: Spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) provides an attractive possibility for explaining the origin of CP violation and the observed CP-violating phenomena in the quark sector. We investigate SCPV in the two-Higgs-doublet model as one of its simplest realizations, in which the additional Higgs bosons are necessarily non-decoupling and flavor misalignment in the Yukawa sector is required. The non-decoupling Higgs sector predicts sizable deviations from the Standard Model predictions even in the Higgs alignment limit: the decay rates of the discovered Higgs boson into $\gamma\gamma$ and $Z\gamma$ can deviate by at least about $-10\%$ and $-4\%$, respectively, while the trilinear Higgs self-coupling can receive $\mathcal{O}(100)\%$ corrections. We consider a scenario in which the down-type quark and charged-lepton Yukawa matrices are flavor aligned, while flavor-violating interactions are allowed in the up-type quark sector to reproduce the Kobayashi-Maskawa phase. We explore the viable parameter space by imposing theoretical constraints together with experimental constraints from electroweak precision observables, flavor measurements, electric dipole moments, and LHC data. We find that a sizable flavor-violating top-charm Yukawa coupling remains allowed, giving rise to distinctive LHC signatures, including same-sign top-quark and three-top production as well as scalar cascade decays. We also find that the deviation in the trilinear Higgs self-coupling is correlated with the decay patterns of the additional neutral Higgs bosons, providing a connection between precision Higgs measurements and direct searches for the additional Higgs bosons. Our results demonstrate the importance of combining searches for additional Higgs bosons with precision Higgs measurements, complemented by flavor and electric-dipole-moment experiments, to probe SCPV.

title: Neutrino self-interactions in light of DESI and CMB-SPA
abstract:
We present an updated analysis of non-standard neutrino self-interactions, where the interaction is effectively mediated by a heavy particle, using the latest available data from DESI and the CMB. The considered data include combinations of DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy clustering (FS), BAO distance measurements, Lyman-$\alpha$ 1D power spectra (Ly-$\alpha$), and a combined CMB likelihood (CMB-SPA) using data from Planck, ACT, and SPT. First, we probe two DESI DR1-only datasets, where the effective interaction parameter $G_{m eff}$ is multimodal in the profile likelihood, leading us to analyze two different regimes: moderately interacting (MI$_
u$) and strongly interacting (SI$_
u$) neutrinos. With FS+BAO, the evidence disfavors the SI$_
u$ mode, a trend that becomes slightly stronger with the inclusion of Ly-$\alpha$. However, in the latter dataset, the MI$_
u$ region shows a bimodality in which the intermediate mode is very sharp and peaks around $G_{m eff\,} \simeq 10^{-3} \mathrm{MeV}^{-2}$; interestingly, this mode is not penalized versus the weaker standard-like mode. Furthermore, we test CMB and DESI joint data and show that the SI$_
u$ mode is more disfavored by CMB-SPA than by Planck-only data. In particular, the evidence against this mode becomes the strongest thus far (with odds of 5:100000) in the FS+BAO+CMB-SPA combination.

title: Lorentz-Invariance Violation with neutrinos from gamma-ray bursts using IceCube High-Energy Starting Events 12-year dataset
abstract: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos provide a unique probe of Lorentz-invariance violation (LIV), as small energy-dependent deviations from the speed of light can produce measurable time delays over cosmological distances. We search for LIV-induced correlations between neutrinos and gamma-ray bursts using the public 12-year IceCube High-Energy Starting Event dataset and a catalog of 746 bursts with measured redshifts. We develop a likelihood analysis accounting for neutrino directional and energy uncertainties, a possible intrinsic time offset between neutrino and gamma-ray emission, and the decay of superluminal neutrinos expected within effective field theory. For linear LIV, the data show a mild preference over the background-only hypothesis, with a $p$-value of $3.1\%$, corresponding to a one-sided Gaussian significance of approximately $1.9\sigma$. The best fit corresponds to a LIV scale $\Lambda_{\rm LIV}=5.8\times10^{17}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and is effectively driven by the subluminal component, as superluminal neutrinos are strongly suppressed by LIV-induced decays at the analyzed energies. The preferred LIV scale and the most significant neutrino--gamma-ray burst associations are consistent with previous studies based on different statistical approaches. No evidence for quadratic LIV is found. These results motivate further searches with complementary neutrino datasets, particularly at lower energies, where the superluminal component may become observable.

title: Froggatt-Nielsen mechanism with non-invertible symmetry
abstract: We formulate the Froggatt-Nielsen mechanism in the framework of non-invertible symmetries obtained by $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauging of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ or $U(1)$. While the non-invertible selection rules can constrain the texture-zero structure of fermion mass matrices, they do not by themselves determine the magnitudes of the allowed couplings. Introducing a flavon field allows the fusion rules to fix the leading powers of the small parameter $\varepsilon=\langle S\rangle/\Lambda$, thereby determining both the texture zeros and the orders of magnitude of the nonzero entries up to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ coefficients. We have constructed explicit quark and lepton models and study their predictions for the fermion mass and mixing hierarchies through analytical estimates and numerical analysis. In particular, a benchmark model with nine texture zeros in the quark sector can well accommodate the quark masses and mixing parameters with non-Hermitian Yukawa matrices. Its lepton sector admits a minimal type-I seesaw realization with normal neutrino mass ordering and one massless neutrino. These results provide a common symmetry framework for fermion mass hierarchies and texture zeros.

title: Flavon assisted low scale leptogenesis
abstract: Low-scale leptogenesis scenarios, such as the resonant leptogenesis, typically require a highly degenerate mass spectrum of right-handed neutrinos (RHNs). This requirement can be circumvented by extending the seesaw framework with a scalar singlet $S$ that couples to RHNs via the $S N^{}_I N^{}_J$ terms (with $I \neq J$), which opens up new decay channels $N^{}_I \to N^{}_J S$ and provides additional sources of CP violation, thereby enabling successful leptogenesis at the TeV scale without the need for mass degeneracy. In this work, for the first time, we point out that the flavon fields, which are introduced in many flavor-symmetry neutrino mass models to be responsible for the generation of RHN masses through the acquisition of non-zero vacuum expectation values, serve as ideal candidates for the $S$ field. Taking as an example a flavor-symmetry neutrino mass model that naturally realizes the experimentally allowed TM1 mixing pattern and has the attractive features that only one flavon field plays the role of $S$ and that it couples to only two RHNs, we demonstrate that the observed neutrino masses and mixing angles can be consistently reproduced, while the observed baryon asymmetry can be achieved within a parameter space compatible with current experimental constraints.

title: Detection Forecasting for Blazars at MeV Energies with Fermi-LAT Swift-BAT Cross Match
abstract: Over the past two decades, the lack of an MeV $\gamma$-ray all-sky instrument has left an observational gap in blazar broadband emission. Recently, a new suite of MeV $\gamma$-ray instruments with sensitivity in the $10^{-11}$ to $10^{-12}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ range has been proposed, with the potential to far surpass the capabilities of previous all-sky MeV instruments. In this work, we forecast the capabilities of future MeV $\gamma$-ray instruments including COSI, GRAMS, newASTROGAM, and AMEGO-X to observe blazars. We pair total source count estimates of blazar luminosity functions with SED-modeled flux estimates of 76 blazars selected from a sample of 115 blazars cross-matched between the latest Fermi-LAT and Swift-BAT catalogs. We forecast that an instrument with a sensitivity limit of $10^{-11}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ could detect 61 of the 76 SED-modeled blazars, and expect a total population of a few tens to a few hundreds of Flat-Spectrum Radio Quasars (FSRQs), as well as a few hundred BL Lacs (BLLs). An instrument with a sensitivity limit of $10^{-12}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ could detect all 76 of the SED-modeled blazars, and we expect a total population of a few hundred to one thousand FSRQs and roughly one thousand BLLs. As MeV blazars have been observed to be extremely luminous and MeV $\gamma$-rays are minimally attenuated by the extragalactic background light, we use luminosity functions to estimate that blazars could be detected out to $z\approx6$. Lastly, we demonstrate detectability for blazars that have been proposed as neutrino-emitting candidates, as the MeV regime could provide a window into resolving lepto-hadronic degeneracies.

title: Where are the higher excited $B$ and $B_s$ mesons with coupled-channel effects?
abstract: Inspired by the newly observed $B_{s0}^*(5700)^0$, whose mass agrees well with our previous unquenched prediction for $B_s(1^3P_0)$ [Phys.~Rev.~D \textbf{109}, 116006 (2024)], we study the mass spectra and OZI-allowed two-body strong decays of the higher $3S$-, $2P$-, $2D$-, and $1F$-wave $B$ and $B_s$ mesons in the same unquenched quark model. Our results show that coupled-channel effects significantly lower the masses and modify the relative level spacings. The scalar state $B(2^3P_0)$ is strongly affected: its mass is lowered well below the quenched quark model predictions, and it mainly decays into $B\pi$. Furthermore, the mass ordering of the vector states $B(2^3D_1)$ and $B(3^3S_1)$ is reversed, and the lighter $B(2^3D_1)$ state mainly decays into $B_1(5721)\pi$. To test these results, the $B(2^3P_0)$ and $B(2^3D_1)$ states are worth searching for in the $B\pi$ and $B_1(5721)\pi$ channels, respectively. In addition, some higher excitations are predicted to be relatively narrow and can be searched for in the $B^{(*)}\pi$, $B^{(*)}K$, $B_1(5721)\pi/K$, and $B_2^*(5747)\pi/K$ channels. These predictions provide useful references for future experimental searches and help clarify the role of coupled-channel effects in the heavy-light meson spectrum.

title: Two-loop HTL-resummed thermodynamics for pure $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory
abstract: We compute the two-loop hard-thermal-loop (HTL) resummed thermodynamic potential of pure four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory using regularization by dimensional reduction. Our result is gauge invariant and was renormalized using vacuum energy, gluon mass $m_d$ and quark mass $m_q$ counterterms. The thermal mass parameters are determined self-consistently and numerically from gap equations incorporating the running coupling. Based on these solutions, we numerically calculate the scaled pressure, entropy density, energy density, and trace anomaly and compare them with the results in the static perturbative limit through $\mathcal O(\lambda^2)$. For the first three quantities, next-to-leading-order (NLO) corrections are positive and have discernible effects at small coupling, and reduce the renormalization-scale dependence at relatively large couplings. We assess $m_q$-prescription dependence by comparing these results with those obtained by setting $m_q=0$. We find that it has a substantial impact on $m_d$ and the scalar mass $m_s$ at large couplings, and it reverses the signs of the NLO corrections to the first three quantities and qualitatively alters the trace anomaly.

title: Spin-dependent interactions and fine structure in the negative-parity singly heavy baryons
abstract: In order to meet the high-precision measurement of the current baryon spectroscopy, for the first time, we rigorously analyze the spin-dependent interactions and the fine structure of the negative-parity singly heavy baryons in the relativized quark model, which was previously unfeasible in the three-quark system. This gains access to the exploration of the strong interactions dominated by the non-perturbative QCD, and reveals how the various forms of strong interactions in a baryon compete with each other, affect the evolution of the energy levels, cause the energy level splitting and contribute to the mixing effect responsible for the formation of the fine structures. It is shown that the rigorous calculation can nicely reproduce the data, the averaged deviation between the calculated and experimental energy levels is less than 5 MeV for the negative-parity singly heavy baryons. This confirms the reliability of the calculation and also helps make reasonable assignments for the observed negative-parity baryons. The large amount of data obtained by the rigorous calculations contains a wealth of interaction information and is helpful for both of the theoretical and experimental studies. The key to the rigorous calculation in this work is the proposal of a new method, namely the two-step Gaussian expansion method. This new method not only overcomes the long-standing unresolved problem in the relativized quark model, but also provides an effective approach for the high-precision calculation of other few-body systems such as the compact tetraquarks and pentaquarks, especially for the treatment of spin-orbit interactions and tensor interactions which actually appear ubiquitously in all of quantum many-body systems.

title: Quantum Veto Parton Shower Algorithm in the Conformal Window
abstract: We develop a quantum veto parton shower algorithm for a confining dark sector with gauge symmetry $\mathrm{SU}(3)_D \times \mathrm{U}(1)_D$ operating in the conformal window ($N_C = 3$, $N_F = 12$). The non-Abelian gauge coupling exhibits two-loop running toward an infrared fixed point before decoupling at a finite dark-quark mass threshold, while the dark quarks carry non-degenerate $\mathrm{U}(1)_D$ charges with unitary flavor mixing between the interaction and mass bases. Shower evolution proceeds coherently in the interaction basis, with states prepared and measured in the mass basis. Compared with the classical Markovian shower, the flavor-coherent quantum simulation produces a significantly enhanced zero-emission rate, and a characteristic U-shaped mass-eigenstate spectrum. Furthermore, energy-energy correlators exhibit approximate linearity in the double-logarithmic coordinates over an intermediate angular range, suggesting power-law scaling in that region. This framework demonstrates the capability of quantum algorithms to capture multi-flavor quantum interference in strongly interacting hidden sectors.

title: Pulse Morphology and Spectral Study of LPT J1634+44 Using GMRT
abstract: Long-period radio transients (LPTs) are a recently discovered class of Galactic coherent radio emitters characterized by rotation periods of minutes to hours and highly polarized radio pulses. Their nature remains uncertain, with proposed scenarios invoking isolated or binary systems containing neutron stars (NSs) or white dwarfs (WDs). We investigate the nature of CHIME/ILT J1634+44 through multi-band observations with the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT), examining its pulse morphology, spectral evolution, and timing behavior. The pulses show substantial profile variability, and the subpulse features evolve significantly across observing frequencies. Using our measurements of quasi-periodic microstructures in J1634+44 pulses as well as those of other LPTs available from literature, we show that the scaling relationship between the rotation and microstructure periods is not limited to only neutron stars but extend to white dwarfs as well. The radio spectrum of J1634+44 is highly variable and exhibits a spectral turnover that shifts toward lower frequencies across observing epochs. Interpreting this turnover as free-free absorption, we constrain the physical properties of the intervening absorbing medium. Complementing these emission diagnostics, we also present analysis of pulse arrival times spanning approximately a decade to probe the previously proposed spin-orbit resonance models for this LPT.

title: Is there gluonium in the $\eta^\prime$? The flavour structure of $\eta$ and $\eta^\prime$ mixing in radiative $V\to P\gamma$ and $P\to V\gamma$ decays
abstract: Radiative $V\to P\gamma$ and $P\to V\gamma$ decays are conventionally described using constituent-quark mass differences and phenomenological wavefunction-overlap factors as sources of flavour-symmetry breaking. We investigate whether the overlap factors can instead be understood as the effect of mixing of the $\eta$ and $\eta^\prime$ with an additional pseudoscalar state, described by an $SO(4)$ rotation among four basis states. A global fit to current data yields a significantly better description than the corresponding three-state limit without overlap factors, while preserving the established $\eta$-$\eta^\prime$ and vector-meson mixing angles, and shows that the additional state mixes predominantly with the non-strange component. The conventional overlap-factor description is recovered exactly as the special case in which this mixing is purely non-strange. The non-strange pattern disfavours both a flavour-singlet admixture, as expected from mixing with a pseudoscalar glueball, and the gluonium scenario considered in previous analyses. Radiative decays therefore provide no compelling evidence for gluonium in the $\eta^\prime$, and the overlap factors are better interpreted in terms of a radially excited non-strange state.

title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows
abstract: Compressible multiphase flows involving shocks and material interfaces arise in applications such as bubble collapse and droplet breakup, where strong nonlinear interactions produce complex interface deformation, mixing, and multiscale dynamics. Developing reliable machine learning surrogates for these flows remains challenging due to the simultaneous presence of compressibility, sharp discontinuities, and multiphase effects. In this work, we introduce the first large-scale benchmark specifically designed for shock-driven compressible multiphase flows, comprising 3 TB of high-fidelity 2D and 3D datasets featuring shock-induced bubble collapse and droplet breakup. We evaluate diverse surrogate model families on our benchmarking framework: Neptuna, including convolutional, spectral, transformer-based, and pre-trained PDE foundation models. Beyond standard MSE training, we investigate composite losses that combine MSE with Sobolev, interface-aware, and structure-aware terms, along with adaptive loss balancing using SoftAdapt and GradNorm. Evaluation includes pointwise, spectral, feature-focused, structural, and physics-informed metrics. Results show that no single model performs best across all datasets and metrics, while composite losses significantly improve interface preservation and spectral fidelity. Among adaptive weighting strategies, SoftAdapt provides the most consistent improvements with almost no overhead compared to MSE-only training. The benchmarking repository and the dataset are made available at \url{https://tumaer.github.io/Neptuna/}

title: Ab initio calculations of 229 Th band-to-band internal conversion rate in 229 ThO 2
Spontaneous nuclear fusion
abstract: We present the first experimental investigation of deuteron fusion at thermal energy performed underground. Using deuterated palladium targets, we measured spontaneous proton emission attributed to nuclear fusion reactions between deuterons. Protons with energies around 3 MeV, consistent with the expected signature of the deutron-deutron fusion reaction, were observed in palladium foils. Despite extensive efforts, we found no evidence for the predicted 0 + resonance near the reaction threshold.

title: A general decay form and absolute nuclear stability
abstract: A nucleus is conventionally called stable when no decay has been observed. We replace this phenomenological definition with a criterion based on conservation laws. For this purpose, we formulate a general decay form (GDF) for finite charge-neutral nuclear systems that includes all possible final configurations. A nucleus is absolutely stable if no allowed configuration has lower mass. A global search over all nuclei with measured atomic masses yields 84 absolutely stable nuclei.Besides the criterion of absolute stability, we introduce a dimensionless decay-accessibility entropy SGDF as a coarse-grained measure of the relative accessibility of GDF-allowed decay channels. We rank all naturally occurring isotopes according to their maximum SGDF values, identify their favored decay modes, and estimate the corresponding partial half-lives. We further identify promising candidates for natural alpha and two-neutrino double-beta decays. The resulting framework also provides a nuclear-scale perspective on the far-future evolution of matter, in which nuclear decay drives matter toward combinations of these 84 absolutely stable nuclei before still slower processes of matter evolution. These findings extend the conventional phenomenological stable-radioactive classification to a conservation-law-based framework for nuclear stability and provide a systematic guide for future rare-decay searches.

title: The FU Ori Outburst of PR Ori B
abstract: Abstract We report the discovery of a nearby FU Ori–type outburst (FUor), PR Ori B, in the L1641 cluster of the Orion star-forming region. The high-amplitude variability was first identified in the NEOWISE (3–5 μ m) photometry of the unresolved PR Ori binary system. Long-term, resolved optical photometric monitoring demonstrates that PR Ori B is the driver of a Δ G = 5 mag outburst, while PR Ori A has remained constant over the past 20 yr. The near-IR spectrum of PR Ori B changes from a late K-type spectral type during quiescence to a viscously heated disk during outburst, including deep absorption in 12 CO and H 2 O bands. The optical spectrum also exhibits features that are commonly associated with FUors, including P Cygni profiles in Na i D lines and absorption in the Ca ii infrared triplet. The luminosity of the outburst ( L acc ∼ 30–40 L ⊙ ) is similar to that commonly observed in FUors. The comparison of Spitzer/Infrared Spectrograph and Very Large Telescope/VISIR spectroscopy shows some evidence of silicate crystallization during the outburst. PR Ori B is one of the closest and brightest FUors discovered over the past few years, only one magnitude fainter than the archetype of the class FU Ori. The proximity and brightness will allow for future high angular resolution observations to probe the physics of the inner disk and to evaluate changes in the disk due to the increased luminosity.

title: Resonance-dominated heavy-ion fusion and structures with negative components in the representation d 2 ( E σ ) / d E 2 of the fusion cross section
Precise mass measurement of the La 149 − Ce 149 − Pr 149 isobaric chain
Machine Learning on Heterogeneous, Edge, and Quantum Hardware for Particle Physics (ML-HEQUPP)
abstract: The next generation of particle physics experiments will face a new era of challenges in data acquisition, due to unprecedented data rates and volumes along with extreme environments and operational constraints. Harnessing this data for scientific discovery demands real-time inference and decision-making, intelligent data reduction, and efficient processing architectures beyond current capabilities. Crucial to the success of this experimental paradigm are several emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML), silicon microelectronics, and the advent of quantum algorithms and processing. Their intersection includes areas of research such as low-power and low-latency devices for edge computing, heterogeneous accelerator systems, reconfigurable hardware, novel codesign and synthesis strategies, readout for cryogenic or high-radiation environments, and analog computing. This white paper presents a community-driven vision to identify and prioritize research and development opportunities in hardware-based ML systems and corresponding physics applications, contributing towards a successful transition to the new data frontier of fundamental science.

title: Short-range correlated pair formation and nuclear shell structure
abstract: Short-range correlated (SRC) nucleon pairs, caused by brief, high-momentum interactions between two nucleons, are dominated by neutron-proton pairs with large relative and smaller center-of-mass momenta. However, which nucleons form pairs is not fully understood. Measurements of 40,48Ca and 54Fe showed that intra-shell pairing was much stronger than inter-shell pairing. We measured high- missing-momentum protons knocked out in electron scattering from selected nuclei with a range of shell configurations, A, and N/Z, including 9Be, 10,11B, 12C, 40,48Ca, 54Fe, and 197Au, focusing on the four light nuclei. Unexpectedly, we found that adding one proton to 9Be (to make 10B) increased the number of correlated protons far more than adding one neutron to 10B or adding one proton to 11B, perhaps due to the large spin (J = 3) of 10B or the unusual structure of 9Be. In addition, the increase in pairing probability from 9Be to 12C and from 40Ca to 54Fe was much steeper than the increase from 9Be to 197Au. This shows the importance of low-momentum nuclear structure on the probability of high-momentum nucleon pairing.

title: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
abstract: Abstract Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

title: Quenching of the axial-vector coupling constant g A in β decay: Joint effects from chiral two-body currents and many-body correlations

Neutrino Emission from Gamma-Ray Burst Jet Inside the Cavity within Active Galactic Nucleus Accretion Disks
abstract: Abstract Active galactic nucleus (AGN) accretion disks are promising sites for compact binary mergers. Short gamma-ray burst (SGRB) jets from binary neutron star coalescence can propagate within low-density cavities carved by circumbinary outflows. We investigate the high-energy neutrino emission and detectability of such SGRB jets, adopting three seed-photon components: prompt GRB emission, AGN disk thermal radiation, and external inverse Compton (EIC) scattered photons. Our results show that neutrino emission is dominated by proton–photon (p γ ) interactions, with prompt GRB photons and AGN disk photons serving as the dominant target components. The inclusion of AGN disk photons significantly reshapes the neutrino spectrum, shifting the emission peak to lower energies. This effect becomes more pronounced as the mass of the central supermassive black hole decreases and the burst location approaches the black hole. For a fiducial model with a 10 6 M ⊙ central black hole and the burst at 10 Schwarzschild radii, IceCube and IceCube-Gen2 achieve maximum luminosity distances of ∼180 Mpc and ∼400 Mpc, respectively. Next-generation high-sensitivity neutrino observatories, combined with multimessenger observations, hold promise for identifying such GRBs in AGN environments.

title: Is the large uncertainty of δ C P fundamentally encoded in the neutrino quantum state?
First measurement of flux of the neutron background induced by accelerated neutrinos at the J-PARC facility
Effects of kinematic cuts on $v_0(p_T)$
abstract: We show that the analysis of $v_0(p_T)$ is biased when low-$p_T$ particles are not detected. The low-$p_T$ threshold shifts $v_0(p_T)$ by a constant negative value, which depends on the threshold. We evaluate the shift using hydrodynamic simulations. Correcting for this bias significantly improves agreement between ALICE and ATLAS results for $v_0(p_T)$ in Pb+Pb collisions.

title: Searching for Black Hole Candidates in Quiescence by Using Multiband Observations in Globular Cluster M22 (NGC 6656)
abstract: Abstract We present a multiwavelength investigation of radio sources in the globular cluster M22 (NGC 6656) using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array, Chandra, and Hubble Space Telescope. By crossmatching the radio and X-ray source catalogs, we identify eight radio/X-ray counterparts, of which VLA22 is the most promising stellar-mass black hole (BH) candidate. Its radio and X-ray luminosities are consistent with the established L X − L R correlation for BH low-mass X-ray binaries. The observed X-ray variability supports an accreting nature. One possible optical counterpart ( M 814 ≈ 16.695 ± 0.011 mag) is identified. Based on its inferred stellar parameters, the estimated orbital period of P orb ∼ 16 ± 6 h places the proposed counterpart predominantly in the BH region rather than in the neutron star (NS) region in the L X − P orb plane. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of joint radio, X-ray, and optical observations in identifying quiescent BH candidates in globular clusters.

title: Reactor Antineutrino Detection with JUNO-TAO: Commissioning Performance and First Results
abstract: The Taishan Antineutrino Observatory (TAO) is a satellite experiment of JUNO, designed to measure the reactor antineutrino energy spectrum with high precision at a baseline of 43.2~m from a reactor core using a 2.8-ton spherical liquid-scintillator detector, 1.8~m in diameter, operated at -50 degree and instrumented with 4,024 silicon photomultiplier tiles. The TAO detector installation was completed in 2025, and physics data taking began on 10 February 2026. This paper reports the detector design, calibration strategy, and performance based on commissioning data and the first physics runs. Stable cryogenic operation has been achieved, and about 90\% of the readout channels are retained for physics analysis after channel-quality selections. The detector light yield is measured to be about 4000~photoelectrons/MeV after correction for dark noise and optical crosstalk, using neutron capture on hydrogen in inverse beta decay (IBD) events. The energy resolution is about 2.8\% for \(^{68}\)Ge at the detector center and about 3.7\% for \(^{137}\)Cs at \(R=193\)~mm. This energy-resolution performance is among the best reported for reactor-antineutrino detectors and enables TAO to measure the reactor antineutrino spectrum with high precision. Within the fiducial volume of \(R < 800\)~mm, the vertex reconstruction bias remains within \(\pm 30~\mathrm{mm}\), and the resolution is approximately \(70~\mathrm{mm}\) over most of the fiducial volume. The combined muon-tagging efficiency of the veto system is about 97\%. Using 31.3 days of reactor-on data and 29.4 days of reactor-off data, a significant excess of IBD candidates is observed in the reactor-on sample relative to the reactor-off sample, with candidate rates of 2900$\pm$10 events/day and 419$\pm$4 events/day, respectively. The results demonstrate that TAO has reached a high performance level in reactor antineutrino measurement.

title: Impact of soft versus hard equations of state on hybrid stars
abstract: The nuclear stiffness as a dominant contribution of nuclear symmetry energy is analyzed on the properties of compact stars considering constraints from nuclear physics and astrophysics. A compact star can be a neutron star composed only of nuclear matter or a hybrid star with a quark core. Two typical models (soft and stiff) are considered for the nuclear equation of state, and for the hybrid one, a parameterized first-order phase transition approach, completed with a linear quark matter equation of state, is implemented. We show that the phase transition reduces the tension between GW170817 and NICER observations, and we illustrate the impact of nuclear stiffness for the understanding of the nature of the binary system in GW170817. The implication on nuclear symmetry energy is also discussed. We also confirm our previous findings that the GW170817 waveform is best described as a binary HS with a low-density onset of stiff quark matter. This could also be interpreted as a quarkyonic cross-over.

title: Revisiting the Wess-Zumino-Witten Term in Nuclear and Quark Matter under Magnetic Fields and Rotation
abstract: We study anomalous Wess-Zumino-Witten terms associated with the chiral anomaly in dense QCD matter under magnetic fields and rotation. By introducing electromagnetic, baryon number, and isospin background gauge fields, we write down the topological couplings of neutral mesons for the $N_f=2$ and $N_f=3$ cases. The resulting terms contain characteristic contributions proportional to $\vec{B} \cdot \vec{\nabla} \phi$ and $\vec{\Omega} \cdot \vec{\nabla} \phi$, where $\phi$ denotes $\pi^0$, $\eta$, or $\eta'$. These results are relevant to chiral soliton lattices in dense rotating matter.

title: Isovector Monopole Resonance
abstract: We present a theoretical study of the three isospin channels of the isovector giant monopole resonance (IVGMR) within self-consistent Skyrme Hartree-Fock plus Random-Phase Approximation. A modified charge-exchange monopole operator is introduced to remove the dominant isobaric-analog-state contribution, thereby isolating the genuine radial isovector response. We derive the associated non-energy- and energy-weighted sum rules and establish approximate relations between the charge-exchange and non-charge-exchange strengths. The relative locations of the three IVGMR centroids are interpreted in terms of Coulomb displacement energies, the neutron-proton mass difference, and the finite-nucleus symmetry potential. Calculations for \(^{48}\)Ca, \(^{90}\)Zr, and \(^{208}\)Pb show that the non-charge-exchange centroid is accurately approximated by the average of the two charge-exchange centroids in medium-heavy and heavy nuclei. Using a broad set of Skyrme energy-density functionals, we find that the centroid energies of the three channels display a weak model dependence for a fixed nucleus, whereas the non-charge-exchange monopole polarizability exhibits a clear sensitivity to the density dependence of the symmetry energy. These results clarify the isospin structure of the IVGMR and support its use as a complementary probe of isovector nuclear properties.

title: Systematic Effects of Hydrogen and Helium Atmosphere Mismatch on Radius Inference in PSR J0740+6620–like Synthetic NICER Data
abstract: Abstract Constraints on neutron star radii provide insight into the properties of the cold, dense matter in their interiors. Previous studies using synthetic Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER) pulse waveform data have demonstrated that radius inferences derived therefrom are robust against several classes of modeling systematics. Here we explore the consequences of assuming the wrong atmospheric composition, using synthetic data based on the ∼2.1 M ⊙ pulsar PSR J0740+6620. We find that the assumption of a hydrogen atmosphere when the synthetic data assumed a helium atmosphere, or vice versa, produces little bias in the inferred radius at the spot-to-background ratio of the actual PSR J0740+6620 data. However, when we increase the spot-to-background ratio by a factor of ∼20 while keeping the total number of counts fixed at the observed ∼5.5 × 10 5 , we find that composition mismatch can produce significantly biased radius estimates while remaining hidden inside a fit with statistically acceptable residuals. Even in these cases, the Bayesian evidence consistently identifies the correct atmospheric model. Our findings reinforce the importance of using the Bayesian evidence for model comparison and goodness-of-fit tests.

title: Spectral Evolution and Secular Shift of the Z-source GX 340+0: An Interpretation in the Spreading Layer Paradigm
abstract: Abstract We present a comprehensive spectral and timing study of the bright neutron star low-mass X-ray binary and Z-source, GX 340+0, using broadband X-ray observations with AstroSat in 2020 and 2024, focusing on the evolution of physical parameters along the Z-track and the origin of secular shifts of this track across different epochs. The spectra are consistently described by the same model, comprising blackbody emission from a spreading boundary layer (BL) near the neutron star surface, an accretion disk, and a Comptonizing corona. We observe a significant decrease in the blackbody temperature from ∼1.2 keV on the horizontal branch (HB) to ∼1.0 keV on the normal branch (NB), which likely contributes to the harder spectra on the HB and softer spectra on the NB. At the same time, the blackbody normalization varies substantially from ∼440 to 860, indicating changes in the effective emitting area. Within the spreading layer (SL) framework, this evolution reflects changes in the extent of the radiating layer, while the large absolute normalization values suggest an additional contribution from the BL. We also detect variations in the absorption column density, suggesting structural changes in the inner accretion disk, possibly linked to radiation-driven puffing-up. The Comptonized flux shows a branch-dependent behavior, remaining relatively stable along the HB but decreasing along the NB. We interpret these results within a unified framework where the BL, corona, and inner disk evolve coherently with accretion rate, explaining both the Z-track behavior and its secular shifts.

title: Reaction-constrained composition g -modes in neutron stars with antikaon condensates, hyperons, and Δ ( 1232 ) resonances
abstract: We investigate core composition ${g}_{1}$ modes of cold, nonrotating neutron stars containing antikaon condensates, hyperons, and $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}(1232)$ baryons. To our knowledge, this is the first fully general-relativistic calculation of the continuous-composition core ${g}_{1}$-mode frequency and gravitational-wave damping time for stars with a ${K}^{\ensuremath{-}}$ condensate. Using the BigApple equation of state (EOS), we compute frequencies and damping times in full general relativity (GR) and evaluate frozen-composition tidal overlaps from full-GR eigenfunctions within a leading-order hybrid resonance prescription. A species-resolved Ledoux decomposition, cross-checked through mode-frequency sensitivities, identifies the driving channels. We compare frozen composition with a fast-$K$ limit for $n\ensuremath{\leftrightarrow}p+{K}^{\ensuremath{-}}$ and a strong-equilibrium limit for the $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}$ quartet. Fast-$K$ equilibration retains 36%--44% of the peak local value of ${c}_{s}^{2}\ensuremath{-}{c}_{e}^{2}$. At the physical maxima or EOS-validity end points, the frequencies retain 65.7%--73.4% of their frozen values and the gravitational-wave damping times increase by factors of 14.3--31.9, while the kaon-associated mode remains above the nucleonic band. Strong $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}$ equilibration removes most of the direct $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}$-induced enhancement, returning the $N\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}$ mode toward the nucleonic band, whereas the high-frequency $NY\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}$ branch survives because of the frozen $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}$ gradient. Eigenfunction tracking confirms a continuous ${g}_{1}$ branch, and DD-ME2 reproduces this hierarchy. For circular, equal-mass binary neutron-star inspirals, the frozen-composition phase-shift estimates satisfy $|\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Phi}}}_{{g}_{1}}|\ensuremath{\le}1.410\ifmmode\times\else\texttimes\fi{}{10}^{\ensuremath{-}3}\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{rad}$, a factor of 21 below the 0.03-rad favorable-event benchmark reported for the Einstein Telescope. An exotic species therefore produces a distinct composition mode only if its composition gradient, or a coupled slowly equilibrating gradient, survives over the oscillation period.

title: Measurement of the F 19 ( p , α γ ) O 16 astrophysical factor at threshold energies
abstract: Proton-induced reactions on F 19 can lead to different branches of the CNO cycles, possibly resulting in the synthesis of heavier nuclei. For instance, CNO breakout is considered to be a viable path to the production of calcium in the most metal-poor stars. Present-day observational studies indicate that F 19 is mostly produced in the asymptotic giant branch phase of low- and intermediate-mass stars, and its synthesis and surface abundance are strictly intertwined with the production of heavy elements through slow neutron captures (s-process). Therefore, F 19 can act as a probe of nucleosynthesis scenarios and stars inner structure. In recent years, new experimental data on F 19 destruction reactions have been published, highlighting the occurrence of several resonances at astrophysical energies close to the proton threshold. While direct measurements relied on extrapolation from higher energies, indirect measurements made it possible to cover the astrophysical energies. In this work we will focus on the threshold region, which has been studied by means of the Trojan Horse method (THM) in the framework of the modified R -matrix approach. Thanks to this novel measurement, we could derive the asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) of the − 448 keV subthreshold resonance and the strength of the 11 keV one, which turned out to be significantly lower than previously extrapolated. To evaluate the astrophysical impact, we calculated the astrophysical reaction rates using a modern Monte Carlo approach, constraining them with the ANC and threshold resonance strengths measured via the THM.

title: A Sample of Long-period Binaries with Dormant Compact-object Candidates from LAMOST DR13 MRS and Gaia DR3
abstract: Abstract Identifying dormant compact objects in noninteracting binaries is crucial for constraining the hidden population of stellar remnants. We present a systematic search for long-period compact-object candidates by combining Gaia DR3 astrometry with multiepoch LAMOST DR13 medium-resolution spectroscopy. Starting from sources with elevated RUWE values, we required at least five LAMOST spectroscopic epochs and peak-to-peak radial velocity (RV) variations exceeding 20 km s −1 . After RV extraction, orbital fitting, and subsequent screening, we obtained Bayesian Keplerian orbital solutions for 19 long-period single-lined binary candidates, with periods spanning approximately 30–1500 days. Multiwavelength spectral energy distribution fitting was used to constrain the visible stars and evaluate the expected luminosities of unseen companions under a main-sequence assumption. Two systems are identified as the highest-priority compact-object candidates in our sample, each with a minimum companion mass exceeding 1 M ⊙ . Their spectra and optical-to-infrared photometry show no detectable secondary-light contribution, although such a contribution would be expected if the unseen companions were normal main-sequence stars. These systems therefore represent the strongest compact-object candidates in our sample, although further observations are required to distinguish massive white dwarfs or neutron stars from faint stellar companions or unresolved hierarchical systems. We also identify five intermediate-priority and 12 lower-priority systems for follow-up spectroscopy, ultraviolet imaging, and future astrometric constraints.

title: Tilted geometry of the pion emission source in Au+Au collisions in the beam energy scan at the BNL Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider

title: Regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics and non-perturbative renormalization of the shear viscosity of incompressible fluids
abstract: We propose a regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics that preserves all relevant symmetries. By considering an incompressible fluid, we demonstrate explicitly that the regularized theory is UV finite, and therefore admits a continuum limit. Strikingly, the regularized theory of stochastic fluid dynamics is not only amenable to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory, but also to functional methods in the continuum. We exploit this to perform renormalization group improved perturbative calculations of the renormalization of the shear viscosity of an incompressible fluid in two and three spatial dimensions, and compare our results to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory.

title: Exploring QCD Matter through Energy Correlators of Soft Hadrons
abstract: We propose energy-energy correlators (EECs) of soft hadrons and their azimuthal harmonics as new soft observables to probe the collective flow and correlations beyond flow for large and small systems created in high energy nuclear collisions. We separate the soft EEC into a disconnected contribution determined by the mean energy flow and a connected contribution encoding correlations beyond it. Viscous hydrodynamic simulations demonstrate that the soft EEC of a fluid system is governed by the disconnected contribution, while its elliptic and triangular harmonics respond to the initial geometry and shear viscosity as traditional flow harmonics do. Comparisons between iEBE-VISHNU and PYTHIA for p+p, O+O, and Pb+Pb collisions show that the disconnected contribution dominates at large angles in all systems, whereas connected correlations beyond the mean energy flow grow toward small angles and small systems, most strongly for the harmonics. Soft EECs thus provide a unique window into collective flow and correlations beyond it across collision systems.

Suppression of $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ photon hits in large liquid scintillator detectors via spatiotemporal deep learning
abstract: Liquid scintillator detectors are widely used in neutrino experiments due to their low energy threshold and high energy resolution. Despite the tiny abundance of $^{14}$C in LS, the photons induced by the $\beta$ decay of the $^{14}$C isotope inevitably contaminate the signal, degrading the energy resolution. In this work, we propose three models to tag $^{14}$C photon hits in e$^+$ events with $^{14}$C pile-up, thereby suppressing its impact on the energy resolution at the hit level: a gated spatiotemporal graph neural network and two Transformer-based models with scalar and vector charge encoding. For a simulated test dataset in which each event contains one $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ and one e$^+$ with kinetic energy below 5 MeV, the models achieve $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ recall rates of 25%-48% while maintaining $\mathrm{e}^{+}$ to $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ misidentification below 1%, leading to a large improvement in the resolution of total charge for events where $\mathrm{e}^{+}$ and $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ photon hits strongly overlap in space and time.

title: Automated end-station at the soft X-ray beamline featuring robotic air-to-ultrahigh-vacuum sample transfer, scanning probe spectroscopy, and machine learning analysis
abstract: Driven by the growing integration of artificial intelligence and robotics in experimental science, we redefine the execution of user experiments at synchrotron soft X-ray beamlines by developing a highly automated end-station that can be operated without on-site staff. Installed at beamline BL08U of NanoTerasu, the system comprises four chamber units and two robots that automatically transfer samples from ambient air to an ultrahigh vacuum measurement stage for spectroscopic evaluations, before returning them to their original locations post-measurement. Soft X-ray absorption spectra are automatically acquired once programmed by scanning the micro-focused beam over the designated sample area, followed by automated evaluation using machine learning techniques such as principal-component analysis, multidimensional scaling, t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding, and uniform manifold approximation and projection. The high-throughput data are systematically accumulated in the database for remote user examination. This unstaffed end-station provides efficient beamtime for users and allows beamline scientists/technicians to pursue more human and creative endeavors.

title: Unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry in nucleus-nucleus collisions at CERN SPS energies
abstract: The NA61/SHINE experiment at the CERN SPS reports an unexpectedly large excess in the inclusive production of charged over neutral kaons in 0-10% central Ar+Sc collisions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{{NN}}}=8.8$ and 11.9 GeV. This effect corresponds to an unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry, that cannot be explained by known mechanisms contained in the present theoretical models. The comparison of the NA61/SHINE results to data from other experiments reveals, within sizeable uncertainties, a consistent isospin symmetry-violating excess of charged kaon production in the energy regime $2.6<\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}<200$ GeV. At LHC energies ($0.9<\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}<13$ TeV) the charged-over-neutral kaon ratio appears consistent with unity, but the uncertainties remain sizeable. A similar excess of charged over neutral kaon yields is observed by NA61/SHINE in minimum bias $\pi^-$+C reactions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}=17.3$ and 25.7 GeV, also in disagreement with model predictions. No clear theoretical explanation of these phenomena has been provided so far. An unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry brings potential heavy consequences for our understanding of particle production, and calls for a concentrated experimental and theoretical effort.

title: A New High-Intensity Source for Ultracold Neutrons
abstract: The TRIUMF UltraCold Advanced Neutron (TUCAN) collaboration has completed a new superthermal source for ultracold neutrons (UCNs) at TRIUMF. Neutrons produced in a spallation target are moderated in heavy water and liquid deuterium, and are converted to ultracold neutrons by inelastic scattering inside superfluid $^4$He at around 1.1 K. During commissioning of the completed moderation and conversion system, including the liquid-deuterium moderator, up to $1.47(2)\times 10^7$ UCNs were detected outside the source in the experimental area following a 60 s accumulation period. At the same location, continuous operation produced detector rates of up to $6.75(3)\times 10^7$ UCN/s, and a density of 165.6(1) UCN/cm$^3$ was achieved in a 25.4 L external vessel. These measurements demonstrate high-intensity operation of a spallation-driven He-II UCN source, including extraction and transport to an external experimental area.

title: Two-nucleon scattering amplitudes at light quark masses from lattice QCD
abstract: We present a lattice-QCD determination of nucleon-nucleon scattering amplitudes at pion masses of $M_\pi \approx 200$ MeV and $M_\pi \approx 280$ MeV at a single lattice spacing $a \approx 0.064$ fm on two CLS ensembles. The finite-volume energy spectra are extracted from large Hermitian correlation matrices constructed within the distillation framework using an extensive basis of two-nucleon interpolating operators. To reliably relate the finite-volume spectra to the infinite-volume scattering amplitudes, we employ two recently developed formalisms that explicitly account for the long-range interaction generated by one-pion exchange: the plane-wave quantization condition and the relativistic left-hand-cut formalism. We discuss the quark-mass dependence of the nucleon-nucleon scattering lengths, effective ranges, shape parameters and pole positions. At all pion masses considered, our analysis prefers virtual states in both isospin channels by more than $1\sigma$. Comparing also results from our previous calculation at $M_\pi \approx 710$ MeV, we observe that the inverse scattering lengths and binding momenta approach their physical-point phenomenological values monotonically as the pion mass is varied.

title: Reconstruction of Magnetic Fields with a Physics-Informed Neural Network
abstract: Accurate reconstruction of magnetic fields and their gradients is essential for assessing and controlling systematic effects in precision measurement experiments. We have developed a physics-informed neural network (PINN) method which reconstructs three-dimensional magnetic fields subject to the source-free Maxwell equations, $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{B}=0$ and $\nabla\times\mathbf{B}=\mathbf{0}$. In an extension of our previous work on PINN methods for reconstruction of magnetic fields in inaccessible interior regions via measurements at exterior locations, we now demonstrate the feasibility of applying PINN methods to the extraction of magnetic field gradient terms from discrete measurement points subject to constraints from Maxwell's equations.

title: Proton-Number Fluctuations in $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV with the CEE Fast Simulation
abstract: The Cooling Storage Ring External-target Experiment (CEE) at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou (HIRFL) offers a unique opportunity to map the QCD phase diagram in the high-baryon-density region. In particular, higher-order cumulants ($C_r$) of event-by-event proton number distributions have been proposed as sensitive probes of the nuclear-matter phase structure. In this work, $^{\text{238}}$U+$^{\text{238}}$U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV are generated using the JAM2 model and then processed through the CEE fast simulation with detector responses. Experimental analysis procedures, including centrality determination and particle identification, are also implemented. Proton-number cumulants up to fourth order and their ratios are calculated and compared with the true values. A track-by-track efficiency correction method is tested by introducing reconstruction efficiency within the TPC acceptance. An additional factor is also included to account for acceptance losses caused by the azimuthal gap between the two TPCs. Within the uncertainties of the current data sample, the corrected cumulants and cumulant ratios are consistent with their generator-level values. The event-sample dependence of the cumulant-ratio uncertainties is further investigated to estimate the statistics required for future measurements, revealing a substantial statistical cost associated with the acceptance compensation. These results provide a simulation-based assessment of the analysis feasibility and statistical requirements for proton-number fluctuation measurements at CEE.

title: Improved aluminum film transport properties and enhanced TES response in athermal phonon detectors: implications for quasiparticle dynamics
abstract: Our detectors for Dark Matter and Coherent Elastic Neutrino--Nucleus Scattering (CE$\nu$NS) use photolithographically patterned superconducting athermal phonon sensors that are coupled to kg-scale absorbers of different materials (germanium, silicon, sapphire). Following a particle interaction, athermal phonons from the bulk absorber break Cooper pairs in a superconducting aluminum film that surrounds a tungsten Transition Edge Sensor (TES) in equilibrium through electrothermal feedback. This sensor design is called Quasiparticle-trap-assisted Electro-thermal-feedback Transition-edge-sensor (QET). The QET aluminum film that absorbs the athermal phonons is patterned into fins with lengths limited by the quasiparticle diffusion length in aluminum. Improving the quasiparticle diffusion length in the superconducting aluminum is an area of vigorous research to improve phonon collection efficiency and increase the signal strength for lower-threshold searches. We report significantly improved aluminum films that show systematically larger grain sizes and residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) compared to detectors we have fabricated in the past. The improved RRR and grain sizes were expected to improve the collected signal for a given energy. We report higher signal strength achieved in a detector in comparison to another detector in which all other fabrication parameters were kept identical except for the aluminum film deposition.

title: Impact of neutron captures on the r-process: I. Propagation of statistical model uncertainties
abstract: Background: The r-process is responsible for producing about half of the elements heavier than iron in the Universe, but the underlying nuclear physics is still largely inaccessible to experiments and relies on theoretical calculations. Purpose: We aim to quantify the impact of statistical model uncertainties on the r-process with a large set of neutron-capture rates within the Hauser-Feshbach framework with varied statistical model parameters. Propagating neutron-capture rates to r-process calculations of various astrophysical sites allows us to link abundance features to nuclear uncertainties. Methods: We calculate neutron-capture reactivities using different nuclear level density (NLD) and gamma-ray strength function (GSF) prescriptions. We study their impact on r-process calculations for individual trajectories, mass-integrated ejecta from a neutron-star-merger, and a broad set of 10,000 parametric trajectories with a wide range of electron fractions and entropies. Results: The final abundances are more sensitive to NLDs than to GSFs. Selected NLDs produce pronounced abundance changes between the lanthanides and the third peak. Although the variation is reduced in the mass-integrated total ejecta, a subpeak at A=172-178 and systematic abundance changes at A=180-194 persist. The parametric trajectories show that the NLD sensitivity is greater in the cold r-process regime, where neutron captures continue after photodissociations have become ineffective. Additional conditions with large NLD sensitivities are found at intermediate electron fractions, where small changes in the matter flow can lead to significant differences in the final abundances. Conclusions: Systematic differences in neutron-capture rates between NLD prescriptions affect the final r-process abundances. Therefore, improved experimental constraints and theoretical descriptions of NLDs in these regions are needed.

title: A dry cryogenic platform with picometre stability for nanoscale and quantum technologies
abstract: Mechanically ultrastable environments within maintenance-free dry cryostats are needed for high-precision surface probe microscopy experiments, as well as next-generation quantum technologies. The most demanding applications require picometre-scale precision combined with multi-axis and millimetre-scale scanning range, while offering access to optical, microwave, and radiofrequency control and a vector magnetic field. We demonstrate a versatile platform for such systems based on passive and active vibration control for a commercial dry cryostat. Using a tunable optical microcavity as a sensor, we report vibration levels of 4.2 pm root mean square at 2.3 K over one hour without postselection. We further demonstrate drift-free long-term operation with stability below 8.6 pm RMS over 12 hours. Our system enables continuous and automated operation for next-generation high-throughput applications without the need for liquid helium infrastructure. Requiring only standard machining facilities and commercially available hardware, the design can be readily adapted for cryogenic optical, electrical and magnetic high-precision measurements across quantum science, surface science, and nanotechnology.

title: Equiprobability Anomaly Detector Using Angular Distributions
abstract: We use the angular distribution of top quark pairs ($t\bar{t}$) in the semileptonic final state $b\bar{b}\,\ell\nu q\bar{q}'$ to construct an anomaly detector for non-$t\bar{t}$ events. Wigner $D$ functions expand the distribution with coefficients determined by orthogonal series density estimation. Its equiprobable surfaces bin the events, the non-$t\bar{t}$ concentrate at low $t\bar{t}$ density. The separation is quantified by the Kullback-Leibler divergence, which makes connection to variational autoencoders. The performance is comparable to normalizing flows at parton level, but is limited by jet assignments at reconstruction level.

title: Bayesian inference of moments of inertia for wobbling motion in 135 Pr
Towards Low-Energy Electron High-Resolution Spectroscopy with Transition-Edge Sensors
abstract: We present a study of the energy resolution of transition-edge sensors (TESs) for the detection of electrons in the 100~eV kinetic energy range. The TES is a Ti-Au bilayer with an active area of ($60 \times 60$) $\mu$m$^2$ and a critical temperature of $\sim 80$~mK. The electron source is based on vertically-aligned multiwall carbon nanotubes located inside the cryostat, with electrons generated via field emission. For electrons in the $(92 - 99)$~eV kinetic energy range, we obtain a Gaussian energy resolution for fully-absorbed electrons of ($0.48 \pm 0.04 \pm 0.06$)~eV, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic}. When considering the full-width at half-maximum of the peak \textcolor{black}{of the signal amplitude distribution}, the corresponding resolution is of ($1.4 \pm 0.2 \pm 0.3$)~eV. The former represents an improvement of $(47-60)\%$ with respect to previous results, and is mainly attributed to the reduction in the TES active area. The latter is instead an improvement of over a factor of 21, and is mainly due to the reduction in the emitting area of the electron source, which significantly suppresses electron back-scattering in proximity of the TES. These results represent a major milestone towards high-precision spectroscopy on low-energy electrons, which is a key objective for the PTOLEMY experiment.

title: Self-calibration of the neutrino-argon cross section with solar neutrinos
Results from the GIF++ Long-Term Study of Eco-Friendly Gas Mixtures for RPCs
abstract: Gaseous detectors play a crucial role in high-energy physics experiments, yet their operation often relies on fluorinated gases with a very high Global Warming Potential (GWP). Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) operated in avalanche mode typically use high-performance gas mixtures based on high-GWP F-gases such as C$_2$H$_2$F$_4$ and SF$_6$. As environmental concerns grow and regulations become increasingly stringent, the development of sustainable gas mixtures has become a global priority. Within the RPC ECOGas@GIF++ Collaboration, a long-term R&D program has investigated eco-friendly gas mixtures for RPCs and assessed their performance under irradiation. RPCs operated with an HFO-1234ze/CO$_2$ mixture were exposed to high particle fluxes at CERN GIF++, accumulating $\mathcal{O}(10^2~\mathrm{mC/cm^2})$ over three years. This ageing campaign is now complete, and the detector performances have been systematically evaluated across a broad range of particle rates. This paper presents preliminary final results from the campaign, along with future perspectives.

title: Residual diagnostics for detecting the breakdown of the single power-law approximation in photoelectron yield spectroscopy: application to doped silicon
abstract: Our automated analysis of photoelectron yield spectroscopy (PYS) estimates the threshold Ith and the exponent n of a single power law for every spectrum. When this model fits poorly, however, the analysis cannot tell whether the data or the model is at fault. Here we present residual diagnostics that separate the two causes. The exponent is scanned continuously on a 1/n-power fit with an Akaike information criterion (AIC) based on the mean absolute error (MAE), and the spread of the resulting Akaike weights ($P \times \Delta n$) quantifies the uncertainty of the estimate. The normalized MAE (NMAE) and the RMSE-to-MAE ratio (RMR) assess the data quality, the Durbin-Watson (DW) statistic assesses the model adequacy, and the three checks are reported in parallel. With criteria set from an Au reference, the diagnostics were applied to 60 continuous measurements in air of four HF-treated Si samples. For heavily doped p-type Si, DW fell below its criterion, whereas the means of NMAE and RMR remained within their criteria. Prompted by this flag, we fitted the spectrum with a two-component model with fixed exponents (n = 1 and 2.5); the AIC decreased by 56, DW increased from 0.86 to 1.99, and the two components set in at 4.70 and 5.28 eV. For heavily doped n-type Si, the change during air exposure was consistent with a single component. The diagnostics thus identify the spectra that require a multi-component analysis without assuming an emission mechanism.

title: Optical Characterization Measurements of Commercial Polyvinyltoluene Scintillators for Accurate Geant4 Detector Modeling
abstract: Accurate Monte Carlo simulation of plastic scintillator detectors requires precise wavelength-dependent optical properties. We present measurements of wavelength-dependent refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and bulk absorption length $L_{\mathrm{abs}}(\lambda)$ for six commercial polyvinyltoluene (PVT)-based scintillators (Saint Gobain BC-400, BC-404, BC-408, BC-418, BC-422, and BC-430) at five wavelengths between 372 and 660 nm. Using a precision refraction apparatus and variable-thickness transmission measurements, we characterize material-specific dispersion that deviates substantially from both the manufacturer specification and literature values for pure PVT.
