title: When do quantum views help? Complementary classical-quantum representations in multi-view fusion
abstract: Recent studies have reported promising results from quantum machine learning in drug discovery, healthcare, materials science and cybersecurity. Research includes comparisons with classical machine learning algorithms and the development of sequential hybrid pipelines. We propose that fusion can improve prediction when classical and quantum representations capture complementary predictive relationships. Our classical-quantum multi-view framework preserves the full classical input alongside simulated quantum features. Concatenation and attention combine the views; single-view comparisons, replacement and masking controls assess both views' contributions. Controlled angular-polynomial experiments distinguish targets adequately represented by a single view from those that depend on complementary angular and polynomial relationships. For these mixed targets, fusion improves prediction by combining the relevant feature sets, while matched classical representations recover the same benefit, linking the improvement to their complementary predictive content. Controlled classification tests further show that gains depend on alignment between the chosen representation and the target, and on a suitable fusion rule. Benchmark validation shows improved mean predictive performance over classical baselines on Wine, Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer, three-class Fashion-MNIST and Steel Plates Faults within the evaluated protocols. Classical replacement and masking controls remain competitive, classical baselines lead on Digits and Covertype, and outcomes with missing or corrupted views depend on the available inputs. These findings support evaluating quantum representations for their complementary predictive contribution and matching the representation and fusion strategy to the target relationships.

title: Predictions for the scalar partner of the LHC tetraquark X ( 6600 )
abstract: We consider how the recent CMS measurements of the masses and quantum numbers of X ( 6600 ) , X ( 6900 ) and X ( 7100 ) can help to reveal the internal structure of these apparent c c c ¯ c ¯ tetraquarks. The measured J P C = 2 + + quantum numbers of X ( 6600 ) are consistent with our previous prediction, and imply the inevitable existence of a lighter 0 + + partner X ( 6400 ) which also decays to J / ψ J / ψ . There are strong indications for this scalar partner in the recent CMS data fits, which include a Breit-Wigner peak with mass around 6400 MeV. We provide predictions for the masses and decay properties of the scalar and other partner states, which are key experimental tests to discriminate between quark and diquark models. Dedicated experimental scrutiny of this mass region is therefore required, to establish an S-wave multiplet of c c c ¯ c ¯ states (the first of its kind for tetraquarks), leading to a breakthrough in exotic hadron research and our understanding of heavy quark exotics.

title: Three-nucleon dynamics in dp breakup collisions at 190 MeV/nucleon using the WASA detector at COSY-Jülich
abstract: The differential cross section for the $^{1}\mathrm{H}(d,pp)n$ breakup reaction at deuteron beam energy of 380 MeV has been determined with high statistical precision for 189 angular configurations of outgoing protons in the region of forward laboratory angles. The cross-section data were compared to theoretical predictions based on the state-of-the-art nucleon-nucleon potentials, combined with a three-nucleon force, the Coulomb interaction or carried out in a relativistic approach. In the region of the lowest differential cross section, the discrepancy between the data and the theoretical predictions is observed, also in the case of relativistic calculations.

title: Directional recoil detection for CEvNS measurements with light nuclei at the Spallation Neutron Source
abstract: The coherent elastic scattering of neutrinos on nuclei, also known as CE ν NS , has been studied for several years by the COHERENT program of experiments using neutrinos from stopped-pion decays produced at the Oak Ridge Spallation Neutron Source (SNS). We propose a new approach for CE ν NS measurements at the SNS that aims to complement the COHERENT experiments in two main ways: by reconstructing the distribution of CE ν NS -induced recoils, and by measuring CE ν NS on much lighter target nuclei such as helium, carbon, and fluorine. The proposed detector would employ a gaseous time-projection chamber with a highly segmented charge readout to enable the spatial reconstruction of ∼ 10 – 500 keV ionization tracks created by CE ν NS -induced recoils. This would enable the simultaneous measurement of the CE ν NS recoil energy and scattering angle, thereby allowing event-by-event reconstruction of the neutrino energy. We estimate that a 60 ∶ 40 He: CF 4 gas mixture at atmospheric pressure offers a good trade-off between total target mass and good directionality and could deliver a detection of the angular distribution of CE ν NS , even under pessimistic background conditions. We project the sensitivity of 1 and 10 m 3 -scale detectors in the context of several physics cases, including: the measurement of the Standard Model CE ν NS cross section, reconstruction of the flavor-dependent neutrino fluxes, observing the neutrino-induced Migdal effect, constraints on beyond-Standard-Model neutrino interactions, and probing 10-eV-scale sterile neutrinos.

title: Production cross sections of neutron-rich nuclides near the N = 126 neutron-shell closure from 1000 MeV/u Pb 208 on Be 9
abstract: The production cross sections of neutron-rich nuclides near the N = 126 neutron shell closure have been measured for the elements ranging from tungsten ( Z = 74 ) to gold ( Z = 79 ) in the fragmentation of a 1000 MeV / u Pb 208 beam on a Be 9 target. Several cross sections, namely those for W 196 − 199 , Re 199 − 201 , and Os 202 − 203 , were determined for the first time with this projectile-target combination. The results are compared with the predictions of several nuclear reaction models and semiempirical parametrizations; special attention is devoted to multiple proton-removal channels and the formation of nuclides with neutron number N = 127 .

title: 3 He ( α , γ ) 7 Be γ -ray angular distribution: Measured, and calculated by effective field theory
Letter of Intent for Alpha Knockout from Nuclei in Hard Exclusive Processes with ALERT
abstract: We propose to measure hard exclusive $\alpha$-knockout reactions from the light $\alpha$-conjugate nuclei $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, and $^{20}$Ne using electron scattering. Three reaction channels will be measured for the first time on the same target set: (i) the quasi-elastic knockout $(e, e' \alpha)$ knockout, which establishes a baseline against $\alpha$-clustering model calculations and tests final-state-interaction (FSI) models; (ii) coherent deeply virtual Compton scattering (DVCS) on a bound $\alpha$, which provides a quark-level probe of the bound system through the beam-spin asymmetry; and (iii) coherent vector-meson production ($\phi$ and J/{$\psi$}) on a bound $\alpha$, which probes the gluon distribution of the bound cluster through two-gluon exchange. The central observables are ratios of cross sections and beam-spin asymmetries between the bound $\alpha$ in $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, and $^{20}$ Ne and the free $^4$He ground state. Together these measurements directly address the question of the role of QCD in the structure of light nuclei : do the quark and gluon distributions of an $\alpha$ embedded in a heavier nucleus differ from those of a free 4He, and do those modifications track the increasing $\alpha$-clustering strength along the $\alpha$-conjugate chain? The measurement will use the 12 GeV CEBAF accelerator in Hall B with the CLAS12 spectrometer instrumented with the ALERT low-energy recoil detector and high-pressure gas straw targets. ALERT, which replaced the CLAS12 silicon vertex tracker, was successfully commissioned and operated during Run Group L (RG-L) from April through August 2025. It uniquely provides identification of low-momentum recoiling light ions (p, d, t, $^3$He, and $^4$He) close to the beamline at the high luminosities required by these exclusive channels.

title: Experimental review on global polarization and spin alignment in heavy-ion collisions
abstract: Polarization phenomena in heavy-ion collisions have attracted considerable interest since the first experimental observation of global spin polarization. Over the past few years, particle polarization has emerged as a rapidly growing field, with new measurements that have stimulated intense theoretical efforts to understand the puzzling experimental results. In these proceedings, we review recent experimental progress on hyperon global polarization, local polarization along the beam direction, and vector-meson spin alignment in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, and newly emerging measurements of spin-spin correlations. These measurements provide new insights into the vortical structure of the quark-gluon plasma and the spin dynamics during the system evolution.

title: Four-dimensional QCD equation of state with a critical surface from contours of constant entropy density
abstract: We present a new lattice-QCD-based equation of state in the four-dimensional space of $(T,\mu_B,\mu_Q,\mu_S)$ which features a critical surface. This is obtained by generalizing the expansion of constant entropy density contours across the multiple conserved charges of QCD. Since this expansion permits the presence of a first-order phase transition, this is the first lattice QCD based equation of state in four dimensions with a critical surface. We parametrize the chemical potential space using spherical coordinates $(\mu,\theta,\varphi)$, reducing the problem to a one-dimensional extrapolation in $(T,\mu)$ at fixed angles that, together, span the full 4D space. By integrating the extrapolated entropy density, we reconstruct the pressure, from which we obtain the conserved charge densities, their susceptibilities and the speed of sound. Our results agree quantitatively with other lattice QCD constructions at low chemical potentials in the crossover region, and predict the emergence of a first-order phase transition at higher chemical potentials. We study equation of state properties in detail under heavy-ion collision (HIC) conditions for the strangeness and electric charge densities ($n_S=0,~n_Q=0.4n_B$), where we find the CP location at $(T_c,\mu_{B,c},\mu_{Q,c},\mu_{S,c})=(115\pm7,646\pm72,-12\pm3,117\pm16)$ MeV. In particular, we find a strong non-monotonic dependence of baryon number susceptibilities along the chemical freeze-out line at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} \lesssim 7.7$ GeV. Finally, we outline further applications of the 4D equation of state, including charge-neutral matter relevant to neutron stars and large isospin density relevant to cosmic trajectories in the early Universe.

title: Gallium Anomaly and Solar Neutrinos
abstract: The Gallium Anomaly is the disagreement between the measured capture rate of neutrinos by $^{71}$Ga and the rate theoretically expected from the electron capture decay of $^{71}$Ge. The experimental measurements were performed with intense artificial sources. In the present work we consider the sun as a neutrino source that can be calibrated via the fundamental, standard-model neutrino-electron elastic scattering reaction in terrestrial detectors. The result is found to be not anomalous, with good agreement between the measured value of $66.1\pm3.1$ SNU from SAGE and Gallex/GNO, and the total measured source strengths of solar sources, $67.5^{+1.4}_{-1.1}$ SNU. It may be concluded that neither the $^{71}$Ga charged-current cross section nor gallium experiment extraction and counting efficiencies account for the Gallium Anomaly.

title: Asteroseismic Detection of a Massive Unseen Companion to the δ Scuti Star TIC 160582982
abstract: Abstract We present TIC 160582982, an eccentric δ Scuti binary with a dynamically massive unseen companion. Six coherent high frequency pressure modes used as pulsation clocks yield a phase modulation orbit with P orb = 89.29 ± 0.19 days, e = 0.53 9 − 0.037 + 0.040 , and a 1 sin i / c = 145 . 6 − 3.4 + 3.7 s , corresponding to K 1 = 42 . 2 − 1.8 + 2.2 km s − 1 and f ( M ) = 0.41 6 − 0.028 + 0.032 M ⊙ . An independent frequency-modulation analysis of the two strongest modes gives a consistent orbital solution. Rotating MIST isochrones constrained by the atmospheric parameters and spectral energy distribution (SED) give M 1 = 1.93 ± 0.19 M ⊙ and R 1 = 2.65 ± 0.23 R ⊙ . The mass function implies a formal edge-on minimum companion mass of approximately 1.80 M ⊙ . Assuming a luminous main-sequence companion and including the noneclipsing geometry gives M 2 = 2.1 9 − 0.34 + 1.24 M ⊙ and i = 61 . 5 − 19.6 + 16.6 deg . However, no clear evidence for the presence of a luminous counterpart is found, either photometrically or spectroscopically. This suggests the presence of a massive compact object, such as a neutron star or even a stellar-mass black hole, as the massive unseen binary companion. Future phase resolved high resolution spectroscopy will be crucial for obtaining an independent orbital constraint and clarifying the nature of the companion.

title: Rapidity-even dipolar flow in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
abstract: Rapidity-even directed flow, $v_{1}^{\rm even}$, provides a sensitive probe of fluctuation-driven dipolar asymmetry in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but its extraction is complicated by strong first-harmonic non-flow correlations, particularly those associated with global momentum conservation (GMC). In this study, $v_{1}^{\rm even}$ and its multi-particle correlations are investigated in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$\~GeV using the AMPT and HIJING models. An $\eta$-dependent weighting procedure is applied to suppress the leading GMC contribution. The GMC-suppressed HIJING results are strongly reduced for most $v_1$-related observables, while AMPT reproduces the characteristic sign-changing $p_T$ dependence of $v_{1}^{\rm even}$ and exhibits clear sensitivity to the partonic transport setting. The non-normalized mixed-harmonic correlations show a stronger transport dependence, whereas the normalized observables are substantially less sensitive to the absolute final-state response. Comparison with the initial-state eccentricity correlations shows that these normalized observables retain the underlying dipolar, elliptic, and triangular correlation structure after modification by the medium. These results demonstrate that GMC-suppressed rapidity-even dipolar flow correlations provide complementary constraints on initial-state fluctuations and their transformation during the final-state evolution.

title: The Carbon-dependent Binary Frequency of CEMP-no Stars
abstract: Abstract Studies of the oldest and most metal-poor stars in the Milky Way confirm a common chemical signature of high carbon abundances and subsolar neutron-capture enrichment. The so-called carbon-enhanced metal-poor (CEMP)-no stars are speculated to be bona fide population II stars, potentially tracing the nucleosynthesis of the first stars in the Universe. However, constraining the binary nature of CEMP-no stars is crucial for understanding their origins. The binary fraction of CEMP-no stars has tentatively been found to vary with carbon enhancement, independent of metallicity. Here we present the results of radial-velocity monitoring of 30 CEMP-no stars over 5 yr, increasing the total number of CEMP-no stars with a constrained binary status by ∼30% in order to better investigate the CEMP-no binary fraction as a function of carbon. Combining our results with literature data, we find an overall binary frequency of 5 0 − 13 + 13 % among high-carbon ( A (C)≥7.3) CEMP-no stars, compared to 1 8 − 4 + 5 % for low-carbon ( A (C) < 7.3) stars, establishing a statistically significant increase in the CEMP-no binary frequency as a function of carbon for the first time. Our results indicate no correlation between metallicity and binary frequency. Additionally, we derive orbital parameters for three new CEMP-no stars in binary systems and estimate secondary masses for these stars as well as seven binaries from the literature. We discuss these mass estimates in the context of investigating the nature of the unseen companions and the plausibility of a mass-transfer formation channel for high-carbon CEMP-no stars.

title: Generation of mode-locked EUV and soft X-ray radiation via coherent Thomson scattering from a density-modulated electron bunch
abstract: Mode-locked laser frequency combs underpin precision measurements and ultrafast science. However, their applications in short wavelengths are limited by gain bandwidth and wavelength coverage. In this work, a compact scheme for generating coherent radiation in the EUV and soft X-ray range with a comb-like spectrum based on the head-on collision between a density-modulated relativistic-electron beam and an intense long-wavelength Gaussian laser is proposed. A theoretical analysis of the spectral structure is developed and validated by numerical simulations. Our simulations numerically reproduce the spectral positions, spacings, and number of comb lines, showing that frequency combs can be realized without conventional optical cavities or electron-beam delay lines. The distribution of periodically microbunched electron slices leads to the formation of ultrashort pulse trains with stable temporal spacing. These results demonstrate a viable route toward coherent EUV and soft X-ray frequency-comb sources, thereby providing new opportunities for compact and tunable platforms in ultrafast science and precision spectroscopy.

title: First observation of dispersive shock waves in an electron beam
Environment-induced phase modulation of threshold resonances in low-energy H 2 + H 2 nuclear reactions
abstract: Low-energy $\mathrm{D}+\mathrm{D}$ reactions in condensed-matter environments (where $\mathrm{D}$ denotes $^{2}\mathrm{H}$) exhibit several reported features, including suppression of the neutron channel, enhanced angular anisotropy, plateaulike relative-yield behavior, and nonmonotonic time evolution of the enhancement factor. These features are not always reproduced by conventional descriptions based solely on a static electron-screening potential. In this work, a phase-sensitive, observable-level framework is developed in which the reaction response arises from the coherent superposition of a slowly varying background amplitude and a possible narrow near-threshold ${0}^{+}$ contribution. Within this framework, local environment-dependent variations of the relative interference phase are represented phenomenologically by a distribution of effective resonance conditions. The measured response is consequently described as an ensemble average over locally different interference patterns, without requiring the intrinsic nuclear pole to acquire a material-dependent displacement or width. For the reported Pd and PdD relative yields, a core phase-sensitive model combining electron screening with a distributed coherent near-threshold contribution gives ${\ensuremath{\chi}}^{2}=13.26$ for 13 degrees of freedom, compared with ${\ensuremath{\chi}}^{2}=43.10$ for 20 degrees of freedom for the strict screening-only description. Among the tested static parametrizations, the core model provides the best overall balance between fit quality and model complexity. More flexible extensions containing explicit effective-condition and barrier modifications reduce the raw ${\ensuremath{\chi}}^{2}$ only modestly, are strongly penalized by the information criteria, and drive several nuisance parameters to their imposed bounds. A joint profile of the core model gives the conditional central effective resonance condition ${E}_{R,0}=1.{11}_{\ensuremath{-}0.62}^{+0.39}$ keV above the $\mathrm{D}+\mathrm{D}$ threshold in the center-of-mass system. This result is conditional on the adopted $\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Gamma}}=5\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}\mathrm{eV}$ amplitude-level width scale and the imposed bound ${a}_{\mathrm{res}}\ensuremath{\le}200$. It should not be interpreted as a model-independent determination of a bare $^{4}\mathrm{He}$ pole energy or as evidence for an additional narrow nuclear level. The reported time-dependent enhancement is summarized by an empirical rise-and-decay parametrization, with a relatively rapid buildup followed by a slower relaxation. This nonmonotonic behavior is compatible with an evolving target environment, but the limited time-series data do not identify a unique microscopic mechanism or independently establish an environment-induced nuclear phase shift. The results show that a distributed coherent contribution provides a viable phenomenological extension of the conventional static-screening description for the observables examined. They do not establish the existence of an additional narrow ${0}^{+}$ level and do not exclude explanations based on the known multilevel structure of $^{4}\mathrm{He}$, target evolution, or other nonequilibrium effects.

title: Zero of the proton electric form factor in the finite value of the spacelike momentum transfer squared
abstract: The behavior of the polarization data on $\mu_p(G^p_E(t)/G^p_M(t))$ ratio, at the present day available up to $t=-8.5$ GeV$^2$, obtained in the Jefferson Lab experiments carried out by the Akhiezer-Rekalo polarization method, demonstrates a decreasing tendency, which indicates the possible existence of a zero of the proton electric form factor $G^p_E(t)$ in the finite spacelike momentum transfer squared value. However, recently appeared two papers, investigating these data, one of them also included all other existing data on the nucleon electromagnetic structure in the spacelike and timelike regions, where the existence of such zero was questioned. Nevertheless, the reinvestigations we provide in this paper by means of the Unitary and Analytic model of the nucleon electromagnetic form factors give arguments for the possible existence of such a zero.

title: The Sill distribution for all partial waves
abstract: In high-energy physics, short-lived resonances appearing in scattering processes are described by energy-dependent spectral functions. The relativistic Breit--Wigner distribution (rBW), obtained as a relativistic extension of the standard Breit--Wigner form, is commonly employed owing to its simplicity. However, when the lower-energy threshold lies sufficiently close to the resonance peak, sizable deviations from the rBW line shape are expected. The Sill distribution provides a simple way to incorporate the physical threshold while preserving exact normalization, but in its original formulation it is inherently restricted to $s$-wave decays. Here, we extend the Sill distribution to arbitrary partial waves. The correct $\ell$-wave threshold behaviour is implemented while exact normalization is retained through a simple modification of the mass term of the propagator. As a benchmark, the $p$-wave Sill provides a very good description of the $\Delta(1232)^{++}$ line shape up to 1.35 GeV and simultaneously reproduces its on-shell mass and width and its complex pole position, in agreement with independent determinations compiled by the PDG.

title: Representation dependence of the neutron-proton kinetic energy in adiabatic deuteron stripping
abstract: Deuteron stripping reactions such as (d,p) are a main tool for studying the single-particle structure of nuclei, and they are usually analyzed with the adiabatic distorted-wave approximation (ADWA). With nonlocal nucleon optical potentials, ADWA cross sections change by tens of percent, up to a factor of two, depending on which realistic neutron-proton interaction describes the deuteron. Continuum-discretized calculations change much less, and exact Faddeev calculations reduce the spread by about a factor of ten. Should this sensitivity be read as a probe of neutron-proton physics at short distances? One identified route for it in ADWA is a single number, the neutron-proton kinetic energy averaged over the region where the two nucleons interact. I change the AV18 interaction only at short distances, keeping neutron-proton scattering, the deuteron binding energy, and the long-range tail of the deuteron unchanged. This number then rises from 218 to 314 MeV, more than half of its spread among five realistic interactions, while the coefficient that sets the low-momentum shape of the form factor moves by only one percent of its realistic range. The number therefore reflects how the interaction is written, not anything measured. It enters ADWA through two features that the other calculations treat differently: ADWA weights the deuteron where the two nucleons are close, and it assigns the deuteron energy to the pair however fast the two nucleons move. For this short-range change, an average that keeps the full Gaussian shape of the nonlocal potential, instead of expanding it to lowest order, rises by only 6 MeV against 96 MeV.

title: Radiative corrections to the parity-violating spin asymmetry
abstract: The parity-violating spin asymmetry Apv for elastic electron scattering from spin-zero nuclei, together with its QED corrections, is evaluated non-perturbatively within the phase-shift analysis. Dispersion corrections, taking into account low-lying transient nuclear excitations, are estimated with the help of the lowest-order $\gamma Z$ box diagrams. Collision energies between 5 $-$ 500 MeV are considered, and results are provided for the $^{12}$C and $^{208}$Pb target nuclei. In addition, we have evaluated Apv at GeV energies and small scattering angles -- relevant for the Pb Radius Experiment (PREx) -- revealing that the low-lying nuclear excited states give no measurable dispersive contribution. However, they are important at lower energies and backward angles.

title: Localized states of the non-Hermitian Schr{\"o}dinger equation with a complex $1/r^{2}$ potential: from Efimov states to bipolarons
abstract: We study the non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger equation with a complex $1/r^{2}$ potential, which bridges Hermitian few-body and non-Hermitian many-body physics: a real attractive potential describes Efimov bound states, whereas a purely imaginary one describes the medium-induced interaction between two heavy polarons at large separations. We solve this equation analytically, obtaining both the localized and continuum states, and compare the solutions with numerical and WKB results. As the imaginary part of the potential is increased, the energies of the Efimov bound states acquire imaginary parts and rotate counterclockwise in the complex plane. On approaching the purely imaginary potential, the excited states disappear sequentially, while the Efimov ground state is smoothly connected to a bipolaron state localized at short distance. Such a bipolaron is localized solely by the medium-induced imaginary interaction, without any attractive real potential. Solving the equation by finite differences, we find that each bipolaron state is necessarily accompanied by another localized state that oscillates on the scale of the mesh size and hence has no counterpart in the continuum limit. Each such pair coalesces at an exceptional point as the strength of the purely imaginary potential is varied, whereas the coalescence is lifted once a finite real part is introduced. We show that this behavior originates from a symmetry of the discretized Schr\"odinger equation that holds for any purely imaginary potential.

title: Effective shear viscosity from the friction term in relativistic multi-fluid hydrodynamics
abstract: Within a three-fluid description of heavy-ion collisions, we investigate how nuclear friction can be used to model shear stress. In this multi-fluid approach, the individual fluids (projectile, target and fireball) are each treated as locally equilibrated ideal fluids at all times, while the local energy-momentum tensor of the superposed system exhibits characteristic anisotropies in its Landau rest frame. From the corresponding non-vanishing shear stress densities and the gradients of the Landau velocity field, we infer an ``effective shear viscosity'' according to the Navier-Stokes relation. We present the time evolution of the resulting values of $\eta_{\rm eff}$ and the generated entropy density in nuclear collisions at different beam energies ($1.23\,A\text{GeV} \le E_{\mathrm{lab}} \le 29.7\,A\text{GeV}$). The resulting dimensionless ratio $\eta_{\rm eff}/s$ is determined dynamically and self-consistently within the non-equilibrium friction model. We discuss the relation to previous calculations using alternative methods in hydrodynamics and to estimates based on microscopic transport models.

title: Improved fusion yields at the National Ignition Facility via ramped-profile capsule doping
Hyperon--nucleon interactions at BESIII
abstract: Hyperon--nucleon interactions provide essential information on the strange sector of baryon--baryon forces, with implications for hypernuclei, dense baryonic matter, and non-perturbative QCD. Direct experimental information, however, remains scarce because hyperons are short lived and intense conventional hyperon beams are difficult to produce. At BESIII, hyperons and antihyperons produced in charmonium decays can instead be used as incident particles, while the detector material serves as an effective fixed target. This approach has enabled a new program of hyperon--nucleon studies at an $e^+e^-$ collider. Representative results include the first study of $\Xi^{0}n\to\Xi^-p$ using $\Xi^0$--nucleus scattering, measurements of elastic $\Lambda p\to\Lambda p$ and $\bar{\Lambda}p\to\bar{\Lambda}p$ scattering, and recent observations of $\bar{\Lambda}p$ annihilation into multi-meson final states. These measurements demonstrate that BESIII can operate as an effective hyperon--nucleon scattering facility and provide new experimental constraints on the poorly explored strange sector of baryon--baryon interactions.

title: Identification of ultra-high-energy neutrinos in vertical air showers with surface detectors
abstract: We investigate the potential of surface detector arrays to identify ultra-high-energy neutrinos using vertical air showers with zenith angle $\theta \leq 60^\circ$, a region largely unexplored in current searches. The method exploits the enhanced electromagnetic component at ground level arising from energetic leptons produced in neutrino interactions. Using detailed air-shower and detector simulations, we show that observables sensitive to the electromagnetic and muonic content provide genuine discrimination between neutrino-induced and hadron-induced showers. This is demonstrated both with idealized shower quantities and with realistic detector-level signals based on water-Cherenkov and scintillator detectors. The corresponding neutrino identification efficiency is used to derive the effective mass and, primarily, the effective area of the array under background-rejection requirements appropriate to targeted multi-messenger searches. Although not competitive with inclined-shower searches under the stringent background rejection factors required for diffuse-flux analyses, this approach establishes the feasibility of a vertical detection channel, extending the field of view of surface arrays and providing a complementary tool for multi-messenger observations of transient sources.

title: Soft H-L back transitions induced by RMP coils in high q 95 plasmas on EAST
abstract: Abstract Soft H-mode to L-mode (H-L) back transitions, combined with simultaneous particle and heat pumping via n = 2 resonant magnetic perturbations (RMPs), have been achieved in EAST plasmas at low safety factor ( q 95 = 3.5 − 4.0 ) without reducing auxiliary heating power (Shao et al 2024 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 66 035018). For the termination control of ITER, which is also equipped with RMP coils, this process inevitably drives the plasma toward a high q 95 , where the established n = 2 RMP is unlikely to produce a soft H-L back transition, because the edge-resonant surface at such high q 95 requires a high poloidal mode number m , and the n = 2 RMP field is strongly attenuated at such high m and couples only weakly to the edge. However, an n = 1 RMP can restore edge coupling, enabling reliable particle and heat pump-out without radiative collapse or current-profile magnetohydrodynamics risks on EAST. Within an operating window constrained by impurity and neutral beam injection conditions, both the n = 1 and n = 2 RMPs exhibit a reproducible energy confinement time threshold at the H-L transition τ e H-L ∼ 49 ms, which can serve as a control trigger.

title: Nuclear PDFs
abstract: We summarize the current status of global analyses of model-independent nuclear parton distri- bution functions (nPDFs). A carefully conducted global analysis of nPDFs in the era of heavy-ion collisions at the LHC is key to gaining access to new information through the data measured by the collider experiments. This implies incorporating as large and diverse a dataset as possible, as well as the latest theoretical calculations, in order to capture a faithful representation of nuclear structure that reflects the current state of knowledge. On the other hand, the uncertainties in par- ticular must reflect what is not known. For many observables, nuclear uncertainties represent the most significant source of error in current theoretical models; nevertheless, they should not, where possible, be artificially constrained (for example, through parameterization bias). The quality of a global (n)PDF fit is often measured by the $\chi^2$ per degree of freedom, which is approximately one for a fit that describes the data precisely without overfitting. Many additional aspects allow to characterize a good fit, e.g. the $\chi^2$ distribution per experiment, the shape of the uncertainties, and the sensitivity to different types of data. We inspect various fit quality indicators for fits obtained by different groups. Morever we pay close attention to the $A$-dependence. Traditionally, the A-dependence had a primarily functional role in global nPDF analyses and comparatively less attention has been paid to it when characterizing a fit. However, we have now entered the era of nuclei collisions at the LHC and need to investigate the $A$-dependence properly.

title: Low-Scale See-Saw Mechanism and the Majorana Nature of Heavy Neutrinos
abstract: We investigate the possibility to determine the Majorana nature of the heavy Majorana neutrinos present in the low-scale type I seesaw mechanism of neutrino mass generation in experiments at $e^+ \text{-} e^-$ and $\mu^+ \text{-} \mu^-$ colliders. This is done on the examples of two specific symmetry-protected seesaw scenarios with two right-handed (RH) singlet neutrinos and one seesaw realization with three RH neutrinos. We use the forward-backward symmetry in the angular distribution of the heavy neutral leptons produced in the $e^+ \text{-} e^-$ and $\mu^+ \text{-} \mu^-$ collisions as an indicator of their Majorana nature. Our results indicate that the experiments at FCCee during its first phase of operation have a remarkable potential not only to discover the heavy neutral leptons associated with the type I seesaw mechanism if they have masses smaller than the $Z^0$-boson mass, but also to probe and provide evidence for their Majorana nature.

title: A grid of fast-rotating, chemically-homogeneous, supernova and/or long-GRB progenitors
abstract: The understanding of the mechanism(s) by which massive stars collapse and possibly explode is rapidly maturing. Uncertainties in the structure of the stellar core at the onset of collapse are often dominant in numerical simulations, and a limited number of progenitor grids are available. This is especially true for explosions where rotation and magnetic fields play a significant or primary role. We present a grid of 113 single-star models with initial masses $M_{\rm ZAMS}=30-90\,M_{\odot}$ and initial rigid rotation $\omega_{\rm ZAMS}=0.5-0.99\,\omega_{\rm crit}$ computed at $Z=0.001$ with the open-source stellar evolution code \textsc{MESA}. We adopt a 128-isotope nuclear reaction network capable of following the weak reactions deleptonizing the core during and after silicon core burning. By construction, these models experience rotationally-induced chemically-homogeneous evolution, and reach the onset of collapse ($v_{\rm infall}\lesssim -300\,\mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$) with large and structured amounts of angular momentum, possibly sufficient to form accretion disks on a proto-compact object. Therefore, these progenitor structures provide a homogeneous set of models with updated input physics and improved algorithmic accuracy to understand stellar explosions of (some types of) stripped-envelope supernovae, possibly jetted and/or broad-lined, collapsars or magnetar-powered, and/or long $\gamma$-ray bursts.

title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
abstract: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). After retuning the simulation parameters to precisely match these two definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD, and after carrying out an extrapolation to the continuum limit based on the data at lattice spacings $a \simeq 0.049, 0.057, 0.068$ and $0.079$~fm, and spatial lattice sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm, we obtain $a_\mu^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_\mu^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Our results, which have a relative uncertainty of about $1 \%$, agree well with the corresponding determinations by other lattice groups. After adding to our determination of $a_{\mu}^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso})$ the leading isospin-breaking corrections provided in the WP25, namely $a_{\mu}^{\rm HVP, WP25}({\rm IB}) = 0.1(3.4)\times 10^{-10}$, we obtain for the full HVP the value $a_{\mu}^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$. This result translates into a Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment that is fully consistent with the latest result by the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment and strengthens the tension between lattice QCD and data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.
authors: A. De Santis (Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration)

title: Search for charged long-lived particles at the Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee)
abstract: Long-lived particles (LLPs) have emerged as a compelling signature of physics beyond the standard model, offering unique discovery opportunities at current and future colliders. We present an analysis of charged LLPs leading to signatures with kinked tracks and displaced vertices. Using timing information the search is extended to detector-stable LLPs. We explore the discovery prospects of such particles at the Future Circular Collider~(FCC-ee), a proposed $e^{+}e^{-}$ collider. The clean collision environment of FCC-ee and excellent tracking performance of the IDEA detector enhance the sensitivity to kinked-track signatures, which are considerably more challenging to reconstruct in the high-occupancy environment of hadron colliders. The excellent timing resolution of the timing layer enables us to infer the mass of the detector stable particles. As a benchmark the stau pair production in the gauge mediated supersymmetry breaking (GMSB) within the minimal supersymmetric standard model scenario is considered. In this model the lightest supersymmetric particle is a gravitino and the next-to-lightest supersymmetric particle is the stau, the superpartner of the tau lepton. Discovery sensitivity up to the kinematic limit is obtained for the $ZH$ and $t\bar{t}$ runs of the planned FCC-ee operation. We demonstrate that a potential discovery would allow for a precise $\tilde\tau$ mass measurement.

title: Negative- Σ Σ ¯ angular-parameter puzzle in J / ψ and ψ ( 2 S ) decays
abstract: Experimental measurements of J / ψ and ψ ( 2 S ) decays to octet baryon pairs reveal a negative- Σ Σ ¯ puzzle in the angular distributions, α Σ J / ψ < 0 , whereas the other measured J / ψ octet channels and the corresponding ψ ( 2 S ) channels have positive angular parameters. We show that an SU ( 3 ) F -exact singlet description is strongly disfavored in a χ 2 fit, giving χ 2 ≃ 10 5 . By contrast, a reduced scenario in which a common final-state interaction mixes the S - and D -wave amplitudes gives χ 2 = 4.21 for the 22 isospin-reduced inputs and two nominal degrees of freedom. We find that the negative- Σ Σ ¯ puzzle can be reproduced with direct-production SU ( 3 ) F breaking at the 40% level. This is larger than the conventional quark-mass expectation of about 30%, but numerically smaller than the order-one channel variation suggested by the experimental data. The sizable observable effect is amplified by SU ( 3 ) F -breaking rescattering paths involving S–D mixing. These paths feed the much larger D-wave source into the final SU ( 3 ) F -breaking S-wave amplitude. The largest remaining pull comes from the ψ ( 2 S ) → N N ¯ angular input, motivating a renewed experimental check of ψ ( 2 S ) → n n ¯ .

title: Displacement-noise-free gravitational-wave detector using quantum tomography of photon orbital angular momentum states
abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) induce quantum transitions between photon orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) states with amplitudes $\alpha_{\pm}$. Exploiting this effect, we present a displacement-noise-free detection framework that extracts GW information from the OAM Hilbert space. Parametrized quantum state tomography of the GW-induced OAM sidebands enables a single V-shaped detector to resolve all seven wave parameters: the frequency, propagation direction, two polarization amplitudes, and initial phase of each polarization. Direct detection of the sidebands yields a weak signal of approximately $10^{-15}\,\mathrm{W}$. We therefore introduce a stronger reference state $r |0>_{\mathrm{P}}$, with $r=0.01$, to enhance the detected signal. For an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $\gamma=0.1$, an incident light power of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, a wavelength of $\lambda_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$, and GW amplitudes of $A=10^{-18}$, we estimate sideband transition amplitudes of $|\alpha_{\pm}|\sim10^{-10}$ and signal powers of order $1\,\mathrm{nW}$, scaling as $P_{\mathrm{BS}}\alpha_{\pm}\propto P_{\mathrm{BS}}ANL\gamma/\lambda_{\mathrm{opt}}$. The shot-noise-limited sensitivity floor is $S^{1/2}_n=1.6\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$. Because the scheme measures OAM transition amplitudes rather than differential arm lengths, it is intrinsically free from displacement noise and provides a broadband probe of GWs, specifically bridging the $0.1$--$10\,\mathrm{Hz}$ mid-frequency gap.

title: Revisiting $B_c^{(*)}$ production in $Z$-boson decays at NLO in QCD
abstract: We study $B_c^{(*)}$ production in $Z$-boson decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD within the color-singlet nonrelativistic QCD framework. The analysis covers both the $1S$ and $2S$ pseudoscalar and vector states, extending the phenomenological study to radially excited $B_c$ mesons. We calculate direct production widths and energy-fraction and invariant-mass distributions, including both charm- and bottom-quark production topologies. For the central inputs and $\mu_R=2m_b$, the $K$ factors are $1.52$ for $B_c$ and $1.33$ for $B_c^*$. We examine uncertainties from the renormalization scale, heavy-quark masses, and wave functions at the origin, and apply the principle of maximum conformality to fix the renormalization scale from the $\beta_0$-dependent NLO contribution. The NLO corrections enhance the small- and intermediate-energy-fraction regions and modify the invariant-mass spectra. We discuss these features in relation to heavy-quark fragmentation. The results provide production-rate and kinematic inputs for studies of ground-state and radially excited $B_c$ mesons at high-statistics $Z$ factories.

title: Direct large-area observation of subsurface plastic activity in conditioned copper electrodes
abstract: High-field conditioning is the process by which radio-frequency structures in particle accelerators and other high-gradient devices reach their operating fields, yet the underlying physical mechanism remains an open question. Models and indirect measurements point to subsurface dislocation dynamics, but large-area structural measurements have been missing. We present electron backscatter diffraction measurements spanning millimeter-scale regions on a copper cathode conditioned at pulsed direct-current fields up to $\sim$80~MV/m in a sloped-anode geometry, which imposes a known gradient of field exposure across a single electrode. Across nine regions of interest spanning this exposure range, the mean intragrain misorientation of field-exposed regions exceeds that of unexposed references by $\sim$75\%; the difference is reproduced by three independent misorientation metrics and confirmed by Kolmogorov--Smirnov tests. To our knowledge, this is the first large-area observation of structural differences between conditioned and unconditioned regions of a high-field electrode. The misorientation separates into three tiers (high-field center and edge, low-field periphery, and unexposed reference) that match the spatial profile of the conditioning-state variable $E_S$ predicted by Monte Carlo simulations. These observations point to the evolving subsurface dislocation population as a candidate physical basis of conditioning.

title: Picometre-scale real-time drift correction in TEM and STEM by dynamic control of the specimen stage for atomic-resolution imaging
abstract: In this work, we show how the specimen drift can be actively compensated by controlling the stage with precision down to the picometre scale. We do this by dynamic control, a generic real-time feedback framework designed to actively stabilize electron microscopy experiments by continuously monitoring an experimental variable from the detector data stream and compensating its evolution during acquisition. The framework, applicable to a broad range of controllable experimental instabilities, includes automated calibration procedures, operates in parallel with image acquisition and is implemented as a software plugin without requiring any hardware modification of the microscope. Results for live drift correction are shown for a selection of TEM and STEM instruments using conventional mechanical stages as well as piezoelectric stages. Experimental results are presented for medium resolution TEM, high-resolution TEM, HR-STEM and in situ observations. With piezoelectric stages, specimen stabilization down to the picometre scale was achieved allowing drift-corrected atomic-resolution imaging. Specimen stage-based stabilization significantly improves long-exposure imaging and in situ experiments by increasing the effective exposure time, preserving the field of view, maintaining identical optical conditions and eliminating the need for numerical alignment of large datasets. Beyond the specific application presented here, dynamic control provides a versatile framework for real-time regulation of electron microscopy experiments and opens new perspectives for quantitative imaging, automated in situ studies and multimodal acquisitions.

title: Gravitational synchronization in bosonic dark matter admixed neutron stars
Full Characterization of a Mock Nuclear Waste Barrel with Muon Tomography using Micromegas Detectors
abstract: Muon tomography based on multiple Coulomb scattering provides a non-destructive method to image dense and shielded objects using naturally occurring cosmic-ray muons. In the context of nuclear waste characterization, we present the experimental imaging of a 205-L mock waste barrel using a dedicated 1m$^2$ muon scattering tomography test bench. The system employs multiplexed resistive Micromegas detectors, enabling stable and high-precision muon tracking. Monte Carlo simulations are first used to characterize material-dependent scattering signatures and to quantitatively assess identification performance using statistical reconstruction. These simulation-based results are then used to define objective discrimination thresholds, which are subsequently applied to experimental data for the localization and identification of internal anomalies. Using an Angle Statistics Reconstruction algorithm, we achieve a spatial resolution of 10 mm and demonstrate the three-dimensional imaging of an internal structure containing both low- and high-radiation length materials. Material discrimination performance is evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, yielding high identification efficiency for dense metallic inclusions such as lead and steel (AUC $\geq$ 0.96) within acquisition times of a few days, while cavities also exhibit strong contrast. Experimental results show good agreement with detailed Monte Carlo simulations. By establishing a continuous workflow from simulation-based performance characterization to practical application on measured data, this work provides a quantitatively validated framework for muon scattering tomography applied to complex, shielded objects.

title: Electromagnetic form factors of singly charmed baryons Σ c and Λ c in a covariant quark-diquark model
Effect of mass loss and convective overshooting on the precollapse structure, composition, and neutrino emission of red supergiants
Bounds on hadronic contributions to the anomalous magnetic moment of the $\tau$ lepton from QCD Sum Rules
abstract: A QCD sum-rule study is performed to place bounds on the leading-order (LO) hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the $\tau$ lepton ($a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO},\, a_\tau = (g-2)_\tau/2$). The QCD contributions to $a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$ are modeled as a combination of Laplace QCD sum rules (LSRs) and finite-energy QCD sum rules (FESRs) of various weights, which are bounded by H\"older and related fundamental inequalities. The light-quark ($u,\,d,\,s$) contributions are evaluated up to five-loop order in perturbative contributions in the chiral limit, LO in light quark mass corrections, next-to-leading order (NLO) in dimension-four QCD condensates and to LO in dimension-six QCD condensates. Extending previous work on $a_\mu^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$, we present a robust methodology for using QCD sum rules to constrain $a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$, and more generally any lepton $g-2$. A criterion is developed to extract from the bounds analysis a final result of $a_\tau^\mathrm{QCD} = \left( 3.385\pm 0.048 \right) \times 10^{-6}$, which after inclusion of charmonium and bottomonium contributions gives a final result $a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO} = \left( 3.501\pm0.048\right) \times 10^{-6}$, comparable to data-driven and lattice predictions. Lattice QCD results along with our value for $a_\tau^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO}$ are used to obtain a combined QCD determination from lattice and sum-rule methods of $a_\mu^\mathrm{HVP,\,LO} = (7.217\pm0.233)\times10^{-8}$. Our analysis provides fundamental QCD sum-rule inputs into the theoretical determinations of $a_\tau$, and establishes new methodologies for QCD sum-rule determinations of low-energy observables.

title: Vacuum breakdown: Phenomenological description and hydrodynamical modeling of crater formation
Spin-dependent interactions and fine structure in negative-parity singly heavy baryons
abstract: In order to meet the high-precision measurement of the current baryon spectroscopy, for the first time, we rigorously analyze the spin-dependent interactions and the fine structure of the negative-parity singly heavy baryons in the relativized quark model, which was previously unfeasible in the three-quark system. This gains access to the exploration of the strong interactions dominated by the nonperturbative QCD, and reveals how the various forms of strong interactions in a baryon compete with each other, affect the evolution of the energy levels, cause the energy level splitting, and contribute to the mixing effect responsible for the formation of the fine structures. It is shown that the rigorous calculation can nicely reproduce the data; the averaged deviation between the calculated and experimental energy levels is less than 5 MeV for the negative-parity singly heavy baryons. This confirms the reliability of the calculation and also helps make reasonable assignments for the observed negative-parity baryons. The large amount of data obtained by the rigorous calculations contains a wealth of interaction information and is helpful for both of the theoretical and experimental studies. The key to the rigorous calculation in this work is the proposal of a new method, namely the two-step Gaussian expansion method. This new method not only overcomes the long-standing unresolved problem in the relativized quark model, but also provides an effective approach for the high-precision calculation of other few-body systems such as the compact tetraquarks and pentaquarks, especially for the treatment of spin-orbit interactions and tensor interactions which actually appear ubiquitously in all of quantum many-body systems.

title: Optimal density profiles for phase-locked laser-wakefield acceleration
First beam demonstration of a conduction-cooled Nb 3 Sn superconducting rf photoinjector
Radiative transitions of hybrid mesons
abstract: Radiative transitions of hybrid mesons probe nonperturbative gluodynamics, particularly the interplay between quark spin and gluonic excitations, and are of direct relevance to the search for exotic hadrons at Jefferson Lab. We calculate these transitions across the lowest charmonium-hybrid multiplet in a constituent gluon model based on Coulomb-gauge QCD in the heavy quark expansion. The results for $Y\to\eta_c\gamma$ and $Y\to \chi_{c0}\gamma$ overlap the width obtained in quenched lattice computations, whereas $\eta_{c1}\to J/\psi\gamma$ is substantially below the corresponding lattice estimate.

title: First Observation of the Radiative Decay $D^0 \to \gamma\omega$
abstract: We report the first observation of the radiative charm decay $D^0 \to \gamma \omega$ with a significance of $6.0\sigma$. The analysis uses 20.3\,$\rm{fb}^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at a center-of-mass energy of 3.773\,GeV, and employs a deep learning strategy based on the Particle Transformer architecture. The absolute branching fraction of $\mathcal{B}(D^0\to\gamma\omega)=(2.12\pm 0.40_{\rm stat}\pm 0.25_{\rm syst})\times 10^{-5}$ confirms the dominance of long-distance hadronic dynamics in radiative charm decays and provides a valuable benchmark for testing non-perturbative QCD calculations of $D \to \gamma V$ transitions.

title: Analysis with the Lindblad equation and the instantaneous-pulse approximation: quantum Zeno/anti-Zeno effects in a three-level system
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Pedestal penalty factors for ELM-free regimes in DIII-D and extension to fusion pilot plant design
abstract: Abstract Though the EPED model, which provides a first-principles-based predictive capability for the pedestal height and width in H-mode tokamak plasmas, has been validated extensively in type-I edge-localized mode (ELM) regimes, significant uncertainties remain in predicting the height of the pressure pedestal in fusion pilot plants that must deploy ELM mitigation or suppression techniques. In this work, we compare the EPED1 NN surrogate to measurements from a broad dataset on the DIII-D tokamak, spanning ELMy, Small-ELM, QH-mode, Wide-Pedestal QH-mode, RMP-suppressed, I-mode, EDA H-mode, QCE and ELM-free NT scenarios. Using a robust Bayesian profile-fitting framework, we find that the measured pedestal pressure is systematically reduced relative to the EPED prediction in nearly all regimes, with regime-median pedestal pressures ranging from ∼93% of the predicted value in H-mode like regimes to below 40% in scenarios in which the edge region is governed by other transport mechanisms. We show that this deficit – termed a “pedestal penalty” – is not a fixed per-regime offset and that some scenarios recover toward the EPED prediction at high normalized pressure (β N ) and low pedestal collisionality (ν * e,ped ). While a simple scaling for the pedestal penalty can help illustrate model uncertainties on the DIII-D database, it misses key scenario-specific physics and should not be taken as a substitute for the development of predictive pedestal models for ELM-free FPPs. Uncertainties in FPP performance associated with a reduction of the pedestal height relative to EPED are quantified using the FUSE code, which shows that the achievable fusion power on ITER may be reduced by a factor of two if the pedestal is limited to 60% of the EPED prediction, a value well within the uncertainties observed on DIII-D. Further implications for FPP design are discussed, including the need for regime-dependent pedestal models that do not rely on a degraded EPED variant.

title: Another relation among the neutrino mass-squared differences?
abstract: Determining the absolute neutrino mass scale remains a compelling challenge in particle physics. Establishing precise mathematical connections among the neutrino masses could significantly facilitate this task and shed additional light on the underlying mass-generation mechanism. We highlight the possible existence of a simple algebraic relation between the mass-squared differences, $$\frac{\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{31}}+\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{21}}}{\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{31}}-\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{21}}}=\sqrt{2},$$ which agrees remarkably well with the best-fit values of recent global analyses of neutrino oscillation data. We then investigate the implications of adopting this relation and how it decreases the number of independent parameters in the neutrino sector. We demonstrate that there are alternative representations well known in quark and charged-lepton physics. Furthermore, we place a tight constraint on the solar neutrino mass splitting, $\Delta m^2_{21}=(7.445 \pm 0.062) \times 10^{-5} \text{ eV}^2$, and also obtain $\Delta m^2_{31}=(2.548 \pm 0.041) \times 10^{-3} \text{ eV}^2$. Next-generation reactor and accelerator neutrino experiments are expected to significantly reduce systematic uncertainties. In particular, the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) will measure these parameters independently of each other at the sub-percent level, thereby providing a stringent and direct test of our results.

title: From Axion Detection to Dark Matter Astronomy
abstract: A global haloscope network could turn an axion discovery into astronomy of dark matter substructure and transients. We combine interferometric phase, spatial coherence, and spectroscopy to study the formation and evolution of axion substructure through measurements of flow directions and velocity distributions. For tidal streams, a four-site forecast shows how longitudinal and transverse velocity dispersions can be measured jointly. Interpreted with dynamical and population models, these measurements could test axion production scenarios. Extensions to miniclusters, axion stars, and emitted bursts would broaden the astrophysical reach of laboratory detection.

title: Construction and Performance of the sMDT Precision Muon Tracking Chambers for ATLAS at the HL-LHC
abstract: In order to improve the muon trigger efficiency and the rate capability of the ATLAS muon detectors for operation at the high luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC), the Monitored Drift Tube (MDT) tracking chambers in the inner barrel layer of the ATLAS Muon Spectrometer will be replaced by small-diameter Muon Drift Tube (sMDT) chambers integrated with new thin-gap RPC trigger chambers. The sMDT chambers are in serial production since January 2021. This documentation provides insight into the drift tube production and every step performed in the chamber construction at the MPI Munich. The serial production involves a stringent quality control program to assure the reliability and high mechanical precision of the chambers. This program consists of tests of the individual drift tubes, measurements of the chamber geometry and proof of gas tightness. Final certification at the production site is provided using cosmic rays. The dedicated quality control database and monitoring Web interface that is used commonly for both production sites of the sMDT chambers is presented

title: Stimulated capture of axion dark matter around primordial black holes
abstract: We study the stimulated capture of axion and axion-like particles around primordial black holes, mediated by quartic self-interactions. We identify the parametric regions where Bose-enhanced growth overcomes cosmological dilution and derive analytic criteria for efficient formation and long-term survival of the hydrogenic ground-state cloud, confronting them with current bounds on axion-photon couplings. We discuss observational implications of these PBH+cloud systems, including resonant axion-to-photon conversion in neutron star magnetospheres and finite-size microlensing distortions. In the former case, the resonance condition selects a conversion shell outside the neutron star surface, and we show that the large axion occupation number of the cloud can compensate for the small conversion probability. The resulting transient line flux densities can exceed nominal VLA and ALMA sensitivities in regions where the Galactic encounter rate is observationally relevant. Independently, when the cloud size becomes comparable to or larger than the Einstein radius, finite-size effects can modify the standard point-lens microlensing light curve.

title: Radial Oscillations of Viscous Stars
abstract: Oscillation modes of neutron stars, a key target for third-generation gravitational wave detectors, encode key information about their constituent nuclear matter. In this work, we study the effect of viscosity on oscillations of cold, polytropic, spherically symmetric neutron stars. We focus on purely radial oscillations and work perturbatively to linear order within two hydrodynamic frameworks: the acausal covariant generalization of the Navier-Stokes equations proposed by Eckart, and the causal generalization formulated by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK). We find that viscosity damps the radial modes on millisecond timescales and induces fractional shifts in the oscillation frequency which increase both with the compactness and viscosity of the star, reaching up to the percent level for the fundamental mode with bulk viscosities $\zeta\sim10^{30}\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. For more viscous stars, the oscillation frequency decreases, becoming zero (i.e., an overdamped mode) for $\zeta\gtrsim10^{31}\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. We also study the linear threshold of gravitational collapse. Consistent with recent analytic results in the zero heat conductivity limit, we find that viscosity in Eckart theory cannot stabilize an unstable inviscid star. We provide numerical evidence that viscosity in BDNK theory is similarly unable to prevent gravitational collapse, but it slightly modifies the threshold of collapse. Overall, our results advance our understanding of the impact of viscosity on the oscillation modes of neutron stars, a key component of viscous asteroseismology with next-generation gravitational wave detectors.

title: Numerical simulations of low-mass black hole-neutron star mergers with moderate eccentricities
abstract: A confident detection of orbital eccentricity in gravitational-wave signals from black hole-neutron star systems would be a strong indicator of their dynamical formation origin. While eccentric waveform models have recently been developed, their validity for analyzing black hole--neutron star signals has yet to be tested against numerical-relativity simulations. Building upon our previous study of quasicircular black hole--neutron star mergers, we perform simulations of a subset of these systems with orbital eccentricities around five times larger than those inferred for GW200105_162426. Additionally, we perform simulations with magnetized matter to assess whether trapped $g$-mode oscillations persist in strongly magnetized disks. Regarding the emitted gravitational-wave signal, we find that the effective one-body waveform model SEOBNRv5EHM shows reasonable agreement unless tidal contributions become important, and the inspiral-only post-Newtonian models pyEFPE/pyEFPEHM show larger disagreement in the late inspiral. For the equal-mass system, which has the largest effective tidal deformability, eccentric tidal corrections have a small but noticeable impact on the phase, $\sim0.1$ rad. We find an almost negligible impact of eccentricity on the properties of the remnant black hole, and differences of up to a factor of two in the remnant disk mass. Trapped $g$ modes in the accretion disks have the same frequency regardless of the eccentricity, confirming that they depend mainly on the properties of the remnant black hole. We find that when accretion disks are strongly magnetized, they become less dense and have less pronounced structure, and that the trapped $g$ modes previously identified in the unmagnetized cases are efficiently damped.

title: Mock Catalogs of Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves via a Halo Model Approach with Space-borne Detectors
abstract: Future space-borne gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as LISA and DECIGO, are expected to detect a large number of GW events, a fraction of which may be strongly lensed by intervening galaxies or galaxy clusters. In this work, we develop a comprehensive framework to simulate strongly lensed GWs in the context of space-borne detectors. Based on realistic astrophysical models for both the source population and the lens distribution, we construct mock catalogs of lensed GW events, referred to as \textbf{GW-LMC-Space}. Our results show that, for a four-year LISA observation, the expected number of lensed events ranges from $0$ to $131$, depending on the adopted formation model of massive black hole binaries (MBHBs). The corresponding lensing probability for MBHBs can reach up to $\sim 0.3\%$. For DECIGO, we find that the number of lensed events in a one-year observation is expected to lie in the range of $0$--$44$, with a lensing probability of $\sim 0.15\%$ for stellar-mass binary black holes (BBHs), binary neutron stars (BNSs), and neutron star--black hole binaries (NSBHs). We further show that the overlap of lensed signals is a common feature in space-borne detectors, which can significantly affect both the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) estimation and event identification. These results highlight the importance of accounting for signal overlap in the analysis of strongly lensed GW events in future space-borne GW observations.

title: Jittering jets in stripped-envelope core-collapse supernovae
abstract: We compare the expected explosion time of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) in the jittering jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) to that in the neutrino-driven (the delayed neutrino) mechanism, and conclude that for most, but not all, stellar models, even when the neutrino-driven mechanism might have led to an explosion, the JJEM starts to operate before the neutrino mechanism fully revives the stalled shock. To achieve this goal, we conduct comprehensive one-dimensional stellar evolution simulations using the code \textsc{mesa} to determine the expected explosion time according to the JJEM, which corresponds to the time when the inner convective layer of the core is accreted onto the newly born neutron star (NS). We present results for many hydrogen-rich, hydrogen-stripped, and helium+hydrogen-stripped envelope CCSN progenitor models. We find that most, but not all, of our models in the initial mass range of $M_{\rm ZAMS}=12M_\odot$ to $M_{\rm ZAMS}=40M_\odot$, have at least one strong convective zone inside the mass coordinate that is the maximum baryonic mass of an NS, $m \simeq 2.65\ M_\odot$, which can facilitate the JJEM. This study contributes to establishing the JJEM as a viable explosion mechanism of CCSNe.

title: From Non-Thermal to Thermal: Cosmological Imprints of Self-Interacting Secluded Dark Matter
abstract: Dark matter (DM), secluded from the Standard Model (SM), can attain internal thermalization through self-interactions. We investigate the thermalization of a real scalar DM field with a quartic self-coupling, initially produced from the perturbative decay of the coherently oscillating inflaton field during reheating. The thermalization process has been studied numerically by solving Boltzmann equation of the DM momentum distribution function in presence of $2\rightarrow2$ DM elastic self-scatterings. In the absence of number-changing processes, the thermalized dark sector is characterized by a temperature and a nonzero chemical potential, determined by the inflaton mass and the reheat temperature. We find that if the inflaton mass is greater (smaller) than the reheat temperature, the DM temperature can be greater (smaller) than the SM temperature during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis, without violating any cosmological constraints. This is realized with a negative (positive) chemical potential for the DM temperature greater (smaller) than the SM one. Depending on DM production history, we can achieve the lower limit on the DM mass much below than in warm DM scenarios. The thermalization via self-scatterings tends to suppress the DM co-moving free-streaming length, compared to the non-thermal scenario without any collisions. Consequently, the lower limit on the DM mass weakens approximately by $40\%$ for a suitable choice of quartic self-coupling than in the non-thermal scenario. We obtain the lower limits on the thermal DM mass to be $2.2\times10^{-10}$ GeV and $0.47$ GeV for reheat temperatures, $5\times 10^6$ GeV and $5$ MeV respectively, while the inflaton mass is set at $10^3$ GeV.

title: Coherent states of neutrinos in rotating matter
abstract: We study coherent states of neutrinos electroweakly interacting with rotating matter. We start with the Dirac equation for a massive neutrino propagating in background matter with a coordinate dependent effective potential. Then, we consider the limit of massless particles and the specific matter velocity profile. It allows us to reduce the neutrino Hamiltonian to the harmonic oscillator form. We find the exact solutions of the Dirac equation and construct the creation and annihilation operators. Using these results, we build the generalized coherent states of neutrinos. We provide the interpretation of these coherent states in terms of the classical physics. In particular, we demonstrate that the coherent states constructed approach plane waves in the limit of slow matter rotation. We also define the effective neutrino mass owing to the interaction of a massless neutrino with rotating matter. Then, we consider a special case of the generalized coherent states which are called the neutrino coherent states. The situation of the degenerate parameters of the system is also studied. Finally, we apply our results for astrophysical neutrinos propagating in dense matter of a rapidly rotating neutron star (NS). We calculate the effective neutrino masses for different neutrino energies for realistic parameters of NS.

title: All three-loop four-point massless integrals with one off-shell leg
abstract: We present the complete set of massless three-loop four-point master integrals with one off-shell external leg. These are essential building blocks for the three-loop virtual corrections to Higgs-boson or vector-boson production in association with a jet at the Large Hadron Collider, required for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD predictions. We construct a complete basis of canonical integrals by identifying integrands with simple poles and unit leading singularities, solely by integrand analysis. This includes an integral family with 371 master integrals and a 19-dimensional top sector. The solutions for all relevant integrals are provided as a map to a minimal set of iterated integrals graded according to their analytic properties, together with high-precision series expansions.

title: Origin of the magnetic ground state of Tb 2 Ir 2 O 7
abstract: Magnetic-rare-earth pyrochlore iridates exhibit a rich variety of unconventional phases, driven by the complex interactions within and between the rare-earth and the iridium sublattices. In this study, we investigate the peculiar magnetic state of Tb 2 Ir 2 O 7 , where a component of the Tb 3 + moment orders perpendicular to its local Ising anisotropy axis. By means of neutron diffraction and inelastic neutron scattering down to dilution temperatures, complemented by specific heat measurements, we show that this intriguing magnetic state is fully established at 1.5 K and we characterize its excitation spectrum across a broad range of energies. Our calculations reveal that bilinear interactions between Tb 3 + ions subjected to the Ir molecular field capture several key features of the experiments, but need to be supplemented to fully reproduce the observed behavior.

title: From local chemistry to galactic evolution: unlocking the power of interstellar isotopes with ALMA2040
abstract: Molecular isotopic ratios provide a unique window into the chemical evolution of the interstellar medium, linking stellar nucleosynthesis and Galactic chemical evolution to the physical and chemical processes shaping molecular clouds, star-forming regions, and planetary systems. However, molecular isotopic ratios do not necessarily trace the underlying elemental composition, as chemical isotopic fractionation, isotope-selective photodissociation, grain chemistry, and radiative-transfer effects can significantly alter the observed values. Disentangling these effects requires simultaneous observations of multiple transitions, isotope systems and molecular families, including rare, doubly, and multiply substituted isotopologues involving D, $^{13}$C, $^{15}$N, $^{17,18}$O, $^{29,30}$Si, and $^{33,34,36}$S (e.g., $^{13}$C$^{15}$N, $^{13}$C$^{34}$S, and $^{13}$C$^{18}$O). ALMA2040, with an order-of-magnitude improvement in sensitivity and at least 512 GHz of instantaneous bandwidth, will make these species accessible across statistically significant samples of Galactic and nearby extragalactic sources. By enabling systematic isotopic inventories from molecular clouds and prestellar cores to protoplanetary systems, across the Milky Way and in external galaxies, ALMA2040 will establish molecular isotopes as quantitative probes of chemical inheritance, stellar nucleosynthesis, and galaxy evolution, disentangling local chemical processing from the large-scale evolution of matter from stars to new planetary systems.

title: Extracting the Central Sound Speed of Neutron Stars through Intrinsic Stellar Structure Scaling with Reduced Equation-of-State Model Dependence
abstract: Inferring neutron star (NS) core properties remains sensitive to the assumed equation of state (EOS). Using a nonlinear Walecka model with generalized $\omega$-meson self-interactions, we construct six EOS families, each containing $10^3$ samples subject to identical nuclear and astrophysical constraints. Despite satisfying these constraints, the families predict markedly different high-density behavior and core properties; higher-order $\omega$ interactions can also generate interior sound-speed peaks within purely nucleonic matter. To reduce this model dependence, we use the intrinsic and perturbative analysis of the dimensionless Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations (IPAD-TOV) to derive an EOS-independent estimator $\Theta(\rm{X},\Psi)$ of the central squared sound speed $s_{\rm c}^2$, where $\rm{X}=P_{\rm c}/\varepsilon_{\rm c}$ is the central EOS-parameter and $\Psi$ characterizes the stellar-mass response to central energy density. For canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NSs, $\Theta$ correlates linearly with $s_{\rm c}^2$ across the families ($R^2\approx0.94$-$0.99$). The family-dependent relations converge toward a common optimum: minimizing their dispersion yields $s_{\rm c}^2\approx 0.523\pm0.044$ and $\rm{X}\approx 0.173^{+0.020}_{-0.018}$ for all six families, or $s_{\rm c}^2\approx 0.496\pm0.092$ and $\rm{X}\approx 0.167^{+0.030}_{-0.029}$ when the family without $\omega$ self-interaction is excluded. The corresponding radii are $11.73^{+1.08}_{-0.92}$ and $11.92^{+1.76}_{-1.28}\,\rm km$, respectively, with $95\%$ confidence intervals. A unified scaling fitted to all EOS samples supports both extractions. These results show how common stellar-structure relations can constrain NS core properties with reduced EOS-model dependence, even when existing observations cannot distinguish among the underlying EOS descriptions.

title: Breakdown of hydrodynamic universality in causal first-order viscous neutron star oscillations
abstract: Hydrodynamic modeling of viscous neutron stars requires a choice of theory of relativistic hydrodynamics. That distinct formulations contain the same physical content in the long-wavelength limit is referred to as ``hydrodynamic universality.'' It has been recently shown that hydrodynamic universality can break down in radial neutron star oscillations: causality and finite-size effects restrict access to the long-wavelength universal hydrodynamic regime in sufficiently viscous stars. We show that this breakdown occurs for a broad range of causal hydrodynamic frames in Bemfica--Disconzi--Noronha--Kovtun (BDNK) theory. Increasing viscosity collectively pushes this class of causal frames away from the BDNK regime of validity, eventually forcing all to lie outside it at bulk viscosities in the range $\zeta\sim10^{30}$--$10^{31}\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. This breakdown of universality is accompanied by material changes in the oscillation mode structure: non-hydrodynamic modes become damped on timescales comparable to those of hydrodynamic modes, the first overtone can become longer lived than the fundamental mode, and unphysical instabilities with sub-millisecond timescales can emerge. Even in regimes where universality has broken down, we find that the inviscid threshold of gravitational collapse remains unchanged in BDNK theory. These results provide evidence that first-order theories of relativistic hydrodynamics may be insufficient for modeling sufficiently viscous neutron stars.

title: Probing fundamental physics with ALMA2040 mm-wavelength observations of neutron stars
abstract: Bursty or (rotation-induced) pulsed coherent radio emission from pulsars, magnetars, and fast radio transients originates in some of the most extreme environments in the Universe. However, the exact physical mechanism behind the scenes remains poorly understood.
