Specifically, in DIII-D H-mode plasmas with the ion B × ∇B drift driven into the active divertor, the Te cliff arises from a bifurcation-induced Te drop above the magnetic X-point accompanied by reversal of the E × B flow pattern in the private-flux region. Time-dependent simulations reveal a two-phase transition mechanism: the inner-divertor radiation front first extends across the last closed magnetic flux surface and stabilizes above the X-point, causing the local Te to drop from ∼ 70 eV to ∼ 10 eV and inducing an E × B flow reversal in a thin layer below the X-point in less than 0.5 ms (Phase I); this flow reversal subsequently triggers the sharp drop in outer-divertor target temperature on a timescale of 1–2 ms (Phase II), establishing deep plasma detachment a few ms thereafter. We show that a bifurcation transition occurs when the high-field-side radiation front crosses the separatrix while the outer divertor remains attached, with the Te cliff manifesting distinctly when the outer-target Te ≳ 10 eV prior to the bifurcation transition, implying that the bifurcation is fundamentally linked to in–out divertor asymmetry and asymmetric radiation-front evolution.

title: TD-Link: A Daisy-Chain Optical Architecture for Integrated Data Readout and Deterministic Timing Distribution in Large-Scale Detector Systems
abstract: TD-Link is an optical communication architecture that combines high-throughput data readout and sub-nanosecond timing synchronization over a single fiber for large-scale detector systems. It adopts a multidrop daisy-chain ring topology connecting a Data Concentrator to up to sixteen FERS front-end boards per link, with up to eight links per concentrator. Operating at 3.125 Gb/s, TD-Link carries data, synchronization, and control traffic in the same serial stream through a token-based streaming protocol that minimizes per-hop latency and supports on-the-fly payload fragmentation. Deterministic latency is enforced at two levels. On the concentrator, transmitter lanes are aligned by using the half-full flag of the multi-gigabit transceiver (MGT) elastic buffer as a one-bit phase detector: a firmware state machine steps the transmit phase interpolator (PI) until the buffer pointer difference crosses half-depth, locking every lane to the same phase condition. On each front-end board, where the synchronization pulse must also cross from the recovered-clock to the transmit domain, the residual three-to-five-cycle ambiguity of the synchronizer is removed by a calibration-free multiphase oversampling time-to-digital converter (TDC) with 0.8 ns bins, which time-stamps the incoming edge on the transmit time base so that a scheduler regenerates it at a fixed, programmable latency. A Digital Dual Mixer Time Difference (DDMTD) circuit measures the inter-concentrator phase. Tests with CERN PicoTDC-equipped FERS boards show a board-to-board synchronization $\sigma$ of 24 ps on the same ring, 27 ps across transceiver quads, and 28 ps across two cascaded concentrators, against an intrinsic front-end floor of 7 ps. Over more than one thousand cold boots without re-calibration, the boot-to-boot spread of the board-to-board skew stayed below 20 ps, consistent with the 18.6 ps phase-interpolator step.

title: Prediction of the thermal neutron response of grain-boundary impedance in Gd-doped ceria based on the radiation-ionic effect
abstract: The radiation-ionic effect was recently reported in 3 mol% Gd-doped CeO$_2$ (3GDC): under $^{60}$Co gamma irradiation at 35 Gy/min, the grain-boundary (GB) ionic resistance of a bulk pellet decreased 680-fold at room temperature, because electrons trapped at the GB core lower the space-charge potential. The effect has been demonstrated only with photons. Gd has the largest thermal-neutron capture cross section of any stable element and is also the dopant that creates the GB barrier in GDC, so the same mechanism could link GB impedance to thermal-neutron sensing; whether it does, and under what conditions, has not been examined. Here the thermal-neutron response of 3GDC is modelled with the gamma-calibrated Mott-Schottky/Seager framework, with unmeasured parameters carried as intervals and propagated jointly. Each capture deposits about 50 keV by conversion and Auger electrons within 1 $\mu$m, the remaining 8 MeV leaving as prompt photons; Gd segregation to the GBs adds a factor of only 1-2 because the electron range exceeds the grain size. A thermal flux of $8\times10^{9}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ (6-12$\times10^{9}$) matches the GB-effective generation rate of the 35 Gy/min calibration, and the predicted room-temperature GB resistance ratio is 110 (70-170) at $10^{9}$ and 970 (600-1500) at $10^{10}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, falling to 2 at 61 (55-68) and 81 (73-92) $^\circ$C. The neutron case differs from gamma irradiation in three respects: capture events are discrete, so the continuous-source approximation depends on the unmeasured trapped-charge lifetime; self-shielding (mean free path 0.27 mm) makes the response thickness dependent; and capture photons absorbed in the pellet add a gamma term comparable to the local term for pellets of 0.3 mm or more. The intervals are conditional on the model and exclude its structural error. The conditions under which the prediction can be tested are given.

title: Population pumping of vibrational and rotational quantum states in the triatomic hydrogen ion observed by electron-beam-assisted high-resolution spectroscopy
abstract: We present a technique to observe the optical manipulation of individual quantum states of H 3 + ions stored inside a heavy-ion storage ring, where the excitation is detected by electron-beam-assisted action spectroscopy. The transitions addressed here are chosen to enable multicolor spectroscopy of states far above the energetic barrier, where this molecule—with a triangular ground state—can sample linear geometries. This region of the spectrum has so far been inaccessible due to extremely weak direct transition strengths from the ground vibrational level. Our experiments pave the way for spectroscopy of the simplest polyatomic molecule in a previously unexplored energetic territory, which would benchmark theoretical data crucial for the understanding of this fundamental molecular system. Our results also demonstrate laser pumping to vibrationally and rotationally excited states of H 3 + , gaining model-dependent access to their relative dissociative electron recombination rates.

title: Plasma-neutral collision operators for hydrogen isotopes: kinetic and gyrokinetic descriptions, comparison to fluid
abstract: Plasma-neutral interactions critically affect the edge dynamics of magnetically confined fusion devices. Neutral atoms modify ion and electron velocity distributions, potentially affecting local instabilities Standard fluid models simplify these processes (namely charge exchange, ionization and recombination) using Maxwellian assumptions and linearized source terms. We revisit these assumptions for a hydrogen plasma interacting with hydrogen atoms. We derive plasma-neutral interaction terms in the kinetic and gyrokinetic frameworks. Accounting for velocity-dependent differential cross-sections, the model captures the kinetic impact of inelastic collisions on ions and electrons beyond energy and momentum exchange. We demonstrate that the fluid moments of the kinetic model reduce to standard fluid source terms under the appropriate assumptions of Maxwellianity and linearity. We compare the kinetic model with fluid models through their effects on distribution functions and fluid moments. Substantial discrepancies are observed, even for Maxwellian distributions. For charge exchange, the kinetic model yields momentum and energy exchange rates up to twice those predicted by fluid descriptions. We show that a fluid treatment of ionization greatly overestimates the mean kinetic energy of the produced electrons. These results highlight the limitations of fluid descriptions and the importance of kinetic effects in edge-plasma momentum and energy exchange.

title: Neutrino Tridents and $W$-boson production at the Muon Collider
abstract: Muon colliders are exceptionally intense sources of multi-TeV neutrinos, allowing even relatively small detectors to record large rates of neutrino interactions. In addition to serving as neutrino-ion collider for precision measurements of neutrino deep inelastic scattering, this setup allow to study even rare neutrino processes with at high statistics. In this study, we investigate the feasibility of measuring neutrino trident and on-shell W-boson production, predicting over one million trident events and one hundred thousand W-boson events in a 100 kg silicon-based active target over ten years and allowing to detect these processes for the first time. We further show that these measurements could constrain new vector and axial-vector interactions beyond projected DUNE sensitivities and provide unprecedented constraints on the high-x photon distribution through W-boson production near threshold. We also discuss strategies for signal-background discrimination and the resulting detector requirements.

title: Multimessenger Constraints on Nuclear Acceleration in Neutrino-Emitting Seyfert Coronae
abstract: High-energy neutrinos from Seyfert galaxies probe particle acceleration near supermassive black holes, but the accelerated nuclear composition remains uncertain. We connect stochastic acceleration to nuclear and radiative cascades to assess nuclear contributions. Acceleration and losses limit the energy per nucleon available to nuclear cascades; without secondary reacceleration, fragmentation cannot raise this scale. For NGC~1068, joint neutrino and gamma-ray constraints depend on the nuclear mixture: helium-dominated injection permits larger nuclear power fractions than the heavier mixtures considered. For the harder candidate {neutrino} spectrum of NGC~7469, the adopted model yields more energetic nuclear cascades, while the source-specific flux selections allow larger nuclear fractions for the heavier mixtures than in NGC~1068. These results show that composition constraints depend on nuclear yields as well as acceleration conditions and available power.

title: Icosahedral-group beam layouts for highly uniform direct-drive laser fusion
abstract: Abstract We investigate irradiation uniformity in direct-drive laser fusion using beam layouts generated from the full rotational icosahedral group. By expanding the incident intensity in spherical harmonics, we show the selection rules imposed by exact icosahedralinvariance and identify the forbidden multipole degrees. These exclusions are independent of the single-beam profile and therefore remain valid for both delta-function and finite-width beams. Using flat-top and von Mises–Fisher beam profiles, we evaluate theresulting root-mean-square nonuniformity and compare an optimized 60-beam icosahedral layout with the conventional OMEGA 60-beam geometry. For smooth beam profiles, this model predicts substantially lower nonuniformity for the optimized icosa-hedral layout than for the OMEGA-60 geometry, because exact low-degree cancellation is combined with eﬃcient high-degree attenuation by the beam-profile transfer coeﬃcients. We further examine random beam-weight imbalance and show that optimizedhigh-beam-count icosahedral layouts remain robust over the range studied. These results establish a symmetry-based design principle for low-mode control and improved irradiation uniformity in direct-drive laser implosions.

title: First next-to-next-to-leading-order extraction of fragmentation functions for Lambda hyperons
abstract: We present MAPFF1.0_Lambda, the first global analysis at next-to-next-to-leading order in perturbative QCD of the collinear unpolarised fragmentation functions of Lambda hyperons. The fit is based on data from single-inclusive electron-positron annihilation, and from both neutral-current and -- for the first time -- charged-current semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering. We have adopted a statistical framework based on Monte Carlo sampling and parametrised fragmentation functions in terms of a neural network. The fragmentation function set comprises a total of seven independent parton flavours, allowing for the first independent determination of valence-quark distributions. Our analysis offers new insights into the hadronisation mechanism of strange baryons and establishes a baseline for future phenomenological and experimental investigations.

title: Femtoscopic parameters of pion emission sources in EPOS4 Au+Au collisions from 7.7 to 200 GeV
abstract: Three-dimensional femtoscopy probes the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The collision-energy dependence of L\'evy source parameters may reveal the evolution of strongly interacting matter and possible signatures of the QCD phase diagram. We previously studied the excitation function of three-dimensional L\'evy source parameters for pion pairs in Au+Au collisions with EPOS4, analyzing the pair-distance distribution \(D(\rho)\) through one-dimensional projections. Here, we analyze the full three-dimensional source distribution and correlation function directly. We construct \(D(\rho_{\rm out},\rho_{\rm side},\rho_{\rm long})\) as a 3D histogram, transform it into \(C(q_{\rm out},q_{\rm side},q_{\rm long})\) using a Fast Fourier Transform, and fit the correlation function with the analytic L\'evy formula. This approach can reduce biases arising when one-dimensional projections are used to describe a non-elliptical source. We apply the method across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan range and compare the extracted energy dependence with results from the projection-based method and recent UrQMD calculations. We focus on the out-side observables \(R_{\rm diff}^{2}=R_{\rm out}^{2}-R_{\rm side}^{2}\) and \(R_{\rm out}/R_{\rm side}\), whose different energy dependences in EPOS4 and UrQMD may illuminate the roles of emission duration and source dynamics. This work establishes a direct three-dimensional framework for comparison with future femtoscopic measurements and for exploring possible non-monotonic structures associated with the QCD phase diagram.

title: Axisymmetric perturbations and vertical displacement oscillatory modes driven by fast ions in tokamak plasmas
abstract: Abstract Recent progress on the theory and numerical simulations of Vertical Displacement Oscillatory Modes (VDOM) in tokamak plasmas is reported. VDOM are driven unstable by energetic particles and can have an impact on plasma disruptions, plasma edge stability and confinement. These modes are a candidate, together with Global Alfvén Eigenmodes (GAE), to explain Alfvén-frequency n=0 modes driven by fusion alpha particles recently observed on JET (H.J.C. Oliver et al 2025, Ref. [1]). Differences in the physical mechanisms underlying VDOM and GAE are discussed. An analytic dispersion relation that contains both VDOM and ideal-MHD unstable vertical displacements is derived. Limits on plasma elongation for stable plasma operation against ideal-MHD vertical displacements are discussed. While VDOM are generally immune against continuum damping, if the wall is brought very close to the plasma boundary and the plasma density remains relatively large up to the last-closed-flux-surface (as in the case of H-mode discharges), the VDOM oscillation frequency may interact with the Alfvén continuum spectrum, giving rise to continuum damping. Specific types of fast ion distribution functions that can provide an instability drive for n=0 modes are considered. Numerical simulations of n=0 modes obtained with the NIMROD code are shown, including a preliminary assessment of the fast ion instability drive for these modes.

title: Searching for the N -naturalness tower of neutrinos
abstract: We present the first experimental search for the N -naturalness tower of neutrinos using a global analysis of publicly available neutrino data. As a potential solution to the hierarchy problem, the N -naturalness model employs a varying Higgs mass parameter among N dark sectors and encodes the required fine-tuning of the placement of the sectors in a parameter r . We report exclusion limits on the parameter space ( r , N ), for normal and inverted ordering and in case the neutrino is Majorana or Dirac. In the case of a Majorana neutrino, we can rule out N ≤ 10 4 sectors with r ≥ 0.1 . This is particularly exciting as it shows that a gauge and gravitational unification around M GUT , which is a benchmark scenario of the N -naturalness framework with N = 10 4 without fine-tuning, is ruled out by neutrino experiments.

title: Performance and Radiation Damage of the Heavy-Ion Silicon Beam Tracker in the BM@N Experiment
abstract: The Silicon Beam Tracker (SiBT) of the BM@N experiment at the NICA complex (JINR, Dubna) is designed to reconstruct trajectories of beam ions upstream of the target. It consists of three stations based on double-sided silicon strip detectors (DSSDs) installed directly in the relativistic heavy-ion beam. The SiBT performance and radiation damage were studied using data from the 2026 experimental run with $^{124}$Xe beams at~$1.6$,~$2.2$, and~$3.0$~AGeV. During the run, the leakage current of the DSSD of the third station of SiBT increased by $28.95~\mu\mathrm{A}$, while the charge collection efficiency in the beam center decreased to approximately $68\%$ at the nominal bias voltage of 30~V. Increasing the bias voltage to 90~V restored the charge collection efficiency to approximately $95\%$. Despite the radiation-induced signal degradation, the tracking efficiency remained close to $99\%$. The accumulated radiation damage was also used to reconstruct the spatial distribution of the integrated beam fluence from strip-by-strip leakage-current measurements, yielding an average fluence of approximately $1.3\times10^{12}~\mathrm{n_{eq}/cm^2}$.

title: Mortality of ultra-thin LGADs and PiN diodes from high energy deposition
abstract: Low Gain Avalanche Diodes are prime candidates for high-resolution timing applications in High Energy Physics, Nuclear science, and several other fields. Operating these devices in high-radiation environments presents various hazards, including the risk of their permanent degradation or destruction caused by effects such as Single Event Burnout. Studies using minimum ionizing particles found a greatly reduced Single Event Burnout risk by operating below a bias voltage corresponding to an average electric field of 12 V/$\mu$m - however, as high energy particle colliders produce a wide energy spectrum of radiation, it is crucial to understand this phenomenon and other possible damage mechanisms at energy deposition levels greater than those of minimum ionizing particles. This was achieved by pre-irradiating LGADs and PiN diodes with active thicknesses of 20, 30, and 50 $\mu$m up to 1.5 $\times$ 10$^{15}$ $\mathrm{n_{eq}/cm^2}$, and exposing them to beams of protons and heavy ions (C, O, Fe, Au) at the BNL Tandem van de Graaff accelerator. Several mortality categories were observed, defined by different electrical and mechanical damage signatures. This furthers our understanding of permanent radiation damage of silicon devices, crucial towards mitigating Single Event Burnout and other damage mechanisms to safely operate future detectors.

title: Implications for new physics solutions to the LSND and MiniBooNE anomalies after MicroBooNE results
abstract: Over the past couple of decades, the Liquid Scintillator Neutrino Detector (LSND) and MiniBooNE (MB) neutrino experiments have provided statistically significant evidence of persistent and as yet unexplained electron-like event excesses. The MicroBooNE experiment, with sensitive particle identification capabilities designed to shed light on these anomalous results, has conducted a number of analyses to test whether the excess is due to photons, electrons or $e^+e^-$ pair productions, all of which give almost identical signals in LSND and MB. Recent MicroBooNE searches, in addition to checking Standard Model (SM) processes, have focused on proposed new physics scenarios involving new mediators and dark portals beyond the SM. We study the consequences and effects of these analyses for the many theoretical proposals put forth to generate the three types of signals above in order to understand the observed excesses. We discuss which classes of solutions are allowed, disallowed or require further scrutiny involving theoretical and experimental efforts. We give an example of a new solution that survives the restrictions imposed by MicroBooNE results and other existing bounds. We point out that a light ($m\leq 30$ MeV) dark neutral spin zero mediator with dominantly pseudoscalar couplings, decaying to an $e^+e^-$ pair, can account for the observations. We indicate that if such a model is realised, it may point to the possibility that neutrinos are Dirac particles, and that there are dark Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) of mass ${\cal O}(100)$ MeV. We discuss issues related to CP violation and ultra-violet completion of these models. Finally we stress that a search for the excess in incoherent scattering channels in MicroBooNE and SBND could help clarify the physics behind these persistent anomalies.

title: Finite-Temperature Equations of State for Neutron-Star Mergers within the Quark Mean-Field Model
abstract: We extend the quark mean-field (QMF) model to finite temperature and systematically investigate the thermodynamic properties of uniform nuclear matter, using the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model as a reference. For each model, we consider two parameter sets calibrated to the same selected nuclear-matter saturation properties but with different nucleon Dirac effective-mass ratios at saturation. We examine the effective nucleon mass and the composition of $\beta$-equilibrium matter, together with the free energy, energy density, pressure, entropy, and heat capacities of symmetric nuclear matter, pure neutron matter, and $\beta$-equilibrium matter. The QMF and RMF models exhibit similar qualitative trends, but their predictions increasingly differ at high density, where the effective masses have distinct density dependences. These differences are particularly evident in the thermal pressure and thermal index. For the two parameter sets considered in this work, we further provide compact analytical representations of the thermal index, $\Gamma_{\rm th}(\rho_{\rm b},T,\beta)$ over baryon densities of 0.08-1.0 $\rm fm^{-3}$, temperatures of 5-100 MeV, and isospin asymmetries of 0-1. The fits reproduce the numerical results with an accuracy better than $2\%$ and can be directly implemented in binary neutron-star merger simulations. This study establishes a finite-temperature extension of the QMF framework and provides a basis for future assessments of how a quark-structure-based description of nuclear matter affects thermal support and post-merger dynamics in binary neutron-star mergers.

title: Effective Theory for Light Portal Dark Matter Detection
abstract: We develop a general framework for the computation of light portal dark matter direct detection, incorporating a consistent treatment of finite momentum transfer. In this framework, dark matter interacts with Standard Model matter through a light mediator, which simultaneously serves as the force carrier for dark matter self-interaction, potentially with a distinct coupling strength. The corresponding effective theory relevant for detecting this class of dark matter is systematically constructed. Our analysis focuses on light (semi)relativistic dark matter, which may originate from cosmic-ray boosting and can be probed in high threshold experiments such as large-volume neutrino detectors. In this context, the nucleon matrix elements of the effective operators at finite momentum transfer are required, made available through recent advances in lattice QCD and related nonperturbative methods. The relativistic Fermi gas model is used to convert the nucleon-level momentum transfer to the nuclear level, thereby incorporating nuclear effects pertinent to heavy target experiments. To demonstrate the utility of the framework, we present ultraviolet-complete examples featuring spin-1 and spin-2 portal dark matter. For these models, we compute the differential cross sections with respect to momentum transfer, adopting parameter choices that address the so-called core-cusp problem in astrophysical observations via dark matter self-interactions.

title: Cryogenic characterisation of the FBK NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers for the DarkSide-20k dark matter experiment
abstract: Liquid Argon Time Projection Chambers (TPCs) are highly promising detectors for dark matter searches due to their uniform response, scalability to large target masses, and compatibility with ultra-low background conditions. The DarkSide-20k (DS-20k) experiment, currently under construction at Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare (INFN) Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), aims to achieve unprecedented sensitivity to Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs), approaching the neutrino fog. At the heart of the detector is a dual-phase TPC filled and surrounded by low-radioactivity argon from underground sources (i.e. Underground Argon (UAr)), functioning both as the WIMP target and detection medium. The experiment employs Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) as the chosen photon sensors for its optical planes. Key SiPM properties such as dark noise rate, gain and direct crosstalk were measured using specialized test setups at 77 K. The photon detection efficiency (PDE) was measured under vacuum at 77 K over the wavelength range 350-820 nm. Secondary photon emission, which can give rise to external optical crosstalk, was measured under vacuum at 86 K over the wavelength range 550-1020 nm.

title: Cosmological signature and light dark matter in Dirac L μ − L τ model
abstract: We revisit an anomaly-free extension of the Standard Model viz. the gauged L μ − L τ model in the Dirac framework, where the local U ( 1 ) L μ − L τ symmetry breaks and gives rise to a new gauge boson Z ′ and corresponding gauge coupling g μ τ . Three additional heavy vectorlike fermions, three light right-handed neutrinos and two heavy singlet scalars are added to complete the model framework for Dirac neutrinos. Another singlet vectorlike fermion is added with a new gauge charge, which serves as a viable dark matter (DM) candidate, and the correct relic abundance is obtained via the resonance effect. The resonance effect triggers early kinetic decoupling of the DM candidate, which significantly influences the cosmological sector of this study. The parameter space is considered after satisfying the current bounds on M Z ′ and the gauge coupling g μ τ . The influence of dark radiations coming from the additional light degrees of freedoms are studied in connection with the dark matter. After imposing the relevant theoretical and experimental constraints, the viable parameter space is found to be significantly restricted while remaining accessible to ongoing and near-future experiments. The framework provides a consistent setting in which neutrino masses, dark matter, and cosmological observables can be studied simultaneously. In particular, we identify viable regions of the parameter space that satisfy the constraints from neutrino masses, dark matter relic abundance, and cosmological observables.

title: Confining density functional approach to the QCD phase diagram at low temperatures and thermal twin stars
abstract: We present a density functional-based equation of state for warm, dense nuclear matter with a transition to deconfined quark matter for applications to simulations of supernova explosions and neutron star mergers, but also for the cosmological evolution of Q-balls. For the quark matter equation of state, we employ a recently developed confining density functional approach while nuclear matter is described within a relativistic density functional model of the DD2 class. The phase transition is obtained by a Maxwell construction at constant entropy per baryon. We discuss the solutions of TOV equations for isentropic hybrid stars for two hybrid equation of state models: DDf-SFM without and DD2-$\chi$CDF with color superconductivity. We find that at finite temperatures above a critical value of entropy per baryon sequences of disconnected third family branches ("thermal twin stars") may appear for the DDf-SFM model, while they are absent for the color superconducting model and at $T=0$. We discuss the relation of this critical entropy per baryon to the Seidov criterion of gravitational instability for $T=0$ and find that it is a good guide. We suggest that the presence of thermal twin stars may be regarded as an indicator for the core-collapse supernova explodability of massive blue supergiant stars with solar metallicity and thus serve as a new criterion for the reliability of hybrid equation of state models. By this argument, strong color superconductivity shall be excluded and it remains to be shown whether models with moderate diquark pairing could fulfill the thermal twin constraint. For the case of symmetric matter, we compare the resulting hybrid EOS with the flow constraint by Danielewicz et al. and find a a sensitivity of the onset density for deconfinement to the presence or absence of color superconductivity.

title: Characterizing the energy resolution of the MicroBooNE LArTPC at the MeV scale using monoenergetic features of $^{208}$Tl decays
abstract: A detailed understanding of the capabilities and fidelity of low-energy reconstruction is crucial for taking advantage of MeV-scale neutrino physics opportunities in liquid argon time projection chambers (LArTPCs). This study presents a measurement of the resolution of reconstructed energy in the MicroBooNE LArTPC at $\approx 1.5$ MeV. The characterization is performed using monoenergetic signals generated by $2.614$ MeV $\gamma$-rays from $^{208}$Tl decays undergoing pair production in the detector. The resolution is found to be ($7.52 \pm 0.78 \text{(stat)} \pm 0.92 \text{(syst)}$)%. This value is consistent with the MicroBooNE simulation prediction of ($9.70 \pm 0.65 \text{(stat)}$)% at the $1.6 \sigma$ level. This study represents the first ever measurement of LArTPC energy resolution at the MeV scale and provides a pathway for monoenergetic energy calibrations in future experiments using LArTPC detectors.

title: Branching fraction measurement of the $B^0\to K^+\pi^-\mu^+\mu^-$ decay at high dihadron mass
abstract: This Letter presents the first measurement of the $B^{0} \to K^{+}\pi^{-}\mu^{+}\mu^{-}$ differential branching fraction in the region of the dihadron $K^+\pi^-$ mass, $m_{K\pi}$, $1000< m_{K\pi} < 1835\,\text{MeV}/c^{2}$. This decay mode is mediated by the quark-level transition $b \to s\ell^{+}\ell^{-}$, for which the measured effective couplings show tensions with Standard Model predictions. The analysis is performed using proton-proton collision data collected with the LHCb detector between 2011 and 2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $8.4\,\text{fb}^{-1}$. The differential branching fraction is determined across different regions of dimuon mass squared, $q^2$, in the interval $0.1 < q^2 < 18.0\,\text{GeV}^2/c^{4}$, as well as in different regions of $ m_{K\pi}$ in the interval $1.1 < q^2 < 6.0\,\text{GeV}^2/c^{4}$. The results represent the first differential measurement of the branching fraction across $m_{K\pi}$ within the selected dihadron-mass region, and the first observation of the decay within this region above the $J/\psi$ resonance.

title: Octupole parton structure of spin-3/2 targets
abstract: In spin-$3/2$ targets, octupole polarization can reveal quark and gluon correlations beyond those probed by vector polarization and quadrupole alignment. Here, we construct the complete leading-twist gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distribution basis, with 32 independent coefficients for each specified Wilson-line and color structure. Fourteen of these describe octupole dependence in gluon number, helicity, and linear polarization. In heavy-quark-pair leptoproduction at small, nonzero pair imbalance, comparing target states with opposite octupoles and identical lower moments isolates the octupole contribution. Beam-helicity reversal and joint angular projections in target orientation and pair-imbalance azimuth can then separate all fourteen gluon octupole responses at leading-power Born order. We also derive the incoming-target quark responses in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering and Drell-Yan production. Time-reversal relations between distributions remain valid under symmetry-preserving renormalization and evolution, while predictions across processes require factorization formulas connecting those distributions to scattering observables. Finally, we connect this framework to polarized $^{7}$Li through its collinear limits and nuclear spin-orbital correlations.

title: Numerical calculations of neutron star mountains supported by crustal lattice pressure
abstract: ABSTRACT Gravitational waves may set the spin frequencies of neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). One mechanism for facilitating such emission is the formation of a mass asymmetry – or ‘mountain’ – supported by elastic strains driven by thermal gradients. Most studies have focused either on the origin of the elastic strains or the temperature asymmetry in isolation, and have not considered the entire formation process. In previous work, we showed that anisotropic heat transport in magnetized accreting neutron stars can source a significant temperature asymmetry, and made rough estimates that suggested temperature-induced perturbations in the pressure supplied by the crustal lattice may be competitive with the widely known model of temperature-induced capture-layer shifts. In this paper, we carry out detailed calculations to properly explore this scenario. We self-consistently calculate the temperature asymmetries, the perturbations in crustal lattice pressure, and the mass asymmetries within a single framework. For the first time, we make use of the set of realistic equations of state from the Brussels–Montreal nuclear energy-density functionals BSk19, BSk20, and BSk21 which describe all regions of accreting neutron stars in a thermodynamically consistent, unified way. We find these mountains are too small to dictate the spin-equilibrium of LMXBs, and estimate the level of gravitational wave emission they produce.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: High-efficiency klystrons from a dream to a reality
abstract: During the past decade, a comprehensive research and development (R&D) program on high-efficiency klystrons has been carried out in collaboration with industry. Initial prototypes have undergone testing, with experimental results showing significant promise. This paper is an extended and updated version of the work presented in Catalan-Lasheras [ , FRYD1 (2024)]. After a brief overview of the R&D program, it presents the latest experimental findings and discusses future developments, including novel vacuum tube topologies aimed at next-generation collider applications.

title: ENGRAVE follow-up of a type IIb supernova spatially coincident with the sub-threshold gravitational wave trigger S250818k
abstract: The candidate gravitational wave (GW) event S250818k was one of only three non-retracted LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA public alerts issued during the fourth observing run of the network (O4) with a binary neutron star (BNS) merger classification probability exceeding one percent. This triggered a prompt search for a potential electromagnetic (EM) counterpart in the large localization error region (949 deg 2 projected in the sky at the 90% credible level). The transient supernova (SN) 2025ulz discovered by the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) during the search, attracted a great deal of attention due to a potential spatial and temporal coincidence, and due to its initial fast decay and featureless spectrum. Here, we report on the follow-up of this transient by the Electromagnetic counterparts of gravitational wave sources at the Very Large Telescope (ENGRAVE) Collaboration. We conducted an extensive multi-wavelength observational campaign, which led to the spectral classification of the transient as a type IIb SN, indicating that it is unrelated to the candidate GW event. In this article, we describe our observing strategies, data reduction, and interpretation. All of our results confirm and strengthen our classification of the source, and also show that shock-cooling tails associated with type IIb SNe are one of the most prominent contaminants in kilonova searches.

title: Cosmological Constraints and Bayesian Evidence for Coupled $\phi$CDM with DESI DR2 Observations
abstract: Abstract We investigate a coupled $\phi$CDM cosmological model in which energy exchange between dark energy and dark matter is governed by the derivative interaction term $Q = 3\alpha \dot{\rho}_m$. We constrain the model using baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from DESI Data Release~2, combined with compressed CMB likelihoods and Type~Ia supernova datasets, including Pantheon$^{+}$, DES-Dovekie, and Union3. Parameter estimation is performed via Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, and Bayesian evidence is used for model comparison with $\Lambda$CDM. We find that the interaction parameter $\alpha$ is tightly constrained at the $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4})$ level and remains consistent with zero within $1\sigma$ across all dataset combinations, indicating no statistically significant evidence for dark sector interaction. The dark energy equation-of-state parameter remains close to $w_{\phi}=-1$, with only mild and statistically insignificant deviations toward a quintessence-like regime. While the inferred Hubble parameter shows a slight shift to higher values relative to $\Lambda$CDM, it remains insufficient to resolve the $H_0$ tension. The matter density parameter is consistent between both models within uncertainties. Bayesian model comparison consistently favors the $\Lambda$CDM model, with evidence ranging from moderate to strong depending on the dataset combination. Overall, the \textcolor{red}{coupled} $\phi$CDM model does not provide a significant improvement over the standard cosmological scenario in light of current observations.

title: Beam transient studies in high-intensity linacs
abstract: Space charge is one of the main challenges for high-intensity linear accelerators (linacs). To overcome this, most linacs have adopted the space charge compensation (SCC) scheme at the low-energy beam transport (LEBT). However, SCC is a buildup process that produces beam transients, i.e., nonoptimal beam conditions, which can lead to significant beam degradation and losses. Furthermore, most LEBTs are equipped with a chopper to provide a beam structure intended for the downstream sections and for the gradual ramp-up of power. However, operation of the chopper will destroy the SCC, leading to additional beam transients. SCC studies on beam transients focus primarily on the LEBT section, resulting in insufficient analysis of the downstream section, where beam transients can cause significant losses. This work addresses this gap by analyzing beam transients generated in the LEBT and their propagation throughout the linac to assess beam losses. This analysis challenges conventional notions by revealing that the worst-case scenario does not occur when the SCC is zero, but rather within twice the compensation time ( τ * ). This is because, although mismatch and emittance growth are at their maximum at the beginning, 80% and 450%, respectively, the current transmitted to the superconducting linear accelerator is minimal (30%); consequently, beam instabilities caused by the mismatch are less severe. Most nonoptimal beams were intercepted by the cone collimator and the radio-frequency quadrupole at energies below the activation threshold (2.16 MeV), with a peak power loss density that remained within cooling capacity limits. Furthermore, any residual risk was safely eliminated by the collimators in the medium-energy beam transport. As a result, transient losses in the superconducting linac were estimated to be below 1 W / m and were confined to the low-energy section.

title: Universal Boolean Computation in Negatively Coupled Circle Map Lattices
abstract: We investigate the computational capabilities of a one-dimensional lattice of negatively coupled circle maps in its traveling wave regime. We interpret propagating waves as information carriers and exploit their interactions to implement Boolean logic. The logical states are encoded by the propagation direction of the traveling waves, while the presence or absence of a wave at a designated output location represents the logical output. Using controlled wave collisions, we demonstrate the realization of NAND and NOR gates along with other basic gates. Since NAND and NOR operations are functionally complete, the results establish that the traveling wave regime of the negatively coupled circle-map lattice supports universal Boolean computation in principle. The demonstrated logical operations remain valid over a finite range of the coupling strength \epsilon and map parameter \omega, indicating robustness of the computational scheme to parameter variations. Our results therefore demonstrate that computational functionality can emerge from the collective nonlinear dynamics of a coupled map lattice, providing a con- nection between the dynamical properties of traveling wave states and collision based information processing.

title: Two-variable longitudinal distribution of the Λ b in a three-quark light-front model
The Energetic Particle Detector Instrument on ELFIN
abstract: We present the design methodology, implementation, and data products of the Energetic Particle Detector (EPD) instrument on-board the Electron Losses and Fields Investigation (ELFIN) dual SmallSat mission. ELFIN was designed to study the time-evolution of energetic particle distributions in Earth's magnetosphere, having operated in polar Low Earth Orbit (LEO) from 2018 to 2022. Each satellite's instrument payload contained a pair of detector heads to sense differential-directional fluxes of 50 keV to $\sim$5 MeV electrons (EPDE), and 50 keV to $\sim$2 MeV atomic ions (EPDI), with an energy resolution better than 50% ($\Delta E/E<0.5$). The satellites were spinning with a nominal period of 2.8 s in a plane containing Earth's background magnetic field, with particle counting intervals subdivided into 16 consecutive spin sectors. Each EPD was paired with a three-axis Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) sampled at 80 Hz for local pitch-angle determination. Each detector head operated on the principle of pulse-height analysis (PHA) in solid state media, collimated by a rectangular 22.5$^\circ$ field of view and entrance aperture. The EPDE contained a stack of 6 silicon detectors (0.7 cm total thickness) with 0.15 cm$^2$ str geometric factor, with ion contamination mitigated by an aperture foil and digital coincidence logic. The EPDI contained a stack of 2 silicon detectors (0.1 cm total thickness) with 0.03 cm$^2$ str geometric factor, with electron contamination mitigated by a magnetic broom stage and digital anti-coincidence logic. The total assembled mass, volume, and power required for the EPD detector heads and circuit boards were 939 g, 10$\times$9.8$\times$8.4 cm$^3$, and 2.3 W, respectively. We describe each EPD design element alongside instrument data products and processing.

title: Response of GAGG(Ce) scintillators to different charged particles
abstract: Charged-particle telescopes play an essential role in studies of nuclear clustering, which require high-resolution detection of charged breakup fragments. GAGG(Ce) is a promising scintillator for charged-particle detection at high counting rates because of its high light yield, fast response, and non-hygroscopic nature. However, systematic data on its light-output response to different charged particles remain scarce. In this work, we present a systematic study of the scintillation light-output response of GAGG(Ce) crystals to various charged particles and quantify the associated quenching behavior. The relationship between the scintillation light output and the deposited energy is established over a broad range of particle species and energies, providing essential experimental input for response modeling and energy calibration of GAGG(Ce)-based charged-particle detector systems.

title: Readout chain of SPD DAQ system
abstract: The Spin Physics Detector (SPD) experiment at the NICA collider of the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research (JINR) aims to study the spin structure of the nucleon and spin-related phenomena. The experimental conditions, including the high interaction rate and the large number of readout channels, require a triggerless data acquisition system with high throughput and a scalable architecture. This work presents a hardware implementation of the readout chain that extends the previously proposed SPD DAQ architecture. The chain is based on two levels of concentrators. The L1 concentrator provides the interface between the front-end electronics and the next system level and distributes synchronous signals. The L2 concentrator aggregates data streams from several L1 concentrators before transmitting them to the computing system. A key feature of the L2 implementation is the offloading of data reception, buffering, and aggregation from the host CPU to the FPGA, motivated by the large number of small packets generated by the readout electronics. The developed hardware platforms and their operating logic are presented, together with experimental results for the main interfaces and data-path components. The obtained results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed hardware architecture and its application in a scalable SPD data acquisition system.

title: Nonreciprocal Polychromatic Radiation from a Space-Time-Modulated Omega-Topology Meta-Transceiver
abstract: Time-modulated metasurfaces offer a magnet-free route to nonreciprocal wave control, but existing realizations modulate only the electric response of the structure, and proposals for simultaneous electric-magnetic modulation have so far remained theoretical. We experimentally demonstrate a space-time-periodic meta-transceiver whose omega-topology unit cell integrates varactor-loaded electric (dipole) and magnetic (ring) resonators, both modulated by a common unidirectional traveling-wave bias. This modulation gives rise to two independent, experimentally resolved manifestations of nonreciprocity: on transmit, the incident field is efficiently converted into a polychromatic comb of harmonics that radiate at distinct, bias-reconfigurable angles, while on receive, the same modulation instead suppresses frequency conversion and routes the incoming wave preferentially toward one port over the other. These two effects - nonreciprocal polychromatic conversion and unidirectional wave routing - arise from a single unidirectional space-time modulation but act on distinct physical observables, frequency content and spatial direction, respectively. Measured near the electric resonance with a shared bias, these effects characterize the complete cell and do not separate its electric and magnetic contributions. Our results establish the space-time-modulated omega-topology cell as an experimentally viable platform for reconfigurable, full-duplex nonreciprocal wave transformation.

title: Non-contact lens metrology from optical flow and differentiable ray tracing
abstract: Accurate lens surface metrology is essential to determine the manufactured geometry of refractive optical elements and their deviation from the specified design. We demonstrate a transmission metrology method that reconstructs refractive lens surfaces from the displacement of a wavelet-noise-patterned mask. Lens-induced distortion is represented by a dense displacement field. A differentiable ray tracer fits the lens geometry using a calibrated near-telecentric camera model with an effective finite ray origin. We validate the method on commercial lenses. The recovered geometries agree with nominal specifications, and the plano-aspheric reconstruction is compared with chromatic confocal profilometry.

title: Neutral Pseudoscalar Mesons, Hadron Light-by-Light Scattering, and the Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment
abstract: Continuum Schwinger function methods\linebreak (CSM) are used to provide estimates of pseudoscalar meson pole contributions - $\mathsf P = \pi^0$, $\eta$, $\eta^\prime$, $\eta_c$, $\eta_b$ - to the muon anomalous magnetic moment. The analysis framework is benchmarked via successful applications to an array of other meson and nucleon properties. It uses the leading order CSM truncation, augmented by a parametrisation of non-Abelian anomaly effects, to deliver an internally consistent treatment of all the pseudoscalar--two-photon transition form factors required to complete such a calculation. Employing those form factor predictions, the following results are obtained (units $10^{-11}$): $a_\mu^{\pi^0} + a_\mu^{\eta} + a_\mu^{\eta^\prime} = 84.3(0.8)$ - a value lower than some other contemporary estimates; $a_\mu^{\eta_c} = 0.82(0.04)$; and a value of $a_\mu^{\eta_b}$ that is negligible. The total contribution is $\sum _{\mathsf P} a_\mu^{\mathsf P} = 85.1(0.8) / 10^{11}$. Our analysis suggests that this pole contribution to $a_\mu$ is still not known with precision better than 5\%.

title: Lepton Flavour Universality in Semileptonic $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$ Transitions
abstract: Using continuum Schwinger function methods, we deliver parameter-free pointwise predictions for the complete set of twelve Standard Model (SM) $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$, i.e., $b\to c$, semileptonic transition form factors on the entire kinematically accessible domain. Therewith, we calculate SM theory values for the decay-rate ratios of $\tau$ and $\mu$ final states: $\{ R(D) \, , \, R(D)^\ast \} = \{ 0.290(11) \, , \, 0.267(5) \}$, $\{ R(D_{s}) \, , \, R(D_{s}^{\ast}) \} = \{ 0.283(11) \, , \, 0.251(5) \}$. The former is consistent with an existing average of SM estimates, but disagrees with the experimental average by $2.8\sigma$. Comparing transitions with light quark and strange quark spectators, we find a $2.3\sigma$ signal for violation of SU$(3)$ flavour symmetry, expressed at the 5% level in $D_{(s)}^\ast$ final states. It is induced by Higgs boson couplings into the strong interaction and modulated by phenomena deriving from emergent features of the strong interaction.

title: Impact of errors in the shape function of rotating neutron stars in the oblate Schwarzschild approximation
Impact of Window Observables on the Transversity Quark Parton Distribution Function
abstract: We study the potential impact of lattice QCD window observables on nucleon isovector quark transversity parton distribution functions (PDFs) using the ePump Hessian-updating framework. Window observables, recently proposed in arXiv:2505.22795 as benchmark quantities enabling direct quantitative comparison between lattice QCD and phenomenological PDF extractions, are weighted integrals of PDFs over a range of Bjorken-$x$ for which both approaches are reliable. Experimental determinations of transversity PDFs carry uncertainties of 50--100%, while current lattice calculations have achieved comparable or better precision, creating an opportunity for lattice inputs to significantly constrain a global analysis. We evaluate the constraining power of existing lattice QCD computations of transversity window moments and Gaussian windows against current phenomenological PDF. We additionally examine prospective tensor charges in the transversity channel and estimate the PDF uncertainty reduction achievable at current and near-future lattice precision. Our results provide quantitative guidance on which window observables will most constrain global PDF analyses.

title: Feasibility demonstration of a high-momentum, high-purity muon beamline at the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility
abstract: Abstract We have established and characterized a novel high-purity muon beam delivery scheme, designated as the μ20 mode, at the high-momentum hadron beamline (B-line) of the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility. This scheme delivers tertiary muons produced via the in-flight backward decays of secondary pions in the straight section of the beamline, inherently suppressing parent hadron contamination. In a systematic performance evaluation, the muon beam achieved a standalone intensity of 1.7 × 103particles/spill with a spatial spread (standard deviation, σ) of approximately 15mm at the downstream detector position.A systematic attenuation analysis utilizing an iron absorber verified a high muon purity of 98.0 ± 0.6% for the 3GeV/c muon beam mode. Crucially, this work marks the first successful feasibility study of a pure multi-GeV/c muon beamline operation at an experimental facility in Japan.
source: Progress of Theoretical and Experimental Physics

title: Energy, vertex, and time response of a LiquidO detector with an opaque-scintillator target to Compton-tagged electrons
abstract: LiquidO detectors confine scintillation light near its point of production by stochastic scattering in an opaque medium and collect it with a lattice of wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibers. The elementary signal of such a detector is the point-like sub-MeV energy deposition, yet the response to that signal at the center of the detector volume has not been measured against an event-by-event ground truth. To close this gap, we couple BPULSE, a 4-liter prototype LiquidO detector, to a Compton-coincidence calibration setup that selects electron recoils of known energy on a constrained beam axis. The prototype is a 160 mm cube of opaque scintillator with 64 WLS fibers in alternating orthogonal layers at a 20 mm pitch, read out by silicon photomultipliers. Compton scatters of collimated gamma-ray beams from $^{137}$Cs and $^{60}$Co sources are tagged by a NaI(Tl) spectrometer. For 373.4 keV electrons, tagged from $90^{\circ}$ scatters of the $^{137}$Cs beam, the detector collects $19.04 \pm 0.07$ photoelectrons (p.e.). Across four operating points, the two sources at two scattering angles, it responds linearly at $48.3 \pm 1.5$ p.e./MeV. The energy resolution of $(23.4 \pm 0.4)\%$ matches the Poisson statistics of the detected photoelectrons. Collection at both fiber ends and larger sensors would raise the light yield of this target to an estimated 108-124 p.e./MeV. Center-of-mass reconstruction locates each recoil to the width of the delivered 20 mm beam spot, which bounds the intrinsic localization of the detector from above. The arrival time response sets a lower bound of 1.5 ns on the single-scatter start time at the observed $\approx 19$ p.e. light level. This single-scatter response is the building block for reconstructing multi-site events. It constrains the light collection, confinement, and timing models on which reconstruction in future LiquidO detectors will rest.

title: Dual deconvolution multifocal fluorescence response matrix microscopy for aberration-free high-throughput super-resolution imaging
abstract: Fluorescence response matrix imaging enables separate computational correction of excitation and emission aberrations through dual deconvolution, but single-focus acquisition requires a large number of camera frames, limiting its practical use. Multifocal excitation can accelerate acquisition by recording many illumination positions in parallel, but denser foci also increase inter-focus crosstalk, which can bias the estimated excitation and emission optical transfer functions and degrade aberration correction. Here, we introduce high-throughput aberration-free fluorescence response matrix imaging with adaptive multifocal illumination, in which the inter-focus spacing of the multifocal lattice is adjusted according to specimen-dependent crosstalk. A programmable digital micromirror device generates multifocal excitation lattices, and the resulting detector-resolved fluorescence responses are assembled into a two-coordinate fluorescence response matrix. Dual deconvolution separately estimates and corrects the excitation and emission optical transfer functions, and the aberration-corrected matrix is then combined in the spatial-frequency domain to reconstruct the aberration-free image. This strategy reduces the number of required camera frames by approximately three orders of magnitude, allowing response matrices with $\sim 10^6$ illumination positions to be acquired within seconds to a few minutes. The accelerated acquisition preserves the aberration-correction capability of dual deconvolution and achieves an estimated lateral resolution of $\sim$100 nm. Applied to heterogeneous mouse brain and kidney tissue, the method enables high-resolution, depth-resolved volumetric imaging while correcting specimen-dependent aberrations. Together, these results establish adaptive multifocal illumination as a practical route to high-throughput aberration-free fluorescence response matrix imaging.

title: Broadband 600- and 1200-GHz Subharmonically Pumped Schottky Diode Mixers
abstract: A subharmonic mixer topology is introduced that uses quarter-wave stubs to create virtual RF/LO grounds and provide impedance matching in close proximity to the antiparallel Schottky barrier diode pair, thereby reducing the electrical length and enabling broadband operation. The RF/LO matching topology is demonstrated at 600 GHz and 1200 GHz, with good agreement between measured and simulated performance. The 600-GHz mixer demonstrates approximately 20% RF bandwidth with a DSB receiver noise temperature below 1300 K across most of the measured band, while the 1200-GHz implementation achieves DSB receiver noise temperatures below 3000 K over a broad frequency range. Both mixers are characterized at room temperature with approximately 2 mW of LO power. The 600-GHz mixer is used in the Submillimeter Wave Instrument (SWI) onboard ESA's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer. Overall, these results demonstrate state-of-the-art room-temperature performance for broadband receiver front ends targeting atmospheric research and remote-sensing applications.

title: A Low-Temperature Tool for Acousto-electric Detection
abstract: We have developed an apparatus for the measurement of the acousto-electric effect (AEE) from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperatures. The AEE is excited by bulk acoustic waves (BAWs) for which a lithium niobate piezoelectric actuator is employed. A very low background noise level is realized through careful electrical and mechanical design of the setup. The validity of the setup is tested by measuring the AEE in heavily doped P-type and N-type silicon. The opposite sign of the AEE signal was seen for both samples, showing dependence of the signal on the type of charge carrier being dragged by acoustic waves. The signal showed quadratic dependence on the driving voltage, which is consistent with the AEE literature. Further, a temperature dependence of the AEE signal was measured, which exhibits a monotonic increase with a rise in temperature. The ability to probe the AEE in bulk samples at low temperatures makes this setup a promising tool to investigate the AEE and related phenomena in different materials at cryogenic temperatures.

title: Theoretical study of multinucleon transfer reactions with a 208 Pb target using master equation
abstract: Abstract Combining with the dinuclear system concept, we developed the traditional master equation approach by incorporating the nucleon transfer probability influenced by the optimal Q -value. That approach was applied to calculate the production cross sections of the fragments in the 58 Ni+ 208 Pb, 136 Xe+ 208 Pb, and 136 Xe+ 198 Pt reactions and the mass distributions in 58 Ni+ 208 Pb and 136 Xe+ 208 Pb reactions. The calculated results are in favorable agreement with the available experimental data. For the observed asymmetry in the production cross sections of the fragments for 58 Ni+ 208 Pb and 40 Ca+ 208 Pb systems, it is attributed to the constraint of the optimal Q -value window on the transfer process. Due to the small difference between Q -value of nucleon transfer and optimal Q -value, the projectile 58 Ni and 40 Ca tend to pickup neutrons and strip protons. Furthermore, owing to the shell effect, the Q -values for the 40 Ca+ 208 Pb reaction in the proton pickup and neutron stripping channels are farther from the optimal Q -value than those for the 58 Ni+ 208 Pb reaction, making it harder for 40 Ca to lose neutrons and gain protons than for 58 Ni.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Pressure-induced unconventional charge-density-wave states in kagome metal AV 3 Sb 5 ( A = K , Rb, Cs)
abstract: Since the discovery of charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity, kagome metal AV 3 Sb 5 ( A = K , Rb, Cs) provides a new platform for exploring novel many-body quantum phenomena. In CsV 3 Sb 5 , a stripelike CDW with commensurate wave vector q = 3 / 8 was observed under moderate pressures, which leads to a peculiar superconducting double-dome behavior in pressure-dependent phase diagram. Previous density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that the pressure-induced stripelike CDW is beyond conventional phonon softening scenario, suggesting a nontrivial role of electronic correlations. However, an in-depth understanding for the pressure-induced unconventional CDW remains elusive. Here, we performed pressure-dependent V 51 nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements on KV 3 Sb 5 and RbV 3 Sb 5 . Although the superconducting double-dome behavior is absent in pressurized KV 3 Sb 5 and RbV 3 Sb 5 , a pressure-induced CDW phase, ascribed to a possible incommensurate triple- Q CDW, is identified by NMR spectra in both materials, indicating that the pressure-induced unconventional CDW beyond DFT calculations is a common feature for kagome metal AV 3 Sb 5 . In contrast to the stripelike CDW, the pressure-induced incommensurate triple- Q CDW does not strongly suppress the superconducting temperature ( T c ) but coincides with an almost plateau behavior at intermediate pressure regime in the pressure-dependent superconducting phase diagram. Furthermore, by systematically analyzing the Korringa relation between Knight shift and nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate in AV 3 Sb 5 , Van Hove singularity-driven electronic fluctuations are revealed as an effective knob for the pressure-induced unconventional CDW. Finally, our present findings underscore the pressure-induced unconventional CDW as a novel correlated quantum state in kagome metal AV 3 Sb 5 .

title: IViS: Interferometric Visibility-domain inversion Software. A GPU-accelerated Python framework for joint deconvolution with ASKAP
abstract: Wide-field spectral-line imaging with modern radio interferometers remains challenging when the emission is extended, multiscale, and distributed over many overlapping pointings. In this regime, accurate reconstruction requires a joint treatment of the calibrated visibilities, control of image-domain regularity, and, when necessary, recovery of missing short spacings from single-dish data. We present of Galactic foreground emission and LMC emission with reduced residual side-lobe structure and realistic multiscale morphology. A comparison with using multiscale CLEAN shows that, for this specific target and a single observing block, (Interferometric Visibility-domain Inversion Software), a GPU-accelerated Python framework for visibility-domain joint deconvolution, and assess its performance for wide-field ̋I imaging with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). The current model, reconstructs a nonparametric sky cube directly from calibrated visibilities by minimizing a regularized least-squares criterion. The forward model relies on a nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT), supports joint deconvolution across all mosaic pointings, and allows positivity constraints through bounded optimization. Short-spacing information can be incorporated through a fusion term that models single-dish data from the same sky estimate. We validate the method using synthetic point-source, noise-only, and multiscale diffuse-emission simulations, and apply it to ASKAP full-survey observations toward the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). The simulations show that recovers point-source flux accurately in the absence of regularization and that the regularization strength sets the trade-off between noise suppression and effective resolution. Relative to linear mosaicking of independently deconvolved pointings, joint deconvolution can recover more large-scale power. When single-dish information is included, the reconstructed power spectra closely reproduce the input sky statistics over a broad range of spatial frequencies. Applied to ASKAP data, yields 10,h mosaics with an effective resolution of 22 ASKAPSoft exhibits fewer residual side-lobes and recovers substantially more power at low spatial frequencies. provides a flexible visibility-domain framework for joint deconvolution of large spectral-line mosaics, and illustrates the potential of regularized inverse-problem approaches as an alternative to traditional CLEAN-based imaging for next-generation radio surveys.

title: Exact Traversable Wormhole Solutions in Finsler--Randers Gravity: Geometry, Physical Viability, and Equilibrium
abstract: Abstract We construct a static, spherically symmetric traversable wormhole in Finsler--Randers (FR) gravity using the osculating-Riemannian formulation, in which the spacetime anisotropy is encoded by a weak time-like vector field $\zeta_a(r)$ rather than introduced by hand at the matter level. Starting from the general FR field equations for a static spherically symmetric line element, we specialize to a zero-tidal-force Morris--Thorne wormhole and derive closed-form expressions for the energy density, radial pressure, and tangential pressure sourcing a fixed shape function $b(r)=r_0^2/r$. Adopting a decaying weak-field ansatz for the anisotropy field, $\zeta_0(r)=\zeta_c\,r_0/r$, we show that the amount of null-energy-condition (NEC) violating matter required to hold the throat open decreases monotonically with $\zeta_c$, and that the radial extent of the NEC-violating region shrinks from the entire spacetime (the general-relativistic limit $\zeta_c\to0$) to a compact neighbourhood of the throat. We further derive the generalized hydrostatic-equilibrium (TOV-type) equation for this geometry and identify an explicit geometric force $F_\zeta$, sourced by the gradient of $\zeta_0(r)$, that supplements the usual hydrostatic and anisotropic forces. The model reduces smoothly to the general-relativistic Morris--Thorne wormhole as $\zeta_0\to0$, and all reported effects remain within the weak-anisotropy regime $|\zeta_0|\ll1$ under which the field equations were derived. We further examine tidal forces (finding the radial component vanishes identically for every observer), sound speeds and the Herrera cracking criterion, a corrected convergent exotic-matter measure, a Herrera-type complexity factor adapted to the wormhole geometry, an analytic classification of the critical anisotropy strength across the shape-function and anisotropy-decay parameter space, a thin-shell realization with reduced surface exotic density, the absence of a photon sphere with the corresponding light-deflection angle, and a linearized generalization to a nonzero redshift function.

title: Detecting seven new glitches in PSR J1341-6220 using six-year timing observations from the Parkes 64 m radio telescope
abstract: This paper aims to report seven newly detected glitches in pulsar (PSR) J1341-6220 from six-year timing observations of the Parkes 64 m radio telescope, and to conduct a detailed analysis of the post-glitch recovery processes via Bayesian methods and the vortex creep model. We used six-year (MJD 58222-60589) timing observations obtained from the Parkes 64 m radio telescope to search for glitches and study the rotational evolution of PSR J1341-6220. We measured the key parameters of the detected glitches and examined their temporal distribution and recovery behaviours. Bayesian analysis and the vortex creep model were used to quantitatively study glitches with sufficient post-glitch data and interpret the delayed spin-down rate increase as the response of inward-moving vortices transported by crustquake-driven platelet motion. We further evaluated the relative decrease in moment of inertia assuming starquake-driven glitches, and compared the result with standard neutron star structure models. We detected seven new glitches (G36-G42) for PSR J1341-6220. Reliable parameters are successfully measured for five of these glitches (G36 and G39-G42), with Deltaν/ν from 136.4 to 953.4 10^ -9 and Δ from 0.36 to 1.57 The intervals between successive glitches range from 149 to 579 days and show no significant periodicity. None of these glitches exhibits definite exponential or linear recovery behaviour, but instead show a pronounced non-linear recovery process. Unidentified small-amplitude glitches may exist between the two unconstrained glitches G37 and G38, and a possible overshoot is observed in the recovery of G41. We performed a Bayesian analysis of glitches G39-G42 with the vortex creep model. G36 was excluded from the vortex-creep modelling because of insufficient post-glitch data. The model reproduces the observations well and indicates that non-linear responses dominate the post-glitch recovery. For G40 and G41, inward vortex motion is invoked to explain the delayed spin-down rate increase after the glitches.

title: A0538-66: A transient ultraluminous X-ray source with a relativistic outflow, 69,ms pulsations, and anomalous optical activity
abstract: A0538-66 is a peculiar Be/X-ray binary in the Large Magellanic Cloud, hosting the fastest spinning neutron star of its class (sim69,ms) and showing the brightest optical bursts of any system of this type. We report four observations obtained near periastron in 2025, together with MAXI and REM monitoring, and a reanalysis of archival RXTE data. On 30 September 2025 the source reached L_ ̊m X ≈ 1.5 ,erg,s-1 (0.2-10,keV), the highest level since 1980, and in February, May, and August 2026, MAXI detected similarly bright outbursts. During the =69.25878(2),ms and dot 10^ 39 observation taken on 30 September 2025, we detected the pulsations, measuring P_ ̊m spin P _ ̊m spin =6.58(9) ,s,s-1; the pulsed fraction was low ( ≈ 1.5 ,erg,s , and it makes >10^ -10 in 1$-10,keV), increased with energy, and the soft and hard pulse profiles were shifted by half a cycle. A new detection in RXTE data of 3 December 1998 gives a faster spin period of P=68.88813(28),ms. The spectra show emission lines from photoionised plasma at rest and blueshifted absorption lines that imply an outflow at ∼ 0.12c. This indicates a highly super-Eddington accretion rate and an intrinsic L_ ̊m X 10^ 39 -1 a transient ultra-luminous X-ray pulsar, a class of which only a few objects are known so far. Since 2023 the optical bursts observed by REM have become longer and brighter, resembling those of the 1980s, but most of them lack a luminous X-ray counterpart (L_ X 37 ,erg,s -1 ). We interpret these results in terms of a radiation pressure dominated accretion disc whose geometrically thick inner regions intermittently screen the innermost emitting regions.

title: Solutions of Roy equations for variable pion mass
abstract: The Roy equations for the $S$ and $P$ waves are solved for pion masses below the physical value in the region between threshold and $s_A=0.84\GeV^2$. The analysis is based on the assumption that the phenomenological input above $s_A$ can be used essentially unchanged. Moreover, for $M_\pi \le M_{\pi,\mathrm{phys}}$, the chiral perturbation theory predictions for the two $S$-wave scattering lengths provide a very reliable additional input to the Roy equations. The outcome is an accurate description of the $S$ and $P$ partial waves as the light-quark masses decrease towards the chiral limit. As a test of the approach, we evaluate the first few threshold parameters of the $S$, $P$, and $D$ waves via Wanders' sum rules and find excellent agreement with chiral perturbation theory across the entire range $0 \le M_\pi \le M_{\pi,\mathrm{phys}}$. We further solve the Roy equations for pion masses above the physical value (up to $240\MeV$) and show that the resulting solutions agree well with existing lattice data at $M_\pi=239\MeV$. The present work paves the way for analyses of lattice data that fully incorporate the constraints of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry, and provides the basis for an accurate study of the dependence of the $\sigma$ and $\rho$ resonances on the light-quark masses, both of which will be addressed in future work.

title: Measuring the Acceleration-Dependent Temperature of the Minkowski Vacuum
abstract: Relativistic quantum field theory is the structure on which the Standard Model and beyond-Standard Model physics are built. One of its most striking predictions is the Unruh effect: an observer undergoing uniform linear acceleration measures the Minkowski vacuum as a thermal bath at a fixed temperature. Despite decades of theoretical interest, this effect has never been directly observed. We propose to use the high acceleration gradients provided by wakefield accelerators, coupled with a forward laboratory-frequency ~THz detector array, to measure the resulting forward-beamed radiation, and outline the unique signature provided by quantum detailed balance to extract the signal from backgrounds. While challenging, such a measurement appears within reach of present-day accelerator and detector technologies.

title: Indirect Dark Matter Detection in the Multi-Messenger Era: Experiments, Systematics, Anomalies, and Prospects for Discovery
abstract: Indirect searches for dark matter (DM) span gamma rays, charged cosmic rays, neutrinos, X-rays, radio emission, the cosmic microwave background (CMB), and the 21~cm signal, but reported constraints and anomalies vary in evidential strength. This critical review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature from January 2000 through October 2026 using a structured search strategy. We assess observations through a framework linking particle interactions and halo source terms to propagation or cosmological energy deposition, instrumental response, background modeling, and statistical inference. Fermi-LAT observations of dwarf spheroidal galaxies provide robust GeV-scale benchmarks for DM annihilation, whereas Galactic-center searches offer higher expected signals but depend more on foregrounds and halo profiles. Charged-cosmic-ray measurements are precise but limited by propagation and source uncertainties, while neutrino searches offer complementary sensitivity through solar capture, directional and flavor information, and high-mass annihilation or decay. Several widely discussed signals, including the 3.5~keV line, 511~keV emission, the Galactic-center GeV excess, charged-particle features, cluster radio excesses, and candidate gamma-ray lines remain inconclusive because of limited independent confirmation, uncertain target scaling, spectral degeneracies, or background-modeling limitations. Cosmological observations provide complementary constraints from CMB energy-injection limits and 21~cm measurements of the intergalactic medium. Artificial intelligence increasingly supports reconstruction and inference but requires rigorous calibration and domain-shift validation. The strongest case for DM discovery would require statistically consistent evidence across independent targets, instruments, or messengers, under common particle-physics parameters, and with well-characterized uncertainties.

title: Anomaly Detection in Bunch Oscillations for Early Warning of Sudden Beam Loss at SuperKEKB
abstract: Sudden beam loss (SBL) events at the SuperKEKB collider result in the loss of a large fraction of the stored beam within just a few revolutions, on a timescale comparable to or shorter than the 20-30 {\mu}s latency of the existing abort system. Such events have damaged collimators and threaten Belle II subdetectors. Bunch Oscillation Recorders (BORs) capture transverse bunch positions at each revolution, which often show sizable oscillations that precede significant beam current loss. We test whether these precursors can be detected earlier than a charge-based reference that mimics the existing abort sensors. We apply several oscillation-based anomaly detection algorithms to 208 SBL events recorded in the low-energy ring during the 2024 run period, ranging from simple rolling statistics to machine learning models trained to forecast bunch oscillation. On 173 events not used for training or calibration, the best-balanced model (DeepLSTM) triggers before the charge-based reference in 86-90% of events across five training seeds, with a mean lead time of 25-30 {\mu}s. The only trigger classified as a false alarm fires on an oscillation that begins about 60 turns before the abort and persists until the beam is lost, making it more likely an early precursor than a spurious trigger. These results establish bunch oscillations as a viable early abort trigger and motivate a shadow-mode deployment to measure the false-alarm rate in continuous operation.

title: Separating charm and bottom decay electrons with point-cloud deep learning on the charged-hadron environment
abstract: Electrons from semi-leptonic decays of charm ($D$) and bottom ($B$) hadrons are important probes in high-energy collisions, while their separation remains challenging due to the similarity of the underlying decay topologies. In this work, the charged-hadron environment associated with each electron is represented as an unordered point cloud and combined with the electron kinematics and charge. Several set-based machine learning architectures, including DeepSets, Transformer, and graph neural networks, are used to distinguish electrons from prompt $D$ and direct $B$ decays without explicit vertex observables. The three architectures achieve comparable performance. Moreover, the Transformer is found to perform better than a boosted decision tree trained on physics-motivated high-level observables. At an efficiency of about 40\%, the classifier reaches a purity level close to 80\% on the test sample. The classifier response is strongly related to the geometric and topological properties of the charged-hadron environment. The information learned by the classifier is further studied using non-prompt $D$ electrons and charged hadrons from different angular regions. Our results indicate that the learned separation is driven mainly by the later stages of the decay chain rather than by initial production effects. The angular-region study further shows that useful discriminating information extends beyond the near- and away-side cones. This method is also evaluated for mid-rapidity proton--proton collisions at both RHIC and LHC energies.

title: Two-body scattering observables from finite-volume real-time evolution
abstract: Abstract We study two-body scattering observables from real-time evolution in a finite periodic box.
