In order to fix the plasma volume of $1500~m^3$ during optimization, the VMEC code was modified to renormalize the boundary coefficient to the desired plasma volume. The STELLOPT stellarator optimization code was modified as well to include new bootstrap current targets, a new target for the radial electric field, and the capability to hold the magnetic field on axis at a fixed value. An intermediary conceptual design plasma and final evolved fixed boundary equilibria are compared to the original modified W7-X equilibrium. The final evolved equilibrium is shown to achieve all the necessary requirements for the GIGA fusion power plant through more detailed modeling of stability, fast ion confinement, and transport.

title: Relativistic Six-Fluid Rotating-Plasma Force-Balance Equilibria for p-11B Fusion Conditions in Spherical Tori
abstract: We formulate an axisymmetric spherical torus (ST) six-component magnetofluid equilibrium model for p_11B plasmas composed of thermal and suprathermal proton, boron, and electron fluids. The model is designed for p_11B parameter regimes where ion energies, strong current drive, energetic electron populations, and ion-electron temperature separation can render a single_fluid static_equilibrium description inadequate. It generalizes rotating_plasma equilibrium theory by incorporating relativistic thermal enthalpy corrections to the electron fluids via h(T/m_ec^2) and by constructing modified flux functions Y_{\alpha} associated with canonical angular momentum for each component {\alpha}. The equilibrium is determined by a Grad-Shafranov-like Ampere law for the poloidal magnetic flux Psi, algebraic density relations constrained by quasineutrality, and prescribed profile functions F_{\alpha}(Y_{\alpha}), T_{\alpha}(Y_{\alpha}) and K_{\alpha}(Y_{\alpha}). The manuscript includes the relativistic magnetofluid equations, the axisymmetric equilibrium formulation, the six_fluid computational method, and four numerical equilibria: two reactor_relevant ST p_11B parameter sets and two EHL-2 ST cases. The examples span toroidal beta b_T = 0.058_0.253, plasma currents I_p = 2.697_12.59 MA, and suprathermal electron temperatures T_eh = 287 keV_2.37 MeV, with h up to 19.1. Over these parameter ranges, Ampere's law accuracy, electrostatic potential accuracy, and component_resolved radial force balance can have errors ranging from 3% to below 0.1%. These results indicate that high-temperature p_11B ST equilibria can differ qualitatively from the single_fluid tokamak equilibria and require analysis of equilibrium component_resolved force balance, relativistic electron enthalpy, and explicit reproducibility diagnostics.

title: Dynamic Optimization Workflow for Gyrokinetic Stability and Transport
abstract: A dynamic optimization workflow for linear gyrokinetic stability that couples the gyrokinetic code CGYRO with the libEnsemble framework for ensemble management has been developed. The workflow is designed to efficiently explore multi-dimensional plasma parameter spaces and to address the practical challenges of simulation-driven optimization in fusion plasma physics, including expensive objective evaluations, unavailable gradient information, non-smoothness arising from transitions between dominant instability branches, and simultaneous multi-core simulations on high-performance computing resources. Rather than optimizing the growth rate at a single wavenumber, the objective maximizes the growth rate-to-wavenumber ratio over the ion-scale spectrum. A derivative-free, model-based optimization algorithm employs manifold sampling to handle the nonsmooth composite structure of the objective function. The approach is applied to the optimization of local magnetic flux-surface shaping parameters, with an equilibrium baseline drawn from DIII-D negative triangularity experimental parameters. The workflow is general and extensible and provides a foundation for future optimization studies involving nonlinear transport objectives and higher-dimensional parameter spaces.

title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking
abstract: Inferring tumor-growth laws from sparse, noisy observations requires more than accurate curve fitting. We study an AI-assisted workflow involving symbolic regression, mathematical admissibility checks, coefficient refitting, and large language model (LLM) ranking. Synthetic Gompertz data allow trajectory fit, forecasting, and recovery of the governing growth law to be assessed separately. A dense noiseless control recovers the generating family, but sparse noisy sampling frequently leads to alternative forms. Among retained candidates in the tested configurations, physics-informed neural network refitting often increases growth-law error, whereas classical nonlinear least squares usually reduces it. A separate exploratory analysis of archived LLM rankings shows no consistent improvement over selection by training error and identifies errors in mathematical reasoning. Plausible saturation, accurate trajectory fits, and convincing explanations can therefore coexist with incorrect growth laws. Mathematical validity and law recovery require evaluation alongside predictive performance.

title: Testing Minimal $U(2)^3$ Right-Handed Flavor Breaking in a Singlet-Scalar Vector-Like Quark Portal
abstract: We study a portal of a $Z_2$-odd singlet scalar and a vector like down quark, in which a right handed flavor breaking spurion extends the portal coupling from $b_R$ to $d_R$ and $s_R$. This single coupling vector links the $b\to s$, $b\to d$, and $s\to d$ transitions. We compute the one loop dipole and $\Delta F=2$ Wilson coefficients, and show that a real scalar generates no $\Delta F=2$ amplitude at one loop. Using a seven observable profile likelihood of $B$ meson mixing, $\epsilon_K$, and radiative decays, with the CKM, lattice, and short distance inputs treated as nuisance parameters, we compare a generic spurion, minimal $U(2)^3$ with a free size of the light quark couplings, and a CKM-aligned ansatz. We have found that the present data cannot yet test the flavor structure: the Standard Model is compatible with the data, with a pseudo experiment $p$-value of $0.20$, and no direction of the light quark couplings can be excluded at 95% CL. For $M_D\simeq m_{\mathcal{S}}=1$ TeV and $|\lambda_b|=1$, the relative light quark coupling $\epsilon_R$ is bounded at 95% CL by $0.227$ for a generic spurion and by $0.211$ for minimal $U(2)^3$. More precise measurements of the $B_s$ mixing phase at the LHC and of $\sin2\beta$ at LHCb and Belle-II, together with improved lattice and CKM inputs, can make the minimality of the flavor structure testable if a deviation from the Standard Model is observed.

title: Testable neutrino mass and TeV-scale leptogenesis in a $D_4$ inverse seesaw model
abstract: An inverse seesaw model for neutrino masses and mixing is proposed, based on the spontaneous breaking of a $D_4$ flavor symmetry. The model simultaneously accounts for the neutrino oscillation parameters, the baryon asymmetry of the Universe through TeV-scale leptogenesis, and makes predictions for charged-lepton flavor violation (cLFV) that are consistent with present experimental limits. A phenomenological analysis shows that the model is consistent with the observed neutrino oscillation data for both normal and inverted mass orderings. Successful leptogenesis is realized for the lightest pseudo-Dirac pair in the multi-TeV range. The predicted cLFV branching ratios lie well below experimental upper bounds, ensuring compatibility with existing constraints. These results establish the model as a viable framework that links low-energy neutrino observables to TeV-scale leptogenesis and cLFV phenomenology.

title: Spectral function approach in NuWro: modeling of multinucleon final states in quasielastic scattering
abstract: Neutrino-oscillation experiments performed in the few-GeV energy region create an urgent demand for a significant improvement in the accuracy of modeling of neutrino interactions with atomic nuclei. Here, we report an updated implementation of the spectral function approach in the \nuwro{} Monte Carlo generator, which consistently treats multinucleon final-states in quasielastic scattering at the inclusive and exclusive level. After validating its accuracy against inclusive electron-scattering data, we compare its predictions to various neutrino cross sections from MicroBooNE. We find that with the multinucleon contribution, these data are reproduced with values of $\chi^2$ per degree of freedom of 0.8--2.5, compared to 2.3--7.3 without it

title: Search for single vector-like quark production in opposite-sign dilepton final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
abstract: A search is presented for single production of a vector-like top quark T, decaying into the standard model top quark and Higgs boson, in a final state including two opposite-sign leptons (electrons or muons), jets, and missing transverse momentum. The data were recorded by the CMS experiment in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV at the CERN LHC in the years 2016$-$2018, and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of up to 138 fb$^{-1}$. No excess in data over the background expectations is observed. Upper limits at 95% confidence level on the product of the T production cross section and its decay branching fraction to tH are set. The observed limits are 2.0 pb at a T mass 600 GeV and 0.3 pb at $M_\mathrm{T}$ = 1200 GeV, with a minimum of 0.1 pb at $M_\mathrm{T}$ = 1000 GeV. This is the first search for single vector-like T quark production, followed by a decay to a top quark and the Higgs boson, in opposite-sign dilepton final states.

title: Search for single production of a vector-like B' quark decaying to a top quark and a W boson in the single-lepton final state in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
abstract: A search is presented for the single production of a narrow-width vector-like B' quark that decays to a t quark and a W boson. This search targets a single-lepton final state, where a muon or electron originates either from the semileptonic decay of the t quark or from the leptonic decay of the W boson, with the other particle decaying hadronically. The (semi-)leptonic portion of the event is reconstructed from an electron or muon, missing transverse momentum, and a small-radius jet identified as a b quark jet if the muon or electron originates from the t quark. The hadronic portion of the event is reconstructed as a single large-radius jet. The originating particle of the large-radius jet is identified using a neural-network-based tagger, and the dominant background contributions are modeled from data using a neural autoregressive flow network. The data were collected from 2016 to 2018 by the CMS experiment at the LHC in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. This search is the most sensitive to date to the production of single narrow-width B' quarks. It excludes electroweak-singlet B' quarks with $\Gamma/m_\mathrm{B'}$ = 5% for masses between 0.8 and 1.23 TeV. Limits are also placed on the production cross section of single B' quarks produced in association with t quarks, and on the coupling factor of the B' quark to electroweak bosons.

title: Search for charged Higgs bosons decaying into top and bottom quarks in lepton+jets final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
abstract: A search is presented for charged Higgs bosons (H$^\pm$) in proton-proton (pp) collision events via the pp $\to$ (b)H$^\pm$ processes, with H$^\pm$ decaying into top (t) and bottom (b) quarks. The search targets final states with one lepton, missing transverse momentum, and two or more b jets. The analysis is based on data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV with the CMS detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. We search for charged Higgs bosons in the 200 GeV to 1 TeV mass range. The results are interpreted within the generalized two-Higgs-doublet model (g2HDM). This model predicts additional Yukawa couplings of the Higgs bosons to the top quark $\rho_\mathrm{tt}$, the top and charm quark $\rho_\mathrm{tc}$, and the top and up quark $\rho_\mathrm{tu}$. This search focuses on the real components of $\rho_\mathrm{tt}$ and $\rho_\mathrm{tc}$, which are probed up to values of unity. An excess is observed with respect to the standard model expectation with a local significance of 2.4 standard deviations for a signal with an H$^\pm$ boson mass ($m_{\mathrm{H}^\pm}$) of 600 GeV. Limits are derived on the product of the cross section $\sigma$(pp $\to$ (b)H$^\pm$) and branching fraction $\mathcal{B}$(H$^\pm$ $\to$ tb, t $\to$ b$\ell\nu$), where $\ell$ = e, $\mu$. The values of $\rho_\mathrm{tc} \gtrsim$ 0.11$-$0.38 are excluded at 95% confidence level, depending on the $m_{\mathrm{H}^\pm}$ and $\rho_\mathrm{tt}$ assumptions. The results represent the first search for charged Higgs bosons within the g2HDM framework and complement the existing results on additional neutral Higgs bosons performed on the same-sign top quark pair, three top quark, or four top quark pair final states, constraining extra Yukawa couplings for the neutral Higgs boson below the TeV scale.

title: Reconstruction of Interstellar Cosmic Ray Anisotropy via Heliospheric Propagation Modeling and SVD Inversion
abstract: Ground-based experiments such as the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the High-Altitude Water Cherenkov Gamma-Ray Observatory detect cosmic-ray anisotropy on Earth, but magnetic deflections within the heliosphere complicate interpretation. Understanding the original spatial distribution of cosmic rays in the interstellar medium requires modeling particle propagation across the heliospheric boundary. We constructed a simulated transport model that backtracks antiprotons from Earth to the interstellar medium and maps spatial transfer probabilities across energies using HEALPix representations. Because our transfer matrices are singular, inversion relies on singular value decom- position regularization. Ground-based observations lose the equatorial North-South anisotropy component, severely degrading interstellar map recovery. We developed a geometric circle-fitting algorithm to estimate and reintroduce the missing component into the observed signals. Our results show that restoring the North-South anisotropy en- ables more accurate recovery of the interstellar dipole structure. Furthermore, Poisson statistical fluctuations on the detected event counts dominate matrix-transformation errors when spread over multiple energies.

title: Probing the chromo-electric dipole moment of top quark near the toponium production threshold at LHC
abstract: The recent observation of an excess near the kinematic $t\bar{t}$ production threshold by the CMS and ATLAS collaborations suggests the existence of a color-singlet and $S$-wave quasi-bound state of top quark. Due to the non-relativistic nature of top and anti-top quarks in this threshold region, toponium production provides an ideal system to probe the anomalous dipole moments of the top quark. In this work, we investigate the impact of chromo-electric dipole moment (CEDM) in $t\bar{t}$-gluon vertex on toponium production at the LHC. We implement the enhanced near-threshold production of the spin-0 color-singlet toponium state $\eta_t$ via gluon fusion. The resonant toponium contribution is then combined with the continuum $t\bar{t}$ production amplitude, including the interference effects induced by the top CEDM. Furthermore, we construct a set of asymmetries based on the angular distributions of charged leptons in the leptonic decay channel of $t\bar{t}$. Finally, we derive the expected exclusion limit on the top quark CEDM parameter $d_t^g$ using these lepton angular asymmetries.

title: Pair production of $h$ in the $U(1)_X$SSM
abstract: Higgs pair production provides an important probe of the Higgs self-interaction and the Higgs potential structure. We study the lightest neutral Higgs pair production process $gg \to hh$ via gluon fusion at the 14 TeV LHC, in the $U(1)_X$ supersymmetric standard model. As a $U(1)$ extension of the minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM), this model introduces new superfields that bring additional one-loop contributions to the production amplitude. We analyze the parameter dependence of the cross section numerically and present contour distributions in two-dimensional parameter planes. The results indicate that the gauge couplings $g_X$ and $g_{YX}$ are the most sensitive parameters, and the model yields sizable new physics corrections under current experimental constraints. This work helps to understand Higgs physics in the $U(1)_X$SSM and guides new physics searches at the high-luminosity LHC.

title: Modular $S_4$ Inverse Seesaw at the LZ High-Recoil Frontier
abstract: The extension of the LUX--ZEPLIN nuclear-recoil analysis to approximately $270\,\mathrm{keV}$ probes a qualitatively new dark-matter regime in which endothermic scattering can suppress conventional low-energy recoils and concentrate the surviving spectrum near the Galactic high-velocity tail. We construct a modular-$S_4$ realization in which a minimal $2N_R+2S$ inverse seesaw accounts for lepton flavor, while a separate pair of Standard-Model-singlet fermions forms the pseudo-Dirac state relevant for high-recoil xenon scattering. The sectors share a common complex modulus $\tau$, so the modular forms selected by charged-lepton and neutrino data also enter the operators generating the dark Dirac mass and Majorana splitting. Our scan yields $181447$ lepton-sector solutions satisfying $\chi^2_{\ell+\nu}<30$, distributed among several disconnected modular regions, and predicts one effectively massless light neutrino at leading order. Restoring the physical scales allows TeV-scale heavy quasi-Dirac neutral fermions with small non-unitarity. We subsequently scan $2\times10^6$ dark-sector points only over flavor-accepted values of $\tau$ and identify common-modulus solutions in the LZ-oriented region $300\,\mathrm{GeV}\le m_\chi\le2\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and $300\,\mathrm{keV}\le\delta\le400\,\mathrm{keV}$. An exploratory two-bin Poisson likelihood, including endothermic xenon kinematics, the Helm form factor, Standard-Halo-Model velocities, Gaussian energy smearing, and profiling over the signal normalization, gives a best grid point at $(m_\chi,\delta)\simeq(1.847\,\mathrm{TeV},371.5\,\mathrm{keV})$, close to the terrestrial inelastic kinematic ceiling. The construction provides a direct link between modular lepton flavor, TeV-scale inverse-seesaw dynamics, and high-recoil inelastic dark matter.

title: Mixed leptogenesis sources and low-energy neutrino portals
abstract: A mixed leptogenesis source and its low-energy neutrino portal depend on the same heavy-particle amplitudes. We determine how this common origin restricts matching cancellations and the scalar population produced during reheating. For two Majorana mass levels, each containing a degenerate pair, the inclusive lepton-number-violating invariant fixes an allowed norm domain for the mixed dimension-five coefficient at specified threshold strengths. An aligned flavour texture makes the conventional source vanish as a matrix and gives equal coupling norms for the two massive neutrinos. A continuous family preserves the neutrino-mass fit while relating the source to unequal light coupling strengths. The matched couplings give benchmark vacuum lifetimes of $1.62\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{s}$ and $2.80\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{s}$, while reheating normalized to the baryon abundance determines the primary spectrum. In the massless Born approximation with dilute outgoing states, bath-produced scalars carry $4.81\times10^{-5}$ of the primary scalar energy but contribute $11.1$ times its variance. The positive production functional converts the matching constraint into a conditional variance bound. We derive the scalar-mass dependence of stimulated emission and the Hartree moment equation, keeping the scalar mass and quartic as renormalized matching inputs. These results link the leptogenesis source to light-neutrino decay and the finite-density quantities entering subsequent coupled transport.

title: Interplay of Lorentz Invariance Violation and Earth's Matter Potential in High-Energy Neutrinos
abstract: Searches for Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) in the neutrino sector have traditionally focused on non-standard neutrino oscillations induced by LIV in vacuum. In this work, we study anisotropic LIV in matter. First, we review vacuum LIV phenomenology, explaining the energy and direction dependence of sidereal modulations for anisotropic coefficients in the Standard Model Extension. We then demonstrate that for high-energy neutrinos, the interplay between anisotropic LIV operators and the Earth's matter potential produces distinct, observable signatures absent in the vacuum case. We identify a crossover regime where the energy-dependent LIV Hamiltonian becomes comparable to the matter potential, leading to strong interference effects. By analyzing the propagation of neutrinos through a realistic Earth model, we establish three key phenomenological consequences: (1) direction-dependent resonant enhancements of oscillation probabilities, (2) a macroscopic breakdown of neutrino-antineutrino symmetry for CPT-even operators, and (3) a significant increase of the $\nu_\tau$ flux due to LIV-driven injection of high-energy neutrinos into the $\tau$ regeneration cycle. These results highlight that accounting for the interplay between LIV and matter is essential for future LIV searches at large-scale neutrino telescopes.

title: In-ice Radio Signatures of Cosmic Ray Particle Cascades
abstract: To detect ultra-high-energy neutrinos, experiments such as the Askaryan Radio Array and the Radio Neutrino Observatory in Greenland target the radio emission induced by these particles as they cascade in the ice. This is done by, amongst others, using deep in-ice antennas at the South Pole or in Greenland. A crucial step toward this goal is the characterization of the in-ice radio emission from cosmic-ray-induced particle showers. These showers form a primary background for neutrino searches, but can also be used to validate the detection principle and provide calibration signals for in-ice radio detectors. In this work, we use the Monte-Carlo framework FAERIE to perform the first characterization of cosmic ray signals with simulations that incorporate both their in-air and in-ice emissions. We investigate cosmic ray signatures such as their radiation energy, timing, polarization and frequency spectrum and quantify how they depend on shower properties. These results provide key guidelines for cosmic-ray identification and cosmic-ray/neutrino discrimination in future in-ice radio experiments.

title: From Dirac Neutrino Mass to Dark Radiation: An $A_4$-Symmetric FIMP Dark Matter Framework
abstract: We propose a unified $A_4\times Z_2\times U(1)_L$ framework for generating small Dirac neutrino masses and address dark matter through feeble interactions in an extended particle physics model. The model extends the Standard Model with a pair of heavy vector-like neutral $A_4$ fermions $N(N_{L,R})$, two additional flavon fields $\eta$ and $\phi$, among which $\eta$ being a $Z_2$-odd inert scalar and a dark-sector vector-like fermion field $\chi$. We numerically explore the Dirac-sector Yukawa couplings and identify the parameter region that is consistent with the {\tt NuFit 6.1} neutrino oscillation data at the $3\sigma$ level. The dark matter candidate $\chi$, stabilized by the $Z_2$ symmetry, is produced non-thermally through the decay $N_L\rightarrow\chi+\eta$. By solving the Boltzmann equation, we find that the observed relic abundance, $\Omega_{\rm DM}h^2\simeq0.12$, can be reproduced for freeze-in couplings of order $\lambda\sim10^{-5.5}$--$10^{-7.5}$ over the considered dark matter mass range. For the chosen parameter space, we also verify the interaction rate remains below the Hubble expansion rate, confirming $\chi$ never reaches thermal equilibrium. Thus, our results demonstrate that the model provides a consistent realization of Dirac neutrino masses and FIMP dark matter within a common symmetry-based setup. The presence of light Dirac RH neutrinos can contribute to the dark radiation and hence the effective degrees of freedom via thermal and non-thermal processes. We further estimate the contribution of the light right-handed neutrinos to \(\Delta N_{\rm eff}\), finding a maximum characteristic value of \(\Delta N_{\rm eff}\simeq0.14\) in the benchmark parameter region.

title: Does $\psi(4660)$ exist?
abstract: The nature of the vector charmoniumlike states $\psi(4360)$ and $\psi(4660)$ is controversial, and the existence of the $\psi(4660)$ has been questioned: the BESIII measurement of $e^+e^-\to \Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$ reveals a nearly flat line shape around 4.66 GeV with a nonzero value at threshold, in contrast to the near-threshold enhancement reported earlier by Belle. We address this puzzle in an S-wave coupled-channel framework for $e^+e^-$ annihilation in $\sqrt{s}\in [4.0,5.0]~\mathrm{GeV}$. The formalism includes the open-charm channels $\Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$, $\Xi_c^+\bar{\Xi}_c^-$, $\Xi_c^0\bar{\Xi}_c^0$ (via SU(3) symmetry), the inelastic $\psi(2S)\pi^+\pi^-$ channel mediated by $\sigma(500)$ and $f_0(980)$, and the bare $\psi(4360)$ and $\psi(4660)$ as the 4S and 5S excitations. Short-range contact potentials in the heavy-quark limit are used, and the amplitudes follow from solving the Lippmann-Schwinger equation. A combined fit to Belle and BESIII data on $e^+e^-\to \Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$ and $e^+e^-\to \psi(2S)\pi^+\pi^-$ yields two poles, at $(4401.93 \pm 16.96i)~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $(4631.39\pm 62.96i)~\mathrm{MeV}$, for the $\psi(4360)$ and $\psi(4660)$. Tracing the pole trajectories as the coupling to the bare states is switched off, we show that both poles originate from the bare $4S$ and $5S$ states strongly renormalized by coupled-channel dynamics. In particular, the $\psi(4660)$ emerges as a broad resonance about 58~MeV above the $\Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$ threshold; its flat line shape follows from this threshold interplay, providing evidence for its existence. Results are cutoff-robust.

title: Dark Matter Stability from residual flavour symmetries
abstract: We propose a model-independent framework in which Dark Matter stability emerges naturally from residual discrete $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries left unbroken by the spontaneous breaking of continuous flavour symmetries, both Abelian and non-Abelian. No ad hoc stabilizing symmetry is required, as Dark Matter stability is an inherent consequence of the underlying flavour dynamics. As an explicit example, we construct a prototype model based on a $\text{SU}(2)_\text{F} \otimes \text{U}(1)_\text{F}$ Froggatt-Nielsen symmetry, which successfully reproduces the observed charged lepton mass spectrum and the PMNS mixing matrix, while identifying the lightest sterile neutrino as a stable Dark Matter candidate. Furthermore, we study the Dark Matter phenomenology within our model in the freeze-in regime, including production channels mediated by higher-dimensional operators suppressed by the cutoff scale $\Lambda$. Our analysis shows that continuous flavour symmetries can provide a unified, self-consistent framework addressing both the flavour puzzle and the origin, stability, and production of Dark Matter.

title: Cosmology & Astrophysics of the Dark Dimension with Bulk Majorana Neutrinos
abstract: Recently, the possibility of having sterile Majorana neutrinos charged under $B-L$ gauge symmetry in the bulk of the dark dimension has been explored. We point out a cosmological restriction on the Majorana mass of bulk neutrinos leading to mass $\gtrsim 100~{\rm GeV}$. This avoids the over-production of Kaluza-Klein neutrino towers in the early universe thus resolving the cosmological neutrino catastrophe of extra dimension scenarios. If the mass of the bulk neutrino is at the lower end of this bound, it can potentially also explain the recently observed Fermi halo excess on gamma rays through the evaporation of long-lived 5d (i.e. dark) black holes through Hawking radiation to bulk neutrinos, which promptly decay into standard model particles.

title: Cosmological Consequences of a Highly Decoupled Right-handed Neutrino
abstract: In the minimal type-I seesaw, one right-handed neutrino (RHN) can decouple from neutrino mass generation. Such a state is usually neglected, yet its feeble couplings make it long-lived, and it can dominate the energy density of the Universe before decaying. We study this in a minimal $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, where the RHNs are produced through $B-L$ gauge interactions, for the cases of a decoupled lightest RHN $N_1$ and a decoupled heaviest RHN $N_3$. The resulting early matter-dominated era dilutes the baryon asymmetry, and for decoupled $N_3$ it also delays the equilibration of the charged-lepton Yukawa interactions, allowing a lighter $N_1$ to generate the asymmetry in the unflavoured regime. Breaking $U(1)_{B-L}$ forms cosmic strings whose gravitational-wave background acquires a spectral break from the early matter-dominated era, with a frequency set by the decoupled RHN mass and the lightest neutrino mass, within reach of future detectors such as SKA, THEIA, LISA, $\mu$ARES, DECIGO and ET.

title: Chiral partners of strange doubly heavy baryons: Mass relations and decay predictions after the 2026 LHCb discoveries
abstract: Three spectacular LHCb measurements in 2026---the observations of $\Omega_{cc}^{+}$, $\Xi_{cc}^{+}$, and the beauty-strange structure $B_{s0}^{*}(5700)^0$---make possible an experimentally constrained analysis of chiral partners of strange doubly heavy baryons. The doubly charmed masses test the earlier Ma--Harada prediction and support a compact, internally S-wave $cc$ color source. We combine this comparison with the heavy-quark--diquark hyperfine relation and with chiral gaps from the theory of chiral doublers, to construct consistent $ccs$ and $bbs$ parity multiplets and a conditional extension to $bcs$. Under meson-to-baryon parity-gap transfer, the $349$ MeV input from the $D_s$ sector gives negative-parity $ccs$ targets near $4.075$ and $4.183$ GeV. The separate $332$ MeV input from the $B_s$ sector fixes the $bbs$ partner masses relative to their unknown ground-state mass, conditional on the new beauty-strange state's chiral-partner assignment. We relate the differences of hyperfine splittings in the two parity sectors of mesons and baryons, and identify equal reduced single-pion widths, an E1 reduced-width ratio $1:8:4:5$, and a kaon selection rule whose leading predictions contain no new transition parameters. Absolute widths are estimated by matching the published Bardeen--Eichten--Hill and Harada--Rho--Sasaki meson calculations to a common convention. In the reference calculation, all members of the predicted $ccs$ and $bbs$ multiplets are narrow. In the proposed $\Omega_{QQ}\pi^0$ and $\Omega_{QQ}\gamma$ searches at LHCb, these states are expected to produce peaks dominated by detector resolution, allowing their masses and decay patterns to be investigated even when their intrinsic widths remain unresolved. The upper charm state is above kaon threshold but protected in the spectator limit.

title: A Comprehensive Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event: A Minimal $U(1)_B$ Dark Sector and Its Experimental Tests
abstract: The $248$ keV nuclear-recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation, in which scattering converts the DM particle into a slightly heavier state. We provide a comprehensive study of this interpretation in an anomaly-free model of gauged baryon number, where a new vector boson, $Z_B$, mediates interactions between DM and quarks. Breaking the baryonic gauge symmetry generates the new particle masses and a small splitting between two DM states, while a residual symmetry keeps the lighter state stable. We identify regions compatible with the LZ candidate, the observed DM abundance, and current ATLAS and CMS dijet constraints. Within the scanned domain, these regions span DM masses $m_\chi\simeq0.19$-$4.5$ TeV, mediator masses $M_{Z_B}\simeq0.05$-$5.0$ TeV, and gauge couplings $g_B\simeq0.004$-$0.74$, with correlated values of these parameters. A representative thermal solution has $m_\chi=1$ TeV, $M_{Z_B}=1.44$ TeV, $g_B\simeq0.228$, and a mass splitting of $300$ keV. A small electroweak mixing allows the heavier DM state to decay rapidly, suppressing unwanted signals from its surviving population. This interpretation can be tested through complementary measurements: additional LZ and XENONnT data can establish whether the high-energy recoil signal persists, ATLAS and CMS Run-3 dijet searches can probe the mediator mass and coupling, and a dedicated IceCube analysis of four-quark final states can test DM capture and annihilation in the Sun. Together, these measurements can test complementary parts of the surviving region and assess whether the LZ candidate is consistent with this interpretation.

title: $t\bar t$ production as a probe of dimension-six SMEFT at higher orders
abstract: We study top-antitop pair production in proton-proton collisions within the Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT) at dimension six. We focus on the top chromomagnetic operator $C_{tG}$ together with the four-quark operators relevant for unpolarized $t{\bar t}$ production. We analyze the top-quark single-differential transverse-momentum ($p_T$) and rapidity ($y$) distributions and the double-differential distributions in $p_T$ and $y$ ($p_T\times y$) at 13~TeV, and we present projections for 13.6~TeV using the same binning. Our highest-order setup combines next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) Standard Model (SM) predictions with approximate NNLO SM-SMEFT interference corrections. We find that higher-order QCD effects are essential for a stable SMEFT interpretation, yielding substantially more robust bounds and milder parameter degeneracies. The strongest sensitivity is obtained for $C_{tG}$. In the combined highest-order analysis of the 13-TeV results and 13.6-TeV projections, we obtain sensitivity to effective scales up to $3.9~\TeV$. Our results show that higher-order differential top-pair production provides a precise and theoretically controlled probe of the top chromomagnetic interaction.

title: Theoretical calculations for $t{\bar t}H$ production
abstract: We calculate higher-order perturbative corrections for $t{\bar t}H$ production. By adding second-order and third-order soft-gluon corrections to NLO QCD and NLO electroweak (EW) results, we present total and differential cross sections at LHC energies through approximate N$^3$LO (aN$^3$LO) in QCD and NLO in EW. Our aN$^3$LO QCD + NLO EW results provide significant enhancements and a reduced scale dependence for the cross section and the top-quark transverse-momentum and rapidity distributions.

title: The $R$-Process Alliance: On J0010$-$1735, an Accreted, Chemically Unusual, Metal-poor Star with $R$-process Enhancement
abstract: We present a detailed chemo-dynamical analysis of the chemically peculiar very metal-poor ([Fe/H]$=-2.22\pm 0.11$) Milky Way (MW) halo star, 2MASS J00101758$-$1735387 (hereafter J0010-1735), discovered by the $R$-Process Alliance. We derive abundances for 45 elements, including 28 neutron-capture elements, and confirm that \thestar\ is highly $r$-process-enhanced, with [Eu/Fe]=$+1.30$. The light, $\alpha$, and Fe-peak element abundances ratios relative to Fe are all sub-solar, aside from C, Si, and most extremely, Ca. We investigate three possible formation scenarios based on the star's chemical abundances and orbital kinematics: whether it formed in the \textit{in-situ} MW halo, in a MW dwarf galaxy satellite, or in a satellite of the Magellanic Cloud system. Using the position of \thestar\ in the [Mg/Mn]--[Al/Fe] plane, the abundance pattern of both the light and heavy elements, and the kinematics, we conclude that J0010-1735 most plausibly originated in a now-disrupted ultra-faint dwarf galaxy that was accreted into the MW halo. We examine potential chemical enrichment scenarios of J0010-1735, including one similar to the $r$-process-enhanced UFD Reticulum II, or enrichment via a sub-Chandrasekhar Type Ia SNe, potentially supplemented by a Ca-rich gap transient and by a separate neutron-rich site that facilitated $r$-process enrichment. A nuclear cosmochronometric age of $12.5\pm4.2$ Gyr is derived from the [Th/Eu] ratio, consistent with an ancient origin in one of the earliest star-forming systems in the universe.

title: Seeking a possible approach to understanding the origin of the proton mass using twist-4 contributions in inclusive reactions
abstract: Most of the mass of the visible universe originates from the strong interaction. Quantitatively reproducing the origin of the nucleon mass is one of the important challenges in fundamental science. Since the next-generation Electron-Ion Collider has identified resolving this problem as one of its major goals, further theoretical studies are needed to develop approaches to investigating the origin experimentally. In this paper, we explore the possibility of evaluating the ``gluon condensate term'' which is particularly difficult to determine among the contributions to the nucleon mass, using high-energy scattering experiments. We first express the gluon condensate term in terms of experimentally accessible twist-4 lightcone matrix elements. We then derive, for the first time, analytic formulas for the cross section including all twist-4 contributions from pure quark, quark-gluon, and pure gluon matrix elements in $ep$ collisions, and show how these contributions can be related to the gluon condensate term.

title: Search for the $\boldsymbol{B^0 \to K^0_{\rm S} \tau^+ \tau^-}$ decay
abstract: We present the first search for $B^0 \to K^0_{\rm S} \tau^+\tau^-$ decays. We look for signal decays in $B^0\bar B^0$ events produced in asymmetric-energy electron-positron collisions. This work uses samples from the Belle and Belle~II detectors, comprising 1.16 billion $\Upsilon(4S)$ events. In $\Upsilon(4S)\to B^0\bar{B}^0$ decays, the non-signal $\bar{B}^0$ meson is fully reconstructed in a hadronic channel. For the signal $B^0$ meson, $\tau$-lepton decays into final states with a single charged particle are selected. We observe no evidence for the signal and set an upper limit on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}(B^0\to K^0_{\rm S} \tau^+\tau^-) < 8.3 \times 10^{-4}$ at the 90\% confidence level. Combining this with the recent measurement of the isospin-partner decay $B^+\to K^+\tau^+\tau^-$, we determine an upper limit $\mathcal{B}(B\to K\tau^+\tau^-) < 5.4\times10^{-4}$ at the 90\% confidence level.

title: Quasi-four-body semileptonic decay $\bar B^0\to a_0(1450)^+ (\to\pi^+ \eta)\ell^-\bar\nu_\ell$ within $a_0(1450)$-resonance leading-twist LCDA under QCDSR
abstract: The finite width of broad scalar resonances should be taken into account when relating semileptonic $B$-meson transitions to experimentally reconstructable multihadron final states. The quasi-four-body semileptonic decays $\bar B^0\to a_0(1450)^+ (\to\pi \eta)\ell^-\bar\nu_\ell$ with $\ell=(e,\mu,\tau)$ provide a platform for investigating the scalar $a_0(1450)^+$-resonance as the lowest-Fock-state quark-antiquark component. We calculate the first five odd $\xi$-moments of $a_0(1450)$-resonance twist-2 light-cone distribution amplitude (LCDA) using QCDSR within the background-field theory, including vacuum condensates up to dimension six. Based on these moments, two twist-2 LCDA schemes are constructed: a light-cone harmonic oscillator model (S1), whose free parameters are fitted to the first five odd moments, and a truncated Gegenbauer expansion (S2) retaining only $a_{1,3}(\mu)$. The $\bar{B}^0 \to a_0(1450)^+$ transition form factors are then calculated using light-cone sum rules. At large recoil region, we present the TFFs with different scheme. The finite-width effect of $a_0(1450)$-resonance is further incorporated through a two-channel Flatt\'e parametrization including the $\pi \eta$ and $K\bar{K}$ channels. The $\pi \eta$ invariant-mass distribution exhibits a pronounced resonance peak around $s\simeq m_{a_0(1450)}^2$. The spectra of the electron and muon channels are nearly identical, while the $\tau$-channel is significantly suppressed because the larger lepton mass reduces the available phase space. After integration over the full quasi-four-body phase space, the branching fractions are given. We expect that these results will provide useful guidance for future experimental and theoretical studies of $\bar B^0\to a_0(1450)^+ (\to\pi \eta)\ell^-\bar\nu_\ell$ decay and help improve our understanding of the internal structure of $a_0(1450)$.

title: Quantum numbers of excited $\Xi_c^\prime$ and $\Omega_c$ baryons and the $P$-wave $\Sigma_c$ spectrum
abstract: Heavy quark effective theory (HQET) permits seven $P$-wave states in each of the $\Sigma_c$, $\Xi_c^\prime$, and $\Omega_c$ flavor-sextet sectors, yet the experimentally visible spectra differ strikingly among the three sectors. We show that strong decays, kinematic thresholds, and configuration mixing act as a dynamical filter between the underlying multiplet structure and the observed resonance spectrum. Using QCD sum rules for the masses and light-cone sum rules for the strong decays, we find that only four $\Sigma_c$, four $\Xi_c^\prime$, and five $\Omega_c$ states are sufficiently narrow to contribute to experimentally identifiable resonance structures. The four narrow $\Xi_c$ states, $\Xi_c(2882)$, $\Xi_c(2923)$, $\Xi_c(2939)$, and $\Xi_c(2965)$, and the four narrow $\Omega_c$ states, $\Omega_c(3000)$, $\Omega_c(3050)$, $\Omega_c(3066)$, and $\Omega_c(3090)$, exhibit similar mass-splitting patterns and provide spectroscopic anchors for a common $\lambda$-mode multiplet structure, supporting the successive assignments $J^P=1/2^-,3/2^-,3/2^-$, and $5/2^-$. We tentatively interpret $\Omega_c(3119)$ as a predominantly $\rho$-mode state with $J^P=3/2^-$. With this multiplet structure constrained by the $\Xi_c$ and $\Omega_c$ spectra, we predict four relatively resolvable $P$-wave $\Sigma_c$ states that may overlap within the observed $\Sigma_c(2800)$ and $\Sigma_c(2900)$ structures, providing concrete targets for future amplitude analyses.

title: Proton Structure from Neural Simulation-Based Inference at the LHC
abstract: The precise determination of the parton distribution functions (PDFs) of the proton is an essential ingredient for LHC analyses, including for those at the upcoming High-Luminosity LHC. So far, PDFs are determined from global fits to binned low-dimensional data obtained from unfolded hard-scattering cross section measurements. In this work we demonstrate for the first time the feasibility of neural simulation-based inference (NSBI) for constraining the proton PDFs using a high-dimensional unbinned data set. Exploiting the full statistical power of unbinned data removes the loss of information inherited by the binning procedure. As a proof-of-concept, we determine the gluon PDF from simulated data of top quark pair production at the LHC with $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. Taking into account both experimental and theoretical systematic uncertainties in the detector-level features, we demonstrate how the NSBI pipeline achieves significant improvements in precision compared to low-dimensional binned analyses. Our results illustrate the potential of unbinned inference to reduce the reliance on coarse approximations of uncertainties and their correlations entering PDF determinations, hence contributing to a new paradigm of unbinned detector-level ML-assisted measurements at the LHC.

title: Parton and nuclear dynamics at large $x$: the CJ26 global QCD analysis
abstract: We present the new CTEQ-JLab global QCD analysis, called CJ26, that simultaneously fits parton distribution functions of the proton and nuclear effects in deuteron targets. This work includes, for the first time in a global fit, the full set of JLab 6 GeV inclusive DIS measurements and the first published JLab 12 GeV data. The analysis focuses on the large-$x$ region, and carefully treats the interplay between higher-twist effects and off-shell corrections in low-energy proton and deuteron target data. We discuss their effect on quark and gluon distributions, and highlight the importance of quantifying the experimental correlated systematic uncertainty to achieve fits of the highest accuracy. We also outline how upcoming data may help unravel the nuclear and partonic dynamics in light nuclei. The extracted next-to-leading order parton distributions are available on the CJ web pages in LHAPDF format for general use, accompanied by leading- and higher-twist structure functions calculated with the simultaneously fitted PDFs, higher-twist corrections, and off-shell corrections. This write up clarifies several points that became clearer while finalizing the CJ26 paper and can be read as a companion to the latter.

title: Mass and decay angles in the $\Xi_c$--$\Xi_c'$ mixing tension: Virtual hybrids and a single-direction criterion
abstract: We compare three definitions of $\Xi_c$--$\Xi_c'$ mixing within a constituent-quark model: a spin-component probability angle, a common-source overlap angle, and an SU(3)-breaking mass-operator angle. The probability angle is $3.11^\circ$, while the two operator-based definitions give $2.48$--$2.58^\circ$; a second parameter set gives $2.38$--$2.49^\circ$. The operator-based angles are closer to the lattice determinations $1.2(1)^\circ$ and $0.810(50)(200)^\circ$, but remain larger. We then couple conventional $qsQ$ states to virtual $qsQg$ configurations, where $q=u,d$ and $Q=c,b$. An orbital-$S$-wave chromomagnetic transition containing both $j_{Qg}=1/2$ and $3/2$ raises the source and mass-operator charm angles to $2.67$--$3.16^\circ$ when normalized to reference short-range mass shifts. The hybrid probability stays below $1.7\%$, and the corresponding bottom angles are $0.42$--$0.48^\circ$. Eliminating the hybrid sector gives a rank-one mass correction precisely when all weighted transitions select the same retained-state combination. The mode-resolved calculation separates the flavor-breaking response that changes the mixing angle from the response that generates a second transition direction. The accompanying effective-current relation connects this mass analysis to radiative and semileptonic amplitudes through their current matrix elements.

title: MadNIS, Ready for Production at LO
abstract: We extend neural multi-channel importance sampling in MadNIS to full proton-proton processes in a production-ready event-generation setup. We benchmark a wide range of LHC processes, including multi-jet, vector-boson, top-quark, and Higgs production, and obtain event-generation speed-ups of up to a factor of 250 without process-specific hyperparameter tuning. We quantify how the speed-up scales with training time and final-state multiplicity, and when the training cost amortizes. MadNIS will become the default for phase-space integration and event generation at leading order in MadGraph.

title: Kernel moments and thermodynamic stability in nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio models
abstract: We study thermodynamic consistency and stability in a covariant two-flavor nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at zero chemical potential in the homogeneous quark mean-field approximation. A controlled large-source expansion gives a sufficient entropy-sign criterion directly from Euclidean kernel moments, without locating propagator poles. At fixed couplings and kernel, every admissible positive Gaussian mixture develops negative total entropy at sufficiently large source mass for each fixed positive temperature. In a separate light-source fit to pion observables and a subtracted condensate, one quartic-exponent kernel has positive entropy and heat capacity for all $T>0$, while $dP/d\epsilon=s/C_V$ exceeds unity on a finite interval. This constructive example separates thermal positivity from the static EOS slope test. Numerical refits show that the enhancement weakens with the condensate input, and a certified counterexample excludes uniform thermal positivity over the adopted matching domain. The results provide diagnostics of the mean-field functional, rather than a preferred phenomenological kernel. Omitted thermal mesons can change the low-temperature slope test, and the static derivative does not determine a real-time front velocity.

title: Gluon GTMDs in the exclusive electroproduction of heavy-quark pairs
abstract: We study exclusive electroproduction of heavy quark-antiquark pairs off nucleons in the framework of generalized transverse momentum dependent parton distributions (GTMDs) for gluons. The short-distance part of the process is treated at leading order in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics and in first order in a collinear expansion, which allows identification with the description in terms of Generalized Parton Distributions (GPDs). For the results for the structure functions in terms of GTMDs and GPDs we consider only unpolarized (spin-averaged) nucleons, but include all possible azimuthal modulations that can arise. The presented results extend known expressions in the literature and are relevant for experimental studies of this exclusive process at the future Electron Ion Collider. Furthermore, we introduce a convenient decomposition of the gluon-gluon correlation matrix in terms of GTMDs, expanded in a Lorentz basis of symmetric traceless tensors obtained from the partonic momentum $k_T$ and the momentum transfer $\Delta_T$. The adopted notation for the GTMDs relates to the nucleon helicity states at the amplitude level, rather than to polarization states of the incoming nucleon or of the gluons, which makes it more transparent which contributions from helicity difference and helicity flip matrix elements can be accessed with unpolarized nucleon beams.

title: Functional renormalization group study of the quark-meson model beyond the local potential approximation: Kurganov--Tadmor versus the grid method
abstract: We solve the functional renormalization group flow of the two-flavor quark-meson model at finite temperature and quark chemical potential with Litim's regulator, using the Kurganov--Tadmor central scheme and the standard grid method, both in the local potential approximation (LPA) and in an LPA$'$ truncation with running wave function renormalization factors for the pion, sigma, and quark fields. Using the Kurganov--Tadmor scheme as a high-resolution benchmark down to very low temperatures, where the Fermi surface produces the sharpest fronts in the field derivative of the potential, we find that, with sufficiently fine resolution, the grid method gives virtually identical results in both truncations. We discuss the difficulties that the wave function renormalization factors bring into the parametrization of the model and into the flow at finite density, related to the choice of the expansion point. Contrary to some expectations, the peculiar backbending of the first-order phase boundary at low temperature, known from LPA, persists in our implementation of the LPA$'$ truncation, both with a fixed and with a running expansion point.

title: Energy-momentum tensor at small $x$ from gravitational transverse-momentum distributions
abstract: We investigate the momentum-space mechanical properties of small-$x$ gluons and sea quarks using gravitational transverse-momentum distributions (gravitational TMDs). For gluons, we formulate these distributions using the light-front gauge-invariant canonical energy-momentum tensor and derive their relations to ordinary TMD correlators, identifying momentum densities, the transverse flux of inertia, and transverse stresses. In the eikonal approximation, the longitudinal and transverse canonical gluon momentum densities are determined by the unpolarized distribution, whereas the transverse flux of inertia and transverse stresses vanish. For an unpolarized target, we numerically evaluate the gluon and sea-quark momentum densities using a common initial condition based on the McLerran--Venugopalan model and fixed-coupling leading-order Balitsky--Kovchegov evolution. We also evaluate the sea-quark transverse flux of inertia through the twist-three quark TMD at the high transverse-momentum region. These results illustrate departures from the free-particle relation between canonical transverse momentum and the effective transverse velocity governing inertia flow.

title: Dynamical gluon effects in twist-3 generalized parton distributions of the proton
abstract: Within the Basis Light-Front Quantization framework, we systematically investigate the subleading-twist (twist-3) generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the proton's valence quarks beyond the Wandzura--Wilczek (WW) approximation. The twist-3 GPDs are not independent; through the equations of motion they decompose into a non-genuine contribution and a genuine twist-3 term. The latter encodes quark--quark--gluon correlations and involves interference between the light-front Fock sectors |qqq> and |qqqg>, which are typically neglected in the WW approximation. Using light-front wave functions obtained from diagonalizing the proton light-front Hamiltonian for its |qqq> and |qqqg> Fock components, we compute these GPDs via their overlap representations. To further explore their physical implications, we also evaluate several twist-3--related quantities, including the quark orbital angular momentum, the total quark spin contribution, and the quark spin--orbit correlation. Our results provide new nonperturbative input on higher-twist dynamics particularly multi-parton interference effects relevant for future measurements at the EicC and the EIC.

title: Conserved-charge diffusion in hot and dense QCD matter
abstract: We study the coupled diffusion of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness in hot and dense quark matter using a three-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model with self-consistently generated constituent quark masses. The complete diffusion matrix is evaluated within a relaxation-time kinetic approach, including its diagonal and off-diagonal components. We find that the off-diagonal transport coefficients exhibit distinct temperature and baryon-chemical-potential dependence associated with the flavor-dependent composition of the charge carriers. We further investigate generalized charge diffusivities and mobilities obtained from the corresponding susceptibilities. At finite baryon chemical potential, the baryon and strangeness mobility scales cross, reflecting the different density dependence of their transport coefficients and susceptibilities. The results provide model benchmarks for coupled conserved-charge transport in baryon-rich QCD matter.

title: Color Lorentz force on a transversely polarized quark in the nucleon
abstract: The $x^2$ moment of the genuine twist-3 component of the unpolarized scalar parton distribution function $e(x)$ is related to the average transverse color Lorentz force experienced by a transversely polarized quark in an unpolarized nucleon. This higher-twist quantity probes quark--gluon correlations and provides unique insight into the nonperturbative dynamics of quantum chromodynamics. For the first time, we study the corresponding off-forward matrix element and derive its Lorentz-covariant decomposition in terms of generalized form factors. We calculate these form factors from light-front wave functions obtained by solving the light-front Hamiltonian eigenvalue problem within the Basis Light-Front Quantization framework. Their Fourier transforms provide a spatial picture of the transverse color forces in impact-parameter space. In particular, $\mathscr{F}_2$, whose forward limit is directly related to the twist-3 matrix element $e_2$, can be interpreted as the impact-parameter-space representation of the Boer--Mulders force, providing an intuitive spatial picture of the final-state interaction mechanism underlying the Boer--Mulders effect.

title: Analytic next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to Higgs boson pair production at high energies
abstract: We compute the complete top-quark-induced next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to the form factors entering gluon-induced Higgs boson pair production. We consider the top quark contribution in the limit where the Mandelstam variables are much larger than all other scales involved in the process and compute about a hundred expansion terms in analytic form. They are used to obtain precise numerical results even for fairly low values of the transverse momentum of the Higgs boson. We show that these electroweak corrections at high energies are of the order of $-10\%$. We also discuss the leading logarithmic corrections of the analytic expressions.

title: A toy model for hadronic bonds in exotic hadrons
abstract: Three hadronic-bond mechanisms were proposed in our previous studies to describe near-threshold exotic hadrons in terms of hadronic molecular configurations: the covalent bond arises from the sharing and exchange of valence light quarks between hadronic clusters, the creation bond originates from the activation of coherent sea $q\bar{q}$ degrees of freedom followed by the formation of effective covalent correlations, and the annihilation bond arises from valence $q\bar{q}$ annihilation and the associated mixing with a nearby compact state. A simple toy model was previously constructed only for the covalent bond, and in the present study we extend this model to incorporate the creation and annihilation bonds within a unified framework. The resulting framework organizes covalent-bond configurations as tending to lie below threshold and creation-bond configurations as tending to appear above threshold, while the annihilation bond can shift a pre-existing molecular configuration either downward or upward through mixing with a nearby compact state. An effective activation energy $E_{\rm{act}}$ is introduced for the coherent sea four-quark component involved in the creation bond, with the $Z_c(3900)$ providing the benchmark value $E_{\rm{act}}\sim17~{\rm{MeV}}$. Intriguingly, this value is numerically close to the reported mass of the $X_{17}$ particle, which we previously interpreted as a low-energy bare four-quark structure. This numerical proximity may therefore reflect common low-energy (four-quark) dynamics, although the microscopic connection remains to be established. For the isoscalar $D^*\bar{D}^*B^*\bar{B}^*$ configuration involving the $Z_c(4020)$ and $Z_b(10650)$ creation-bond subsystems linked by two additional covalent bonds, we estimate a binding energy of approximately $36~{\rm{MeV}}$ below its four-meson threshold and propose searches in the $4\mu$ and $4\mu2\pi$ final states.

title: Quantum-Classical Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Reservoir Seepage Equations
abstract: Solving reservoir seepage partial differential equations (PDEs) is critical for hydrocarbon development optimization and production forecasting. Conventional numerical solvers suffer from mesh errors and high computational cost. Standard Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are limited by inefficient parameters. They also face weak high-dimensional representation and poor nonlinear fitting ability. We adapt the Discrete Variable (DV)-Circuit Quantum-Classical Physics-Informed Neural Network (QCPINN) to tackle these drawbacks. This work applies the method to four representative reservoir seepage models. The models cover heterogeneous single-phase pressure diffusion. They also include nonlinear Buckley-Leverett two-phase waterflooding. Another case is adsorption-coupled convection-diffusion compositional flow. The last one refers to fully coupled pressure-saturation two-phase flow with exponential permeability heterogeneity. The QCPINN combines classical preprocessing and postprocessing networks with a DV quantum core. It leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to boost high-dimensional feature mapping. Physical constraints are embedded within the framework to guarantee physically consistent solutions. We evaluate three quantum circuit topologies including Cascade, Cross-mesh and Alternate. Numerical tests prove QCPINNs outperform classical PINNs in prediction accuracy, and the circuit topologies show case-specific performance with clear applicable ranges. This work verifies QCPINN's practicability for reservoir engineering. It bridges quantum computing research with oilfield industrial applications.

title: Measure Neural Mappings
abstract: We introduce and define measure neural mappings (MNMs), which combine measure-dependent neural transport with ensemble consistency for learning operators on probability measures. Ensemble consistency requires outputs from growing ensembles sampled from an input law to converge to the specified population output in probability. We establish quantitative continuum limits for attention on noncompact laws under strong sub-Gaussian and tail-integrability assumptions. These laws accommodate unbounded state spaces in scientific machine learning, including Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification. For fixed self-attention transformers, the expected output Wasserstein error is bounded by the empirical input Wasserstein error plus an additional $N^{-1/2}$ attention term. These self-attention transformers are MNMs under the stated assumptions: pre-norm architectures follow from compact stability after normalization, while post-norm architectures are covered under the stated tail conditions. We prove corresponding cross-attention estimates and extend the results to multihead attention and grouped transformer evaluation, with convergence as the group size grows. For Set Transformers viewed as measure-to-vector mappings, we obtain an $N^{-1/2}$ bound on the expected Euclidean output error under the stated assumptions. Experiments on seven operators in dimensions $d=1,2,3,5,10$ support the predicted particle-count dependence, using one-dimensional Wasserstein computations and Sinkhorn approximations in higher dimensions. The observed Wasserstein and sliced Wasserstein decay rates are close to their respective theoretical sampling benchmarks.

title: An Attention-Guided Graph Neural Network Surrogate for Boundary Integral Computation in Physical Field Reconstruction
abstract: In practical engineering and scientific computing, a real physical system can be reduced to a boundary value problem, and the adequate boundary information to determine the interior spatial distribution and evolutionary state of the physical field can be solved with linear equations, alternatively, the the real physical problem can be treated with boundary problems with in adequate information problems in field of machine learning. This paper proposes a deep learning framework for the recovery of missing boundary information using an attention-guided graph neural network (GNN) surrogate. The framework extracts features from the physical information on the discretized boundary into a latent space, and the missing boundary quantities are then predicted by the network. Thus, the nonlinear mapping from known boundary quantities to missing boundary quantities is learned using a variational autoencoder (VAE) architecture, while an attention mechanism is incorporated to better model the correlations among different types of boundary information. Furthermore, the interior physical field can be reconstructed using the conventional boundary element method (BEM) integral formulation. The effectiveness of the GNN-BEM framework is evaluated using numerical examples of the two-dimensional Laplace and Poisson equations, which demonstrate good performance in reconstruction accuracy, local detail preservation, and model stability. The results show that GNN-BEM provides a feasible computational framework for boundary information recovery and fast interior physical field reconstruction for partial differential equations under complex boundary conditions.

title: A Physics-Informed Hybrid Forward-Inverse Machine Learning Framework for High-Dimensional Sparse Recipe Reconstruction
abstract: High-dimensional sparse recipe formulation in process industries involves nonlinear association of various covariates, bounded by sparsity constraints and multi-criteria tolerances. Traditional physics-based classical methods (such as Kubelka-Munk) fail to generate sparse candidate recipes properly due to their simplified assumptions and industrial process variations. This study proposes a hybrid physics-informed uncertainty-aware framework that is structured into three modules: (a) Module A, a multi-target forward quality model; (b) Module B, a sparse inverse reconstructor; and (c) Module C, a feasibility-constrained ranking layer. Then it has been validated in an industrial textile dyeing context with recipe-grouped cross-validation under multi-illuminant quality assessment comprising process and production information, target reflectance, K/S values, and spectral descriptors. Histogram Gradient Boosting (HGB) with spectral-only features ($R_\lambda$, K/S) and Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBDT) with recipe-process features outperforms other configurations with out-of-Fold MAE of 0.1655 and 0.1523 in the forward quality model. For inverse reconstruction, a component-wise median blend achieved a recipe-vector MAE of 0.0295. Exploratory conditional treatment effect (CATE) suggests an observational association that alkali adjustment reduces error for red and pale shades (CATE = -0.196). This framework provides a human-in-the-loop decision-support tool that minimizes costly laboratory trials across industrial formulation domains.

title: Sequential clusterization of light nuclei and hypernuclei in heavy-ion collisions within a Wigner function coalescence framework
abstract: We investigate the formation of light nuclei and hypernuclei in $\mathrm{Au}\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}+\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}\mathrm{Au}$ collisions at $\sqrt{{s}_{NN}}=3$ GeV within a coalescence framework embedded in the microscopic N-body parton-hadron-quantum-molecular dynamics (PHQMD) transport model. The Wigner phase-space distributions employed in the coalescence calculation are constructed from realistic $N$-body wave functions obtained by solving the Schr\"odinger equation in the hyperspherical harmonics formalism, providing a solid and parameter-free description of nuclear clusters and hypernuclei. By comparing calculated rapidity distributions with STAR data, we extract species-dependent coalescence times, revealing a non-universal formation pattern among different clusters. The resulting yields and kinematic distributions of light nuclei and hypernuclei are systematically analyzed and shown to be sensitive to the underlying wave-function structure and formation time. In addition, we explore cluster-nucleon formation channels for $A=4$ systems. These additional channels improve the description of $^{4}\mathrm{He}$ and $_{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}^{4}\mathrm{H}$ yields and help address the underestimation of $A=4$ cluster production in theoretical approaches. Finally, we provide predictions for heavier hypernuclei, including $_{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}^{5}\mathrm{He}$ and $_{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}^{5}\mathrm{He}$, which are of interest for future experimental measurements.

title: Renormalization of the shell-model neutrinoless double- β decay operator starting from effective field theory
abstract: In this work, we approach for the first time the task to perform a shell-model calculation of the matrix element for the neutrinoless double-beta decay, within a fully-consistent framework where the expressions of the nuclear Hamiltonian and of the decay operators have been derived through chiral perturbation theory. More precisely, the effective shell-model Hamiltonian and all transition operators have been constructed by way of the many-body perturbation theory, and then employed to calculate both spectroscopic properties of the nuclei involved in the decays under our consideration - namely 48Ca, 76Ge, and 82Se -, as well as the nuclear matrix elements of the electromagnetic and neutrinoless double-beta decays. We also present a study of the convergence properties of the calculated matrix elements in order to provide the elements for an estimate of the theoretical uncertainty.

title: Astrophysical S factor S 34 ( 0 ) using a Bayesian neural network
abstract: The astrophysical $S$ factor for the radiative capture reaction $^{3}\mathrm{He}(\ensuremath{\alpha},\ensuremath{\gamma})^{7}\mathrm{Be}$ plays a crucial role in big bang nucleosynthesis as well as stellar hydrogen burning. Its precise value is important in the context of primordial elemental abundances and the solar neutrino fluxes. In the present work we carry out a data-driven analysis of the $S$ factor using a Bayesian neural network. Unlike conventional neural networks, the Bayesian formulation produces a posterior distribution of $S$ factor curves consistent with experimental data and their uncertainties. From this distribution we extract the zero-energy astrophysical $S$ factor ${S}_{34}(0)=0.{544}_{\ensuremath{-}0.021}^{+0.022}\phantom{\rule{4pt}{0ex}}\mathrm{keV}\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}\mathrm{b}$. The posterior ensemble is further used to obtain reaction rates over the temperature range $T=0.005--4$ GK. The results are in agreement with existing calculations. This work provides an alternative framework for low-energy $S$ factor determination and uncertainty quantification in nuclear astrophysics.

title: Experimental study of the He 6 ( d , t ) He 5 reaction at 52 MeV: Probing the single-neutron wave function of the He 6 ground state
abstract: New experimental data for the He 6 ( d , t ) He 5 one-neutron pickup reaction at 52 MeV were measured in inverse kinematics at the ACCULINNA-2 isotope in-flight separator at the Flerov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions, Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Dubna. The data were analyzed using two standard direct reaction models, the distorted wave Born approximation (DWBA) and coupled reaction channels. Single neutron wave functions for the He 6 ground state obtained using three different nuclear structure methods, including the new cluster channel orthogonal function method, were tested and the dependence of the results of the reaction calculations on the properties of these wave functions was observed. The data were well reproduced by a DWBA calculation with the wave function obtained using the ab initio variational Monte Carlo method with no adjustable parameters.

title: Dispersive-optical-model analysis of the asymmetry dependence of neutron skins
abstract: New dispersive optical model analyses of ${}^{54}$Fe and ${}^{90}$Zr together with updated results for ${}^{40}$Ca, ${}^{48}$Ca, and the earlier result for ${}^{208}$Pb shed light on the behavior of neutron skins in nuclei. Starting with a negative skin for ${}^{40}$Ca, a trend increasing somewhat stronger than linear emerges when the neutron skin of these nuclei is considered as a function of asymmetry, $(N-Z)/A$, and linked to the Green's function Monte Carlo results for asymmetric He nuclei. This general trend is consistent with the expectation that nuclei near the neutron drip line are expected to have very large neutron skins. The present analysis therefore motivates the question of which nuclei provide the most relevant link to neutron star physics.

title: Calculation of the electromagnetic radiation emitted from the D–T fusion process in tokamak reactors
abstract: Abstract In the deuterium tritium (D–T) fusion reaction an alpha particle is released with the kinetic energy ∼ 3.5 MeV . Since the fusion reaction is governed by the strong interaction, the alpha particle is almost instantaneously accelerated to the final state with its kinetic energy ∼ 3.5 MeV . According to the classical electrodynamics, electromagnetic radiation should be emitted in such an acceleration process. In this work, we calculate the electromagnetic radiation in the D–T fusion process using both the classical electrodynamics and the quantum mechanical models. The radiation is compared with the radiation from the core plasma bremsstrahlung for pure D–T plasmas in large tokamaks. The ratio between the radiation from the D–T fusion reaction and bremsstrahlung depends only on the plasma temperature. The radiation from the D–T fusion reaction is stronger than that from bremsstrahlung if the frequency is higher than a critical value. Although the predicted radiation is much weaker than its high frequency counterpart, it is still possible to be detected in the high fusion gain reactors under some circumstances. Its effect should also be taken into account if one uses the gamma-ray emission spectrum to diagnostic for plasma profiles in tokamaks.

title: Ab initio study of Li 7 with coupled mass partitions
abstract: Background: Lithium is of broad interest in nuclear astrophysics, fusion energy research, and nuclear technology. From a theoretical perspective, the nucleus $^7$Li presents a remarkable challenge, as its bound and resonant states can exhibit contributions from both the $^4$He + $^3$H cluster configuration and configurations involving a neutron or proton coupled to a $^6$Li or $^6$He core, respectively. Purpose: We aim to achieve a unified ab initio description of bound-state and continuum properties of $^7$Li by explicitly including simultaneously the coupled mass/charge partitions $^4$He + $^3$H, $^6$Li + $n$, and $^6$He + $p$. Specifically, we investigate the effect of inter-partition coupling on the spectrum of $^7$Li and calculate cross sections for the $^6$Li($n,p)^6$He, $^6$He($p,n)^6$Li, and $^6$He($p,t)^4$He reactions. Method: We employ the no-core shell model with continuum for the first time in a calculation that couples three mass/charge partitions of the aggregate nucleus $^7$Li, using a chiral nucleon-nucleon interaction as input. Results: The calculated spectrum reproduces all the experimentally observed states of $^7$Li in the correct order and predicts additional resonances. The calculation also reproduces the overall energy dependence of the $^6$Li$(n,p)^6$He cross section. Improved agreement with measured cross sections is obtained after phenomenological adjustment of resonance energies. Conclusions: The present results show that coupling the relevant mass/charge partitions is important for a consistent description of the $^7$Li spectrum and reaction cross sections, and offers a useful framework for interpreting existing data and guiding future measurements.

title: O 17 spectroscopy using C 13 ( α , α ) resonant elastic scattering
abstract: The detailed excitation functions for C 13 ( α , α ) elastic scattering and the additional thick target inverse kinematics measurements were analyzed using the R matrix approach. The analysis covered the excitation region in O 17 from 8.6 up to 11.2 MeV. Information on single particle widths of the levels in the O 17 nucleus and shell model calculations are in good agreement. A comparative analysis of the α -cluster structures of O 16 and O 17 nuclei indicates their common underlying nature. However, the structure in O 17 is more complex. In particular, each α -cluster level with spin J in O 16 corresponds to several levels with spins J = ± 1 / 2 in O 17 . Unexpectedly, the reduced-width-weighted centroids of the higher-spin members of these doublets always lie at lower excitation energies in O 17 .

title: Investigating two-body cluster structures of B 10
abstract: Two-body breakup mechanisms of the weakly bound nucleus B 10 were investigated through an exclusive coincidence measurement in the B 10 + Au 197 system at a beam energy of 57 MeV. Coincident detection of two outgoing charged particles by an array of Si strip detector telescopes shows that the dominant two-body projectile breakup channels are Li 6 + α and Be 9 + p . Projectile excitation energies, reconstructed from the kinetic energies of the fragments, are found to reproduce the energies of specific excited states of B 10 and thereby confirm the coexistence of both Li 6 - α and Be 9 - p two-body cluster configurations for B 10 . Continuum discretized coupled channels (CDCC) calculations, considering each of the above two cluster configurations separately, were able to explain the experimental cross sections for both breakup as well as elastic scattering simultaneously.

title: Comparative study of Langevin and random walk models for nuclear fission in the overdamped regime
abstract: We present a comparative study of Langevin dynamics and a Metropolis random walk model applied to thermal neutron-induced fission of $^{229}$Th, $^{235}$U, $^{239}$Pu, $^{245}$Cm, $^{249}$Cf, and $^{255}$Fm. Both methods are implemented within an identical four-dimensional Fourier-over-Spheroid framework, using potential energy surfaces derived from the macroscopic-microscopic model. We show that the Metropolis walk corresponds to the overdamped limit of the Langevin equations and confirm this correspondence numerically by Langevin calculations performed in the strongly damped regime and with quantum corrections to the random force switched off. Under these conditions, the two approaches produce essentially identical mass distributions for the lighter actinides. Systematic deviations develop for the heavier actinides, where the Langevin dynamics yields a non-negligible symmetric fission component absent in the random walk results. We trace this difference to the kinematic structure of the Metropolis sampling and to the residual inertial dynamics retained in the Langevin framework. A parallel comparison of Langevin calculations with and without the quantum-corrected effective temperature $T^*$ isolates the contribution of zero-point fluctuations and suggests that their standard phenomenological treatment may overestimate their impact in certain cases. Both approaches qualitatively reproduce the asymmetric peak positions and their systematic evolution across the actinide chain, while a common quantitative limitation -- the narrowness of the predicted distributions -- points to the role of higher-dimensional deformation modes not included in the present parametrization.

title: A novel high-performance confinement regime in a tokamak driven by tearing mode locking and rotation shear
abstract: Abstract In magnetically confined fusion plasmas, tearing mode (TM) locking is conventionally regarded as detrimental, often halting rotation and triggering disruptions. Contrary to this expectation, we demonstrate that locked TMs can enhance confinement by inducing an internal transport barrier (ITB). Specifically, the interaction between a locked outer plasma region and neutral beam injection (NBI)-driven core rotation generates a broad and intense toroidal velocity shear layer, which suppresses turbulence and improves core confinement. Beam emission spectroscopy and charge exchange recombination spectroscopy confirm a substantial reduction in turbulent transport and a rise in core ion temperature exceeding T i > 9 keV .
