This phenomenon—termed the Locking-Induced Flow and Transport (LIFT) mode—transforms a traditionally disruptive mechanism into a confinement enhancement strategy.

title: Transport simulations with a constrained momentum-dependent chiral mean-field equation of state at various isospin fractions
abstract: We present a comparison of the ultrarelativistic quantum molecular dynamics model using a chiral mean field (CMF) equation of state with flow and pion production data in heavy ion collisions at low beam energies E lab = 0.2 – 2.0 A GeV and varying isospin fraction. The CMF model parameters are constrained by known properties of the high density equation of state of quantum chromodynamics at varying isospin fractions. This allows us to calculate the equation of state as well as nuclear interactions for different physical systems like neutron stars and heavy ion collisions in a consistent way. It is found that heavy ion reactions at the upcoming FAIR facility will only have marginal sensitivity on the isospin dependence of the high-density equation of state. At lower beam energies, comparing to FOPI, HADES, and S π RIT data, the sensitivity is higher but the observed deviations and systematic uncertainties of the existing data are larger than the sensitivity to the symmetry energy.

title: Implication of multimessenger observations on the relativistic mean-field equation of state of dense nuclear matter and skin thickness of nuclei
abstract: The composition and properties of infinite nuclear matter under extreme conditions of temperature and pressure remain incompletely understood. In this work, we constrain the equation of state (EoS) of nuclear matter$-$constructed within the framework of the Relativistic Mean Field (RMF) model$-$by combining results from chiral effective field theory and multimessenger observations of neutron stars. Using the saturation properties of nuclear matter, we generate a wide ensemble of EoS, which are subsequently constrained within a Bayesian framework. The resulting posterior distributions provide tight bounds on both the saturation parameters and the coupling constants of the RMF model. The radius of a $1.4\,M_\odot$ neutron star is tightly constrained to $12.471_{-0.394}^{+0.427}\,\mathrm{km}$, while the maximum mass reaches $2.156_{-0.120}^{+0.175}\,M_\odot$. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that the $\omega$-$\rho$ coupling, which governs the density dependence of the symmetry energy, becomes increasingly significant under successive astrophysical constraints. Finally, the predicted $\rm r_\mathrm{skin}$ of $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ agrees well with the CREX measurement, whereas that of $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$ remains in tension with PREX-II. In contrast to earlier studies, we do not observe a clear correlation between the $\rm r_\mathrm{skin}$ of $^{208}$Pb and the symmetry energy slope parameter $L$.

title: Structure and decay of α -condensate candidates from cluster effective field theory interactions
abstract: Dilute gas-like configurations of α particles, often termed α condensates, have been proposed to exist in certain excited states of α -conjugate nuclei. This work investigates the structural and decay properties of α -condensate candidates within a few-body framework using leading-order cluster effective field theory interactions. To isolate dilute N α configurations, a constrained model space strategy is implemented inspired by Yamada and Schuck [Phys. Rev. C 69, 024309 (2004)], which constructs a description specifically for suprathreshold states. By explicitly decoupling the nonuniversal, compact configurations lying below the N α threshold, this framework describes N α condensates as quasibound states localized within the Coulomb barrier. The stochastic variational method is used to perform theoretical calculations for the proposed N α condensates ranging from Be 8 to Ne 20 . The results not only map the formation of these novel cluster states in heavier α -conjugate nuclei but also offer critical insights into the applicability of few-body universality to charged particles.

title: Multitask Gaussian process predictions of low-lying excitation observables and shell evolution near N , Z = 20 and 28
Erratum: Identification of a new side-band and proposed octupole correlations in very neutron-rich Ce 152 [Phys. Rev. C 86, 067302 (2012)]
Impact of Decay-Chain Feeding by Long-Lived Heavy Nuclei on Nuclear Cosmochronology
abstract: Abstract Nuclear cosmochronology provides an independent method for determining the ages of astrophysical objects without relying on Galactic chemical evolution models. Long-lived radioactive actinides synthesized via the rapid neutron-capture process (r-process) particularly thorium and uranium serve as ideal chronometric nuclei. However, predicting the initial abundances of these nuclei and their subsequent long-term evolution remains a major source of uncertainty in nuclear cosmochronology. In this work, we investigate the impact of decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei on nuclear cosmochronology and estimate the corresponding age corrections. We develop a self-consistent radioactive decay network that includes all relevant decay pathways and couple it to r-process nucleosynthesis calculations. By tracking the long-term evolution of r-process nucleosynthesis based on neutron star merger trajectories, the dominant long-lived nuclei shaping the evolution of the chronometric elements Th and U are identified as 232Th, 235U, 236U, 238U, and 244Pu. It is found that delayed feeding substantially modifies the long-term evolution of actinides particularly for 232Th, which receives significant late-time contributions from heavier progenitor nuclei such as 244Pu and 236U. As a consequence, the U/Th and Th/X chronometers exhibit significant sensitivity to delayed feeding from the progenitor nuclei 244Pu and 236U, with age corrections reaching ∼5 Gyr. These results suggest that decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei plays a crucial role in nuclear cosmochronology and should be properly accounted for in age determinations based on actinide chronometers.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: QCD crossover temperature and curvature coefficient from unbiased exponential resummation at physical quark masses in (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD
Orbit correction for a rapid cycling synchrotron using an adjacent-difference-constrained neural network
abstract: In a rapid cycling synchrotron (RCS), closed-orbit correction is an important task for maintaining high beam quality and machine stability. Since the orbits in RCS change during energy ramping, response matrix-based orbit correction is performed in segments, which can result in the corrector current ramp rates exceeding safety limits and accuracy loss in orbits. To address these issues, this paper employs machine learning for orbit correction in RCS. An adjacent-difference-constrained neural network (ADCNN) was built and tested in both simulations and machine experiments at the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS). The correction results demonstrate the feasibility of using neural networks for RCS orbit correction. The ADCNN exhibits a correction effect equivalent to that of response matrix-based correction while effectively limiting the current ramp rates of the correctors.

title: Cooling of isolated neutron stars with hyperon-mixed kaon-condensation matter
abstract: We investigate the thermal evolution of isolated neutron stars containing hyperon--mixed kaon--condensed matter, focusing on the role of proton superconductivity. The equation of state utilized for cooling calculation is based upon the minimal relativistic mean--field framework supplemented by chiral SU(3) dynamics for kaon condensation with an additional component on the three-baryon force, which ensures stiffness at high densities enough to meet astrophysical constraints on neutron-star masses and radii. We show that the nucleonic direct Urca processes operate at relatively low stellar masses ($M \gtrsim 1.3\,M_\odot$), erasing any observable signature of strangeness in the absence of superfluidity. However, if the proton $^1{\rm S}_0$ superconductivity works, because of suppression of fast neutrino cooling processes, the cooling scenario could become relevant with the strangeness, depending on the density regions of the pairing gap. In particular, if the proton superconductivity is so strong in high-density regions ($T_{c,p}\sim10^{10}~{\rm K}$), the nucleon and hyperon direct Urca processes shut down, which makes the kaon-induced Urca processes dominant in massive neutron stars. This scenario is in good agreement with several cold isolated neutron stars identified recently recently, such as the Vela Jr., PSR J0205+6449, and PSR B2334+61. Hence, we suggest that strong proton superconductivity can render kaon condensation observationally visible through cold neutron-star observations, providing a potential signature of strangeness in dense matter.

title: Mixture density networks for neutrino reconstruction at hadron colliders
abstract: Neutrino momentum reconstruction at hadron colliders is intrinsically ambiguous because the longitudinal momentum is not directly observed. We study this problem in semileptonic t t ¯ events using mixture of neutrino solutions with transformer event representation (), a mixture density network that predicts a multivariate normal mixture for the conditional distribution of neutrino momentum from reconstructed event objects. The model uses a transformer-based event encoder and yields a sampling-free point estimate of the neutrino momentum from the closed-form density. On the public benchmark introduced with ν -flows, reduces the 68th percentile of the three-momentum residual by 5% and the 95th percentile by 6% relative to the empirical-mode ν -flows baseline, with per-variable root-mean-square errors smaller by 2 to 9% at comparable bias, while running 2 to 8.5 times faster at inference, depending on the device and batch size. These results indicate that mixture density networks are a competitive alternative to normalizing flows for neutrino reconstruction.

title: Fast-detection of hard x-ray emission and correlation with magnetohydrodynamic instabilities on the High-Beta Tokamak-Extended Pulse (HBT-EP)
abstract: Understanding the spatial and energy dynamics of runaway electrons is essential to preventing damage to next-generation fusion experiments and pilot plants. In the High-Beta Tokamak-Extended Pulse (HBT-EP) device, hard x-rays (HXRs) are produced through thick-target bremsstrahlung radiation when energetic electrons are deconfined and strike limiting surfaces. This paper describes a new HXR detector system composed of ten scintillator detectors and a visible-light fast camera, which is used to detect fast bursts of HXR emission that correlate with magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) perturbations. Hard x-rays cause spatially uncorrelated speckling on the fast camera, and the appearance of speckles is strongly correlated in time with x-ray bursts. We also observe a threshold below which an HXR signal is insufficient to produce a given speckle signal. Using these detectors, HBT-EP can measure the toroidal and temporal characteristics of HXRs, which are used to infer the characteristics of deconfined electrons. We report a strong correlation between the phase of a rotating n = 1 HXR source and an n = 1 MHD mode, suggesting that MHD activity directly enhances the radial transport of energetic electrons.

title: Development of a compact induction oven system for an electron cyclotron resonance ion source
abstract: This paper presents the development of a high-temperature induction oven designed for use in the Dubna electron cyclotron resonance ion source with permanent magnets for superheavy element synthesis experiments at the Flerov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions. The focus is on ensuring stable evaporation of refractory metals, specifically 50Ti and 54Cr. Multiphysics simulation was carried out in COMSOL Multiphysics, accounting for electromagnetic and thermal processes as well as radiative heat transfer. Experimental studies confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed design and the consistency between simulation results and real operating conditions. The data demonstrate the potential of the developed oven for generating ion beams of refractory metals.

title: Conceptual design of the electron-optics of the magnetic electron recoil gamma-ray spectrometer
abstract: In nuclear fusion reactors, deuterium and tritium are fused together. Most reactions produce a 4He ion and a 14 MeV neutron, while about 2 × 10−5 of them produce a 5He ion and a gamma photon. One of the most important measurements from a fusion reactor is the total fusion power, which can be measured using the 14 MeV neutrons or the gamma-rays. Using both provides two independent measurements, which is valuable for researchers and regulators. Facilities such as JET use scintillators such as LaBr3 to measure gamma-ray emission, but such detectors could struggle with background on high-power reactors such as SPARC and ITER. We propose that a magnetic electron recoil gamma-ray spectrometer (MERGS) can make gamma-ray measurements in these high-background environments. MERGS will consist of a foil that converts photons to electrons via Compton scattering, a magnetic electron-optic system that focuses and disperses the electron beam, and a detector array that counts the electrons and uses their positions to infer their energy. A conceptual design framework of MERGS is presented, along with three numerically optimized electron-optic geometries for three different resolution requirements. Simulations are presented showing that each presented design can meet its requirements. This shows that MERGS can measure the gamma-ray emission spectrum more effectively than scintillators for a variety of price points, enabling improved measurements of fusion power as well as the study of fast ion physics via other nuclear reactions.

title: Effects of Rotation on 3D Core-collapse Supernova Models for Low-mass Progenitors
abstract: Abstract We explore the dependence upon rotation rate alone of various supernova observables simulated to their saturation for the explosion of a 9 M ⊙ progenitor. We find that the explosion energy is nonmonotonic with, and weakly dependent upon, spin across a broad range of initial spins. The asymmetries of the blast depend weakly on spin, with faster spins leading to only slightly greater asymmetries. There is little significant pole–equator neutrino heating asymmetry during explosion, even for rapid rotation, and only for the fastest rotator does the neutrino heating rate diminish noticeably. Hence the effects of rotation alone on all salient aspects of supernova dynamics are not large. We find that the recoil kick and spin are clearly aligned only for the most rapidly rotating model. Interestingly, for the fastest rotator, we witness T /∣ W ∣ corotation instabilities near a value of 0.05 and spiral-arm modes emerge. We find that the nucleosynthetic yields depend little upon the rotation rate and determine that the ratio of initial to final core spin period is near ∼4000, implying (given the modest inferred radio pulsar periods at birth) that the initial spin periods of most supernova cores are likely quite long. However, we focus on only one progenitor and do not include magnetic fields. Nevertheless, at least for low-mass progenitors that explode early, we find muted consequences of rotation in most major particulars across a wide range of initial spins.

title: The sigma meson (f 0 ) at finite temperature with truncated overlap fermions
abstract: Abstract We study the temperature dependence of meson screening masses in two-flavour lattice QCD using dynamical truncated overlap fermions, a type of lattice chiral fermions. The screening masses for the π, ρ, a 1 , a 0 , and the sigma (f 0 ) mesons are extracted by computing spatial correlation functions. This exploratory study uses meson screening masses and the connected/disconnected decomposition of the scalar correlator as diagnostic observables to examine how the disconnected contribution changes across the pseudocritical region. Above the pseudocritical temperature T pc , the π and f 0 screening masses become degenerate, consistent with chiral restoration. The (ρ, a 1 ) pair also shows the expected degeneracy. Decomposition of the f 0 propagator reveals that the connected contribution dominates above T pc , while the disconnected part becomes significant below T pc , explaining the reduced statistical clarity observed at low T. These results demonstrate that dynamical truncated overlap fermion simulations can capture the qualitative thermal behaviour of the scalar sector.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Revealing the nature of double-strangeness pentaquark states via femtoscopic correlation functions
abstract: Recent discoveries of exotic hadrons, which cannot be classified within the conventional quark model of q q ¯ mesons and q q q baryons, strongly imply the existence of dynamically generated hadronic molecules. Some of these hadron-hadron interactions are accompanied by coupled-channel effects, which remain challenging to quantitatively determine. In this work, we demonstrate that femtoscopy provides a sensitive probe of such coupled-channel dynamics. We calculate correlation functions for the double-strangeness pentaquark candidates P c s s ( 4493 ) ( J P = 1 / 2 − ) and P c s s ( 4633 ) ( J P = 1 / 2 − or 3 / 2 − ), revealing clear signatures of the attractive interactions that can form bound states. The results are markedly different from those obtained in scenarios that neglect off-diagonal transitions, highlighting the importance of coupled-channel effects for understanding the structure of these hadrons.

title: Photon production from gluon splitting and fusion induced by a magnetic field of arbitrary strength in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
abstract: We compute the yield and elliptic flow coefficient for photons produced during the pre-equilibrium stage of semi-central relativistic heavy-ion collisions from the gluon fusion and splitting processes induced by the presence of a magnetic field. The calculation is performed for arbitrary values of the field strength. The pre-equilibrium gluon distribution is modeled with a glasma-inspired Bose-Einstein occupation factor, as well as with an anisotropic distribution that accounts for the rapid initial expansion along the beam axis. In both cases, we find a very good agreement between the calculation and the experimental data from PHENIX. Most notably, the shape and strength of the elliptic flow coefficient are described quite well, representing a step towards solving the outstanding photon puzzle.

title: Light tetraquark states with J P C = 1 − − from QCD sum rules
abstract: We perform a systematic QCD sum rule study of light tetraquark states with J P C = 1 − − in the diquark-antidiquark picture. A complete set of local interpolating currents is constructed and projected onto six flavor-isospin configurations ( q = u / d ): the isoscalar q q q ¯ q ¯ , q s q ¯ s ¯ , and s s s ¯ s ¯ sectors, the isovector q q q ¯ q ¯ and q s q ¯ s ¯ sectors, and the isotensor q q q ¯ q ¯ sector. From the nonderivative currents studied in the present work, the extracted masses of the q q q ¯ q ¯ , q s q ¯ s ¯ , and s s s ¯ s ¯ configurations lie in the ranges 1.53–2.37 GeV, 1.86–2.51 GeV, and 2.46–2.60 GeV, respectively. For the s s s ¯ s ¯ vector sector, we also quote the previous derivative-current result 2.34 − 0.30 + 0.23 GeV as a complementary benchmark. We further compare the present 1 − − tetraquark spectrum with previous QCD sum rule results for the 1 − + tetraquark and hybrid states [N. Su, E.-L. Cui, Y.-W. Jiang, and H.-X. Chen, .], aiming to provide useful information for distinguishing tetraquark and hybrid configurations in the light hadron spectrum. As an additional improvement, we complete the previously missing isotensor 1 − + tetraquark entry and obtain its lowest mass to be M = 2.1 9 − 0.24 + 0.26 GeV , which is included in the spectral comparison.

title: WKB approximation under a Killingbeck potential and its application to double-heavy-meson spectroscopy
abstract: It is well known that nonrelativistic or semirelativistic constituent quark models can describe a large number of the meson and baryon properties with surprising accuracy. In this work, we study the Killingbeck potential using the WKB approximation in the constituent quark model. The implicit approximate solutions for the energy eigenvalues, together with analytical expressions for the root-mean-square radii and the probability densities at the origin, of the Schrödinger equation are obtained by using appropriate quantization conditions. Finally, we discuss applications to double-heavy-meson spectroscopy within the Killingbeck potential.

title: Strange quark stars and spontaneous scalarization
abstract: Strange quark matter, as one of the most extreme dense states in astrophysics, can be explored through relativistic compact objects. Hypothetical relativistic stars composed of dense strange quark matter are characterized by the equation of state of that matter. The spontaneous scalarization of strange quark stars is influenced by the equation of state of strange quark matter. Here, we investigate how the equation of state of strange quark matter influences the spontaneous scalarization of these stars. Considering Normal, color-flavor-locked (CFL), and CFLm quark matter in the bag models and applying the scalar-tensor gravity, we calculate the structure of scalarized strange quark stars. We investigate how the effective bag constant, perturbative QCD parameter, CFL pairing gap, and strange quark mass control the mass-radius relation, the central scalar field, the scalarization thresholds, and the scalar charge. Our results demonstrate that strange quark stars in scalar-tensor gravity are viable, testable objects, and they establish a complete framework for constraining both the gravitational theory and the properties of cold quark matter with current and future multimessenger observations.

title: Possible coexistence of pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation in triaxial nuclei
abstract: It has been conventionally assumed that triaxial deformation breaks the degeneracy of pseudospin doublets, leading to less discussion of pseudospin partner bands in triaxial nuclei. However, by considering the pairing correlations, the quasiparticle states of pseudospin doublets are found to remain nearly degenerate at appropriate Fermi energies in triaxial systems. In this work, we systematically investigate the pseudospin partner bands based on the $\ensuremath{\pi}({g}_{7/2},{d}_{5/2})$ configuration in triaxial nuclei using the particle rotor model. For the first time, we propose the possible coexistence of pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation. Further analysis of angular momentum geometry and wave function components supports the identification of one structure as a pseudospin partner band and the other as a wobbling band. This study reveals a novel coexistence mode between pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation, illustrating the diversity of rotational excitations in atomic nuclei.

title: Systematical examination of the B 4 / 2 anomaly as a signature of enhanced triaxiality at the border of shape-coexistence regions

title: Determination of poloidal field coil currents from target plasma configuration based on deep neural network
abstract: Abstract Precise control of the poloidal magnetic configuration (PMC) is essential for optimizing plasma performance and ensuring the operational safety of tokamaks. The PMC is predominantly controlled by the poloidal magnetic field induced by a set of poloidal field (PF) coils, so determining each PF coil current (I_PF set) based on the target PMC before the experiment is crucial for achieving a desired discharge. This paper proposes a data-driven approach to determine the I_PF set based on a deep neural network (DNN). Using the QUEST spherical tokamak as a case study, a dataset of PMC parameters and corresponding I_PF set was generated through free-boundary equilibrium calculations. Crucially, the models are trained and validated entirely on simulated equilibria, and all predictions are benchmarked against the free-boundary equilibrium solver. Independent limiter and divertor DNN models were first trained to determine I_PF set from target PMC features. These models provide approximate predictions suitable for pre-discharge feedforward design, with all coil current RMSE values below 0.56 kA. To enable unified current determination for both configuration types within a single network, an integrated model was further developed by training on the combined limiter and divertor datasets, with limiter samples embedded into the higher-dimensional divertor feature space. This integrated model achieved comparable prediction accuracy without requiring separate models for each configuration type. Additionally, the role of PF35-1 (a pair of PF coils located near the divertor target) in fine-tuning strike point positions was examined. The proposed method reduces computation time from several seconds to under 1 ms per prediction, and offers strong potential as a feedforward component within real-time plasma control systems in future tokamak experiments. The method is intended to provide approximate feedforward coil currents for pre-discharge configuration design, with centimeter-level accuracy in plasma shape, rather than high-precision equilibrium solutions.

title: AI-based plasma equilibrium parameter inference in KSTAR for DEMO-relevant reactors using only ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a deep neural network for high-fidelity equilibrium parameter inference, serving as a surrogate of the magnetic EFIT reconstruction and relying exclusively on ex-vessel magnetic signals. The objective is to circumvent the long-term integrity constraints of in-vessel magnetic diagnostics in the nuclear environment of the Demonstration Fusion Power Reactor (DEMO)-relevant devices. Using KSTAR data (2021-2024), a baseline model trained solely on measured ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics (the Measurement-only model) is compared with an Augmented model, which addresses informational sparsity via virtual-sensor signals computed from the GEQDSK. The Augmented model achieves predictive fidelity comparable to off-line EFIT, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) above 0.99 and a range-normalized root-mean-squared error (NRMSE) of 0.332 % averaged over all parameters, against 2.385 % for the Measurement-only model. Because the virtual-sensor inputs derive from the EFIT solutions that define the targets, these figures quantify the surrogate fidelity with respect to the magnetic EFIT and constitute an upper bound on the accuracy attainable with physically installed ex-vessel probes, not that of an independent reconstruction. As the reference floor for the Measurement-only model, the magnetic fitting residuals of the parent EFIT reconstructions against the measured probe signals are quantified, yielding pooled range-normalized residuals of 1.55-3.87 % per campaign with structured, campaign-persistent components that random noise perturbations do not emulate. Robust accuracy is maintained during neutral beam injection (NBI)-induced transients, and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based attribution verifies that the Augmented model captures the underlying magnetohydrodynamic physics, specifically the Shafranov shift. With a median single-forward-pass inference latency of 3.47 ms and a 99th percentile of 3.53 ms, the framework is a viable surrogate for conventional numerical solvers. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that an idealized, EFIT-consistent realization of a densified ex-vessel sensor configuration retains sufficient information for high-precision equilibrium parameter inference, provided that magnetic probes are physically installed at the designated locations. This establishes the information-content prerequisite for ex-vessel-only inference in DEMO. The accuracy attainable from physically installed probes, subject to conductor-model, calibration and structured measurement-model errors, is not established and requires validation against measured ex-vessel signals.

title: Transition from Te-ITB sustainment with saturated m/n=1/1 activity to q=3/2 rational-surface-mediated collapse in EAST
abstract: Abstract A collapse of an electron internal transport barrier (Te-ITB) followed by a major disruption, is observed in electron-heating-dominant H-mode plasmas with a core-peaked Te profile on EAST tokamak. Before the collapse, the Te-ITB coexists stably with a long-lived saturated m/n=1/1 mode, where m and n denote the poloidal and toroidal mode numbers, respectively. During this phase, the dominant electron-temperature information-transfer pathway identified by the transfer entropy (TE) analysis remains in the core region, consistent with barrier sustainment. In the pre-collapse phase, nonlinear coupling among core m/n=1/1 modes, secondary destabilization of the saturated m/n=1/1 mode and enhanced core impurity radiation are observed. The dominant TE response then shifts toward the q = 3/2 rational surface, while the inward-directed coupling is weakened. Although an m/n = 2/1 mode already exists before the collapse, it remains relatively passive until the heat perturbation propagates outward. The m/n = 3/2 mode emerges closest in time to the Te-ITB collapse and may participate in the final barrier degradation, which is followed by rapid outward thermal-perturbation propagation, fast-electron redistribution, enhanced impurity radiation, and finally a major disruption. These observations suggest that Te-ITB collapse is associated with the reorganization of electron-temperature information-transfer pathways and local rational-surface coupling, rather than with static magnetic-island topology alone.

title: The multiscale nonlinear interactions between kinetic ballooning mode and drift wave turbulence critical for confinement improvement of hybrid fusion plasmas
abstract: Abstract Nonlinear suppression of short-wavelength drift wave turbulence by long-wavelength kinetic ballooning mode in tokamak fusion plasma is proposed to be the main cause for confinement improvement in the core of hybrid fusion plasmas. Specifically, the ambient ion temperature gradient(ITG) turbulence, which can contribute considerable transport flux if not mitigated, is fully suppressed in the presence of kinetic ballooning mode(KBM). KBM is demonstrated to be robustly unstable from fully electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations. While its flux is low under low magnetic shear, KBM can generate significant stabilizing zonal flow whose velocity well surpasses the normalized linear growth rate of ITG. This multiscale physics phenomenon is convincingly verified on a representative ASDEX-Upgrade hybrid scenario plasma.

title: Phase-space dynamics of fast ions during abrupt MHD Bursts in the large helical device
abstract: Abstract We investigated the phase-space dynamics of helically trapped fast ions during energetic-particle-driven MHD burst events in the Large Helical Device (LHD) using a fast-sampling fast-ion Dα (F-FIDA) diagnostic based on charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy. Conditional averaging synchronized with the timing of RF bursts accompanying the MHD events enabled the extraction of F-FIDA signals associated with the bursts. The phase-space dynamics inferred from the F-FIDA spectra showed two distinct behaviors: a rapid increase in the F-FIDA signal near the plasma edge immediately after the burst, and a delayed decrease inside the plasma occurring a few milliseconds later. The former is likely related to localized deformation and magnetic reconnection during the early phase of the MHD event, while the latter appears to be caused by rotating, downward-chirping MHD modes, leading to phase-space dynamics of fast ions. These results contribute to understanding the fast-ion transport processes during energetic-particle-induced MHD activity in fusion plasmas.

title: Electronic effects on sputtering of fusion materials under light ion impact
abstract: Abstract Understanding material behavior under ion bombardment is a crucial aspect in predicting material surface modification and the lifetime of plasma-facing materials in fusion devices. Atomistic simulations are commonly employed to calculate key ion irradiation outcomes such as sputtering and reflection yields. However, within this simulation framework, the energy dissipation of ions in the electronic system is often neglected or treated using a simple velocity-dependent friction force. Although this approximation can be adequate for slow heavy ions, light ions in the sub-keV range lose a substantial fraction of their energy to electronic excitations, requiring a more realistic energy transfer description. Here, we incorporate trajectory-resolved electronic stopping obtained from ab initio calculations into molecular dynamics simulations of hydrogen and helium irradiation of tungsten and iron. We show that density-dependent electronic stopping leads to systematic variations in sputtering yields, especially for tungsten and lower impact energies, whereas reflection yields are found to be largely insensitive to the model choice. Material-dependent features are identified and mainly attributed to different relative contributions of projectile and recoil electronic energy loss. This work provides a physically motivated approach to improve the accuracy of the sputtering data used in plasma-surface interaction modeling.

title: Disruption halo currents and voltages measured on the HBT-EP tokamak
abstract: Abstract This paper presents measurements of disruption halo currents on the High Beta Tokamak—Extended Pulse (HBT-EP) experiment using 4 high-field side (HFS) tile arrays spaced at equal intervals of toroidal angle. Current flow through the tiles is measured using Rogowski coils external to the tokamak vessel. Tiles can also be operated as floating probes measuring their voltage with respect to the local chamber. Poloidal and toroidal distributions of halo currents are presented, along with a description and explanation of voltage measurements for both axisymmetric and rotating halo currents. Arcing on tiles generates current to components that greatly exceeds ion saturation current limits in the presence of an intact sheath. Furthermore, arcing is observed to occur more frequently as halo current magnitude increases. Measurements of voltages by operating tiles in floating configuration are found to be consistent with the halo voltage generation model presented in Boozer (2013 Phys. Plasmas 20 082510). The dependence of tile polarity on poloidal position as well as halo current peak shape are explained using tile voltage measurements.

title: Comparative study of nitrogen and neon seeding impacts on divertor detachment and core confinement in DIII-D high-βp plasmas with ITER-similar shape
abstract: Abstract Divertor detachment experiments with nitrogen (N2) and neon (Ne) seeding have been performed in DIII-D high-βp scenario at q95~6, and the impacts of impurity seeding on divertor detachment and plasma confinement have been studied. Experimental results demonstrate that both N2 and Ne seeding could effectively reduce the electron temperature at the divertor target (Tet). The reduction in particle flux (jsat) is significantly more pronounced with N2 seeding, indicating a superior capability of N2 to facilitate deep particle detachment compared to Ne under these conditions. SOLPS-ITER simulations corroborate these findings, as the parallel momentum balance analysis reveals that N2 particles are predominantly retained in the divertor region, facilitating strong radiative dissipation near the target with minimal core penetration. In contrast, Ne particles could penetrate upstream, ionize inside the separatrix and lead to higher core radiation. Consequently, the stronger power and momentum loss in the scrape-off layer with N2 seeding is the key to achieve lower Tet and jsat compared to Ne seeding. Furthermore, statistical results suggest that the plasma confinement is maintained with both impurities, as the formation of large-radius internal transport barrier (ITB) compensates for pedestal degradation. Notably, the ITB formed with Ne seeding case is substantially stronger than that with N2 seeding. TGYRO simulations indicate that for Ne seeding case, toroidal rotation shear and the E×B shear play minor roles in ITB formation. Instead, the dominant stabilizing mechanism is identified as the redistribution of the current density and the reduction of magnetic shear at large radius, which is strongly promoted by Ne seeding but only weakly influenced by N2 seeding. These results provide a comprehensive perspective on the impact of N2 and Ne seeding on detachment and plasma confinement sustainment in DIII-D high-βp operations, offering valuable insights into optimizing the core-edge integration in future fusion reactors.

title: What does it take to have N eff < 3 at CMB times?
abstract: The vast majority of extensions of the Standard Model affecting the number of effective relativistic neutrino species ( N eff ) do so additively, namely, they enhance this quantity with some light state contributing to dark radiation. In this work, we consider precisely the opposite case: new physics scenarios that can lead to N eff < 3 that are consistent with all known cosmological, astrophysical, and laboratory data. We are motivated by three main reasons: (1) a recent measurement from Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and the South Pole Telescope (SPT) in combination with Planck that leads to N eff = 2.81 ± 0.12 , (2) by a new and powerful measurement of the primordial helium abundance, which anchors N eff to be very close to the Standard Model value one second after the big bang, (3) by the deployment of the Simons Observatory which will provide precise tests of the radiation content in the Universe and which may detect with a high significance cosmologies with N eff < 3 . We survey the main theoretical possibilities and find that only a few simple scenarios can consistently give N eff = 2.81 ± 0.12 . One class consists of thermal electrophilic relics with masses m ∼ 8 – 13 MeV . Another consists of out-of-equilibrium particles decaying to e + e − or γ γ , with a rather particular lifetime 0.05 s ≲ τ ≲ 3 min , mass 250 MeV ≲ m ≲ 600 MeV , and abundance ρ / ρ γ ∼ 0.1 at decay. Thermal electrophilic particles are especially interesting because they can account for the dark matter in the Universe and can be tested in experiments such as SENSEI, DAMIC-M, and Oscura, and their portals to the visible sector at experiments such as NA64 and LDMX. We conclude that if the Simons Observatory confirms that N eff ≃ 2.8 , it will point to very specific extensions of the Standard Model.

title: Study of 1 − − P -wave charmoniumlike and bottomoniumlike tetraquark spectroscopy
abstract: The masses of 1 − − P-wave charmoniumlike and bottomoniumlike tetraquark states are calculated in a constituent quark model where the Cornell-like potential and Breit-Fermi interaction are employed. All model parameters were imported from previous work, and predetermined by studying the low-lying conventional S- and P-wave light, charmed, bottom, charmonium, and bottomonium meson mass spectra. The lowest 1 − − tetraquark mass is predicted to be around 4.15 GeV. The decay widths of 1 − − P-wave tetraquark states are calculated for possible two-body strong decay channels within the rearrangement mechanism, including ω χ c J and η J / ψ for charmoniumlike tetraquarks, and ω χ b J for bottomoniumlike tetraquarks. The theoretical results are compared with the selected exotic states, also known as Y states, and tentative assignments are suggested. This study suggests that ψ ( 4230 ) , ψ ( 4360 ) , ψ ( 4660 ) , and ϒ ( 10753 ) may be P-wave tetraquark states and that multiple states might exist around 4.36 GeV.

title: Search for proton decay into a single charged antilepton and a massless invisible particle using the full pure water data set of Super-Kamiokande
abstract: A search for proton decay via p → l + + X , where l + is a positively charged lepton and X is an invisible, massless, neutral particle, was performed using a 401 kton · years exposure representing the entire pure water phase of Super-Kamiokande. No significant indication of a proton decay was observed beyond the expected atmospheric neutrino background. Lower limits on the partial lifetime of the proton were set to 1.72 × 10 33 years for p → e + + X and 0.61 × 10 33 years for p → μ + + X at the 90% confidence level. These results improve on previous limits by factors of 2 and 1.5, respectively.

title: Neutrino flux from collisions of red giant cores in globular clusters
abstract: The coalescence of degenerate helium cores during red giant collisions—a process we term “erythrohenosis”—introduces a novel class of transient astrophysical sources of high-energy neutrinos. Using stellar models generated with and smoothed-particle hydrodynamics simulations of the final inspiral phase, we develop a semianalytical model to estimate the amount of hydrogen mixed into the cores, the energy release ( ≈ 4.28 × 10 49 erg ) that heats the remnant to T f ≈ 5.3 × 10 8 K , the magnetic field amplification ( B ≈ 1.77 × 10 10 G ), and the resulting neutrino flux. The predicted TeV–PeV neutrino signal may contribute to the diffuse IceCube neutrino flux; we estimate that the horizon at which a single neutrino event is expected on average at ≳ 100 TeV is ≈ 55 kpc for individual merger events. Furthermore, we discuss the probability of a magnetized helium flash and assess the subsequent activation of the CNO cycle in the remnant core due to hydrogen mixing. In particular, neutrinos from the decay of F 18 offer a direct observational test of the detonation, (as sources within ∼ 4.4 pc would produce a neutrino flux exceeding the solar CNO neutrino background). The simultaneous emission of high-energy hadronic neutrinos, gravitational waves, and—if the optical depth permits ( τ T ∼ 10 14 in the core of the remnant)—an electromagnetic signal would constitute a unique multimessenger signature of red giant core collisions, positioning erythrohenosis events as exotic yet potentially observable phenomena in dense stellar systems.

title: Holographic open-closed exchange in double deeply virtual Compton scattering: Fixed- j structural matching to the ± -basis Wilson kernels
abstract: We show that fixed- j holographic double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS) and its DVCS limit give a fixed-scale structural match to the singlet conformal-operator product expansion Wilson-kernel family of QCD in the leading-twist unpolarized singlet vector channel. The open-string C 1 ( δ , ϑ ) hypergeometric kernel was derived by Nishio-Watari; the new closed-string result is that the Brower-Polchinski-Strassler-Tan (BPST) upper Witten vertex gives the same family with a different near-boundary power count, because Δ c ( j ) is fixed by the BPST trajectory rather than by open-Regge data. The Mellin exponent is therefore derived as δ c ( j ) = j + Δ c ( j ) − 2 = 2 j + γ c ( j ) rather than inserted by hand. The even open branch gives the parallel unprotected counterpart in the projected singlet vector amplitude. At Q = μ = μ 0 = μ * , the point is not merely that equal-endpoint evolution is trivial; it is that the ultraviolet Witten vertex has already produced the fixed- j conformal kernel before the lower conformal moment is matched. In the conformal partial-wave/conformal subtraction representation, beta-proportional conformal-anomaly terms and scheme transformations are coefficient/evolution bookkeeping away from the matching point, not replacements for the projected fixed-scale hypergeometric η / ξ Wilson-kernel family. The protected/unprotected j = 2 split identifies the protected closed branch with the ( − ) conformal partial wave and the even open branch with the unprotected ( + ) counterpart; these are mixed singlet eigenchannels, not literal unmixed quark/gluon operators at finite N c . The comparison therefore gives a direct conformal-basis interpretation of the fixed- j holographic t -channel Witten diagram: the ultraviolet vertex generates the universal Wilson-kernel family, while the lower vertex supplies the channel-dependent nonperturbative conformal moment.

title: Extraction of the pion-nucleon coupling constant using the effective-range expansion with the left-hand cut
abstract: We apply the generalized effective-range expansion of Du [], which incorporates the left-hand cut from one-pion exchange to low-energy neutron–proton scattering in the S 0 1 and S 1 3 channels. The amplitude zero for the center-of-mass momentum near 0.35 GeV in the S 0 1 channel is naturally accommodated within this framework. We extract the pole position, scattering length, effective range, shape parameter, and the pseudoscalar pion–nucleon coupling constant g π N 2 / ( 4 π ) at different expansion orders. The low-energy parameters are stable and consistent with established values, while g π N 2 / ( 4 π ) exhibits larger uncertainties. The extraction of g π N 2 / ( 4 π ) is data driven, relying on the analytic constraints from the left-hand cut and phase-shift data within the one-pion-exchange approximation. Despite larger uncertainties compared to high-precision extractions, the consistency with established values demonstrates that this framework can probe the left-hand-cut singularity.

title: Exact baryon-meson relation for b → s ν ν ¯
abstract: We derive an exact relation among the normalized branching fractions of Λ b → Λ ν ν ¯ and B → K ( * ) ν ν ¯ , within the lepton-number-conserving effective Hamiltonian in which only active neutrinos contribute to the invisible final state. Although the effective Hamiltonian contains 18 independent Wilson coefficients, the three normalized rates depend on only two independent combinations of them, leading to an exact algebraic relation. Remarkably, the central values of the coefficients of this baryon-meson relation are close to 1 / 4 and 3 / 4 , which appear in the heavy-to-heavy b → c semileptonic sum rule among the branching fractions of Λ b → Λ c τ ν ¯ and B → D ( * ) τ ν ¯ . Once the decay rate of B → K * ν ν ¯ is measured, the decay rate of Λ b → Λ ν ν ¯ can be determined in a model-independent manner for new-physics scenarios involving only active neutrino interactions, thereby providing a clean target prediction for future experiments. This clearly demonstrates that observables in baryonic and mesonic b → s ν ν ¯ transitions will serve as a compact consistency test and a powerful probe for discriminating among new-physics scenarios.

title: Constraining ultralight vector bosons via solar neutrino oscillations: The gauged L μ − L τ model and prospects for JUNO and XLZD
abstract: We present an extension of the Standard Model based upon the gauged U ( 1 ) L μ − L τ symmetry, featuring an ultralight vector boson that couples to the difference of muon and tau lepton numbers. This anomaly-free construction, whilst historically motivated by the muon’s anomalous magnetic moment, is here employed as an independent phenomenological framework for solar neutrino physics. Through kinetic mixing with the photon, the Z ′ boson generates an effective matter potential within the solar interior, thereby modifying neutrino flavor oscillations via the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein mechanism. Utilizing recent solar neutrino measurements from Borexino, SNO, and Super-Kamiokande, together with an up-to-date solar standard model, we constrain the boson mass to be below 5.7 × 10 − 17 eV , positioning it as a potential ultralight dark matter candidate. The optimal model, corresponding to a coupling parameter η o ≈ − 2 , yields χ ν 2 = 2.7 , which compares favorably with the standard three-flavor scenario ( χ ν 2 = 3.1 ). This best-fit configuration corresponds to an effective four-fermion coupling g Z ′ 2 ϵ / m Z ′ 2 ≈ 6.6 × 10 − 23 eV − 2 , approximately 5.7 times the Fermi constant, which for ϵ ≈ 1 and a reference mediator mass of 1 eV is equivalent to a gauge coupling g Z ′ ≈ 8 × 10 − 12 . We furthermore present projections for forthcoming experiments. The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO), which commenced operations in August 2025 and has already achieved world-leading precision in oscillation parameter measurements, together with the XLZD consortium, should substantially refine these constraints. Such ultralight particles may address long-standing discrepancies in galaxy simulations within the cold dark matter paradigm, and recent theoretical developments demonstrate their compatibility with nonthermal dark matter production mechanisms. Additionally, terrestrial long-baseline neutrino experiments provide complementary probes of this parameter space.

title: Two-color dual-oscillator infrared free-electron laser
abstract: We report on the design and performance of a two-color dual-oscillator infrared free-electron laser (FEL). The midinfrared (MIR) FEL at the Fritz Haber Institute has been upgraded to include a second oscillator FEL beamline that permits lasing in the far-infrared (FIR) regime from 4.5 to 175 μ m . In addition, a 500 MHz kicker cavity has been installed downstream of the electron accelerator. It allows deflection of electron bunches of up to 50 MeV energy alternately left and right by an angle of ± 2 ° . It can, thus, split the high-repetition rate (1 GHz) electron bunch train from the accelerator into two bunch trains of 500 MHz repetition rate each; one is steered to the MIR FEL and the other one to the new FIR FEL. In this two-color mode of simultaneous, synchronized operation, the wavelengths in both FELs can be tuned independently over wide ranges of up to a factor of 4 each by undulator gap variation. In addition, two-color operation is also available at reduced repetition rates (e.g., 55.6 MHz of both MIR and FIR pulses), as needed for some applications. This unique two-color mode opens up a wealth of novel user applications, such as MIR-FIR pump-probe experiments.

title: Binary neutron stars in the next-generation era: Multi-messenger detection prospects and constraints on the equation of state, mass distribution, and cosmology
abstract: Abstract Next-generation gravitational-wave (GW) observatories will provide crucial insights into the nature of neutron star (NS) matter and the cosmological expansion history. We estimate the number of multi-messenger detections of binary neutron stars (BNS) with the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) and project the resulting constraints on the equation of state (EOS), BNS mass distribution, and cosmology using joint hierarchical Bayesian inference. Our results rely on specific assumptions for the merger rate, EOS, and mass distribution; we consider two different mass functions, a narrow one centred around 1.4 M⊙ and a wide one ranging from 1.1 to 2 M⊙, and a merger rate with a local value of 107 Gpc−3 yr−1. Under this setup, our mock follow-up algorithm results in between ∼40 and ∼100 short-term electromagnetic counterparts per year for ET, depending on the detector layout and mass distribution. In a joint network with CE, this number ranges from ∼100 to ∼500. Additionally, we project tens to hundreds of late-time afterglow detections from gamma-ray bursts or KNe. Based on the generated multi-messenger events, we perform an injection campaign to hierarchically recover the EOS, mass distribution, and cosmology in a fully Bayesian framework. Focussing on KN events from ET alone, the multi-messenger data from our largest analysed catalogue with 78 events can constrain the canonical NS radius R1.4 to ≲ 0.2 km and the Hubble constant H0 to ≲ 1 km s−1 Mpc−1, at least in absence of systematic modelling offsets. By comparing inference results that are solely based on GW data and those incorporating light-curve information, we find that while the latter has negligible impact on the EOS constraints, it can benefit the inference of cosmological parameters.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Non-Markovian heavy-quark equilibration and equilibrium correlation function in a thermal medium
Hyperaccreting magnetized neutron stars inside rotating massive envelopes: Low-power jets and precursor flares
Diffusion and shear viscosity coefficients of hot isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter using a chiral SU(3) model
Vector meson photoproduction on the nucleus and the extraction of the nuclear suppression factor using asymmetric beams
abstract: Abstract The cross-section for photoproduction of a vector meson on a nucleus is usually determined in nucleus-nucleus collisions, which introduces a twofold ambiguity as to which nucleus emitted the photon. This can be resolved in asymmetric collisions of protons and nuclei, where the ratio of photoproduction cross-sections on the proton and nucleus directly measures the nuclear suppression factor with minimal model dependence. The feasibilty of using existing and future proton-lead collisions at the LHC is evaluated.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Outflows in a super-Eddington quasar drive clumpy circumgalactic medium and extended Hα nebulae at z ≳ 6
abstract: Abstract The discovery of gargantuan black holes with masses exceeding a billion solar masses at z ≳ 6 suggests rapid black hole growth and significant energy input into their host galaxies in the early Universe. With JWST probing previously unseen phases of the interstellar (ISM) and circumgalactic (CGM) medium around z > 6 quasars, detailed theoretical studies can now be directly confronted with observations. We use zoom-in simulations of a massive protocluster at z ∼ 6, employing both the fiducial fable galaxy formation model and modifications that allow earlier black hole seeding and mildly super-Eddington accretion. The central quasar remains Compton-thick throughout most of its evolution, with the obscuration arising from the ISM of its compact host galaxy. The onset of sufficiently strong quasar feedback drives a ‘blow-out’ episode, clearing out escape channels for ionizing radiation and leaving the central engine unobscured. This leads to a complete transformation of the CGM, whereby powerful, metal-enriched outflows produce a population of cold, fast, neutral clumps, significantly increasing the covering fraction of neutral hydrogen in the host halo. Radiative transfer calculations performed with a new ray-tracing code show that the CGM responds to quasar activity through the formation of Hα nebulae, whose size and luminosity increase with the strength of quasar feedback and decrease with obscuration level. Enhanced early black hole growth thus fundamentally reshapes the ISM and CGM of z ∼ 6 quasars, leaving clear observable signatures in their obscuration, neutral hydrogen distribution, and extended Hα emission.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Non-equilibrium trace of the energy-momentum tensor and bulk viscous pressure of a massive gas from kinetic theory
abstract: Abstract We investigate the far-from-equilibrium dynamics of a relativistic massive gas obeying Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB), Bose–Einstein (BE), and Fermi–Dirac (FD) statistics, undergoing a boost-invariant Bjorken expansion. We solve the relativistic Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation (RTA) using the method of moments.  We focus specifically on the time evolution of the trace of the energy-momentum tensor $\Theta_{\; \mu}^{\mu}$ and the bulk viscous pressure $\Pi$, quantities that are crucial for understanding the breaking of conformal symmetry in the rapidly evolving fireball created in heavy ion collisions. Our results demonstrate that the non-equilibrium values of $\Theta^{\mu}_{\; \mu}/T^{4}$ exhibits non-monotonic behavior, characterized by a local maximum at early times and a distinct dip around the characteristic collision time scale $\tau_R$. We found the scaled bulk viscous pressure $\Pi/P_{0}$ ($P_{0}$ isotropic pressure) depends significantly on the particle statistics.Along with this, we also observe that the magnitudes of both the bulk viscous pressure and $\Theta^{\mu}_{\; \mu}/T^{4}$ are significantly enhanced by a larger initial chemical potential. We further find thatincreasing mass strongly enhances both the normalized trace and the magnitude of the bulk viscous pressure.Finally, for ensembles of randomly perturbed non-equilibrium momentinitial conditions, the scaled bulk viscous pressure and pressure anisotropylose sensitivity to the initial conditions and approach commonlate-time trajectories but scaled trace is not converging to a common late time trajectory.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Fully heavy multiquarks in neural-network quantum states
abstract: Exotic hadrons beyond the conventional quark model provide a direct window into the dynamics of strong interaction. However, extracting the multiquark spectroscopy has to face the quantum many-body problem, which is still a theoretical challenge. In this case, diquark-antidiquark model is proposed as an approximation. Although this model can describe the spectroscopy roughly, it cannot describe the detailed dynamics. Furthermore, the methods aiming at dealing with many-body problem, e.g., the Gaussian expansion method and diffusion Monte Carlo, are proposed, but face severe computational bottlenecks. In this work, we introduce the neural-network quantum state (NNQS) approach to investigate the spectra of fully heavy multiquark states within the nonrelativistic potential quark model. By employing deep neural networks to represent the complex many-body spatial wave function, and constructing the color-spin part exactly from group theory to enforce fermionic antisymmetry, our approach effectively overcomes the dimensionality obstacles inherent in traditional methods. The results are compared with various model calculations, demonstrating that NNQS offers superior accuracy and flexibility, particularly in treating high-dimensional correlations. This work establishes NNQS as a promising tool for exploring the spectroscopy of exotic hadrons.

title: Development of large-size permanent magnet phase shifters for HEPS

title: Study of parametrized plasma response and regime for consistent stopping power models of α particles in D-T and p-11 B fusion scenarios
abstract: Abstract This work develops a systematic parameterization of plasma response regimes in deuterium–tritium ($D$-$T$) and proton–boron ($p$–$^{11}$B) fusion plasmas using a set of dimensionless plasma parameters. These parameters describe the thermodynamic state of the plasma, its collective response properties, as well as the kinetic properties of energetic fusion-born alpha particles in terms of dimensionless ratios of characteristic velocities, collision/oscillation frequencies, and relevant interaction length scales. Special emphasis is put on $\alpha$-electron and $\alpha$-ion interaction metrics, which define the main energy-loss channels.By determining these dimensionless parameters across representative fusion-relevant density-temperature domains, the numerical analysis identifies the plasma regime controlling alpha-particle transport in ($D$-$T$) and ($p$–$^{11}$B) plasmas. The results show that, under typical conditions for inertial confinement fusion, the plasmas are weakly to moderately coupled, weakly perturbed, and in a weakly non-degenerate regime, implying a consistent physical description where the energy exchange is governed by the collective response of the plasma.This study allows the identification of the operational domains in which reduced-stopping-power descriptions, such as the binary collision or dielectric response approaches, remain physically justifiable and numerically stable. This allows for the development of a physics-based framework in which to validate reduced transport models without the need for kinetic or quantum-level complexities. The parameterization aims at facilitating the integration of validated stopping models into advanced particle simulation toolboxes that include Monte Carlo approaches, such as GEANT4, for more valid virtual experiments in the study of fusion plasmas.

title: Integrating ensemble model and interpretable framework to unveil nuclear binding energy
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Capability of multimodal large language models to describe gravitational wave images
abstract: Abstract The advent of multi-messenger astronomy has highlighted the necessity for a comprehensive analysis of immense datasets generated by multiple astronomical observation instruments. The field of gravitational wave astronomy has employed deep learning for the efficient processing of data. However, the utilization of this technique has predominantly been confined to a single type of input data, such as images. While image-to-text applications with multimodal large language models (LLMs) are growing in other fields, a notable gap remains in the generation of textual descriptions of astrophysical and astronomical images. This study explores the potential of using multimodal LLMs to describe spectrogram images of anomalies captured by ground-based gravitational wave observatories. Three models, GPT-4, GPT-4o, and Gemini 1.5 Pro, were provided only with an image and a single prompt, without additional context. The generated text responses were then evaluated for length, meaning, and accuracy of the answers. All three models correctly identified each image as a spectrogram representation of gravitational wave data and generated appropriate explanations. However, they exhibited difficulties in detailed signal descriptions and source inference under context-free setting, indicating that further research is needed before practical application to gravitational wave data analysis. This study demonstrates the feasibility of using multimodal LLMs to transform spectrogram images into textual data and provides insight into their potential integration into gravitational wave data analysis workflows.

title: Interpretability as a leakage detector: a case study in machine-learning-based exoplanet detection with TESS
abstract: Abstract The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) generates photometric time series for hundreds of thousands of stars, far more than can be vetted by hand, motivating machine-learning triage. We present a low-resource, interpretable pipeline that classifies TESS light curves as transit-bearing or not using a random forest trained on engineered summary features, treating feature-importance analysis as a formal auditing step, and apply it to Sector 68. The positive class comprises TESS-confirmed planet hosts; the negative class comprises Sector 68 targets with no catalogued planet or candidate, assembled from a different source. Auditing the model's feature-importance ranking exposes a confound: the two dominant features, the flux energy and its logarithm, are for median-normalized light curves essentially proportional to the number of cadences, that is, to observational baseline. A transit-blind ranking by this feature alone already separates the classes with an AUC of 0.734, and because our train/test split cannot control for the classes' differing provenance, the full model's held-out ROC-AUC of 0.95 (precision 0.94, recall 0.74, F1 0.83) is best read as performance under the current sampling procedure; isolating the confound's precise causal share is left as an open question for a dedicated ablation study. Some evidence of genuine signal survives this caveat: applied to 400 held-out candidates that share the negative class's baseline and so cannot benefit from the confound, the pipeline still flags 61 (15%) as probable planets, with the highest-probability cases showing genuine periodic transit dips. We give concrete recommendations for detecting and avoiding this failure mode: provenance-matched class construction, baseline-invariant features, controlled ablation, and routine interpretability-based leakage audits. The case study is offered as an instance of auditing scientific machine learning with its own tools, and a cautionary lesson for machine-learning-based exoplanet detection.

title: Generation fusion: the human factor in the fusion equation
abstract: Abstract The human factor in fusion energy development is about those who will take fusion from the laboratory to the grid and under what conditions. While this is among the most strategically important dimensions of the field, it is also among the least formally discussed. During the 51st European Physical Society (EPS) Conference on Plasma Physics in Vilnius, Lithuania, Generation Fusion was held as a satellite event on 9th July 2025. It was set-up as a panel discussion and was a direct sequel to the Visions for Fusion event held at the 50th EPS Conference. The panel brought together six researchers and industry representatives from different career stages, working in magnetic confinement fusion, inertial confinement fusion, and related fields. Using live audience polling of approximately 100 participants, panel discussions, and an open Q&A, the event explored topics including motivation and retention of early-career researchers, the role of mentoring and soft skills, public-private partnerships, mobility between institutions and countries, interdisciplinary collaboration, and communication with society and policy-makers. A clear and consistent finding emerged: the field faces not a lack of motivation, the overwhelming majority of attendees expressed a desire to remain in fusion, but rather structural barriers such as employment instability, limiting mentoring frameworks, and insufficient permeability between academia and industry. The panel closed with a strong consensus calling for greater diversity, more equitable career paths, and a shift away from metrics such as the H-index towards broader definitions of scientific impact, including, for example, public communications.

title: Design and integration studies of a DCLL breeding blanket for a stellarator reactor based on the CIEMAT-QI4X configuration
abstract: Abstract The integration of a breeding blanket in a stellarator reactor poses a major challenge due to the intricate geometry and the reduced free space between plasma and coils and between neighbouring coils, which also makes maintenance by remote handling techniques difficult. Conversely, in comparison with tokamaks, the breeding blanket can benefit significantly from the steady-state operation of stellarators. While previous studies have pointed to the feasibility of a Dual Coolant Lithium Lead (DCLL) breeding blanket in stellarators such as HELIAS-5B, each device introduces a different set of geometrical constraints and integration requirements that must be addressed through a dedicated design approach. This work presents a sequential study on several aspects that have clear impact on the functionality and efficiency of a DCLL breeding blanket integrated into a stellarator design based on the CIEMAT-QI4X plasma configuration. The proposal aims to achieve accurate alignment between the magnetic field and the liquid metal flow to avoid electric insulation of the liquid metal circuits as much as possible. Although it has yet to be confirmed through numerical analysis or experimental testing, the specific alignment strategy proves to be highly effective in reducing pressure drop in the liquid metal circuits. Besides, the neutronic results point to an excellent performance in terms of tritium breeding provided there is an optimal use of the available space between the plasma and the coils, although some arrangements must be done to satisfy also the contemplated shielding requirements. Furthermore, the internal design of the blanket segments and the optimization of the cooling system allows achieving a valuable performance in terms of balance of plant, while meeting the structural integrity criteria that have been studied at a very preliminary stage.

title: Projected Sensitivity to Atmospheric Neutrino Oscillations using a 1725 m^3 Liquid Nitrogen Detector at CJPL
abstract: Abstract In atmospheric neutrino analyses, the usable zenith-angle range is generally restricted to upward-going events to suppress the cosmic-ray muon background. Motivated by the exceptionally low underground muon background at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL), we investigate whether extending the zenith-angle acceptance can improve the sensitivity of atmospheric neutrino oscillation measurements. An existing 1725 m$^{3}$ liquid-nitrogen volume is adopted as the basis of a simplified detector model, in which the accepted zenith-angle range is extended from $\cos\theta_{\mu}\in[-1,0]$ to $\cos\theta_{\mu}\in[-1,0.3]$, and the projected oscillation sensitivity is evaluated for a 10-year exposure. The atmospheric neutrino flux is estimated by interpolating standard flux predictions as a function of geomagnetic latitude. Neutrino interactions in the surrounding rock and the liquid-nitrogen volume are simulated for neutrino energies of $E\ge0.1$ GeV, followed by secondary-particle transport and geometry-based event selection. For the benchmark oscillation parameters $\Delta$m$^{2}_{32}$ = $2.4\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{eV}^{2}$ and $\sin^{2}\theta_{23}=0.5$, the neutrino-induced muon flux from the surrounding rock is estimated to be $(3.65 \pm 1.00)\times10^{-13}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ sr$^{-1}$, corresponding to a muon yield of $(0.13 \pm 0.034)$ day$^{-1}$ in the 1725 m$^{3}$ liquid-nitrogen volume. Three-flavor neutrino oscillations are incorporated into a Poisson-likelihood $\chi^{2}$ analysis to evaluate the sensitivity to the oscillation parameters. Extending the usable zenith-angle range leads to a clear improvement in the projected oscillation sensitivity at the 90\% confidence level over a 10-year exposure. The improvement is most pronounced for $\Delta$m$^{2}_{32}$, while the improvement in the constraint on $\sin^{2}\theta_{23}$ near the best-fit point remains relatively modest. These results demonstrate that the extended zenith-angle coverage enabled by the ultra-low cosmic-ray muon background at CJPL can strengthen the projected constraints on atmospheric neutrino oscillation parameters in a large liquid-nitrogen detector. Any further distribution of this work must maintain attribution to the author(s) and the title of the work, journal citation and DOI. title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
abstract: Abstract Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
abstract: Abstract We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition–specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA–protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Constrained coupled-cluster computations yield negative-parity rotational bands
abstract: Many deformed nuclei exhibit low-lying rotational bands with negative parity. In mean-field calculations, such bands follow from symmetry restoration when the variational solution spontaneously breaks parity. However, they can also be computed in cases where the breaking of parity is not spontaneous but rather enforced by an octupole constraint. In this paper, we extend these techniques to coupled-cluster computations. We introduce octupole-constrained coupled-cluster theory, which explicitly breaks the parity of the correlated intrinsic state and restores parity and angular momentum as good quantum numbers by projection after variation. We perform coupled-cluster singles-and-doubles (CCSD) computations for $^{20}$Ne using two- and three-nucleon forces from chiral effective field theory. The energies of the positive-parity ground-state rotational band are close to data and depend only weakly on the constrained octupole moment and the Hartree--Fock reference. In contrast, the energies of the negative-parity rotational band are more sensitive to these auxiliary quantities.

title: A modular messenger benchmark for rank-two neutrino masses in lepton-number-violating R-parity violation
abstract: Abstract We study the flavor structure of Majorana neutrino masses in a modular messenger realization of lepton-number-violating $R$-parity violation. Homogeneous level-three modular symmetry, with $\Gamma'_3\simeq T'$ and an even-weight sector descending to $A_4$, relates bilinear and third-family lepton--quark couplings at a common modulus. Renormalizable mediator chains generate these interactions, and baryon triality forbids the baryon-number-violating operator. The charged-lepton and soft-sector alignments define the benchmark. The retained neutrino mass texture contains neutralino-tree and bottom--sbottom rank-one contributions and leaves one neutrino massless. For a weight-four loop direction, a bilinear displacement within the weight-two and weight-four plane preserves the massless mixing column. A symmetric weight-six loop contribution allows both deformations to change that column. The extended textures accommodate both neutrino mass orderings. Four $501\times501$ modulus profiles determine their oscillation-compatible regions and associated mass and flavor observables. Representative solutions give $m_{\beta\beta}$ between $1.47$ and $3.75$ meV for normal ordering and between $17.8$ and $48.2$ meV for inverted ordering, within the kinematic envelope of a massless neutrino spectrum. The mass sum and beta-decay mass-parameter provide complementary ordering signatures. We connect the fitted flavor coefficients to weak-scale neutralino and sbottom contributions by inverse matching and derive a conditional charged-current neutralino-decay flavor correlation.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Octupole correlations in the excited $0^+$ states and two-neutron transfers in actinide nuclei
abstract: Impacts of octupole correlations on low-energy excited $0^+$ states and two-neutron transfer intensities in Ra and Th isotopes are analyzed within the interacting boson model, using the Hamiltonian parameters that are obtained from microscopic nuclear density functional theory calculations. Incorporating the octupole degree of freedom in the model is shown to give an overall reasonable description of the ground-state-band energy levels and to lower the $0^+_2$ ones significantly. The calculation yields a number of excited $0^+$ states, most of which are formed by the configurations of more than one octupole boson. Octupole correlations make significant contributions to the $0^+_1 \to 0^+_2$ $(p,t)$ and $(t,p)$ transfer intensities in those nuclei in which the octupole collectivity is most enhanced. Behaviors of the predicted transfer intensities with the increasing neutron number along the isotopic chain reflect nuclear structural evolution.

title: Design and initial characterization of a modular tabletop Penning ion-source beamline for low-energy ion irradiation
abstract: Ion beam implantation is an effective technology for material modification, including surface engineering, doping, and irradiation. Its use in laboratories is, however, not very common due to the expensive nature and rigidity of commercial systems. To address this gap, we present the design, simulation, fabrication, and characterization of a new, modular tabletop Penning Ion Gauge source system. This system uniquely integrates high-precision beam optics, including an electrostatic quadrupole triplet for beam focusing and a Wien velocity filter for ion species selection. IBSimu and COMSOL Multiphysics® were used to model the extraction system and downstream beam dynamics, respectively. Experiments demonstrated multi-species operation (H+, He+, N+) over a large operating energy range. A key achievement is the system’s exceptionally broad, tunable beam current, with on-target currents spanning three orders of magnitude (1 nA–3 μA), accessed by adjusting the plasma discharge, gas pressure, and beam-transport conditions, delivered to an aperture-defined, approximately circular 0.5 cm2 on-target spot. The nitrogen transmission scan at 25 keV demonstrates coarse separation between N+ and N2+, with a first-order experimental resolving power of 2.43, as determined from the N+ peak. This system provides a reproducible and accessible platform, offering a useful and accessible resource for researchers in materials science, low-energy nuclear physics, and particle accelerators.

title: Full-event anomaly detection for new physics searches at the Electron-Ion Collider
abstract: The future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will offer new opportunities to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study resonant anomaly detection using machine learning and the full particle content of an event.
