We consider a new neutral gauge boson and a heavy neutral lepton as illustrative signals with different electron-jet topologies. Weakly supervised learning uses this event information to enhance the sensitivity of an invariant-mass search without identifying individual signal events during training. Comparisons with high-level observables show that the electron kinematics account for an important part of the separation, while correlations among the particles provide further sensitivity. We also construct a conditional full-event generator by adapting a model pretrained on LHC jets to produce EIC background events. A scan over signal fractions demonstrates substantial signal enhancement using the learned background reference, providing a proof of concept for this approach at the EIC. Finally, we consider a fully unsupervised graph autoencoder that provides modest signal enhancement but retains sensitivity at signal fractions too small for effective weak supervision. Our results motivate full-event anomaly detection as part of the EIC physics program and identify directions for developing methods suited to its distinct kinematics.

title: Comparison of Silvaco and Synopsys TCAD predictions including the Perugia radiation damage model in silicon pixel detectors for the HL-LHC
abstract: Abstract At the High Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC), silicon pixel detectors will be exposed to radiation fluences about 5 to 10 times larger than those experienced by the current innermost pixel layers up to today. Due to radiation damage to bulk of pixel detectors, leakage current and depletion voltage will increase significantly over time, posing severe constraints on operating conditions, with important modifications to the electric field profile due to radiation induced deep defects in silicon bulk. It is important to have reliable predictions for all observables — such as leakage current level and breakdown voltage — after irradiation, in order to estimate operational voltage values. In this paper, the predictions of Silvaco and Synopsys TCAD device simulations are compared when the surface and bulk defects and traps of the “New University of Perugia radiation damage model” are included by studying observables like leakage current, depletion and breakdown voltage, along with electric field and trap occupancy profiles. The results are quite promising regarding leakage current, depletion voltage, electric field and trap statistics, at two distinct reference temperatures and fluences.

title: Probing high-momentum components in $^{16}$O via zero-degree $(p,d)$ cross-section ratios
abstract: The $^{16}$O$(p,d)^{15}$O reaction was measured at zero degrees for incident-proton energies of 403, 604, 907 and 1209 MeV. Cross-section ratios for the 6.18-MeV (3/2$^-$) and 5.24-MeV (5/2$^+$) excited-state transitions, normalized to the ground-state transition, were previously reported in Wang et al., Phys. Lett. B 879, 140563 (2026), doi:10.1016/j.physletb.2026.140563, together with their implications for high-momentum neutron components in $^{16}$O. The present work extends that study by providing additional experimental and data-analysis details, and by reporting for the first time the ratio $R_{7.3}$, defined as the cross section populating the 7.28-MeV (7/2$^+$) state relative to that for the ground state. The positive-parity state ratios exhibit a pronounced momentum dependence, consistent with representative variational Monte Carlo trends.
authors: H. J. Ong (State Key Laboratory of Heavy Ion Science
S. Terashima (State Key Laboratory of Heavy Ion Science
I. Tanihata (Research Center for Nuclear Physics
Y. K. Tanaka (RIKEN High Energy Nuclear Physics Laboratory

title: Non-LTE Ionization Modeling for Helium and Strontium in Neutron Star Merger Ejecta
abstract: Abstract The material ejected from a binary neutron star merger produces a “kilonova,” a radioactively powered emission at ultraviolet, optical, and infrared wavelengths. The early-phase spectra of the kilonova AT2017gfo, following the gravitational wave event GW170817, exhibit a strong absorption feature around 1 μ m. Helium (He) and strontium (Sr) have been proposed as the candidate elements contributing to this feature. However, due to the lack of consistent modeling including these two elements simultaneously, the exact contributions of each element to this feature remain unclear. In this study, we develop nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium ionization models for He and Sr that take into account ionization by high-energy electrons, and estimate the abundances of each element required to reproduce the observed feature in the early-phase spectra of AT2017gfo. Our modeling indicates that about 1% of He or 1%–10% of Sr (in mass fraction) are present in the ejecta moving at v ∼ 0.15 c . This Sr mass fraction nicely agrees with the mass fraction in the solar r -process pattern. Based on comparison with nucleosynthesis calculations, our constraints suggest that r -process nucleosynthesis in GW170817 occurs at relatively low electron fraction ( Y e ≲ 0.35) and low entropy ( s ≲ 30 k B /nucleon) conditions. Generally, for Y e ≲ 0.15, the observed feature can be reproduced by He at the mass fraction expected from the α -decay of trans-Pb nuclei, and may therefore serve as an indirect signature for the production of elements beyond the third r -process peak in binary neutron star mergers.

title: Investigation of the Explodability of Massive Stars with Spectral Two-moment Neutrino Transport in Spherical Symmetry
abstract: Abstract We investigate the explodability of core-collapse supernova progenitors with zero-age main-sequence (ZAMS) masses of 9–25 M ⊙ using 1D hydrodynamical simulations with Flash-X and the DG-IMEX method of thornado . We assess one- and two-parameter explosion criteria and their connection to the internal structure of massive stars. We identify two classes of explosion outcomes. Class I requires the shock to pass the bottom of the Si/O interface together with an increasing advection-to-heating timescale ratio, while Class II follows the density-jump and shock-surge criterion, providing a less restrictive condition associated with the potential effects of multidimensional convection. The compactness parameter alone does not provide a unique measure of explodability and shows strong nonmonotonicity. The two-parameter compactness space ( ξ 1.5 , ξ 2.5 ) provides a better classification, although some discrepancies remain. We find that the M 4 – μ 4 M 4 criterion predicts our outcomes with only ∼60%–80% accuracy, lower than previously reported. Finally, the critical relation between neutrino luminosity and mass accretion rate differs between the two classes: M ̇ ∝ L ν 3 for Class I , while Class II gives M ̇ ∝ L ν 1.25 – L ν 2.36 , with the latter close to the classical M ̇ ∝ L ν 2.3 scaling.

title: Impact of ab initio E1 strength on neutron capture rates along the nickel isotopic chain
abstract: Nucleosynthesis simulations of the r-process require neutron capture rates for neutron-rich nuclei, many of which lie beyond experimental reach. Predicting these rates relies on theoretical calculations of the low-energy electric dipole (E1) strength near the neutron threshold. We present the first ab initio computation of the E1 strength along the nickel isotopic chain, for $^{58}$Ni and the even-even isotopes $^{68-80}$Ni. The E1 strength is obtained with the Lorentz integral transform coupled-cluster (LIT-CC) method, extended to axially symmetric reference states to reach open-shell nuclei, using two- and three-nucleon interactions from chiral effective field theory. The approach is benchmarked against the measured photoabsorption cross section of $^{58}$Ni and the E1 strength of $^{68}$Ni. Along the chain we find low-lying E1 strength above the neutron threshold that grows with neutron number. Including it in the reaction code TALYS enhances the neutron capture rates forming $^{68-78}$Ni between 3 and 10 GK, with an effect that increases with temperature and neutron number and an uncertainty dominated by the inversion of the integral transform. For $^{80}$Ni, where strong pygmy dipole strength lies just above threshold, the enhancement sets in already around 0.5 GK. Together, these results open the way to ab initio input for neutron capture rates along isotopic chains far from stability.

title: Why Stellar Sequences Turn Over: Fixed Points, Instability, and Equation-of-State Universality
abstract: We reformulate the stellar structure equations in the language of dynamical systems and show that the maximum mass of stellar sequences arises from the existence of a fixed point in the relativistic regime. In an appropriate representation of the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, this fixed point becomes manifest and is directly associated with the turnover of the mass-radius curve. The existence of a fixed point implies an effective reduction in dimensionality near the onset of instability, which provides a simple explanation for several equation-of-state-insensitive relations and predicts new ones. In the weakly relativistic limit, we identify a complementary universal structure shared by stellar sequences at their maximum mass, which we term the "compressible limit," and derive distinct universal relations governing the maximum mass in the Newtonian and post-Newtonian regimes. Combining these theoretical results with current astrophysical constraints, we show that the J0740+6620 pulsar is unlikely to lie near the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff maximum mass unless the equation of state exhibits a strong first-order phase transition at densities just above its central density.

title: GEANT4-based comparative study of detector response in reduced and fully instrumented silicon-tungsten sampling calorimeter
abstract: Abstract A GEANT4-based simulation study of a silicon-tungsten (Si-W) sampling calorimeter is presented to investigate electromagnetic shower development and detector response in the energy range of 1–120 GeV. Two detector configurations are considered: a reduced sequential-sampling prototype (Configuration-I), where a single silicon detector layer is placed downstream of progressively increasing tungsten absorber depths to sample the longitudinal shower evolution, and a fully instrumented sampling calorimeter (Configuration-II) consisting of twenty silicon layers interleaved with tungsten absorbers. The detector response is studied in terms of longitudinal shower development, shower maximum position, energy deposition, detector linearity, and calorimetric performance. Configuration-II provides simultaneous longitudinal sampling and allows event-by-event reconstruction of the deposited energy, yielding the expected linear response and energy resolution. Configuration-I reproduces the average longitudinal shower profiles and exhibits a strong linear correlation with the integrated shower response of Configuration-II. Although the absence of event-by-event multi-layer sampling prevents a direct determination of calorimetric energy resolution in Configuration-I, the observed correlation between two configurations is used to relate the response of the reduced prototype to that of the fully instrumented calorimeter and to estimate the corresponding calorimetric performance. The results demonstrate that the reduced prototype successfully reproduces the main characteristics of electromagnetic shower development observed in the fully instrumented detector, establishing its usefulness for detector characterization and test-beam studies when the construction of a complete prototype is limited by available resources.

title: Final-state centrality in relativistic heavy-ion simulations from neural networks
abstract: Experiments in relativistic heavy-ion collisions determine centrality from final-state quantities, usually the charged-particle multiplicity. Performing the same in hydrodynamic simulations requires millions of events, which is impractical for state-of-the-art hybrid models, and centrality is therefore commonly approximated by the initial entropy or energy. We show that neural networks trained on a few hundred hybrid events predict the event-by-event multiplicity and mean transverse momentum $[p_T]$ with relative errors of 1--2\%, which makes it possible to generate millions of collisions at a small fraction of the cost of the full simulation. For Pb--Pb collisions at $2.76$~TeV and Au--Au collisions at $200$~GeV, the initial-state and final-state definitions select nearly the same events in 10\%-wide classes, but up to 20\% of the events change class when the classes are 1\% wide. We then compute the fluctuations of $[p_T]$ and its Pearson correlations with a proxy of the elliptic flow, estimated from the initial eccentricity, and with multiplicity. The first correlation is insensitive to how centrality is defined, while the second changes substantially. The approach can be applied at every design point of Bayesian analyses at modest additional cost.

title: First measurement of wind line formation regions in an early O-type star
abstract: Context. Massive stars with their strong ionizing radiation and strong stellar winds are the key feedback agents of the Universe. Stellar winds of massive stars are often measured by fitting resonance lines in the UV using non-local thermal equilibrium (non-LTE) stellar atmosphere models. Aims. We aim to conduct the first measurement of the resonance line formation regions in an early-type eclipsing binary in the Small Magellanic Cloud, namely AzV 75. Methods. We employed photometric data from TESS and ASAS-SN in combination with radial velocity measurements from multi-epoch Hubble Space Telescope UV spectra to derive the ephemeris. We examined the intensity changes in the C IV and N V resonance lines in the UV and combined them with a light-curve analysis to estimate the region in the wind where these lines are formed. Results. We derived that AzV 75 has an orbital period of P orb = 165.925 ± 0.115 d, eccentricity of e = 0.42 ± 0.02, mass ratio of q = 0.72 ± 0.03, and inclination of i = 85.77 ◦ . With this orbital configuration, no secondary eclipse is expected. We report that the optically thick UV resonance lines exhibit flattening and shortening of the absorption trough, and weakening of their emission features, as they approach the phase of the expected secondary eclipse, while the continuum UV flux appears to remain unaffected. We illustrate that this behaviour can be well explained by the primary’s optically thick wind eclipsing the secondary star. The C IV and N V resonance line formation regions in the primary star extend up to 316 R ⊙ . Conclusions. We have measured the line formation regions of resonance lines in a stellar wind of an early O-type star. These are important benchmarks for 1D as well as 3D non-LTE stellar atmosphere models. Even though we have numerous multi-epoch UV spectra at hand, the eclipse is not fully sampled, leaving some freedom in the derived sizes of the line formation regions. A first comparison to 1D stellar atmosphere models indicates that a classical β law with an exponent of β = 0.5 instead of β = 0.8 might be favoured for the primary star’s velocity field.

title: Toward testing antinucleon$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus optical potentials with antineutron scattering lengths
abstract: The antineutron$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus scattering length is currently known only indirectly, via antiproton$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus optical potentials fitted to level shifts and widths of antiprotonic atoms. The antineutron$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus and antiproton$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus potentials are related to each other through charge symmetry. We calculate the scattering length from optical potentials proposed for antiprotonic atoms using nucleon density distributions as input. We find that the scattering length for an $N>Z$ nuclide is largely affected by the poorly constrained neutron density distribution and by a possible isovector interaction, one of the mechanisms introduced to reproduce the isotope dependence of antiprotonic $^{40,48}\mathrm{Ca}$ data. For $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$, the isovector term modifies the scattering length by $0.3\unicode{x2013}0.4\,\mathrm{fm}$ ($0.4\unicode{x2013}0.5\,\mathrm{fm}$) for the real (imaginary) part, an order of magnitude beyond the uncertainty propagated from the isoscalar potential. As no antineutron$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus scattering data are available below $76\,\mathrm{MeV}/c$, a direct measurement with recently proposed low-energy antineutron beams would provide the first access to the antinucleon$\unicode{x2013}$nucleus interaction in the $s$-wave regime.

title: The Fock representation of the Coulomb interaction. II. Three-body bound states
abstract: The Fock representation of the unscreened Coulomb interaction, a block of separable terms with analytic form factors and strengths, is included in the momentum-space Faddeev kernel of three-body bound states beside the separable nuclear terms. A bound-state kernel evaluates every pair interaction at negative pair energies, where the representation is exact and convergent, so the Coulomb force enters without a screening radius and without a limiting procedure. With this representation the $^{3}$H--$^{3}$He splitting of the CD~Bonn potential is in very good agreement with the exact Faddeev result; in the $S$-wave model space the Coulomb-distorted form factors give about half the Fock value. The Feshbach--Schur projection of the Pauli-forbidden states acts on the forbidden eigenstates of the nuclear-plus-Coulomb pair Hamiltonian, the Coulomb-dressed states obtained inside the extended separable problem, as the eigenstate condition requires. The Coulomb displacements of the cluster-model states of $^{6}$Li, $^{9}$Be and $^{12}$C and of the $^{9}$Be--$^{9}$B mirror pair are given. The eigenstate condition is tested in $^{9}$Be and $^{12}$C by replacing the Coulomb-dressed forbidden states with those of the Coulomb-subtracted interaction and with the oscillator functions of the orthogonality-condition model.

title: The Fock representation of the Coulomb interaction. I. Two-body problem
abstract: In the momentum-space few-body theory of light nuclei, where the Faddeev equations with separable two-body input close on one-variable amplitudes, the unscreened Coulomb interaction is exactly separable by the stereographic projection of Fock, with analytic form factors and strengths, and the truncation of the expansion converges at negative energies. It is derived here as an operator identity for the potential and added, without screening or fitting, as a block of separable terms to the separable nuclear input of a charged pair. The representation is compared with the screening--renormalization method and with Coulomb-distorted form factors on two-body benchmarks: the off-shell $t$~matrix, the Coulomb displacement of the $\alpha p$ Pauli-forbidden state, and the Coulomb-modified phases of the $pp$, $\alpha p$ and $\alpha\alpha$ pairs. The Feshbach--Schur projection of the Pauli-forbidden state is shown to require the Coulomb-dressed eigenstate, which the Fock block provides within the same separable problem. At positive energy a finite truncation is a screened Coulomb potential with an analytic, momentum-dependent radius.

title: Separable representations of two-body interactions for Faddeev calculations of light nuclei
abstract: Separable representations of the Ernst--Shakin--Thaler type are constructed for the charge-dependent Bonn (CD~Bonn) nucleon--nucleon potential ($j\le4$; $nn$, $np$, $pp$), for the Kanada--Kaneko--Nagata--Nomoto (KKNN) $\alpha N$ interaction, and for the Buck--Friedrich--Wheatley (BFW) $\alpha\alpha$ interaction. They are the input for momentum-space Faddeev calculations of $A=3$, $6$, $9$, and $12$ systems. The representations are tested against six acceptance criteria: off-shell accuracy at the pair energies sampled by the three-body kernel, phase shifts, effective-range parameters, bound and resonant states, and numerical stability.

title: Novel chiral-wobbling excitation mode in atomic nuclei
abstract: The properties of high-spin band structures in $^{74}$Br nucleus are investigated using the triaxial projected shell model (TPSM) and particle triaxial rotor (PTR) approaches. It has already been demonstrated that lowest three bands observed in $^{74}$Br have a characteristic feature of a chiral-wobbler. The first excited band is the chiral partner of the yrast band and the second excited band is the wobbling band based on the yrast state. We have analyzed the third excited band using the TPSM and PTR calculated quantities, and a unique character of this band is revealed. It is predicted that this band is the chiral partner of the second excited band, and is also a wobbling mode based on the first excited band.

title: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
abstract: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $\Delta=1$ and $\Delta=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.

title: Predictions for neutron-tagged Coulomb dissociation in ultraperipheral Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions
abstract: The photonuclear response reflects nuclear structure and the dynamics of excitation and decay, with neutron-emission channels retaining information that can be obscured in inclusive dissociation yields. We calculate specified-side and mutual neutron-tagged Coulomb-dissociation cross sections in ultraperipheral $^{96}_{44}\mathrm{Ru}+{}^{96}_{44}\mathrm{Ru}$ and $^{96}_{40}\mathrm{Zr}+{}^{96}_{40}\mathrm{Zr}$ collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=200~\mathrm{GeV}$ using an impact-parameter-dependent equivalent-photon framework with photonuclear inputs from TALYS calculations and ENDF evaluations. Across the two input sets, the predicted Ru/Zr ratios span $1.54$-$1.71$ for exact $1n$ and $2.49$-$3.09$ for $1n1n$, while inclusive $Xn$ (at least one neutron) and $XnXn$ ratios remain near unity at $0.96$-$0.99$ and $1.05$-$1.10$, respectively. The one-neutron ratios lie well above the corresponding flux-only $Z^2$ and $Z^4$ charge-scaling references, reflecting differences in the low-energy one-neutron response that are amplified by mutual tagging. This topology hierarchy identifies neutron-tagged isobar ratios as sensitive probes of photonuclear response, revealing response differences hidden in inclusive dissociation. These calculations also provide neutron-emission inputs for neutron-tagged vector-meson photoproduction in isobar collisions.

title: Application and Optimization of the GET Electronics System for Double-Sided Silicon Strip Detector Readout
abstract: Double-sided silicon strip detectors (DSSDs) are widely used for charged-particle detection in nuclear reaction experiments. However, the large number of readout channels associated with DSSDs places stringent demands on front-end electronics and data acquisition systems, particularly in experiments employing large detector arrays. In this work, we investigate the application and optimization of the Generic Electronics for Time Projection Chambers (GET) system for multi-channel DSSD readout. Through optimization of the DC-blocking capacitors on the custom-designed interface board and waveform-based energy extraction algorithms, the readout system achieves an energy resolution of {\sigma} = 22 keV for 5.49 MeV alpha particles. Its performance is further validated in a representative nuclear physics experiment employing charged-particle telescopes. The results demonstrate that the GET system provides a versatile and scalable waveform-sampling solution for multi-channel DSSD readout.

title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
abstract: Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb$^{-1}$. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high $p_\mathrm{T}$. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

title: nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions
abstract: We present the new release of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) from the nCTEQ collaboration: nCTEQ26. In this global analysis, we combine our recent, more selective studies of different experimental measurements and extend them to determine a modern set of nPDFs based on the largest selection of data considered to date. This selection includes neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), fixed-target Drell-Yan, and a large variety of collider data from RHIC and LHC Runs I and II. On the theoretical side, we match this considerably extended kinematic range with a new nPDF parametrization that combines a flexible functional form of the x-dependence with a quadratic logarithmic nuclear A-dependence as well as target-mass and deuteron corrections for the reliable inclusion of high-x DIS data. Following our previous successful work, we partially employ a data-driven approach that allows us to not only include open heavy-quark data, but also quarkonium data. In addition, we establish the consistency of this approach by comparing it to an alternative fit based on perturbative predictions of open heavy-quark data alone. We determine the uncertainties of our nCTEQ26 nPDFs with a Hessian error analysis, test their reliability by comparing our nPDFs to other, similar recent analyses, and make predictions for current and future experimental measurements that have not been included in the analysis.

title: The LZ inelastic splitting as a probe of anomaly mediation
abstract: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate admits an interpretation in terms of pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic $Z$ interaction. In the MSSM, the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound, while a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy. We realize such spectra in the MRSSM, where an $R$-symmetric Dirac bino produces the required $Z$ transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance. We impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of $N=2$ supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy. With the remaining model parameters held fixed, we obtain spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current. If anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV. A five-dimensional warped construction generates this scale through Goldberger-Wise stabilization and a loop correction to the no-scale K\"ahler potential. The spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos and long-lived charged states.

title: Testing coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering N dependence
abstract: Despite its elusive character, coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) detection is evolving as a precision measurement from different neutrino measurements. In this note we show how CEvNS experiments using the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) are robust measurements that enter into a precision era. Despite the interplay of nuclear and elementary particle physics, we demonstrate that CEvNS current measurements are accurately described by using only one extra parameter, the number of neutrons, $N$. By making this test, we illustrate that current CEvNS are precise enough to reconstruct the number of neutrons in the nuclear target. At the same time, determining the number of nucleons in the target material can be used as a benchmark for the precision and accuracy of this kind of detectors.

title: Global gyrokinetic simulations of electromagnetic turbulence in STEP
abstract: Abstract This paper presents gradient-driven global electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations for a conceptual burning flat-top operating point of STEP (Tholerus et al 2024 Nucl. Fusion 64 106030), STEP-EC-HD, and investigates how non-local effects influence the nonlinear saturation and transport of the electromagnetic turbulence at finite β . Local gyrokinetic simulations have shown that including δ B ∥ is essential for the dominant hybrid kinetic ballooning modes, or hKBMs, to be unstable in STEP (Kennedy et al 2024 Nucl. Fusion 64 086049). Using the long-wavelength δ B ∥ solver (Sheffield et al 2024 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 67 015028) implemented in GENE (Jenko et al 2000 Phys. Plasmas 7 1904–10), this work demonstrates that the linear mode spectrum can be accurately captured in global geometry, which results in good agreement with an ensemble of local flux-tube simulations. The global framework reproduces the hKBMs identified in Kennedy et al (2023 Nucl. Fusion 63 126061), while microtearing modes remain challenging to resolve due to their shorter radial scales. Nonlinear simulations reveal clear evidence of an electromagnetic transition to states with extremely large heat fluxes, consistent with local simulations and with the predicted loss of zonal-flow regulation for this proposed operating point (Kennedy et al 2026 Nucl. Fusion ). These findings establish the capability of global gyrokinetics to capture finite- β dynamics in STEP-like plasmas and motivate future work to identify the conditions governing this transition.

title: Dijet hadrochemistry: tomography of jet-induced medium excitation and diffusion wake
abstract: Energetic partons traversing the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions induce a medium response that modifies the production of associated hadrons, whose chemical composition provides a sensitive probe of this response. We study jet-associated hadrochemistry using the coupled linear Boltzmann transport and hydrodynamics model with a hybrid hadronization scheme that combines Cooper--Frye particlization, quark coalescence and string fragmentation. For inclusive charged jets in $p+p$ and 0--10\% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$~TeV, the calculated in-cone $K/\pi$ and $p/\pi$ ratios are enhanced in Pb+Pb relative to $p+p$ collisions, consistent with preliminary ALICE measurements, with coalescence between shower and thermal partons providing a substantial contribution. Extending the analysis to dijet events, we predict that both ratios are enhanced around the leading and subleading jets, more strongly around the subleading jet and more pronounced for larger radial size. After mixed-event acceptance correction and sideband background subtraction, the yields of associated pions, kaons and protons all become negative near $|\Delta\phi|\simeq\pi/2$, signaling a depletion caused by the diffusion wake. The $K/\pi$ and $p/\pi$ ratios of these deficits remain finite and exceed the $p+p$ values around the jet peaks, indicating that the missing hadrons originate from jet-excited medium. These results establish dijet hadrochemistry as an experimentally accessible tomographic probe of jet-induced medium excitation and the diffusion wake.

title: The throttling refrigeration system for high cooling power recovery of the PandaX-xT cryogenic distillation system for radon removal
abstract: The PandaX-xT cryogenic distillation system for removing radon (Rn) is designed to operate at a high liquid flow rate of 856 kg/h, equal to 5 liters per minute (LPM), to meet the required Rn concentration. However, it is challenging to maintain a continuous supply of cooling power (20 kW) for the Rn-removal system. This work proposes a throttling refrigeration system to address the power supply problem for the next-generation PandaX-xT dark matter detection experiment. The system utilizes carbon tetrafluoride (R14) refrigerant to recover power based on heat pump principles. The cooling power from the liquid xenon (LXe) in the reboiler at 178 K is transferred to liquefy the gaseous xenon (GXe) in the cryostat through the phase change circulation of R14, enabling xenon (Xe) to return to the detector in the same state as when it was extracted. Consequently, a stable circulation for liquid distillation is established. Given the high cost of Xe, a research and development (R&D) experiment has been conducted to validate the feasibility of this high-cooling-recovery system by using ethanol as a substitute for Xe. Experimental results indicate that the proposed system could achieve a cooling power recovery of 25 kW, with a recovery efficiency of 99%+-0.5%. Additionally, process simulation and optimization of the throttling refrigeration cycle are performed using Aspen Hysys. The deviation between the simulation and experimental results is found to be <3.64%. These findings demonstrate that implementing Rn-removal distillation at a high flow rate is feasible, eliminating the need for liquid nitrogen or cryocoolers. This system could save approximately 3650 m3 of liquid nitrogen per year or reduce power consumption by 230 kW.

title: Stringent constraints on nonstandard neutrino interactions using high-purity $\nu_{\mu}$ CC events in IceCube DeepCore
abstract: The neutral-current (NC) nonstandard interactions (NSIs) of neutrinos with fermions can modify the flavor oscillations of atmospheric neutrinos as they propagate through the Earth. We present constraints on the NC-NSI parameters $\varepsilon_{\mu\tau}$ and $\varepsilon_{\tau\tau}-\varepsilon_{\mu\mu}$ (one at a time) using a high-purity sample of $\nu_{\mu}$ charged-current atmospheric neutrino events collected by IceCube DeepCore over 7.5 years of livetime. These two parameters significantly affect the $\nu_\mu$ disappearance channel for which this golden event sample is optimized by IceCube Collaboration. The best fit to this dataset is consistent with no NSI hypothesis, and we place the stringent constraints $-\,0.0094 < \varepsilon_{\mu\tau} < 0.0079$ and $-\,0.031 < \varepsilon_{\tau\tau}-\varepsilon_{\mu\mu} < 0.029$ at the 90% confidence level, assuming normal mass ordering.

title: Simulation Study of Reconstruction of Cosmic Ray Extensive Air Shower with Thermal Neutron Detected by ENDA
abstract: In the investigation of the "knee" region within the cosmic ray energy spectrum, extensive air shower (EAS) reconstruction by using different EAS secondary particles are of paramount importance for energy determination and composition separation and finally measurement of energy spectrum of different cosmic ray composition. The Electron-Neutron Detector Array (ENDA) is designed to detect thermal neutrons generated in the ground by high energy hadrons which constitute the "backbone" of EAS and carry vital information regarding the primary cosmic rays. At present, ENDA-64, consisting of 64 detectors, is employed inside the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO). This work simulates the response of ENDA and investigates the lateral distributions of thermal neutrons. A comparison of the NKG and double-exponential functions for describing this distribution using MC simulation data shows that the double-exponential function is more accurate. The mean difference between fitted and measured thermal neutron density is within ~ 6%. Meanwhile, the thermal neutron density at 10 m from the shower axis, $\rho_n$, depends mainly on the sum of all hadrons energy or the number of high-energy hadrons. The relationship between $\rho_n$ and EAS hadron energy or the number of high-energy hadrons can be well fitted by a linear function on a log scale. This work is fundamental for energy determination and composition separation with hybrid detection by using ENDA in the near future.

title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
abstract: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score. Across the configurations and benchmark signals considered, supervised objectives, which exploit simulation process labels during training, generally outperform their self-supervised counterparts and, in their best configurations, improve on an autoencoder trained directly on kinematic features, raising the signal efficiency at 10% background acceptance on all held-out processes. We further introduce a local diagnostic pipeline that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model to the SM latent space, profiles each component through high-level observables without process labels, localizes the flagged events, and ranks observables by their local discriminating power. The ranking recovers the defining kinematics of the held-out processes, while correlating the anomaly score with the same observables quantifies how closely the score tracks them, revealing cases where the most discriminating observable is not the one the score follows most closely.

title: Detector Performance and Dark Matter Sensitivity of CYGNO with HFO-1234ze Gas Admixtures
abstract: The CYGNO project develops optical time projection chambers for directional dark matter searches, using a He:CF4 (60:40) gas mixture at atmospheric pressure and a triple-GEM amplification stage. We investigate the addition of 1-10% HFO-1234ze as a hydrogen-containing additive with low global warming potential. The charge response and scintillation light yield are studied with the MANGO prototype, complemented by secondary-scintillation spectroscopy of the baseline mixture and mixtures containing 1% and 2.5% HFO. Increasing the HFO concentration shifts the charge-response curves towards higher GEM voltages and strongly suppresses the scintillation emission in both the ultraviolet and visible bands. We use the measured optical response to estimate the impact on projected spin-independent WIMP-nucleon and spin-dependent WIMP-proton exclusion limits for a CYGNO-like directional detector. Under the assumed detector-response model, the higher optical energy threshold largely outweighs the benefit of the additional light target, although a 1% HFO admixture retains a limited advantage for low-mass spin-dependent interactions. An idealized fixed-threshold benchmark is also considered to illustrate the potential of the modified target composition without the optical threshold penalty.

title: Beam Spill Structure Measurements at CEE Using the T0 Detector
abstract: The Cooling Storage Ring External-target Experiment (CEE) at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou uses a slow-extracted heavy-ion beam whose temporal profile directly affects detector occupancy. The existing CEE T0 detector, originally designed to provide the event start time, is extended in this work to measure the spill structure immediately upstream of the fixed target. The detector consists of a 0.8-mm-thick EJ-200 plastic scintillator read out by 16 silicon photomultipliers at each end. The SiPM signals are conditioned and discriminated by the NINO front-end electronics, and the resulting timing signals are recorded using an FPGA-based time-to-digital converter. In laboratory tests, with the laser trigger set to its maximum available repetition frequency of 100~MHz, the recorded T0 hit-rate distribution was concentrated around 100~MHz. During the June 2024 beam test with 350-MeV/u Kr ions, the accelerator team varied several operating settings, including RF-KO, sextupole, and feedback settings, while T0 independently recorded the corresponding spill profiles. An empirical representation was used to extract the rise, plateau, and fall durations from the stored profiles. The plateau duration was used as the primary comparison metric while accelerator stability and RF-system load were also considered. The measurements clearly distinguished the spill-profile responses associated with different accelerator settings. The spill obtained with the selected settings exhibited a more nearly rectangular envelope than the initial profile, although residual fluctuations and a terminal spike remained. These results demonstrate that the existing CEE T0 detector can provide independent beam-structure information during accelerator tuning.

title: ASKAP Monitoring of the Rubin Deep Drilling Fields
abstract: In the past decade, time domain astronomy surveys across the multi-messenger spectrum have developed "alert streams" which circulate observational information in real-time to the wider astronomical community. Despite this being standard practice for optical, gamma-ray and gravitational wave time domain astronomy for several years now, this kind of infrastructure has not yet been deployed at-scale for radio telescopes. We are conducting a long-term monitoring program that targets the Rubin Deep Drilling Fields using the Australian SKA Pathfinder (ASKAP). The primary goal of this program is to provide serendipitous radio observations of all objects of interest in these fields, and circulate that information in as close to real-time as possible. In this manuscript we outline the survey plans and status, the infrastructure we have developed to disseminate this information and an initial data release comprising 5 months of ASKAP observations of each field (although only 3 months overlaps with Rubin) conducted on an approximately 10 day cadence with a noise level of $\sim 60\,\mu$Jy. As part of this data release, we present updated high-cadence radio light curves to the tidal disruption event AT2018hyz and the supernova SN2024abfo along with the discovery of two new radio variables, a possible tidal disruption event ASKAP J095711.5+051205 and an in-progress extreme scattering event ASKAP J005026.4-422958. The scientific results from this program along with the infrastructure developed to acquire them will lay the foundation for the integration of future radio imaging surveys into the broader multi-messenger alert stream, leading the way for major facilities such as the Schmidt Observatory System and the SKA.

title: The Instrumented Baffle at the Input Mode Cleaner of Advanced Virgo Plus: Four years of Successful Operation as a Monitor of Stray Light
abstract: The suspended end mirror of the Input Mode Cleaner cavity in the Advanced Virgo Plus interferometer was equipped with an instrumented baffle in Spring 2021, serving as a demonstrator of the technology in preparation for the installation of large instrumented baffles in the main arms of the interferometer. This baffle includes tens of sensors positioned near the mirror to enable monitoring of stray light within the cavity. In this contribution, we assess the stability and performance of the instrument after four years of operation. After introducing the main characteristics of the baffle, we study the distribution of stray light and show that the instrumented baffle can be used to monitor laser stability and alignment within the cavity. Finally, we perform a noise level assessment with data from the final stages of the O4b commissioning and conclude that the baffle does not introduce any additional disturbance to the normal operation of the interferometer.

title: Probing the onset of hydrodynamization in peripheral p-Pb collisions at √ s NN = 5.02 TeV
abstract: Abstract We estimate the multiplicity scale below which the hydrodynamic description of small systems, such as p-Pb collisions, becomes increasingly sensitive to non-hydrodynamic effects. The sensitivity of experimental observables, namely the elliptic flow coefficient, is investigated by varying the shear relaxation time within second-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamics.To achieve this, a representative system of peripheral p-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} =$ 5.02 TeV is simulated utilizing the state-of-the-art JETSCAPE event generator. The soft-sector dynamics are modeled via a sequence of initial conditions, a pre-equilibrium stage, hydrodynamics, and a hadronic afterburner. Transverse momentum spectra and rapidity distributions for light-flavored hadrons are extracted and compared with experimental data. The resulting increase in elliptic flow fluctuations indicates a breakdown of fluid behavior at a rapidity density of $dN/dy \sim 10\text{--}15$ for p-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} =$ 5.02 TeV.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Measurement of the free ion yield and estimate of the electron mobility of Trimethyl-Bismuth (TMBi)
abstract: This paper investigates the physical characteristics of the liquid Trimethyl-Bismuth (TMBi) relevant for charge readout in potential TMBi filled detectors for Positron-Emission-Tomography (PET) instruments. The high photo-efficiency and the possibility of fast timing by detection of Cherenkov light created in the liquid are both favorable for use of TMBi in a PET system. However, to obtain a high position and energy resolution also a readout of the charge signal created due to the absorption of a 511 keV photon is required. For this purpose the liquid has to be clean of electro-negative and ionic impurities. A distillation technique was developed within this study as one of the possible methods to remove such impurities and a measurement on the efficiency of this cleaning method is provided. The relevant quantities for an efficient charge readout are the free ion yield and the electron mobility of the liquid. We report on a new measurement of the zero-field free ion yield in TMBi and, using that result, produce an estimate of the electron mobility. The rather low zero-field free ion yield and its much lower expected electron mobility compared to tetramethyl-n compounds like TMSi question the use of the trimethyl molecule TMBi for a PET detector liquid. But we are also giving arguments that the tetramethyl molecule TMPb could be an interesting alternative.

title: Looking for WIMPs through the neutrino fogs
abstract: We revisit the expected sensitivity of large-scale xenon detectors to Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs). Assuming current primary noise sources can be mitigated, we find that with the present discrimination power between nuclear and electron recoils, the experimental sensitivity is limited not only by atmospheric neutrinos' nuclear recoils (''nuclear recoil neutrino fog'') but also by solar neutrinos' electron-recoil events (''electron recoil neutrino fog''). While this is known by experimentalists, it is often missed or misunderstood by theorists, and we therefore emphasize this effect. We set up a realistic detector simulation to quantify the contamination of the WIMP signal from both these neutrino backgrounds. We observe that the electron-recoil background remains significant even for signal rates exceeding those of atmospheric neutrinos, as predicted by most electroweak WIMP candidates. We update the projections for the required exposure to exclude/discover a given electroweak WIMP, streamlining the computation of their signal rates and uncertainties. We show that all of the real WIMPs with zero hypercharge can be excluded (discovered) with a 50 tonne year (300 tonne year) exposure. A similar exposure will allow to probe a large portion of the viable parameter space for complex WIMP with non-zero hypercharge.

title: CNN-based Position Reconstruction for the T0 Detector in the HIRFL-CSR External-target Experiment
abstract: The T0 detector provides the event start time for the HIRFL-CSR external-target experiment, and its multi-channel readout signals also contain 2D position information of incident particles. In the CEE experiment, the dedicated beam-profile detector has a rate capability of only ~1 kHz, far below the beam event rate of up to 1 MHz, so it cannot provide real-time beam-spot monitoring under high-rate data-taking or an event time reference. To fill this gap, this work studies a CNN-based position reconstruction method that enables the T0 detector to provide both start time and beam-spot information. The over-threshold times and time-over-threshold (TOT) values from 32 SiPM channels are reorganized into a geometry-preserving input tensor. Time features are corrected by event-wise mean-time subtraction, and TOT features are normalized by an event-wise trimmed mean before feature standardization. A customized CNN directly regresses the incident coordinates. Training and validation samples are built with Geant4 simulation and waveform digitization, and the method is evaluated using a pulsed-laser scanning data set with known position labels. On independent test sets, the residual standard deviations for uniformly distributed planar simulation data are about 1.11 and 1.04 mm in x and y. For the discrete laser-scanning geometry, the resolutions are about 2.36 and 1.34 mm in simulation and 2.42 and 1.41 mm in experiment. The trained model is applied to CEE zero-field beam data collected at the Institute of Modern Physics, Lanzhou, in January 2026, and a 2D beam-spot distribution is reconstructed. These results show the T0 detector's potential as a high-rate beam-spot monitor while retaining its role as an event start-time detector.

title: A new device for live cell imaging of biological samples under in-plane shear
abstract: The effect of mechanical stresses and deformations upon the behavior and properties of cells and tissues is a topic of paramount interest in the field of biophysics. Its understanding is essential for deepening our comprehension of cellular responses to environmental stimuli, with implications in fields ranging from embryogenesis to tumor development. For boosting the understanding in this field, it is important to develop devices for the application of simple deformations in order to probe the cellular response to the basic mechanical transformations. While a number of stretching devices have been developed, in-plane shearing deformation has been little investigated. Here, a new device is introduced that allows the application of homogeneous in-plane shear upon a cell monolayer while imaging the sample with a commercial optical microscope. A description of the faced experimental challenges is reported and a full characterization is presented. It is demonstrated the capability of the device to apply reproducible, controlled and homogeneous shear of both single cells and confluent cellular monolayers.

title: The School on Gravity: from motion to commotion
abstract: Understanding the gravitational interaction is one of the great scientific endeavors of the 21st century. The Nobel Prize-winning discovery of gravitational waves in 2015, and subsequent detections by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration, have marked a revolutionary step forward in physics and astrophysics by opening an entirely new window for exploring the Universe. Future upgrades to these detectors, along with upcoming facilities such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and radio and optical instruments, promise other breakthrough discoveries that the next generation of scientists will need to interpret. The School on Gravity (22--26 June 2026, Copenhagen) aimed to introduce junior scientists--graduate students and advanced undergraduates with a background in general relativity--to a wide range of foundational topics in the exciting new field of gravitational-wave physics. Topics spanned from the theory of motion, to new challenges introduced by quantum physics, to the astrophysics of black holes and source modeling for gravitational-wave detectors. The School on Gravity took place at the legendary Auditorium A of the Niels Bohr Institute, inviting students and lecturers to challenge current paradigms in gravitational physics in the spirit of the quantum revolution that unfolded in this very room. These lecture notes aim at opening up those new ideas presented in Auditorium A to the rest of the scientific community.

title: Prospects for detecting axion-like particles via $W^+W^-$ fusion at the FCC-eh
abstract: Abstract We investigate the prospective sensitivity of the FCC-eh to the ALP-$W^{\pm}$ interaction via the ALP-mediated $W^+W^-$ fusion process $e^- p \to \nu_e j W^{+}W^{-}$, followed by the semileptonic decay $W^{+}W^{-} \to l^{+}\nu_{l} jj$. Focusing on the $g_{aWW}$ coupling, we consider a benchmark FCC-eh configuration with $E_e=140~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $E_p=50~\mathrm{TeV}$, assuming an integrated luminosity of 2 $\text{ab}^{-1}$ and an initial electron beam polarization of $P(e^-)=-80\%$. Under the adopted configuration, the FCC-eh can access a broad ALP mass range spanning from approximately 100 GeV to 1 TeV, with the projected sensitivity to $g_{aWW}$ at the $\mathcal{O}(1)~\mathrm{TeV}^{-1}$ level. Our results indicate that the FCC-eh has considerable potential for probing the interaction between the ALP and $W^{\pm}$ bosons.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Constraints on Compact Dark Matters Population from microlensing Effect of Gravitational Wave for the third-generation gravitational Wave Detector
abstract: Abstract Since the first direct detection of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary black-hole merger by the LIGO-Virgo Collaboration, GWs have emerged as a powerful probe of astrophysics and cosmology. If extragalactic compact dark matter (DM) candidates, such as primordial black holes, constitute a non-negligible fraction of the DM component over a broad mass range, they can imprint distinctive microlensing signatures on GW signals. In this work, we develop a framework to infer the population properties of extragalactic compact DM by simulating microlensing GWs in the frequency band of the third-generation ground-based GW detector, the Einstein Telescope, and analyzing them via hierarchical Bayesian inference. For a population described by a power-law mass function, we show that the detection of only several microlensing GW events among $10^4$ binary black-hole coalescences can constrain the compact DMs abundance to the level of $\sim 10^{-3}$. This forecast demonstrates that searching for and identifying microlensing signatures in future GW observations can provide a complementary approach to constraining compact DM scenarios.

title: Investigation of magnetic field ripple effects on charged particles transport in scrape-off layer of Heliotron J
abstract: Abstract The impact of helical magnetic ripples on the transport of plasma and carbon impurities in the scrape-off layer (SOL) of a Heliotron J device was investigated using the EMC3-EIRENE code. Comparisons with a simplified one-dimensional fluid model revealed that the transport behavior varied with the Knudsen number ( K ), defined as the ratio of the ion–ion collisional mean-free path to the ripple scale length. In the weakly collisional regime ( K ≫ 1 ), the qualitative trends suggested by the fluid model indicate that the magnetic mirror effects become dominant, the conductive heat flux governs the heat transport, and the impurity density follows a Boltzmann distribution. Conversely, in the collisional regime ( K ≪ 1 ), the transport exhibits nozzle-like fluid behavior, convective heat flux governs heat transport, and impurities couple to the bulk plasma. These characteristics underscore the importance of charged-particle transport along magnetic field lines in the SOL of fusion devices, where magnetic ripples fluctuate significantly with changes in the magnetic field configuration.

title: Inductive bias and out-of-distribution generalization in deep learning surrogates for 2D PDE dynamics
abstract: Abstract Partial differential equations (PDEs) are a foundational tool for modeling physical systems. However, high-fidelity numerical simulations are often computationally intensive, which has prompted the development of surrogate models in the field of scientific machine learning. While recent approaches have achieved high predictive accuracy by employing complex architectures and extensive datasets, many scientific applications offer only a limited number of simulation trajectories. In this study, we examine the impact of architectural inductive biases on the learning of two-dimensional PDE in data-limited settings. Instead of proposing a highly expressive model, we deliberately adopt a simple multi-channel U-Net modified to enforce periodic boundary conditions. In this study, we compare this architecture with transformer-based and UNet variants such as vision transformer (ViT), adaptive fourier neural operator (AFNO), PDE-Transformer (PDE-T), and UNet with Kolmogorov-Arnold Layers (KAN-UNet) under a common training setup across five PDE families. To keep comparisons uniform and to mimic partial observability in real measurements, we train all models on rollouts of a single representative scalar field per system. Despite its simplicity, the adapted U-Net consistently matches or outperforms these more complex models in forecasting accuracy, spectral similarity, and physics-based metrics while requiring substantially less training time. The findings of this study demonstrate that, in scenarios where data is limited, the judicious selection of inductive biases can often prove to be more advantageous than increasing the model complexity for the purpose of learning the dynamics of PDEs.

title: Holographic generative flows with AdS/CFT
abstract: Abstract Holography, in the form of the anti-de Sitter/conformal field theory correspondence, offers a natural setting for generative modelling. Data on a boundary manifold lifts into a higher-dimensional bulk through a propagator, and this extra dimension plays the role of a flow parameter. We exploit this structure to build Generative AdS (GenAdS), an approach to generative flow matching in which the dynamics are represented by the evolution of fields in AdS, together with a residual correction learned by a neural network. Boundary samples are encoded as scalar sources, transported into the bulk along the flow, and decoded after numerical integration. Our paradigm combines a Fourier-space encoding scheme for the data as AdS sources, a normalised radial phase space in which to stage the flow-matching dynamics, and a Klein–Gordon backbone to guide the flow. On a two-dimensional checkerboard benchmark, our experiments show that most of the benefit of GenAdS comes from the Fourier representation and convolutional architecture. However, when we remove momentum-channel regularisation, our most physics-informed GenAdS variant rivals the strongest physics-free control on boundary violation. On modified National Institute of Standards and Technology, GenAdS models remain close to a convolutional baseline on fidelity while achieving significantly higher recall at comparable precision, suggesting a fidelity-coverage trade-off. Our findings establish GenAdS as a physically interpretable and experimentally controllable framework for generative modelling, with many avenues for future extension.

title: Error field penetration threshold from two-fluids compressible linear drift magneto-hydrodynamics
abstract: Abstract The linear plasma response to a resonant error field (EF) is formalized by the so-called ‘delta-prime’ parameter Δ ′ , representing the amplitude and phase of the current sheet induced at the resonant surface mostly by the electron fluid rotation. In combination with momentum transport, Δ ′ determines the critical EF amplitude above which a wall-locked magnetic island is formed (penetration threshold). In the context of two-fluids drift linear magneto-hydrodynamic a semi-analytical computation of Δ ′ , carried out with a low-beta ordering assumption, and the estimated penetration threshold for the ohmic tokamak, have been recently published (P. Zanca 2025 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 67 105 033). Here we present a necessary completion of that work brought by the inclusion of compressible flow, density perturbation, parallel energy transport and electron viscosity. In particular, electron viscosity has been discovered to be an important term in Ohm’s law in a previous study which adopted the high-poloidal beta ordering (J. C. Waybright, J.-K. Park Phys. Plasmas 31 022502 (2024)). Here, we confirm the relevance of electron viscosity within the scope of a different model. On the contrary, compressible flow, density perturbation and parallel energy transport do not modify significantly the EF penetration threshold, at least within the present linear theory. After reconsidering the ohmic tokamak with the refined model, we present a new analysis of the additionally heated tokamak, showing a strong positive dependence of the EF threshold on the electron fluid perpendicular rotation frequency ω e . All the scaling laws of the EF penetration threshold here derived present a strong density dependence, in general agreement with the experiments. Moreover, the model prediction is compatible with EF penetration experiments performed in JET NBI heated discharges. Finally, we provide a sensitivity study of the model prediction from the electron viscosity strength.

title: Comment on 'Non-equilibrium ignition of proton–boron plasmas via stochastic-adaptive reconnection control'
abstract: Abstract Recently, Oleg Agamalov~\cite{Oleg} proposed a novel mechanism for non-equilibrium ignition of proton–boron fusion, with key parameters $T_i\approx600$~keV, $T_e\approx65$~keV and $Q_\mathrm{eng}>5$. The proposed operating cycle is driven by triggered high-frequency magnetic reconnection and Alfven ``hammers'' that channel energy mainly into ions, heating them in a much shorter time than it takes for the energy to be transferred to electrons via collisional relaxation. A crucial assumption is that the burn time is much shorter than the thermal equilibration time, so that the hot ions are depleted by fusion before the electrons can catch up in temperature. However, we show here that, given the actual proton–boron fusion reactivity, this assumption is not realistic.

title: Adiabatic evolution of hadronic neutron stars
abstract: In this paper we compute several structural properties of static and rotating neutron stars, considering both rigid and differential rotation. To this end, we use a finite-temperature beta-stable equation of state (EOS) extending the zero-temperature hadronic EOS derived by Fortin et al. (2017). We account for the formation of hyperons and the presence of a neutrino-trapped component. Our goal is to provide insights into the long-term evolution of a protoneutron star (PNS) formed after a core-collapse supernova (CCSN) or a remnant resulting from a binary neutron star merger (BNSM). The EOS is derived using a relativistic mean-field quantum many-body theory within the Hartree approximation. Coupling constants are determined using experimental data on hypernuclei and hypernuclear matter to better account for uncertainties in hyperon single-particle potentials. Our EOS models reproduce the typical features of cold neutron stars and PNSs for nucleonic and hyperonic compositions. In particular, they are consistent with measured masses (2.01 M_sun and 2.14 M_sun for PSR J0348+0432 and PSR J0740+6620) and dimensionless tidal deformabilities from GW170817. Thermal contributions act differently depending on composition and rotation state. Finally, our evolutionary scheme provides a simple way to interpret the long-term evolution of BNSM remnants or PNSs from CCSNe, complementing dynamical simulations unable to cover full evolutionary timescales.

title: Semileptonic Decays of Heavy Vector Mesons in Hard-Wall AdS/QCD with $N_{f}=5$
Recent results in $b \rightarrow s\,\ell\ell$ transitions at LHCb
abstract: Rare decays of $B$ hadrons, such as $b\rightarrow s\ell \ell$ processes, provide great avenues to search for the influence of new physics (NP). They are highly suppressed in the Standard Model (SM) and therefore sensitive to NP contributions. In recent years, experimental measurements have shown tension with SM predictions. It is still up for debate whether these stem from genuine NP or an incomplete understanding of the theory. These proceedings focus on the recent efforts of the LHCb collaboration to advance this field. Some of the results covered show that tensions in these processes, like in $B^0 \rightarrow K^{*0}\, \mu^+ \mu^-$, still persist upon higher precision. Others aim to shed some light on the theoretical picture through amplitude analyses of decays like $B^0 \rightarrow K^{*0}\, \mu^+ \mu^-$ and $B^+ \rightarrow K^+ \, \mu^+ \mu^-$. We also present two innovative measurements: the branching fraction of $B^0 \rightarrow K^+ \pi^- \mu^+ \mu^-$ at large dihadron mass; and the first hadron collider measurement of the lepton flavour universality ratio of $B^0 \rightarrow K^{*0} \, \ell^+\ell^-$ at high $q^2$ (dilepton mass squared).

title: News from NA61/SHINE
abstract: NA61/SHINE is a multi-purpose, fixed-target hadron spectrometer at the CERN SPS. Its research program includes studies of strong interactions, as well as reference measurements for neutrino and cosmic-ray physics. A significant advantage of NA61/SHINE over collider experiments is its extended coverage of phase space available for particle production. This contribution summarizes recent selected results from our strong interaction program. These include rapidity spectra of $K^+$ and $\pi^-$ mesons in Xe+La reactions compared to other collision systems, energy dependence of the scaled $\pi^-$ total yield (the `kink` plot) in Xe+La compared to other collision systems and models, $\phi$(1020) rapidity spectra in Ar+Sc collisions compared to models, $\Lambda$ transverse polarization in p+p reactions, energy dependence of intensive quantities of net-electric charge distribution in Ar+Sc collisions compared to p+p results, as well as an update on the evidence of large violation of isospin symmetry in kaon production --- the excess of charged over neutral kaons.

title: Measurements of the absolute branching fractions of the $\Lambda_{c}^{+}$ hadronic decays
abstract: Based on 4.5 fb$^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ collision data collected at center-of-mass energies between 4599.53 MeV and 4698.82 MeV with the BESIII detector, the absolute branching fractions of twelve $\Lambda_c^+$ hadronic decay modes are measured with a double-tag technique. A global least-square fit is implemented simultaneously among different decay modes at different energy points. This paper gives the most precise results on the branching fractions of different decay modes to date, with precision improved by a factor of 2 to 3. Among them, the branching fraction of $\Lambda_c^+ \to p K^- \pi^+$ is determined to be $(6.61\pm0.11\pm0.12)\%$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second is systematic. In addition, the $e^+e^-\to\Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$ Born cross sections and the effective form factors ($|G_{\rm eff}|$) at different energy points have been determined with the highest precision to date.}

title: Reconstructing Early Primordial Black Hole Domination from Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds
abstract: Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) with masses below $\mathcal{O}(10^9)$g occupy an interesting region of parameter space that is largely inaccessible to conventional observations. Despite evaporating before Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN), these PBHs can naturally generate a period of early matter domination in the early Universe. A primordial gravitational-wave background (GWB) provides a window onto this otherwise inaccessible regime, since the modified expansion history leaves a characteristic spectral feature associated with the onset and end of PBH domination. The locations of these characteristic frequencies can be used to reconstruct the underlying PBH parameters, in particular the PBH mass. For a freely propagating GWB, the location of these frequencies additionally allow the initial PBH abundance to be determined. We derive simple numerical relations that map these characteristic frequencies directly onto the PBH mass and initial abundance. Future GW experiments span a vast frequency range, providing sensitivity to PBH masses from the BBN bound of $\mathcal{O}(10^9)\,\mathrm{g}$ down to the lower bound of $\mathcal{O}(10)\,\mathrm{g}$. We find that the nanohertz signal reported by NANOGrav, if primordial in origin, is already probing PBH masses in the range $4$--$90\,\mathrm{Mg}$. GW observations therefore offer access to a vast region of PBH parameter space that is otherwise beyond the reach of current experiments.

title: Real versus Complex Fermion Bare Mass and Multi-Wall String Defect Annihilation
abstract: Particle physics models beyond the Standard Model often contain global symmetries to address various unanswered questions. However, a common criticism of theories based on global symmetries is that such symmetries are generally expected to be explicitly violated by gravitational effects at the Planck scale. In the case of a global $U(1)$ symmetry, this explicit breaking can reduce the symmetry to a discrete subgroup of $U(1)$, leading to the formation of cosmic strings attached to multiple domain walls (DWs). These DWs are usually cosmologically problematic, since their slow scaling behavior can eventually dominate the energy density of the Universe, giving rise to the well-known cosmological DW problem, which is strongly constrained by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis. In this work, we propose a mechanism for the annihilation of these DWs. If a fermion coupled to the symmetry-breaking scalar has a small bare mass, radiative corrections generate a temperature-dependent vacuum bias that drives DW collapse. As an example, we consider a majoron model with right-handed neutrinos, where gravity-induced operators produce a string-wall network. We show that a real bare Majorana mass is sufficient to induce complete DW annihilation for even-dimensional gravity-induced operators, whereas odd-dimensional operators require a complex bare Majorana mass whose phase lifts the residual vacuum degeneracy, enabling complete annihilation.

title: Prominence: A discriminator of gravitational wave signals
abstract: The concept of prominence is familiar to signal engineers, topographers and mountaineers. We introduce Prominence $\cal P$ as a discriminator of gravitational wave (GW) signals. We treat black hole and neutron star binaries as astrophysical background sources, and show how $\cal P$ can be used to distinguish between GW spectra produced by first-order phase transitions, domain walls and cosmic strings, and combinations thereof. Prominence can also be used to discriminate between these and off-piste sources of GWs. The uncertainty in the measured energy density in GWs at Pulsar Timing Arrays needs to be at the sub-percent to percent level for $\cal{P}$ to achieve discrimination at 3$\sigma$. LISA and ET data are expected to have sufficiently small uncertainties that Prominence can play a central role in their analysis. We define and apply a $\chi^2$ statistic based on an inner product in signal space to show that sources indistinguishable at $2\sigma$ using the signal-to-noise ratio can be distinguished using $\mathcal{P}$ with significances above and in some cases far above $3\sigma$.

title: Physics of stabilization and dynamic control of CW magnetrons for superconducting accelerators
abstract: Powerful CW magnetrons were suggested for feeding RF cavities of superconducting accelerators because they provide higher efficiency and lower RF power cost than the traditionally used klystrons, IOTs, or solid-state amplifiers. RF amplifiers driven by a master oscillator serve as coherent RF sources. CW magnetrons are regenerative RF self-oscillators with a huge regenerative gain. This causes regenerative instability with notable noise when a magnetron operates as a self-oscillator, i.e., with the anode voltage above the threshold of self-excitation. An injection locking by a small signal was proposed for phase stabilization of magnetrons. In this case, CW magnetrons with injection-locked (coherent) oscillations generate a notable level of noise. This may preclude the use of CW magnetrons in this mode in superconducting RF (SRF) accelerators. This work discusses our analytical results, PIC simulations, and previously obtained analytical and experimental data regarding the operation and control of CW magnetrons. These results led to the development of methods which are most suitable for SRF accelerators.

title: Global Optimization of Beam Profiles for Suppressing the Bump-On-Tail Instability
abstract: A particle beam with constant intensity that propagates into a plasma triggers a bump-on-tail instability. It has been demonstrated that beam modulation can be used to significantly reduce this instability. However, finding the optimal beam profiles that accomplish this is a complex optimization problem that suffers from an extremely rugged optimization landscape and a relatively high-dimensional parameter space. In this paper, we evaluate a number of optimization algorithms and find that population based methods (in particular, CMA-ES and Differential Evolution) perform best. In particular, we investigate beam profiles where the beam is either completely turned ON or OFF. This configuration is easier to accomplish experimentally, but leads to a higher-dimensional and thus more challenging optimization problem. We obtain ON/OFF beam profiles that reduce the instability by more than 80% and thus perform significantly better than what has been reported in the literature.

title: Macroscopic study of $\phi$-mesic nuclei in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 7 TeV with the PACIAE model
abstract: A macroscopic method of the parton and hadron cascade model PACIAE combined with the coalescence model DCPC is employed to study the $\phi$-mesic nuclei in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 7 TeV for the first time in this work. Based on the final hadronic states of $pp$ collisions simulated by the PACIAE model, the $\phi$-mesic nuclei: $\mathrm{^3_{\phi} H}(\phi-pn)$, $\mathrm{^4_{\phi} H}(\phi-pnn)$, and $\mathrm{^4_{\phi} He}(\phi-ppn)$ are recombined by the DCPC model with constituents of protons, neutrons, and $\phi$ mesons. Their yields, transverse momentum spectra, and rapidity distributions are simulated separately. These theoretical predictions call for experimental confirmation.

title: Levy-shaped femtoscopic sources from an exact solution of relativistic hydrodynamics
abstract: An important goal of high-energy physics is to better understand the spacetime structure of particle emitting sources created in heavy-ion collisions. For a fraction of a second a special form of matter, the so-called quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is created, which can be examined with the toolkit of femtoscopy. With the measurement of correlation functions it was determined that L\'evy distributions describe the shape of QGP sources the most accurately, however, based on hydrodynamics Gaussian distributions are typically expected. In this article we showcase an exact solution of the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics, which aims to resolve this puzzle by providing L\'evy distributions directly from hydrodynamics. A detailed analysis reveals whether the predictions of this solution are in accordance with observations.

title: The PSR J0435+3233 Triple System
abstract: The detailed evolution of triple star systems is complicated and poorly known. Using archived optical/infrared and $\gamma$-ray data, we identified the pulsar PSR~J0435+3233 as a $\gamma$-ray pulsar in a hierarchical triple system, with a helium white dwarf (WD) as a close inner binary companion and a Sun-like star as the distant tertiary. PSR~J0435+3233 and the WD companion are in a circular orbit with a period of $P_{\rm orb1} = 8.0$~days and an eccentricity of $e=0.00016$. The tertiary is a G-type subgiant with a mass of $0.98(12) M_\odot$ at a distance of $2.1(4)$ kpc from the Earth. By simultaneously fitting the observed spin-period variations of the $\gamma$-ray emission (over 16.7 years) and radio emission (over 4.9 years) from PSR~J0435+3233, the changes in the inner orbital parameters, the Shapiro delay, Gaia astrometry, and the outer companion mass, we determined the outer elliptical orbit for the tertiary, with a period $P_{\rm orb2} = 73.5$~yrs and an eccentricity $e_2 = 0.598$. The outer orbit is either nearly perpendicular to the inner orbit with a mutual inclination of $\sim 85^\circ$, or moderately inclined by $\sim 54^\circ$. For the former geometry, the pulsar, the WD, and the tertiary star have masses of $1.16(5) M_\odot$, $0.273(8) M_\odot$, and $0.91(5) M_\odot$, respectively; for the latter geometry, the corresponding masses are $1.34(15) M_\odot$, $0.305(23) M_\odot$, and $1.13(7) M_\odot$. This is a unique triple system for detailed multi-band observations and for studying the evolutionary path and dynamic processes of a primordial triple star system. It will ultimately evolve into a system consisting of a neutron star and two white dwarfs.

title: Neutrino Telescope Event Classification on Quantum Computers
abstract: Quantum computers represent a new computational paradigm with steadily improving hardware capabilities.
